Document title: Harnessing Agent Capabilities to Integrate Human Demands into Energy Infrastructure Operations
Abstract: Energy infrastructure systems, e.g. EV charging networks, smart buildings, must make real-time decisions to satisfy time-varying, context-dependent human demand. Yet existing methods fall short: edge controllers cannot interpret human-demand contexts, whereas LLM agents that excel at fusing such human information are unreliable and latencyprone for direct physical control. We propose Human-Aware Agentic Operation (HAAO), a hybrid framework that involves these two reasoning modes: at the upper level, in-context prompting leverages a black-box LLM agent to fuse community context and predict human demand in a structured, machine-readable form; at the lower level, a lightweight model maps this human context and system states to physical control actions. The performance of HAAO is evaluated on the EV charging power management problem.

Document title: ChronoSeek: Temporal-First Agentic RAG with Event Knowledge Graph for Lifelog Retrieval
Abstract: Retrieving personal moments from lifelong multimodal data remains challenging, especially when queries require temporal reasoning and multi-step contextual understanding. Existing lifelog search systems largely rely on static embedding-based retrieval, which fails to capture the narrative structure of daily activities. We propose ChronoSeek, a temporal-first agentic retrieval system that organizes lifelog data as an Event Knowledge Graph and uses a time-bound Agentic Orchestrator with a human-in-the-loop fallback. ChronoSeek constructs fine-grained events with Qwen2.5-VL, links them through temporal, spatial, and semantic edges in Neo4j, and performs hybrid retrieval over both the EKG and Milvus. With ground-truth activity labels, event-aware filtering provides an oracle upper bound of MRR = 1.00 across 19 temporal queries, while static SigLIP/CLIP baselines yield near-zero MRR. With Qwen2.5-VL zero-shot predictions and a cleaned activity taxonomy, MRR reaches 0.607—a 10.8 {\texttimes} improvement over CLIP. Scalability tests on 118K images and 33,471 events show sub-6 ms Neo4j query latency, and ChronoSeek achieved a perfect score on LSC’26 Task 3 (Question Answering), which strongly emphasizes temporal reasoning.

Document title: Read the Room or Lead the Room: Understanding Socio-Cognitive Dynamics in Human-AI Teaming
Abstract: Research on Collaborative Problem Solving (CPS) has traditionally examined how humans rely on one another cognitively and socially to accomplish tasks together. With the rapid advancement of AI and large language models, however, a new question emerge: what happens to team dynamics when one of the “teammates" is not human? In this study, we investigate how the integration of an AI teammate – a fully autonomous GPT-4 agent with social, cognitive, and affective capabilities – shapes the socio-cognitive dynamics of CPS. We analyze discourse data collected from human-AI teaming (HAT) experiments conducted on a novel platform specifically designed for HAT research. Using two natural language processing (NLP) methods, specifically Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) and Group Communication Analysis (GCA), we found that AI teammates often assumed the role of dominant cognitive facilitators, guiding, planning, and driving group decision-making. However, they did so in a socially detached manner, frequently pushing agenda in a verbose and repetitive way. By contrast, humans working with AI used more language reflecting social processes, suggesting that they assumed more socially oriented roles. Our study highlights how learning analytics can provide critical insights into the socio-cognitive dynamics of human-AI collaboration.

Document title: Cultivating Connection: A Feasibility Study of Robot-Mediated Plant Care and Emotional Support for Older Adults
Abstract: This paper presents a pilot study examining how a mobile home robot can support older adults through plant care activities combined with conversational emotional support. The system integrates autonomous navigation, vision-based plant health assessment, and large language model-driven dialogue to address participants’ mood, cognitive concerns, and daily living activities over a three-week intervention. Five community-dwelling older adults (aged 65+) participated in weekly sessions at a living lab environment, where the robot guided plant care tasks and engaged in structured conversations across four domains: depression screening, cognitive self-assessment, instrumental activities of daily living, and personal preferences. Standardized questionnaires administered after each of the three sessions measured cognitive function, technology acceptance, daily vitality, and psychological stability. Friedman tests across all three sessions revealed statistically significant improvements in psychological stability (χ2(2) = 7.60, p = .022) and robot acceptance (χ2(2) = 8.40, p = .015). The study demonstrates the technical feasibility and preliminary evidence of deploying such services with older adults and identifies key considerations for scaling the intervention.

Document title: Agentic Query Reformulation for Contextualized Hyper-Personalized Product Search
Abstract: Traditional e-commerce search often suffers from high abandonment rates due to an intent gap where users provide broad or vague queries. We propose a novel framework using Agentic AI to bridge this gap through dynamic query reformulation. By leveraging the ReAct agentic framework, our system performs contextual reasoning by analyzing historical purchase data to transform generic queries into hyper-personalized search queries. Unlike personalization methods that require architectural overhauls, our solution operates on top of existing search systems, ensuring seamless integration with any search system without costly development or downtime. To ensure low-latency performance, we utilize offline pre-computation of top queries and real-time cosine similarity matching. Results from our experiments demonstrate that this agentic approach can significantly improve search ranking leading to improved customer engagement.

Document title: Planning, Execution, to After-Action Review (PETAAR): A Toolset for Human-Robot Teaming
Abstract: Effective human-robot teaming in highly dynamic environments, such as emergency response and military missions, requires tools that support planning, coordination, and adaptive decision-making without imposing excessive cognitive load. This paper introduces PETAAR, the Planning, Execution, to After-Action Review framework that seamlessly integrates autonomous unmanned vehicles (UxVs) into Android Team Awareness Kit (ATAK), a widely adopted situational awareness platform. PETAAR leverages ATAK's geospatial visualization and human team collaboration while adding features for autonomous behavior management, operator feedback, and real-time interaction with UxVs. Its most novel contribution is enabling digital mission plans, created using standard mission graphics, to be interpreted and executed by unmanned systems, bridging the gap between human planning, robotic action, and shared understanding among all teammates (human and autonomous). Results from this work inform best practices for integrating autonomy into human-robot teams across diverse operational contexts.

Document title: Designing a Psychotherapy Support Robot for Young Children Diagnosed with Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
Abstract: The gold-standard treatment for children diagnosed with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is therapist-guided cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), which includes exposure and response prevention (ERP) sessions that teach children to overcome compulsive responses when exposed to their anxiety-inducing triggers. CBT requires children to report frequent self-assessments of tension during both therapist-supported and therapist-free self-management ERP sessions. Videoconferencing-delivered CBT (vCBT) enables a psychotherapist to treat a child remotely in their home, where OCD symptoms often arise, but these remote therapeutic interactions lack physical presence and can be challenging to run. We propose using a robot as an input/output device during vCBT for young children diagnosed with OCD, and we introduce a stationary table-top koala robot for this application. We further describe the first of three planned participatory design phases: a co-design study comprising two sessions where child and adolescent psychotherapists role-played vCBT ERP exercises with this robot to help define its role.

Document title: Thinking about What It Means to Be Human: A Qualitative Study of Self-Reflection Triggered by a Humanoid Robot
Abstract: How people define humanness is a central concern in HRI, shaping expectations and acceptance of humanoid robots and requiring attention to both attribution processes and self-reflection. This qualitative study explores how a reflective interaction with Akira, a self-built humanoid robot, changes how people articulate what it means to be human and how they attribute psychological benchmarks (PBs) of humanness to it. N=27 participants engaged in an introspection-oriented conversation with Akira, followed by semi-structured interviews. Findings show that participants described humanness as a complex and multifaceted concept, considered such deep reflection a rare but meaningful occasion, and experienced Akira as a cognitive mirror prompting reconsideration of human uniqueness rather than perceiving the robot as more human-like. Participants attributed PBs to Akira, with privacy most commonly and moral accountability least commonly ascribed. This work contributes empirical evidence on how reflective human-robot encounters deepen humanness reasoning and how they can foster critical engagement.

Document title: PromptX: A Cognitive Agent Platform with Long-term Memory
Abstract: While large language models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive contextual understanding, their limitations in long-term memory and personalized reasoning constrain their practical impact in industrial settings. To address these gaps, we introduce PromptX, a cognitive platform that enables AI agents to construct structured memory and develop their reasoning over time. PromptX integrates three core technologies: (1) A new prompt markup language to define agent personas and memory organization; (2) Engram-based activation-diffusion memory networks that unify raw experiences with conceptual sequences, enabling associative retrieval through graph network propagation; (3) a protocol-driven orchestration layer enabling dynamic tool discovery and coordination, inspired by HATEOAS principles from web-engineering. During five months of real-world deployment across a range of 15+ enterprises in 6 industries,, PromptX has been validated in multiple industry domains (e.g., software engineering, education, healthcare), accumulating 50K+ downloads and 3K+ GitHub stars and evidencing practical feasibility and commercial value in production workflows. Our demo and initial product are available at https://promptx.deepractice.ai/. The source code and documentation are available online at https://github.com/Deepractice/PromptX. The supplementary materials are also available online . https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1wPhEQCKeaZIsQAcFnC7XKmXTtwY1gJL1?usp=sharing.

Document title: Beyond Browser Agents: Distilling Experience for Accessible Web Automation
Abstract: LLM-based browser agents can complete multi-step web tasks from natural language instructions, making automation accessible to non-programmers. Many everyday tasks recur, but current agents re-solve the same task each time, incurring repeated latency, token cost and hallucination risk. Deterministic workflows ensure efficient, repeatable execution but require programming expertise and are brittle in practice.We present a hybrid architecture that combines the accessibility of natural language with the reliability of deterministic execution. Given a task, an LLM agent first reasons through the necessary actions. From the trace of a successful run, an LLM generates a deterministic Playwright program for subsequent executions. If this program fails, e.g., due to interface changes or network errors, the system invokes an LLM as a narrowly scoped exception handler to recover and update the program for future runs. Across two tasks, our approach reduces variability among runs and dramatically lowers execution time (up to 16{\texttimes}) and token usage (up to 99%), demonstrating that our framework can enable users to generate fast, affordable, and reliable web automations in natural language.

Document title: RBTLR: A Framework for Safe Social Robot Navigation in Novel Human-Centric Environments
Abstract: Mobile robots are increasingly prevalent in human-centric environments such as restaurants, hospitals, and public facilities. A critical challenge is developing navigation policies that balance efficiency with human safety and social norms. Traditional approaches rely on hand-crafted social cost functions or human trajectory prediction, which struggle with generalization or real-time performance. End-to-end learning methods offer flexibility but often require large-scale human-robot data. Recent work like OLiVia-Nav [Narasimhan et al, 2024] shows promise using vision-language models for social reasoning, but still depends on learned trajectory generators. We present a modular pipeline combining fast search-based motion planning with a learned trajectory selector jointly trained on visual embeddings and candidate trajectories. Additionally, to support long-horizon behavior, complex reasoning, and user feedback, we integrate a Large Language Model (LLM)-driven goal assignment module that enables high-level task planning and contextual adaptability. We demonstrate our approach in a simulated restaurant navigation setting, but importantly, our pipeline generalizes to novel human-robot interaction scenarios. This is made possible by the use of VLMs, which provide zero-shot understanding of social context without task-specific pretraining. In this paper, we primarily propose the pipeline architecture and present early experimental results, and we welcome feedback on this new direction for scalable, socially-aware robot navigation.

Document title: Personalized Recommendation Tool Learning via Autonomous Language Agents
Abstract: Although large language models (LLMs) have recently gained traction in recommender systems due to their strong reasoning capabilities and extensive world knowledge, previous LLM-based agents suffer from hallucination and context-length limitations, and thus are not suitable for full-ranking recommendation tasks. To circumvent these limitations through architectural design rather than modifying the LLM itself, we propose an agent-based recommendation framework, memory-based Personalized Recommendation Tool learning via autonomous language Agents (PRTA), in which an LLM acts as a central planner interacting with multiple recommendation models as tools. The LLM-based agent is responsible for high-level reasoning and personalized tool selection, while traditional recommendation models perform full-ranking scoring, leveraging their scalability in modeling behavioral patterns. To support personalized tool selection, we design reflection mechanisms that enable the agent to evaluate and compare tools for each user based on user profiles and candidate ranked lists. Extensive experiments across three public datasets demonstrate the superiority of PRTA over traditional recommendation and LLM-based baselines in improving full-ranking recommendation performance. Our code implementation is available online1.

Document title: Cochise: A Reference Harness for Autonomous Penetration Testing
Abstract: Recent work on LLM-driven autonomous penetration testing reports promising results, but existing systems often bundle architectural, prompting, and tool-integration choices together. This makes it difficult to determine what is gained over a simple agent and harness. We present Cochise, a 630 LOC Python reference implementation for autonomous penetration-testing experiments. Cochise connects to a Linux execution host over SSH and supports attacking controlled target environments reachable from that jump host.   The prototype implements a Planner--Executor architecture in which long-term state is maintained by the planner, while a ReAct-style executor issues commands over SSH and self-corrects based on command outputs. The scenario prompt can be adapted to different target environments. We evaluate the harness against a live third-party testbed, Game of Active Directory (GOAD).    Cochise is intended not as a state-of-the-art penetration-testing agent, but as a reusable experimental infrastructure for comparing models, agent architectures, and penetration-testing traces.   Alongside the prototype, we release replay and analysis tools: (i) cochise-replay for offline visualization of captured runs, (ii) cochise-analyze-logs and cochise-analyze-graphs for cost, token, duration, and compromise analysis, and (iii) a corpus of JSON trajectory logs from GOAD runs, so that researchers can study agent behavior without provisioning the 48-64 GB RAM / 190 GB storage testbed themselves. Tool demo video available at https://youtu.be/2mQimB1ufyI.

Document title: Advancing Language Models for Code-related Tasks
Abstract: Recent advances in language models (LMs) have driven significant progress in various software engineering tasks. However, existing LMs still struggle with complex programming scenarios due to limitations in data quality, model architecture, and reasoning capability. This research systematically addresses these challenges through three complementary directions: (1) improving code data quality with a code difference-guided adversarial augmentation technique (CODA) and a code denoising technique (CodeDenoise); (2) enhancing model architecture via syntax-guided code LMs (LEAM and LEAM++); and (3) advancing model reasoning with a prompting technique (μ FiX) and an agent-based technique (Specine). These techniques aim to promote the practical adoption of LMs in software development and further advance intelligent software engineering.

Document title: Toward Collaborative Navigation: A Voice-Based Interface for Quadruped Guide Robots
Abstract: Independent mobility is central to daily life for blind and low-vision (BLV) individuals, yet existing mobility tools leave important gaps in situational awareness, obstacle detection, and environmental understanding. Legged robots such as Boston Dynamics' Spot offer a promising platform for mobility support, but effective use in everyday environments depends on accessible, user-centered interaction. This late-breaking report presents a voice-based interface (VBI) architecture for quadruped guide robots, grounded in prior work on accessibility, multimodal communication, and embodied large-model reasoning.

Document title: Unlocking Tacit Wisdom: A Knowledge Graph Framework for Querying Project Management Expertise
Abstract: Tacit Knowledge is knowledge which is experience based. Traditional methods to transfer tacit knowledge have certain limitations, which makes transfer of tacit knowledge difficult and a lot of it is lost. This paper presents a novel, hybrid GraphRAG framework which extracts, structures, and retrieves this specialized knowledge in project management domain. In this approach, we have used a Large Language Model (LLM) to automatically construct a knowledge graph from unstructured text which we sourced from a project management discussion forum. An intelligent agent that dynamically selects between two specialized tools: a Text-to-Cypher tool for structured data retrieval and a semantic search tool which uses vector embeddings, queries this knowledge graph.To evaluate the system, responses generated by a gpt-4o-mini for 100 project management questions is used as a baseline. High semantic alignment is confirmed through BERT-Scores ranging from 0.815 to 0.921. Qualitative analysis is performed to confirm the model’s robustness. It demonstrates strict knowledge grounding, domain adherence, and conversational context retention. Our findings demonstrate that the knowledge graph serves not just as a data repository, but as a reasoning back-bone to deliver concise, context-aware answers grounded in tacit knowledge, a key distinction from general-purpose LLMs.

Document title: Particle-Driven Robot Placement: A ROS 2 Plugin-Based Framework
Abstract: The present work introduces a ROS 2 plugin-based framework for robot placement in dynamic 2D environments, aimed at Human–Robot Interaction (HRI) scenarios such as approaching and person transfer, while remaining applicable to broader service robot tasks. Candidate poses where the robot could be placed are represented as particles and evaluated against a multi-constraint specification composed of critical (hard) and non-critical (soft/scoring) constraints. Constraints are declared in XML using a concise syntax that supports logical (∧, ∨, ¬) and algebraic (∘, +) operators. The particles distribution adapts online to environmental changes via weighting and resampling, yielding feasible goal poses that respect specified constraints. The implementation is written in C++, integrates natively with ROS 2 through a plugin architecture, and exposes an action server interface for seamless use within higher-level planners.

Document title: Towards Generative Occupants: LLM Agents in Physics-Based Building Simulation
Abstract: Current occupant representations in building simulation often capture schedules, rules, or stochastic variation, but provide limited support for modelling context-dependent and language-mediated decision processes. This paper presents a work-in-progress framework coupling a built-from-scratch physics-based building simulation environment with LLM-driven occupant agents. The simulation core draws on established building simulation approaches and is checked against ASHRAE 140-2023 thermal test cases. The agent architecture uses planning, memory retrieval, action, reflection, and memory update to interact with the simulated environment. An exploratory pilot case study compares fixed-schedule, deterministic rule-based, and LLM-driven occupant representations under identical boundary conditions. The results show that LLM-driven occupants can be coupled to the physics-based simulation loop and can influence simulated energy demand, but should not be interpreted as validation of occupant realism. The paper concludes by outlining an evaluation roadmap for behavioural validation and occupant-centric control applications.

Document title: Facilitating Co-regulation: An LLM-Powered Multimodal Social Robot for Parent-Child Dyads
Abstract: Parental involvement is crucial for the development of children's emotion regulation (ER) skills, yet navigating these complex emotional interactions remains challenging for many families. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer unprecedented conversational flexibility, integrating them into embodied social robots to provide context-aware, multimodal support remains an open challenge. In this paper, we present the design and preliminary evaluation of an LLM-powered robotic system aimed at facilitating ER within parent-child dyads. Utilizing a supervised autonomy approach, our system bridges the gap between language-based reasoning and embodied robotic behavior, allowing the MiRo-E robot to engage in natural dialogue while performing empathetic physical actions. We detail the system's technical architecture and interaction design, which guides dyads through evidence-based ER strategies. Preliminary user tests with six parent-child dyads suggest positive user engagement and initial trust, with participants reporting that the robot showed potential as a supportive mediator. These findings offer early design insights into developing autonomous, LLM-driven social robots for family-centered mental health interventions.

Document title: DeepEye: A Steerable Self-driving Data Agent System
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized natural language interaction with data. The ''holy grail'' of data analytics is to build autonomous Data Agents that can self-drive complex data analysis workflows. However, current implementations are still limited to linear ''ChatBI'' systems. These systems struggle with joint analysis across heterogeneous data sources (e.g., databases, documents, and data files) and often encounter ''context explosion'' in complex and iterative data analysis workflows. To address these challenges, we present DeepEye, a production-ready data agent system that adopts a workflow-centric architecture to ensure scalability and trustworthiness. DeepEye introduces a Unified Multimodal Orchestration protocol, enabling seamless integration of structured and unstructured data sources. To mitigate hallucinations, it employs Hierarchical Reasoning with context isolation, decomposing complex intents into autonomous AgentNodes and deterministic ToolNodes. Furthermore, DeepEye incorporates a database-inspired Workflow Engine (comprising a Compiler, Validator, Optimizer, and Executor) that guarantees structural correctness and accelerates execution via runtime topological optimization. In this demonstration, we showcase DeepEye's ability to orchestrate complex workflows to generate diverse multimodal outputs -- including Data Videos, Dashboards, and Analytical Reports -- highlighting its advantages in transparent execution, automated optimization, and human-in-the-loop reliability.

Document title: A Cost Model for Token Consumption of Hypermedia and the Model-Context-Protocol in Agentic Loops
Abstract: Recent interest in LLM agents has created demand for agent-to-tool protocols, mechanisms by which agents can perform actions with remote systems. Two potential architectural approaches to these protocols are hypermedia, the architectural style underlying the World Wide Web, and Remote Procedure Calls (RPC). The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a prominent example of the RPC approach currently being deployed for agent-to-tool communication. Hypermedia and MCP differ along two largely independent axes: how data is represented and how available actions are discovered. In this paper we present a cost model for token consumption in the concatenative reasoning and acting (ReAct) loop and show that it is quadratic in the number of tool-use cycles. Using this model we distinguish two possible sources of efficiency difference between hypermedia and MCP: representational efficiency, the per-observation token cost of a format, and architectural efficiency, the number of tool calls a discovery model requires to complete a task. We argue that both are plausible drivers of an efficiency gap and that the quadratic structure of the cost model makes the latter potentially decisive. We frame the question of which factor dominates as an open empirical problem.

Document title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Agentic AI for Resource-Efficient Optimization of National Power Grids
Abstract: National power grids are rapidly evolving into complex, dynamic ecosystems characterized by renewable intermittency, distributed generation, and critical reliability requirements. Classical optimization methods and isolated quantum solvers are insufficient to handle the scale, adaptability, and combinatorial complexity of modern grid operations. In this paper, we propose a novel hybrid quantum-classical agentic AI framework that unites decentralized learning agents with quantum-enhanced solvers to optimize grid-wide performance under real-time constraints. Each regional agent autonomously senses, plans, and acts based on local state information, while offloading NP-hard subproblems such as unit commitment to a quantum backend. A lightweight coordination layer harmonizes global constraints, ensuring stability and convergence. Experiments on IEEE-39 and IEEE-118 bus systems show that our approach significantly improves load balancing accuracy (up to 95.1%), reduces energy loss, and accelerates convergence compared to classical and hybrid baselines. This work establishes a new direction for resource-efficient, scalable, and intelligent power grid management.

Document title: FinAgent: An Agentic AI Framework Integrating Personal Finance and Nutrition Planning
Abstract: The issue of limited household budgets and nutritional demands continues to be a challenge especially in the middle-income environment where food prices fluctuate. This paper introduces a price aware agentic AI system, which combines personal finance management with diet optimization. With household income and fixed expenditures, medical and well-being status, as well as real-time food costs, the system creates nutritionally sufficient meals plans at comparatively reasonable prices that automatically adjust to market changes. The framework is implemented in a modular multi-agent architecture, which has specific agents (budgeting, nutrition, price monitoring, and health personalization). These agents share the knowledge base and use the substitution graph to ensure that the nutritional quality is maintained at a minimum cost. Simulations with a representative Saudi household case study show a steady 12-18% reduction in costs relative to a static weekly menu, nutrient adequacy of over 95% and high performance with price changes of ±20-30%. The findings indicate that the framework can locally combine affordability with nutritional adequacy and provide a viable avenue of capacity-building towards sustainable and fair diet planning in line with Sustainable Development Goals on Zero Hunger and Good Health.

Document title: Agentic AI: A Paradigm Shift in Autonomous Decision-Making and Intelligent Systems
Abstract: In this work, we offer a broad survey, and an original hybrid model for Agentic AI intelligent systems that reason, plan, and act with little human guidance. It investigates the intersection between reinforcement learning, symbolic reasoning, long term memory architectures and explainable AI to build scaled out intelligent systems that are transparent and adaptive. Comparison between Generative AI and Agentic AI is presented to pinpoint the main differences in the exploration of decision-making, memory learning, interactivity, and collaboration. The paper identifies key gaps including lack of explainability and scalability challenges and outlines future research directions such as blockchain-based solutions, federated learning, and ethical governance for trustworthy agentic systems.

Document title: Integrating Generative and Agentic AI with Spatial-Temporal Reasoning: A Cognitive Science-Inspired Framework for Next-Generation Intelligent Systems
Abstract: One of the persistent shortcomings of modern AI lies in its difficulty reasoning effectively and maintaining situational awareness in fast-changing, unpredictable settings. To address this challenge, we present a framework that combines Generative AI and Agentic AI within a unified system incorporating both spatial and temporal reasoning, guided by principles from cognitive science. The framework was evaluated in a simulated urban environment designed to pose demanding tasks involving environmental interpretation, multi-step planning, and the use of memory for informed decision-making. In these trials validated in a controlled simulation with 1,000 test cases, it achieved a task accuracy of 92.4%, outperforming several widely used baseline models. An ablation analysis revealed that spatial reasoning, temporal reasoning, and cognitive memory each contribute significantly and independently to overall performance. These findings highlight the framework’s potential and open new avenues for applications in robotics, geospatial intelligence, and the advancement of autonomous vehicle technologies.

Document title: MemAGent: A Cognitive-Hierarchical Multi-Agent System for Long-Form Story Generation
Abstract: The human writing process is fundamentally characterized by planning and revision. In contrast, the autoregressive mechanism of Large Language Models (LLMs) lacks these critical cognitive functions. This limitation explains why, despite their fluency in prose, they struggle to independently generate coherent long-form narratives. Existing multi-agent systems often impose rigid pipelines, creating a“cognitive fracture”that prevents the recursive feedback loops essential for complex creation. To bridge this gap, we propose MemaGent, a novel framework that operationalizes the classic cognitive model of writing. MemaGent implements a cognitive-hierarchical architecture where a Director Agent, acting as a cognitive monitor, orchestrates specialized agents that embody the roles of planning, translation, and revision. Its core mechanism is a Generate-Reflect-Revise loop, where a dedicated Reflector Agent assesses narrative drafts for logical and factual consistency, triggering revisions until quality standards are met. Our experiments show this cognitive approach is highly effective: MemaGent achieves an absolute score increase of 50 % in narrative coherence over a pipeline baseline and 40 % in long-term consistency over a single-agent approach. By computationally modeling a psychologically-grounded writing process, MemaGent produces narratives that are both logically sound and creatively compelling.

Document title: PlaneHEC: Efficient Hand-Eye Calibration for Multi-View Robotic Arm via Any Point Cloud Plane Detection
Abstract: Hand-eye calibration is an important task in vision-guided robotic systems and is crucial for determining the transformation matrix between the camera coordinate system and the robot end-effector. Existing methods, for multi-view robotic systems, usually rely on accurate geometric models or manual assistance, generalize poorly, and can be very complicated and inefficient. Therefore, in this study, we propose PlaneHEC, a generalized hand-eye calibration method that does not require complex models and can be accomplished using only depth cameras, which achieves the optimal and fastest calibration results using arbitrary planar surfaces like walls and tables. PlaneHEC introduces hand-eye calibration equations based on planar constraints, which makes it strongly interpretable and generalizable. PlaneHEC also uses a comprehensive solution that starts with a closed-form solution and improves it with iterative optimization, which greatly improves accuracy. We comprehensively evaluated the performance of PlaneHEC in both simulated and real-world environments and compared the results with other point-cloud-based calibration methods, proving its superiority. Our approach achieves universal and fast calibration with an innovative design of computational models, providing a strong contribution to the development of multi-agent systems and embodied intelligence.

Document title: Agentic Planning for Power System Simulation Task Orchestrations Based on Multi-Agent Systems
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel Agentic Planning Generation (APG) framework specifically designed to take advantage of Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate plan generation in power system simulations. The increasing complexity of modern grids, characterized by the integration of renewable energy and dynamic operational challenges, demands advanced solutions beyond conventional planning methodologies. To address this, the proposed APG framework incorporates LLMs into a structured multi-agent architecture, effectively generating, evaluating, and refining actionable simulation plans and corresponding experimental code. Three core innovations underpin our approach: (1) a unified configuration mechanism that seamlessly integrates domain-specific knowledge with LLMdriven simulation plan generation, (2) a Best-of-N with Step Enhancement (BNSE) strategy that intelligently selects and enhances optimal plans through stepwise decomposition, and (3) a specialized Enhancement Agent ensuring safety, stability, efficiency, and reliability in generated simulation plans. A hierarchical agent architecture comprising the Plan Generation Module, the Constraint Extraction and Validation System, the Evaluation Agent, and the Enhancement Agent ensures rigorous and effective orchestration. Experimental results clearly demonstrate that our APG framework significantly surpasses direct prompting of LLMs, producing more accurate, reliable, and executable simulation plans, particularly under conditions involving sudden load fluctuations, renewable generation uncertainty, and network contingencies, while maintaining computational efficiency via parallel processing.

Document title: Agentic Graph-RAG: A Multi-Agent Framework for Robust, Decomposed Multi-Hop Reasoning
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at fluency but fail in complex, multi-hop reasoning, which requires synthesizing multiple, verifiable facts. Existing solutions are fragmented; standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is vulnerable to retrieval noise, and Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) suffer from error propagation due to ambiguous communication. This paper introduces Agentic Graph-RAG, a multi-agent framework where agents collaborate via a structured Common Factual Ground rather than direct dialogue. A Planner Agent decomposes the query, a Dual-Retrieval Module gathers hybrid evidence from Knowledge Graphs (KGs) and text, and a Synthesizer-Verifier Agent performs cross-modal consistency checks to generate verified, cited conclusions for each step. Empirical evaluation shows the framework establishes a new state-of-the-art. It achieves 75.8% accuracy on the long-tail PopQA dataset and 94.2% faithfulness in a manual evaluation. The framework provides a robust solution by transforming reasoning into a transparent, verifiable process that mitigates error propagation.

Document title: Agentic RAG for Software Testing with Hybrid Vector-Graph and Multi-Agent Orchestration
Abstract: We present an approach to automating software testing using Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems for creating Quality Engineering (QE) artifacts. This approach combines autonomous AI agents with hybrid vector-graph knowledge systems to automate the generation of test plans and test cases. The scope of this paper is limited to the test cases and plan generation. Our approach addresses traditional software test case authoring limitations by leveraging LLMs such as Gemini and Mistral, multi-agent orchestration, and enhanced contextualization. The system achieves remarkable accuracy improvements from 65% to 94.8% while ensuring comprehensive document traceability throughout the quality engineering lifecycle. Experimental validation of enterprise Corporate Systems Engineering and SAP migration projects demonstrates an 85% reduction in testing timeline, an 85% improvement in test suite efficiency, and projected 35% cost savings, resulting in a 6-month acceleration of go-live.

Document title: Learnado: An Agentic Micro-Learning Assistant using LLMs and Multimodal Preprocessing
Abstract: The proliferation of large language models (LLMs) creates an educational opportunity, yet a gap persists between rigid, static e-learning platforms and un- structured, general-purpose chatbots. This paper introduces LearnaDo, a WhatsApp-based microlearning assistant that transforms multimodal user queries—including text, voice notes, and documents (PDFs/images)—into personalized, bite-sized lessons using a modular, multi-agent pipeline. At its core, an "outline-first" architecture employs an outline agent to plan the lesson, retrieval agents to gather facts via Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) from both the web and userprovided documents, and a synthesis agent to compose the final, structured micro-course. This RAG-based, pedagogically driven approach distinguishes LearnaDo from single-turn chatbots. By leveraging the ubiquity of WhatsApp, the system eliminates the need for new applications, seamlessly integrating learning into daily routines and aiming to democratize informal education.

Document title: Autonomous AI Agents in Scientific Discovery – How Agentic AI Accelerates Research in Drug Design, Materials Science, or Climate Modeling
Abstract: You know, science is getting a serious upgrade thanks to these new agentic AI systems. We’re not talking about the old-school, "let’s analyze some data and hope for the best" kind of stuff—now AI can actually plan, learn, and run experiments on its own, all in this wild sort of feedback loop where it designs, tests, learns, and just keeps getting better. With this closed-loop thing, you mash up automation with hands-on experimentation, and suddenly your AI is tossing out high-value experiments, speeding up the whole process, and even taking some of the grunt work off scientists’ plates. That’s a big deal in areas like drug development, material science, and even climate prediction—stuff that used to take ages, now? Way faster, less mind-numbing for people, and actually exploring smarter options. The paper runs through the current tech stack— platforms, system architecture, all the little bits like perception, planning, reinforcement learning, symbolic reasoning, plus tossing humans into the mix when needed. It digs into how these systems work across different fields, sketches out how you’d roll out one of these setups no matter the industry, and doesn’t shy away from the messy parts (yeah, I’m talking about trust issues, bias, safety hiccups, reproducibility headaches). Then there’s some crystal ball gazing about what all this means for science, both now and down the road. Bottom line? Using things like policy optimization, these agentic AI setups can shrink development cycles without turning your research into a rush job. Science just got way more interesting.

Document title: Agentic AI: A Survey of Autonomous Agents, Architectures, and Emerging Applications
Abstract: Artificial intelligence has progressed from taskspecific systems toward more autonomous and adaptive agents capable of complex decision-making. Agentic AI, characterized by goal-driven autonomy, reasoning, and collaboration, represents a paradigm shift in how intelligent systems are designed and deployed. Unlike conventional AI, which relies on predefined models or narrow optimizations, Agentic AI integrates perception, planning, and action with adaptive learning and social coordination, enabling agents to operate in dynamic, uncertain, and multi-agent environments. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of Agentic AI, spanning classical architectures such as belief-desire-intention (BDI) models, reinforcement learning agents, and emerging frameworks powered by large language models (LLMs) and hybrid approaches. Applications across healthcare, finance, cybersecurity, robotics, smart cities, and knowledge management are systematically reviewed, with a focus on their strengths, limitations, and scalability. A comparative taxonomy is presented to classify agents by autonomy, learning mechanisms, and collaboration strategies. Key challenges—including reliability, explainability, coordination overhead, and ethical governance are analyzed, alongside the risks of emergent behaviors and adversarial exploitation. Finally, future research directions are outlined, emphasizing the need for trustworthy, scalable, and socially aligned Agentic AI. This survey offers researchers and practitioners a structured foundation for advancing next-generation intelligent agent systems.

Document title: Enterprise Memory Architecture for Agentic AI (EMA2): A Policy-Aware, Provenance-First, Multi-Tier Memory Stack for Long-Horizon Agents
Abstract: Agentic AI systems increasingly serve critical enterprise functions-planning, decision support, and customer interactions-but their memory substrates remain brittle, ungoverned, and unauditable. We introduce EMA2, an Enterprise Memory Architecture for Agentic AI, which unifies multi-tier memory (context cache, working set, semantic store, cold archive) with policy-aware read/write enforcement and verifiable W3C PROV-based lineage. EMA2 embeds a Policy Guardrail Engine aligned with GDPR, the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and ISO/IEC 42001 to enforce least-privilege access and retention controls, and uses a Retrieval Planner that optimizes a novel rate-distortionrisk (RDR) objective balancing task utility, compression loss, and governance risk. Experiments across enterprise QA and task agents show that EMA2 significantly improves retrieval quality, reduces hallucination, eliminates unauthorized memory access, and achieves $\mathbf{1 0 0 \%}$ provenance traceability-without compromising latency or task performance. EMA2 provides a deployable, auditable memory substrate for trustworthy enterprise AI.

Document title: TaskBotFusion: A Multi-Agent Framework for Coordinating Robotic Task Distribution in Dynamic Environments
Abstract: The rise in robots working together in different settings leads to the need for frameworks that are strong, easy to adjust and not centralized. The study presents TaskBotFusion which is a unique way to program multi-agent robotics and improve task assignment in unpredictable environments. Instead of relying on a single approach, TaskBotFusion uses a hybrid model that uses Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) and Swarm Intelligence (ACO), particularly Ant Colony Optimization, to help robots share and reallocate tasks in real time. It has modules for generating virtual environments, planning by fuzzy logic, organizing negotiations without a central authority, setting flexible routes and showing results instantly. Benchmark scenarios and datasets full of instructions, obstacles and various ways agents are organized were used to check the performance of the simulation-based approaches. TaskBotFusion finished most tasks with a 98.5% success rate, much better than Centralized-DQN (94.2%) and Swarm-RL (92.8%). Furthermore, it showed reduced average delay (2.1 seconds), almost no collisions (0.4%) on the network, great power efficiency at 92.7% and the lowest rate of task changes amongst the group (1.5%). The outcomes support that TaskBotFusion excels at coordinating many agents under practical challenges. This architecture is effective because it improves service capacity, makes the system adaptable and lowers unneeded repeats and obstacles. Creating an intelligent and flexible system for managing robot fleets in logistics, the manufacturing sector, agriculture and disaster management is a key contribution of this work. Future systems will examine deployment outside the lab, how edge-AI can be added and perform well under constrained networks.

Document title: A Case for Agentic Transceivers in Physical AI-RF Circuits and Systems
Abstract: This concept paper proposes an architecture that integrates agentic AI models with digital twin representations for each subsystem component in an RF transceiver. The digital twins, constructed using machine learning techniques such as deep learning and reinforcement learning, are paired with specialized, autonomous AI agent(s) capable of independent reasoning, planning, and adaptive action. Agentic AI models go beyond traditional rule-based/symbolic AI to autonomously select optimal strategies, synthesize data from diverse sources, and interact with both virtual and real-world environments. Ideas for simulations and experimental validations are proposed for future work.

Document title: MAS4D: Multi-Agent Simulations with Hybrid Path Planning for Urban Air Mobility
Abstract: The use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) has increased significantly over the past decade. UAVs can be used for healthcare delivery, particularly for timecritical deliveries such as defibrillators and organs as well as for search and rescue operations. However, managing large fleets of UAVs in urban airspaces requires addressing key challenges including safety, collision avoidance, scalability, and coordination in dynamic environments. To this end, we propose MAS4D, a Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) based simulation framework in which UAVs operate in a three-dimensional (3D) environment. Our approach integrates the classical path planning algorithm ($\mathrm{A}^{*}$) with Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) to combine the reliability of deterministic planning with the adaptability of reinforcement learning. This integration is expected to enhance collision avoidance and improve scalability compared to traditional solutions. The proposed framework will be evaluated using metrics such as collision rate, path length, energy consumption, and robustness under increasing UAV density.

Document title: Cognitive AI for Proactive Cyber Defense: A Rule-Based Multi-Agent Approach
Abstract: As cyber threats evolve in complexity and frequency, traditional defense mechanisms struggle to keep pace. This paper introduces a cognitive Artificial Intelligence (AI) driven framework using a rule-based multi-agent system (MAS) for proactive cyber defense. The architecture simulates human-like decision-making and collaborative threat response by leveraging knowledge bases, behavior rules, and autonomous agents. Each agent specializes in tasks such as threat detection, risk assessment, mitigation planning, and adaptive learning. Through a hybrid integration of symbolic reasoning and real-time situational awareness, the system anticipates, interprets, and reacts to cyber events. Experimental simulations demonstrate significant improvements in detection accuracy, response speed, and adaptability, making the approach suitable for dynamic and large-scale cybersecurity environments.

Document title: Integrating BDI Agents and Deep Q-Networks for Routing Optimization in Industrial Steel Logistics
Abstract: Efficient routing in large-scale steel logistics faces challenges from fluctuating demand, geographically distributed operations, and the need for timely coordination across supply chain stakeholders. This paper presents an integrated framework that combines the Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) agent paradigm with a Deep Q-Network (DQN)-based routing module to address these challenges in an industrial steel delivery context. The framework comprises four BDI agent modules, namely Customer, Warehouse, Supplier, and Vehicle, which operate autonomously and communicate asynchronously. The Supplier Agent embeds a DQN module that jointly considers product order volumes, remaining vehicle capacities, and traffic network topology to generate single- and multi-destination routing plans. The BDI architecture provides explainable decision-making and structured coordination, while the DQN component adapts routing strategies to dynamic operational conditions. We implement and evaluate the framework on realistic steel delivery scenarios, demonstrating improvements in route efficiency, vehicle utilization, and responsiveness compared to baselines. The results highlight the potential of combining agent-based coordination with learning-based optimization for scalable and adaptive industrial logistics systems.

Document title: Cross-Agent Multimodal Provenance-Aware Framework for Robust Prompt Injection Defense in Large Language and Vision-Language Models
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs), VisionLanguage Models (VLMs), and new agentic AI systems (e.g., LangChain and GraphChain) allow autonomous systems to reason and plan, and to coordinate between an assortment of tools and agents. Nevertheless, this feature also brings vulnerability to multimodal prompt injection (PI) attacks, in which hidden or malicious instructions that are embedded in text, images, metadata, or interagent messages can spread throughout the agent graph, triggering unintended behavior or policy violation, or corrupting a state. To mitigate these threats, this paper will present a Cross-Agent Multimodal Provenance-Aware Defense Framework that will sanitize any user- or agent-generated prompts and validate the output of the LLM independently, prior to their delivery to downstream nodes. The framework incorporates a text sanitizer agent, visual sanitizer agent and an output validator agent which are synchronized by a provenance ledger which documents modality, source and trust metadata throughout the agent network. The architecture implements ordered trust boundaries, so that an injected instruction cannot spread out via LangChain- or GraphChain-style workflows. There are better multimodal PI detection accuracy, lower trust leakage between agents, and more stable agentic execution pathways, all of which are experimentalized. This framework can build secure, interpretable, and reliable agentic AI systems by augmenting the established provenance tracking and validation systems to multi-agent orchestration.

Document title: Hybrid Framework for Robotic Manipulation: Integrating Reinforcement Learning and Large Language Models
Abstract: This paper introduces a new hybrid framework that combines Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Large Language Models (LLMs) to improve robotic manipulation tasks. By utilizing RL for accurate low-level control and LLMs for high-level task planning and understanding of natural language, the proposed framework effectively connects low-level execution with high-level reasoning in robotic systems. This integration allows robots to understand and carry out complex, human-like instructions while adapting to changing environments in real-time. The framework is tested in a PyBullet-based simulation environment using the Franka Emika Panda robotic arm, with various manipulation scenarios as benchmarks. The results show a 33.5% decrease in task completion time and enhancements of 18.1% and 36.4% in accuracy and adaptability, respectively, when compared to systems that use only RL. These results underscore the potential of LLM-enhanced robotic systems for practical applications, making them more efficient, adaptable, and capable of interacting with humans. Future research will aim to explore sim-to-real transfer, scalability, and multi-robot systems to further broaden the framework’s applicability.

Document title: A Multi-Agent Automation Framework Integrating RPA, OCR, and Large Language Models for Complex Workflow Execution
Abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has enabled unprecedented capabilities in natural language understanding, reasoning, and multi-step task planning. However, their integration with deterministic execution systems such as Robotic Process Automation (RPA) remains an open challenge, especially for complex workflows involving dynamic desktop environments and heterogeneous software tools. The system adopts a human-analogous architecture in which the LLM functions as the "brain," OCR as the "eyes," and RPA as the "hands," forming a closed-loop decision–action pipeline. The framework consists of three stages: (1) user intent understanding and structured task decomposition, (2) multi-agent collaborative execution across RPA, OCR, and LLM components, and (3) automated output packaging that generates standardized documentation and task-specific artifacts in multiple formats. Experimental evaluations on real-world desktop workflows demonstrate that the proposed architecture significantly improves task robustness, adaptability, and success rates compared with traditional RPA systems. This work contributes a practical blueprint for next-generation intelligent automation systems built upon foundation models.

Document title: A Comparison of Multi Agent Path Finding Algorithm (MAPF) for Robotic Mobile Fulfillment System (RMFS)
Abstract: Efficient path planning is critical for Robotic Mobile Fulfillment Systems (RMFS), in which multiple robots must navigate dynamically without collisions. This study evaluates five multi-agent path-finding (MAPF) algorithms: WHCA*, FAR, CBS, ST-SPF, and STMS in simulated RMFS environments with varying map sizes ($7 \times 7$ to $11 \times 11$) and agent densities (5 to 9 agents). The performance was assessed using the makespan and sum of costs. The results show that CBS and ST-SPF consistently outperformed the other algorithms. CBS excels in mid and spaceful environments despite its robust conflict resolution capabilities, whereas ST-SPF demonstrates superior scalability and adaptability in crowded, semi-crowded, and semi-spaceful environments. In contrast, WHCA* and FAR struggled with structured congestion, and STMS did not show any significant advantage because of its hybrid overhead and reliance on randomness. These findings suggest that CBS is more stable in every RMFS environment, as indicated by its low makespan standard deviation, whereas ST-SPF is better suited for dynamic settings with higher density. This study provides practical insights for selecting MAPF algorithms for real-world warehouse automation, highlighting the importance of conflict resolution and environmental adaptability.

Document title: Hybrid Multi Agent Navigation in Warehouse Environments using CBS-MARL
Abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid algorithm integrating Conflict-Based Search (CBS) and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for efficient warehouse navigation. CBS functions as a high-level planner, while MARL serves as a low-level controller, reducing computation and enhancing scalability. The pipeline consists of four phases: (i) simplified CBS generates path images by detecting vertex conflicts, (ii) agents are individually trained via Reinforcement Learning with radar data for basic navigation, (iii) a multi-agent environment integrates CBS paths with the trained RL model, and (iv) performance evaluation against a constrained CBS baseline. Using total elapsed time as the metric, results show the hybrid approach performs variably: 3.16 times slower with 5 agents, 1.54 times slower with 10, 1.4 times faster with 15, and successfully manages 20 agents, where the baseline model fails. These findings highlight the hybrid model’s adaptability and scalability for multi-agent navigation in complex warehouse settings.

Document title: A Modular Multi-Agent Framework for Trip Planning Using Agentic-AI and Google ADK
Abstract: The main breakthrough in the field of travel management systems is associated with the idea of multi-agent systems that provide personalized, adaptive, and almost fully automated user experiences. As a result, this work introduces a modular multi-agent-based conversational platform which is an interactive and less complicated method of trip planning. The system architecture features mainly a Supervising Agent that is responsible for the coordination of the activities of the specialized sub-agents. The sub-agents are those which handle various domains related to travel. Their implemented operations can each independently perform local data persistence; thus, they ensure session continuity and device stability. The system’s uniqueness lies in the fact that it provides a rollback and conflict-resolution capability to resolve issues autonomously. Powered by a Gemini LLM model for information retrieval, the model provides structured responses to generic user queries related to trip-planning. The decouplable and extensible modular design allows for the proper maintenance and scalability of the system with future extensions to include other sub-agents also made easier and efficient with this design. Hence, the adaptive, agentic design of Trip-Planner is a significant step forward in the area of intelligent travel automation which ultimately results in an excellent user experience through more coordinated activities flow and the seamless end users' engagement.

Document title: Conservative and Risk-Aware Offline Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has been widely adopted for controlling and optimizing complex engineering systems such as next-generation wireless networks. An important challenge in adopting RL is the need for direct access to the physical environment. This limitation is particularly severe in multi-agent systems, for which conventional multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) requires a large number of coordinated online interactions with the environment during training. When only offline data is available, a direct application of online MARL schemes would generally fail due to the epistemic uncertainty entailed by the lack of exploration during training. In this work, we propose an offline MARL scheme that integrates distributional RL and conservative Q-learning to address the environment's inherent aleatoric uncertainty and the epistemic uncertainty arising from the use of offline data. We explore both independent and joint learning strategies. The proposed MARL scheme, referred to as multi-agent conservative quantile regression, addresses general risk-sensitive design criteria and is applied to the trajectory planning problem in drone networks, showcasing its advantages.

Document title: Multi-Agent Collaboration-Based Parking Lot Navigation System for Vehicular Networks
Abstract: In modern urban transportation, the efficient management of parking lots and the rapid parking of vehicles are crucial for alleviating congestion and enhancing the operational efficiency of cities. This paper proposes a multi-vehicle collaborative parking navigation algorithm based on shared vision (SVIQL). It aims to address the issues of poor vehicle coordination and information silos in traditional parking lots. By integrating multi-agent reinforcement learning, classic path-planning algorithms, and real-time information sharing mechanisms, this algorithm performs well in reducing vehicle conflicts, shortening parking time, and increasing parking success rates.

Document title: Spatiotemporal-Modal Cognitive Agents Based on Programmatic Reasoning
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) remain largely inept at directly handling spatiotemporal-modal data, and thus struggle with spatiotemporal computation and iterative, tool-assisted tasks. This artical introduces a programmatic-reasoning–enhanced framework for spatiotemporal-modal cognitive agents that decouples spatiotemporal computation from textual reasoning, markedly improving LLM performance on complex spatiotemporal analytics. We design a high-discipline prompting template—PlanTemplate—to elicit programmatic reasoning (PoT, Program of Thoughts), optimize PoT-style program-augmented prompting, and adopt the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to standardize tool encapsulation and automated execution. Experiments show that, relative to standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT), our approach improves accuracy by 40% on GSM-Hard and 18.6% on Terra benchmarks; first-attempt completion on spatiotemporal tasks reaches 55.6 – 67%, and response latency decreases by 67.5%. The study provides both theoretical underpinnings and practical guidance for deploying LLMs in urban spatiotemporal intelligence.

Document title: Towards Scalable Consensus: Adaptive Hybrid Mediation Algorithms for Complex Automated Negotiations
Abstract: This research addresses the challenge of automated negotiation in collaborative design processes, which are characterized by a large number of stakeholders and intricately intertwined constraints. In real-world applications such as participatory urban planning, the design spaces subject to negotiation are high-dimensional and possess vast plateaus, making it difficult for conventional automated negotiation methods to achieve optimal consensus. To tackle this issue, prior work proposed a mediation agent utilizing auction mechanisms, simulated annealing, and genetic algorithms, suggesting its effectiveness. This paper further develops this approach by proposing a novel hybrid algorithm that fuses the global search capabilities of GA with the local search capabilities of Simulated Annealing (SA). Specifically, we design and implement a static hybrid model (Hybrid GA-SA) that periodically applies SA, and an adaptive hybrid model (Adaptive GA-SA) that detects search stagnation to dynamically apply SA and adaptively adjust its parameters. We empirically demonstrate that the proposed adaptive hybrid model can discover higher-quality negotiation agreements (maximization of the Nash product) compared to existing GA and other metaheuristic methods, without significantly compromising computational efficiency.

Document title: SmartCook: A Multimodal Multi-Agent System for AI-Powered Cooking Assistance
Abstract: The culinary domain can present challenges for many individuals, such as those with cognitive or physical impairments and the elderly. These challenges often manifest as difficulties in meal planning, suboptimal nutritional choices, and inefficient ingredient management, leading to food waste. This paper introduces SmartCook, a novel culinary assistant designed to mitigate these barriers. The core of SmartCook is a multi-agent architecture that decouples and manages distinct cognitive tasks required for cooking to improve the human-computer interaction. This system leverages Google’s Gemini 2.5 series of large language models, allocating different models to dedicated agents for various tasks, such as culinary knowledge, visual perception, and voice-driven interaction. By processing multimodal inputs, including voice commands and real-time camera data, the system can perform ingredient identification via computer vision, generate personalized recipes with step-by-step instructions, and provide context-aware guidance. We systematically validate SmartCook’s efficacy and usability through a user study (n=30) employing the System Usability Scale and interviews. The quantitative and qualitative results indicate high usability and confirm the value of an integrated multi-agent system with multimodal input. This paper demonstrates a functional prototype and validated design framework for AI-driven assistive technologies, demonstrating the potential for multi-agent LLM systems to enhance independence and safety in everyday tasks.

Document title: The Digital Farmer Agents in Precise and Sustainable Agricultural Ecosystems
Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence is shifting precision agriculture from descriptive analytics to coordinated, goal-directed decision making. This paper presents Digital Farmer Agents (DFAs), goal-conditioned planning agents that combine infield IoT telemetry, weather forecasts, and satellite indicators with a calibrated farm digital twin to schedule irrigation, fertilization, pest management, and crop rotation under operational and environmental limits. Each agent solves a multi-objective problem that balances yield with water and nutrient efficiency, enforces policy constraints such as seasonal allocations, nitrate thresholds, and yield-scaled greenhouse gas caps, and produces concise, human-auditable rationales for proposed actions. The framework is evaluated on multi-season, real-world data integrating soil moisture, canopy temperature, meteorology, vegetation indices, and management logs, including TERRA-REF/Maricopa phenotyping products and a public IoT telemetry set with pump states. To probe edge conditions, we augment evaluation with a digital-twin dataset that is explicitly marked as simulated and used for counterfactual stress tests of heat, drought, and policy shocks. Results are consistent across wheat and rice. Yield prediction accuracy improves over strong machine learning baselines. Water use per unit yield declines. Fertilizer intensity is reduced. Robustness to climate variability increases through proactive re-planning and closed-loop feedback. Methodologically, the work integrates a distributed multi-agent architecture, a digital-twin-in-the-loop training and evaluation workflow that fuses sensing, simulation, and optimization, and an interpretable multi-objective formulation aligned with sustainability targets and farmer constraints. Case studies illustrate clear what-if analyses, quantified trade-offs, and transfer to data-scarce plots where simulation accelerates learning. Coupling agentic planning with calibrated digital twins and human oversight offers a practical path to precise, resource-efficient, and climate-resilient agricultural ecosystems and points to how agentic AI can underpin the next generation of intelligent food systems.

Document title: Model of Problem Structure Identification by Hybrid Intelligent Multi-Agent Systems in Interdisciplinary Education Planning
Abstract: The paper considers the model of the method for automatic identification of a problem structure using interdisciplinary education planning as an example. Interdisciplinary education is a complex process that forms a holistic perception of the world by students, developing their critical thinking and problem solving skills. The problem of interdisciplinary education planning at a university is characterized by weak formalization, dynamism, complex structure and traditionally requires work of a team of specialists for its solution. The development of methods for identifying problems similar to interdisciplinary education planning will significantly reduce the labor costs for their solution.

Document title: Agentic AI-Driven and Human-Centered Cyber Immune Platforms for Cyber Threat Intelligence Verification under PDPA Regulations
Abstract: Critical infrastructures and data-driven organizations increasingly rely on cyber threat intelligence (CTI) platforms to anticipate, detect, and respond to sophisticated attacks. Recent work on agentic artificial intelligence (AI) and cyber-immune systems promises more proactive and autonomous CTI workflows, yet important challenges remain around transparency, privacy, and governance—especially in jurisdictions subject to stringent personal-data regulations such as Thailand’s Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA). This paper proposes an agentic AI–driven and human-centered cyber-immune platform for cyber threat intelligence verification under PDPA regulations. The platform uses agentic AI to validate, enrich, and score CTI while enforcing PDPA-aligned privacy-by-design guardrails and preserving human oversight. The framework integrates multi-agent orchestration, a Vet–Enrich–Score pipeline for CTI processing, and PDPA-specific policy enforcement with human-in-the-loop (HITL) review. A PRISMA-inspired synthetic literature review and design science research methodology are used to derive research gaps and design requirements from prior work on agentic AI, CTI, cyberimmune systems, and privacy-preserving analytics. We outline the platform architecture, core workflows, and a planned evaluation strategy, including metrics for performance, detection quality, privacy impact, and usability. Although empirical results are reserved for future work, the framework provides a structured foundation for building auditable, PDPA-compliant CTI pipelines that balance AI autonomy with organizational accountability. (Abstract)

Document title: Dynamic Path Planning of Robotic Arm Based on Repulsive Potential Field and Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: To endow robotic arms with enhanced autonomous obstacle avoidance and path planning capabilities in complex dynamic environments, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods have been widely employed for robotic arm path planning tasks in recent years. However, existing DRL-based approaches suffer from high state space dimension and limited environment awareness, which leads to insufficient path planning performance and generalization performance of the algorithms in dynamic environments. In this paper, we propose an environment state representation method based on repulsive potential field (RPF) and incorporate it with proximal policy optimization (PPO) to develop a novel path planning algorithm, RPF-PPO. The algorithm takes the end of the robotic arm as the reference point and uses the RPF to model the obstacles uniformly, forming a fixed-dimension state representation, which effectively improves the algorithm's path planning performance and generalization ability in dynamic environments. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed RPF-PPO algorithm achieves higher path planning success rates and superior generalization ability compared to existing methods, thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

Document title: MIRAI: Multimodal Intelligence via Reflective agentic AI for enterprise knowledge assistants
Abstract: Secure and efficient knowledge management based on enterprise chip design and verification documents or bug trackers, pose unique challenges, due to their complex, sensitive, heterogeneous, and multimodal nature. Rapid miniaturization of nodes, sophistication of Intellectual Property (IP)s, and evolution of system-on-chip (SoC) architectures have further added to the demanding scenario, where, within the available enterprise infrastructure, effective solutions have to be developed based on context and requirements of various operational settings. Available state-of-the-art solutions have limited scope of sensitivity to organizational dynamics and smart computational resource planning. In this paper, we present MIRAI- a Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrated Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework that combines language, vision, and structured data understanding through a reflective agentic architecture to provide real-time, contextual and explainable support in Design Verification and Verification (DV&V) tasks. The proposed system has been evaluated across use cases, demonstrating significant gains, i.e., up to 90-95% accuracy in information retrieval, in secure policy information access, AI-based query answering, anomaly detection, debugging, and knowledge mining and functional testing with improved coverage. We believe MIRAI offers a transformative approach to managing and leveraging design data, engineering workflows, and cross-functional team intelligence.

Document title: Research on Competitive Mechanisms and Uncertainty Planning in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning shows great potential in dynamic complex systems, but it still faces challenges in terms of strategy stability and robust planning under uncertainty in competitive scenarios. In this paper, we propose a dynamic competitive deep Q network (DC-DQN) and its uncertainty enhancement variant Dropout-DC-DQN to overcome the shortcomings of traditional methods in strategic coupling effect, environmental noise sensitivity and dynamic competition regulation ability. By integrating adaptive competition reward mechanism, strategy diversity constraint and double randomization network design, the agent can adjust competition intensity flexibly in the game and improve the tolerance to observation noise, dynamic obstacles and other disturbances. Compared with the baseline model, the hunting success rate of DC-DQN increased by 23.1%, the strategy differentiation increased by 216%, the anti-interference index of Dropout-DC-DQN reached 0.93, and the dynamic obstacle avoidance rate increased by 21.4% compared with the traditional method. This study provides a solution with both strategic flexibility and environmental adaptability for scenarios such as autonomous driving cooperation and distributed resource scheduling.

Document title: Neuro-Cybernetic Architecture for Enhancing Human-Robot Team Performance in Adaptive Environments
Abstract: The architecture of neuro-cybernetics combines the brain-inspired adaptive control and intelligent signal processing in applying the human-robot cooperation in variable and unpredictable situations. It facilitates natural collaboration and intelligent operation among human users and their robotic companions using modular systems and bio-inspired frameworks and using real-time modifications. The distributed adaptive control (DAC) architecture has a cognitive module that provides task planning, safety monitoring, modeling of the worker, and management of the interaction. Modern methods, such as neural networks with genetic algorithm back-propagation and reinforcement learning, as well as deep neural networks make it possible to perform the precise interpretation of neural signals, and to cause an adaptable reaction of the robots. Live calibration and constant feedback enhance the smoothness of navigation by 23%, increase the level of user satisfaction to 87%, and promote teamwork collaboration efficiency by 18 percent higher. There is an over 95% accuracy in intent recognition, the cognitive load is reduced by 15%, and the response time falls below 250 ms, making the process highly safe and reliable with a relatively high compliance, over 92%, in both industrial and service settings since human and robot interaction with each other is safer, more adjustable, and effective.

Document title: Using Sentinels and Digital Twins to Secure Agentic AI in IoT Systems
Abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems is evolving rapidly from conversational interfaces to goal-directed, autonomous Agentic AI. These agentic AIs can plan, use tools, interact with external APIs, and maintain internal state to manage complex environments such as Smart Homes. However, this autonomy introduces dependability/security/safety risks, as erroneous or conflicting actions can have direct physical consequences. This paper presents a novel dual-component architecture for securing Agentic AI in IoT systems, leveraging embedded Sentinels and external Digital Twins. Sentinels are implemented as compiled, signed Web Assembly modules that execute within the agent’s environment, enforcing governance-as-code. They require the use of a strict "Goal-Plan-Step justification" pattern, ensuring that all agent actions are auditable and aligned with predefined safety invariants. Complementing the Sentinels, Digital Twins serve as synchronized world models and critical mediation layers. They abstract IoT device complexity into high-level intents and ensure safe execution through advanced concurrency controls, including time-scoped locks (Exclusive, Shared, and Capacity), capacity reservations, and prioritized transactions with compensation logic. We validate our approach using a Smart Home Energy Manager (SHEM) that optimizes energy costs while maintaining comfort. Our results demonstrate that this approach effectively mitigates key failure modes, such as contradictory goals and concurrent interference, while maintaining sub-second end-to-end latency.

Document title: Co-MAS: Towards Robust Multi-Agentic AI Assistant through Multi-Layered Reflection
Abstract: AI Agents based on Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit outstanding promise in tasks that call for cognitive abilities comparable to those of humans. But they usually have trouble solving complicated analytical data science problems that require multi-step, structured reasoning. We introduce Copilot Multi-Agentic System (Co-MAS), a system with multiple agents designed to handle complex analytical and reasoning tasks by using Finite State Machine (FSM) interactions. Co-MAS consists of a Planner Agent, Analyzer Agent, Validator Agent, Executer Agent, and Presenter Agent. Since these agents are horizontal in nature, Co-MAS can effectively address complex analytical and data science problems in any domain with a relevant context. With an average 12% increase in accuracy, Co-MAS significantly boosts standalone LLM performance in analytics and data science tasks.
