Experimental validation demonstrates that this framework can provide dynamic, explainable, and actionable decision support for personalized education, driving the efficient implementation of personalized education initiatives.

Document title: Cooperative Driving at Multiple Unsignalized Intersections in Fully Autonomous Driving Scenarios
Abstract: The decision-making process for connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs) at unsignalized intersections is a critical and challenging problem. Previous methods predominantly concentrate on optimizing passage strategies for individual intersections in isolation. However, they often neglect global traffic conditions and task priorities in closed, multi-intersection transportation scenarios, leading to localized congestion. In this work, we propose a method that aims to optimize the passing order of intersections from a global and long-term perspective to enhance overall transportation efficiency. Specifically, we model the coordination of multiple unsignalized intersections as a multi-agent sequential decision problem and solve it through a two-stage method. In the planning stage, we construct fully connected undirected graphs based on vehicle conflict relationships and use the multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) algorithm to learn the global priorities. In the scheduling stage, the local vehicle scheduling is formalized as a multi-objective optimization problem. The learned global priorities are soft constraints, while a hybrid filtered beam search determines safe and efficient CAV passing orders. Extensive offline experiments and online tests on real-world and synthetic datasets demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in minimizing congestion and enhancing transportation efficiency.

Document title: Design and Geometry-Aware Planning of a Novel Probe-Scanning Manipulator with RCM Constraint
Abstract: The remote center of motion (RCM) constraint is a vital requirement in the design of robotic systems for transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) probe-scanning. This paper presents the design and development of a novel RCM-constrained manipulator specifically tailored for TRUS probe-scanning applications. The proposed system features a six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) parallel-serial hybrid mechanism that enables the TRUS probe to perform pivot and spin rotations while maintaining the RCM constraint. Subsequently, the kinematic model incorporating the RCM constraint is derived. Additionally, a geometry-aware path planning method is then introduced, considering variations in the desired rotation targets. This method parameterizes distance metrics on SO(3) (a Lie group) using coordinate-free Riemannian geometry, enabling the dynamic optimization of rotation orders to minimize the calculated Riemannian metrics. Furthermore, a smooth rotational trajectory generation method is proposed, constructing rotation curves between the ordered matrices on SO(3) while minimizing angular acceleration. Both simulations and experimental results validate the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed manipulator and its path planning method.

Document title: LLM-GA: Large Language Model-Enhanced Genetic Algorithm for Path Optimization
Abstract: Path planning is a critical problem in robotic autonomous navigation, requiring the computation of a practical route from the start point to the goal point while satisfying various optimization objectives, such as path length, smoothness, and the number of turns. While Genetic Algorithm (GA) and its variants have demonstrated efficacy in grid-based path planning, they typically demand extensive exploration to achieve high-quality solutions. Furthermore, due to the inherent mechanism of GAs, they are prone to premature convergence. Large Language Model (LLM) excels in providing global insights into the environment through deep contextual understanding, offering a holistic analysis on environmental analysis. However, despite their impressive reasoning capabilities, LLMs struggle with precise spatial-temporal modeling, frequently generating suboptimal or physically infeasible trajectories. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a LLMl-Enhanced GA (LLM-GA). This method integrates the precise optimization capabilities of GAs with the global reasoning strengths of LLMs. Expressly, LLM is incorporated into the initialization and mutation phases of GA to leverage its ability to generate diverse path segments, and to enhance the algorithm's ability to escape from the local optima. While ensuring path feasibility, the method efficiently explores a reduced search space and successfully finds higher-quality solutions within the same grid-map. Experiments demonstrate that the LLM-GA outperforms other algorithms in terms of path length, number of turns, and search space exploration.

Document title: Design of an Intelligent Analysis System for Experimental Data Based on Artificial Intelligence and a Research Assistance Decision-Making System
Abstract: In response to the problems of low processing efficiency of multi-source monitoring data and the reliance on manual experience in water body ecological monitoring, this paper designs an artificial intelligence-assisted system that integrates knowledge graphs in the field of water body ecology and multi-agent collaboration. The system adopts a hierarchical architecture design. Through the multi-modal monitoring data cleaning and feature extraction in the data processing layer, the ecological knowledge graph reasoning in the intelligent analysis layer, and the reinforcement learning cruise path optimization in the decision support layer, it realizes the full-process intelligence from monitoring data collection to cruise decision output. Experimental verification shows that on typical water body ecological parameter datasets, the system's time series prediction accuracy for key indicators such as dissolved oxygen and pH value is 21.3% higher than that of traditional statistical methods, and the recall rate for water quality anomaly detection is 90.7%. Through multi-agent collaborative planning, the cruise monitoring decision response time is shortened by 38%, and the optimization iteration efficiency of sampling points is increased by 35.6%. This system effectively solves the problems of real-time analysis and scientific decision-making of dynamic data in water body ecological monitoring, providing technical support with both interpretability and efficiency for intelligent cruise monitoring.

Document title: SparGate-ACT: A novel method for generating robot movement sequence
Abstract: Bimanual manipulation refers to the coordinated control of two robotic arms to jointly complete complex tasks requiring precise cooperation or synchronized movements. While Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) is a significant method for achieving bimanual manipulation, it suffers from several limitations. The single-layer Transformer architecture struggles to balance local action details and global strategic planning, and its quadratic computational complexity hampers efficiency in processing long sequences. Additionally, it exhibits weak key-action recognition in noisy environments and lacks hierarchical information interaction and adaptive noise-filtering mechanisms. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel method named SparGate-ACT. This method constructs a hierarchical processing architecture: the low layer utilizes windowed attention to capture millimeter-scale fine-grained actions, while the high layer employs sparse attention to establish long-range dependencies. These layers are connected via a cross-layer attention mechanism. Furthermore, a gated decoder is introduced to dynamically filter noise and focus only on key features beneficial for prediction. Simulation experiments demonstrate that this approach significantly improves system performance. SparGate-ACT overcomes the limitations of existing techniques and provides a new solution for enhancing robots' fine manipulation capabilities.

In the era of intelligent automation, autonomous decision-making and trajectory optimization in Multi-Robot Systems (MRS) remain pivotal for mission success, particularly in unstructured and dynamic environments. This paper presents a novel hybrid path planning architecture that integrates classical A* algorithms with a trainable neural heuristic, forming a differentiable A* Neural Network (A* NN). Designed for IoTconnected MRS, the system enables decentralized task execution, where object poses, human positions, and obstacle data are shared across a hierarchical communication layer utilizing MQTT broker based messaging. This structure supports scalable data exchange, coordination, and real-time updates between heterogeneous agents, including drones and humanoid robots. The proposed framework leverages sensor fusion from different sensors, visual cameras, and onboard sensors to construct a unified environmental map for navigation and obstacle avoidance. A decentralized data structure is introduced to manage robot states, task conditions, battery levels, and anomaly signals. These parameters drive a learned guidance function that generates heuristic maps dynamically, allowing the $\mathrm{A}^{*} \text{NN}$ to prioritize efficient, collision-free paths. The network is trained through end-to-end gradient descent to continuously refine decision quality based on real-world feedback. By combining classical path planning with deep learning and decentralized IoT-based communication, the system delivers robust, energy aware, and adaptive navigation performance for mission-critical operations. This work demonstrates a scalable and intelligent solution for real-time decision-making in IoTconnected robotic fleets.

Document title: Adaptive Context-Aware Vision-Based Quality Inspection Using Multi-Modal Deep Learning in Robotic Systems
Abstract: The concept of Edge Cognitive Cohorts presents an edge computing concept that is privacy-aware that delivers retail personalization in real time. It does not follow individual shoppers, rather it creates a temporary micro-group (cohorts) of consumers sharing similar behaviors including movement patterns, dwell time and product interactions, in the store setting. The system uses data gathered by cameras, beacons and mobile apps to generate such cohorts on-site to provide users with contextually relevant promotions to digital displays or mobile devices in their vicinity. Processing and clustering are done locally on the edge devices, and this guarantees low latency and a high level of privacy attack since raw personal data are not transferred out of the plant. With the help of federated learning, the system will constantly improve its cohort models as they go through time without exchanging any single data across networks. Such a structure is a change in personal profiling in favor of behavioral, group-oriented targeting, increasing both consumer trust and data adherence, and it makes retailers offer resilient, responsive and ethical in-store personalization.

Document title: Simultaneous Estimation of Human Motion Intention and Time-Varying Arm Stiffness for Enhanced Human–Robot Interaction
Abstract: Recent advances in physiological human motor control research indicate that human endpoint stiffness magnitude increases linearly with grasp force. Based on these findings, a scheme was proposed in this article to integrate the linear quadratic estimation (LQE) filter with the stiffness model inferred from grasp force, which can simultaneously estimate the human arm's stiffness and motion intention. Then, an online variable impedance controller (VIC) was designed based on these estimations for physical human–robot interaction (pHRI). The proposed stiffness model and estimation method were validated through experiments using a planar robotic interface. To assess its performance in practical pHRI tasks, the implementation of human arm stiffness and intention estimation combining with VIC was extended to teleoperation peg-in-hole and robot-assisted rehabilitation tasks. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively estimate human motion intention and arm stiffness simultaneously. Compared to existing methods, the proposed VIC enhances pHRI in terms of increased flexibility, effective guidance, and reduced human effort.

Document title: A Spatial Transformation Based Next Frame Predictor
Abstract: In recent years, the automobile industry has achieved astonishing success in making autonomous cars safer, more affordable, and more reliable. However, current autonomous driving technology is mainly based on reactive controllers that attempt to respond to the various events the car encounters. Yet, achieving a truly safe and reliable autonomous system necessitates anticipating such events and planning the correct actions in advance to avoid undesirable behavior. Recent advances in deep learning have shown remarkable performance in predicting future frames from video sequences. However, most of these approaches can only handle a few moving elements in the scene and perform poorly when the camera is in motion. This is mainly due to the difficulty of disentangling camera intrinsic motion from object-dependent motion. In this work, we equip autonomous cars with an object-oriented next-frame predictor that leverages Transformer architecture to extract, for each moving object in the scene, a spatial transformation applied to the object to predict its configuration in the next frame. Static elements of the scene are then used to estimate camera intrinsic motion, which is applied to the background to predict how it will be viewed in the next frame. Notably, our approach significantly reduces the complexity typically associated with such models by requiring the estimation of only 14 parameters per moving object, independent of image resolution. We have validated the generalization capabilities of our model through training on simulated datasets and testing on real-world datasets. The results indicate that our model not only outperforms existing models trained solely on real data but also exhibits superior resilience to occlusions and incomplete data in the input sequences. These findings underscore the potential of our model to significantly improve the predictive analytics capabilities of autonomous driving systems, thereby enhancing their safety and reliability in dynamic environments.

Document title: Cloud Robot Indoor and Outdoor Service Scheduling Decision Based on Expanded A* and Gaode Map Navigation
Abstract: At present, the development prospect of robots is broad, and the types of robots are increasing day by day. Facing the scenario of multiple robots providing services, the problem of optimal service scheduling becomes more and more prominent. Optimal service scheduling for the cloud robot, this paper based on SOA architecture of cloud, the service type, the latitude and longitude of the ratings and service as the index, USES the circular area search algorithm(CAS),to determine the optimal service decisions, when certain cloud robot is scheduling, cloud service robots to applicants need planning between indoor and outdoor path, The outdoor path planning of cloud robot is carried out by amap navigation, and the indoor path planning is carried out by extended A * algorithm to realize the indoor and outdoor service scheduling of cloud robot. The experimental results show that the optimal service decision and indoor and outdoor scheduling task under CAS algorithm are realized by integrating the longitude and latitude, service score and service type of cloud robot when the service applicant applies for the cloud robot, which provides reference for the motion control of cloud robot.

Document title: Scalability for Multivehicle Coordination With Dial-a-Ride Application
Abstract: When confronting a practical dial-a-ride problem (DARP), addressing the transportation demands of joining and removal at any operational time is of practical significance yet a theoretical challenge. To this end, this article formulates the DARP into an architecture that integrates a physical agent (vehicle or robot) and an information decision that suffers from a fluctuation of vector fields with respect to mixed-integer linear programming (MILP). Specifically, physical agents ensure that vehicles can interact with their neighbors to service the transportation demands, whereas information decision making ensures a feasible vehicle route with minimal routing cost, despite the presence of fluctuations in transportation demand. For centralized open MILP, the feasibility is determined by the boundedness of a nonempty intersection generated by the involved half-planes and the entire associated vector field. A resource allocation method is subsequently used, and the equivalence between the primal and dual programs is also studied. In this context, the problem at hand is abstracted into a framework of multivehicle coordination in which agents (vehicles) may be removed or added at any operational time. Afterward, conditions guaranteeing definiteness as well as computing the unique optimal solution via the cutting plane and split disjunction are derived. The considered DARP is deemed solvable, provided that the lower bound of fluctuation, the number of vehicles removed, the interacting topology, and the effect of agent removal satisfy certain relations. The effectiveness of the proposed method is illustrated via a numerical instance.

Document title: ContextPilot: Adaptive Open Source Software Onboarding
Abstract: Open source software relies on volunteer contributors, yet onboarding newcomers remains difficult and practices for ensuring quality are fragmented. Existing continuous integration pipelines, linters, templates, and documentation rarely adapt to repository-specific norms or explain failures in actionable terms, producing low-quality pull requests, prolonged reviews, and contributor attrition. This paper presents ContextPilot, a modular, multi-agent framework that provides guidance grounded in project artifacts. ContextPilot ingests repository metadata-such as readme files, contribution guidelines, workflow definitions, and linter and test configurations-into a retrieval index. Specialized agents for repositories, feedback, editing environments, and conversation coordinate with a large language model to transform logs, code differences, and policies into human-readable recommendations. We detail the architecture, data schema, prompting strategies, and safeguards. A prototype integrates with GitHub webhooks and a Visual Studio Code extension. Illustrative scenarios show how ContextPilot explains pipeline failures, offers proactive guidance during local development, and reuses organizational knowledge from prior contributions to reduce repeated maintainer effort. We outline an evaluation plan comparing standard workflows with ContextPilot-augmented workflows across efficiency, contribution quality, maintainer workload, contributor retention, and scalability, and we discuss threats to validity. ContextPilot turns quality enforcement from a gatekeeping step into an instructive experience.

Document title: Autonomous System For The Marine Robotics Path Planning Under Changing Hydro-Meteorological Environmental Conditions
Abstract: Path planning of marine robotics, such as autonomous unmanned underwater vehicles (AUVs), unmanned surface vessel (USVs) or other autonomous marine transport vessels, is a critical task. To ensure highly autonomous and safe path of the marine robotics, it is necessary to take into account many non-determined factors, both anthropogenic nature, caused by the functioning of the marine robotics as part of the existing infrastructure, and natural factors associated with disturbances in the external environment, such as currents, wind, waves, etc. The article presents a variant of the marine robotics path model considering the changing hydro-meteorological environmental conditions. An analysis of modern methods of the marine robotics path planning is presented. The main part of the article describes the process of constructing the architecture of the autonomous path planning system of marine robotics and the process of the system operation mathematical modeling. The process of integrating this system into existing marine robotics samples is described in detail. The conclusion presents the results of the work carried out and the direction of further research.

Document title: Modular production using hierarchical planning and a generic OPC UA skills concept
Abstract: In response to the growing global demand for customized and sustainable aircraft with shorter lead times, this research aims to enhance flexibility and automation in aircraft production. The study focuses on integrating hierarchical process planning with machine skills and simulation to streamline the final assembly phase, where numerous components and modules are combined. Existing research highlights challenges in coordinating module production across various locations, emphasizing the need for cost-effective and adaptable systems to manage demand fluctuations and supply chain disruptions.This study presents a novel approach by expanding the concept of machine skills to include prediction skills, enabling pre-execution, simulation-based outcome estimation for informed decision-making and resource optimisation. The proposed methodology involves a minimal demonstration scenario featuring a warehouse, preassembly stations, a final assembly station, and flexible intralogistics with automated guided vehicles (AGVs), all connected through standardized OPC UA interfaces. This setup serves as a use case to illustrate the application of a generic software architecture and standardised modeling for task-specific skill combinations. By addressing hierarchical planning tasks supported by simulation and standardized interfaces, the research provides a framework for adaptive process orchestration and flexible logistics. The results show a significant improvement in the flexibility and efficiency of production process planning and execution, which has practical implications for the further development of aircraft manufacturing processes.

Document title: Architecting the Future Factory: Industrial PLC-IoT, Digital Twins and Predictive AI based Maintenance
Abstract: This paper presents an integrated smart factory automation framework aimed at overcoming the inherent limitations of conventional Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems in predictive maintenance within Industry 4.0 environments. The proposed architecture synergistically combines four emerging technologies, namely Industrial Embedded Personal Computers (IEPCs), Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) networks, Digital Twins (DT), and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven anomaly detection. This combination enables bidirectional data and control flows between physical equipments and their virtual counterparts, scalable sensor integration, real-time monitoring, and AI-based predictive maintenance to significantly reduce unplanned downtime and improve operational resilience. The envisioned implementation plan includes phased upgrading of existing PLC-based laboratory setups to IEPCs, expansion of multi-modal sensor networks, deployment of a robust IIoT infrastructure, DT development, and application of AI models for anomaly detection. A representative use case, involving a multi-conveyor robotic automation, is detailed to illustrate system capabilities in synchronizing physical and virtual operations, supporting dynamic feedback loops and intelligent decision-making. The framework also addresses key aspects such as interoperability, cybersecurity, and data standardization, laying the foundation for scalable, intelligent mass-production automation aligned with the future of digitalized manufacturing.

Document title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for UAV Wireless Charging and Trajectory Planning: A Review
Abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become essential for various applications, including surveillance, logistics, and disaster response. However, their limited battery capacity and frequent need for recharging disrupt mission efficiency, especially in critical operations. Dynamic Wireless Charging (DWC), which provides in-flight charging autonomously, offers a promising solution to extend operational time. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) enhances this approach by optimizing energy management, charging strategies, and trajectory planning based on real-time conditions. This paper explores the integration of DRL, DWC, and emerging technologies like 6G communications and IoT, aiming to improve UAV energy efficiency and mission reliability. It reviews current research on DRL for UAV charging and trajectory planning, discusses limitations in existing studies, and proposes future research directions, including the integration of laser beaming and hybrid DRL models. The goal is to create more autonomous, sustainable, and efficient UAV systems for diverse applications in intelligent transportation systems (ITS).

Document title: Software Architecture of Autonomous Driving Systems: Concepts, Modules, and Implementation Challenges
Abstract: The rise of autonomous driving systems represents a technological revolution at the intersection of robotics, artificial intelligence, and embedded software. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the software architecture that underpins these systems, focusing on the functional modules, middleware frameworks, and implementation challenges. Based on the Sense–Plan–Act paradigm, the study analyzes the roles of perception, localization, mapping, planning, control, and decision-making, emphasizing their real-time interactions within dynamic environments. The article also explores the importance of robust middleware such as ROS, Autoware, and Apollo, as well as architectural paradigms like microservices. Key challenges, including cybersecurity, scalability, system validation, and large-scale deployment, are discussed in depth, providing insight into current technological constraints and future research directions. This work aims to serve as a reference for engineers, researchers, and decision-makers involved in the development of safe and scalable autonomous mobility systems.

Document title: The Adaptive Sampling of Marine Robots in Ocean Observation: An Overview
Abstract: It is a costly and time-consuming practice to achieve ocean observation with sufficient spatial and temporal resolution. Luckily, it can be more efficient and effective by applying marine robots with adaptive sampling. The ocean environment and its uncertainties can be predicted during sampling to make planning of autonomous sensing for future operations of the marine robot. This article reviews various methods of adaptive sampling as well as robot path planning, weighing the benefits and drawbacks of each. In addition, three primary aspects of adaptive sampling are summarized: adaptive sampling architecture, multirobot sampling, and the dimensionality problem. The operation practice of adaptive sampling approaches in real applications is also investigated. Future trends for adaptive sampling of marine robots are also discussed to conclude several research directions that are not fully developed or remain unexplored, which will aid future studies.

Document title: Decentralized Swarm Formation of Miniature Robots Using the SCOPE Strategy
Abstract: The noncentralized coordination is a must in multirobot systems in order to get the scalable and faulttolerant swarm behavior. The communication bottlenecks, the single points of failure, and the limited scalability are the reasons why centralized control is not appropriate in dynamic or communication-constrained environments. In order to solve these problems, the authors introduce SCOPE (Scalable, Communication-free Offset-based Path-planning and Estimation), which is a new and fully decentralized swarm formation strategy. The SCOPE framework marks the crucial contribution that allows small autonomous robots to create and keep up exact geometric formations without any robot communication or a main controller. Each TurtleBot3 robot works separately in its own ROS namespace and employs a modular control stack: Adaptive Monte Carlo Localization (AMCL) for probabilistic pose estimation, Navfn for global path planning, and the Dynamic Window Approach (DWA) for real-time obstacle avoidance. To compute relative formation positions without a central controller or leader, the authors introduce a new virtual target offset method. The simulations demonstrated that the proposed system is effective by accomplishing 92% of the obstacles avoided, 89% of the formation accuracy, 95% of the shortest path adherence, and 91% of the path-following precision. In simulations, four TurtleBot3 Burgers were used, and three were used in hardware (limited availability) dynamic formation control. These outcomes strengthen the idea of the proposed decentralized architecture being suitable for real-world scenarios such as warehouse automation, decentralized logistics, and autonomous material handling.

Document title: Distributed Autonomous Collaborative Optimization of Virtual Power Plants Based on Hierarchical Game Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: For the scenario where the virtual power plant control platform gathers user side energy resources and jointly participates in the profit of the auxiliary service market, it is urgent to utilize the incomplete information decision-making and collaborative optimization capabilities of hybrid game intelligence technology. By combining multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms with mixed game theory, it is possible to handle interactive game problems between various agents without relying on precise environmental modeling, reduce the operating costs of virtual power plants, maximize the benefits of each agent, and improve the consumption rate of renewable energy, ensuring the safety and stability of the system. This paper investigates the distributed autonomous collaborative optimization requirements of virtual power plants based on hierarchical game reinforcement learning. On the basis of studying the autonomous operation of virtual power plants, a mixed game optimization model considering multiple interests is proposed based on the energy consumption characteristics and self-interest of different decision-making entities within the virtual power plant. Considering the existence of multiple uncertain factors in the system, it is proposed to utilize the powerful learning ability of hierarchical game reinforcement learning to verify the feasibility of effectively reducing the difficulty of solving game optimization problems under multiple constraints and high-dimensional complex working conditions.

Document title: Design and Implementation of the Integrated Mechanism Control System for Deep Space Probes
Abstract: Spacecraft servo mechanisms typically employ distributed control methods, with ground-based remote operation for control and monitoring. To achieve multiple functions such as vehicle mobility, robotic arm sampling, antenna tracking, solar panel deployment/retraction, and mast rotation, deep-space probes are equipped with numerous motors and sensors. Traditional design approaches fail to meet the demands of deepspace exploration for lightweight, compact, integrated, autonomous, and fault-tolerant control. An integrated control system architecture for deep-space probe mechanisms was established and optimized. Integration objectives were achieved through strategies like hardware resource reuse and computational resource sharing. Autonomous management capabilities were implemented across motion planning and control operations. Fault detection, emergency response, and degraded operation functions satisfied fault-tolerant control requirements. Through application in the Chang’e-7 lander mechanism control system, all metrics achieved optimal performance while satisfying multiple constraints, simultaneously validating the correctness and rationality of the design methodology. This approach holds significant reference value for control systems of complex, highly constrained probe mechanisms.

Document title: Rover-71: An Indigenous Multi-purpose Rover Featuring Autonomous Navigation and Control
Abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a cost-effective and modular rover featuring autonomous navigation. Developed for human-assisted applications in both terrestrial and extraterrestrial environments, the system supports missions such as scientific exploration, disaster response, and environmental monitoring. The system integrates a robust mechanical framework, an energy-efficient power architecture, and a long-range communication to ensure reliable performance. The core novelty lies in its modular design, a five-degree-of-freedom robotic manipulator, and a custom navigation system combining depth camera, GPS, SLAM, and real-time perception. The onboard software, powered by Jetson Orin NX and ROS2, enables the rover to perceive its surroundings, make real-time decisions and execute using a fused sensor framework. The autonomous path planning system leverages sensor fusion and priority-based control switching to safely operate in partially structured environments. Field test results confirm successful mission execution across diverse terrains, validating the rover’s effectiveness and adaptability.

Document title: Energy-Efficient Obstacle Avoidance via Iterative B-Spline Optimization for a Mobile Manipulator in Dynamic Environments
Abstract: This paper proposes an energy-efficient collision avoidance system for an autonomous mobile manipulator (AMM) in dynamic environments. The system enables safe obstacle avoidance and energy-efficient path generation. A B-Spline-based path optimization algorithm is developed, incorporating an energy cost function for planning collision-free, energy-efficient paths. The Bi-RRT algorithm generates an initial path, segmenting it at curvature maxima for energy-efficient optimization. The local path planning creates a path with seven control points, applying the same optimization for safe, low-energy avoidance of dynamic obstacles. A Model Predictive Control (MPC) system ensures precise path following. Experiments with a TM5M-900 robot validate the method's effectiveness in avoiding obstacles. Compared to Bi-RRT and Hybrid-RRT systems, it improves motion smoothness by 29.35% and reduces energy consumption by 16.84%, providing a more efficient solution for an AMM in dynamic environments.

Document title: Autonomous Drone Navigation with Natural Language Processing for Human-Centric Smart Manufacturing
Abstract: This paper introduces a natural language-driven navigation framework for autonomous drone operation in smart manufacturing environments. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have great potential for tasks such as emergency response, infrastructure inspection, and warehouse logistics. However, their adoption remains limited in the real world due to challenges, including obstacle avoidance, trajectory planning, and the need for skilled human operators. Our proposed framework, “LUNASM” - LLM-based UAV Navigation Architecture for Smart Manufacturing, combines Natural Language Processing (NLP), path planning, and obstacle avoidance. The system is implemented within the Robot Operating System (ROS) and simulated in the Gazebo simulation environment. Users send natural language commands that are processed through OpenAI’s API and converted into safe, executable flight paths. The system effectively creates accurate waypoint-based navigation paths while modeling realistic flight dynamics and drone physics. Experimental results demonstrate a 95.7% accuracy in command interpretation and a 79% success rate in executing complex navigation tasks, including zone-based navigation and multi-step instructions.

Document title: Bounding Distributional Shifts in World Modeling through Novelty Detection
Abstract: Recent work on visual world models shows significant promise in latent state dynamics obtained from pre-trained image backbones. However, most of the current approaches are sensitive to training quality, requiring near-complete coverage of the action and state space during training to prevent divergence during inference. To make a model-based planning algorithm more robust to the quality of the learned world model, we propose in this work to use a variational autoencoder as a novelty detector to ensure that proposed action trajectories during planning do not cause the learned model to deviate from the training data distribution. To evaluate the effectiveness of this approach, a series of experiments in challenging simulated robot environments was carried out, with the proposed method incorporated into a model-predictive control policy loop extending the DINO-WM architecture. The results clearly show that the proposed method improves over state-of-the-art solutions in terms of data efficiency.

Document title: Terrain-Aware Multi-Uav Cooperative Search Path Planning and Task Allocation Method
Abstract: As UAVs are now being used for more complex environmental tasks, such as disaster rescue and forest patrol, the collaborative path planning and task allocation under terrain constraints may become a key issue for ensuring efficiency in a multi-UAV system. We proposed a new multi-UAV collaborative search and task allocation method based on terrain perception (TA-MUCSTA) that establishes a double-layer terrain perception map neural planner to enhance the collaborative intelligence and terrain adaptability by building on the traditional coverage path planning and multi-agent task allocation model. At the global level, a weighted voxel topographic map was developed from remote sensing digital elevation model data, a task topology map was produced through visibility analysis with terrain risk weight, and mixed integer linear programming was used for the regional-level allocation of tasks. At the local level, we proposed the Dubins-ACO hybrid path planner with terrain constraints for each UAV, where I combined redundant coverage penalty factor and dynamic obstacle avoidance heuristic strategy to optimize search path. A dynamic alliance generation mechanism with terrain awareness was also designed with the improved Contract-Net protocol, for the case of communication constraints, allowing dynamic redistribution and load balancing to make tasks more manageable. Additionally, the method incorporated energy consumption modeling and a priority-aware task scheduling mechanism based on slope and wind speed, improving reliability and robustness in real-world operations. The TA-MUCSTA experimental results showed the method had the potential to reduce redundancy coverage by 23.6 % in a simulated mountainous environment.

Document title: Advancing Agricultural Robotics: AI Control Strategies for Delta Robots
Abstract: Delta robots are the most successful parallel robots; their unique mechanical architecture is known for high-speed and precise movements, and due to these features, they are increasingly employed in the agriculture sectors. Originally designed for high-speed industrial tasks, their mechanical structure makes them ideal candidates for a variety of agricultural operations such as fruit packing, precision planting, and rapid crop inspection. However, deploying Delta robots in dynamic and unstructured agricultural environments presents significant control challenges. To fully benefit from their superior characteristics in such environments, they must be controlled using robust control strategies, which is particularly challenging due to their nonlinear behavior and the uncertainties surrounding their models. This article provides an overview of control methods applied to Delta robots in the literature to evaluate their suitability for agricultural tasks, and it highlights the major technical problems faced in this context. A comparative analysis of these methods is offered, ranging from conventional PID controllers to modern intelligent techniques, including AI-based methods, aiming to enhance performance and adaptability in smart farming applications.

Document title: Embodying Compliant Touch on Drones for Aerial Tactile Navigation
Abstract: Aerial robots are a well-established solution for environmental surveying, exploration, and inspection, thanks to their superior maneuverability and agility. Nowadays, the algorithms that provide these capabilities rely on GNSS and Vision, which are obstructed in some environments of interest, e.g., indoors and underground or in smoke and dust. In similar conditions, animals rely on the sense of touch and compliant responses to interactions embodied in the body morphology. This way, they can navigate safely using tactile cues by feeling the environment surrounding them. In this letter, we take inspiration from the natural example and propose an approach that allows a quadrotor to navigate using tactile information from the environment. We propose to endow a conventional quadrotor with a novel robotic finger that embodies compliance and sensing capabilities. We complete this design with a navigation approach that generates new waypoints based on the robotic finger's contact information to follow the unknown environment. The overall system's evaluation shows successful, repeatable results in 36 flight experiments with various relative angles between the drone and a piecewise planar surface.

Document title: Hierarchical Multi-Robot Data Sampling for Environmental State Estimation through Online Gaussian Process
Abstract: Coverage control presents a promising method for addressing challenges such as environmental monitoring of specific fields. However, when applied to robots, coverage control typically assumes data sampling continuously both in time and space, whereas many external sensors gather data at discrete points and times. To address this issue, this paper investigates a novel cooperative data sampling that reflects the discrete nature of sensors to estimate scalar fields based on the sparse online Gaussian process (SOGP). The control goal of the present problem is formulated by a constraint on the decay rate of the variance function given by the SOGP. We then design a partially distributed constraint-based controller that enforces the constraint in the transient state, while also considering safety constraints. We then point out a drawback inherent in the present "myopic" control strategy through simulation studies. In order to overcome the drawback, we present a hierarchical control architecture, where the high-level path planner generates the optimal path based on a long-term perspective, and the low-level constraint-based control meets the decay rate constraint, while referring to the designed path for designing the nominal control. Finally, the present controller’s effectiveness is demonstrated through simulations.

Document title: Control of a Planetary Rover with Passive Suspension through an Embedded Processing System and Model Based Design
Abstract: This article proposes the control of a Planetary Rover with passive suspension using FeedForward Proportional-Integral controllers to regulate the traction system, and Generalized Proportional-Integral controllers to regulate the steering. These controllers are implemented on an embedded system with ARM architecture through automatic code generation in MATLAB/Simulink, using the Model-Based Design methodology. This solution provides robust and low-power controllers, demon-strating that it is possible to implement an advanced control algorithm on a low-cost embedded controller. Furthermore, the mechanical system of the mobile robot, its instrumentation, the mathematical modeling, and the motion control strategies are described, along with the results obtained.

Document title: A ROS 2-Based Guidance System for Agricultural Vehicles: Architecture and Algorithm Design
Abstract: This paper presents the design of a guidance system for agricultural autonomous vehicles, implemented within the ROS 2 framework. The system is modular and composed of a local planner and a guidance controller, designed to handle real-time path tracking based on reference trajectories. This solution supports scalable deployment on agricultural machines and integrates GNSS-based localization and odometry-based motion estimation. A layered ROS 2 architecture is proposed to facilitate integration and testing of the system. Results of simulations and preliminary experiments are promising, showing the potential of the system to support autonomous field navigation.

Document title: CHASE: LLM Agents for Dissecting Malicious PyPI Packages
Abstract: Modern software package registries like PyPI have become critical infrastructure for software development, but are increasingly exploited by threat actors distributing malicious packages with sophisticated multi-stage attack chains. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer promising capabilities for automated code analysis, their application to security-critical malware detection faces fundamental challenges, including hallucination and context confusion, which can lead to missed detections or false alarms. We present CHASE (Collaborative Hierarchical Agents for Security Exploration), a high-reliability multiagent architecture that addresses these limitations through a Plan-and-Execute coordination model, specialized Worker Agents focused on specific analysis aspects, and integration with deterministic security tools for critical operations. Our key insight is that reliability in LLM-based security analysis emerges not from improving individual model capabilities but from architecting systems that compensate for LLM weaknesses while leveraging their semantic understanding strengths. Evaluation on a dataset of $\mathbf{3, 0 0 0}$ packages ($\mathbf{5 0 0}$ malicious, $\mathbf{2, 5 0 0}$ benign) demonstrates that CHASE achieves 98.4 % recall with only 0.08 % false positive rate, while maintaining a practical median analysis time of 4.5 minutes per package, making it suitable for operational deployment in automated package screening. Furthermore, we conducted a survey with cybersecurity professionals to evaluate the generated analysis reports, identifying their key strengths and areas for improvement. This work provides a blueprint for building reliable AI-powered security tools that can scale with the growing complexity of modern software supply chains. Our project page is available at: https://t0d4.github.io/CHASE-AIware25/

Document title: FAIRM-WSN: A Fault-Aware Intelligent Routing and Maintenance Framework for Enhanced Wireless Sensor Network Performance
Abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are essential in the scope of Internet of Things (IoT) mainly environmental monitoring, industrial automation, and smart city projects. However, in practice, large-scale WSNs have a series of problems such as node failure, energy imbalance and environment uncertain. Hotspot and traffic congestion affects the network lifetime and reliability in case of static sink-based data collection. To address these, in this paper we present FAIRM-WSN an intelligent and comprehensive solution to the problem of fault-tolerance, energy efficiency, and data collection performance. The system contains three main parts: fault detection, clustering-based data collection and adaptive mobile sink path planning. For fault detection, a hybrid scheme is employed including the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) dimension reduction for data feature extraction and Deep Neural Network (DNN) whose parameters are fine-tuned by Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm (GOA) for high accuracy component localization when one fails. As a result, the healthy nodes are collected by DBSCAN to obtain energy and fault-conscious visiting points for the mobile sink. An agent based on Deep Q-Network (DQN) adaptively changes the trajectory of the sink according to network status. Experimental results on UNC WSN benchmark dataset show that FAIRM-WSN obtains the fault detection accuracy at about 99.72%, and energy saving of 22.3%, as well as better data delivery than some state-of-the-art algorithms. The results demonstrate the capabilities of FAIRM-WSN as a powerful and scalable approach for intelligent, fault-tolerant and energy-efficient WSN management over real world IoT systems.

Document title: Local Planning for an Autonomous Mobile Robot to Reduce Pedestrian Uncertainty
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel local planning approach for Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) to reduce pedestrian uncertainty during human-robot interactions in shared spaces. We introduce a quantitative measure of pedestrian uncertainty through a “decision entropy” framework that captures the uncertainty in crossing-order decisions. While existing research has focused primarily on predicting pedestrian physical movements, our method addresses the cognitive aspects of decision-making processes during robot-human encounters. By simultaneously optimizing both linear and angular velocities, our controller minimizes pedestrian uncertainty and creates more predictable robot behaviors. We extend previous decision entropy concepts to incorporate rotational movements, enabling the robot to clearly communicate its intentions through deliberate motion patterns. Experimental validation in real-world crossing scenarios demonstrates that our approach significantly reduces uncertainty metrics when the AMR follows pedestrians, resulting in more decisive interactions and improved pedestrian comfort. This work establishes a foundation for developing socially-aware navigation systems that consider pedestrian psychological responses in shared environments.

Document title: Design and Implementation of an Autonomous Navigation Robot Using Ros and a Multi-Sensor Platform for Educational Applications
Abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an autonomous navigation robot using the Robot Operating System and a cost-effective multi-sensor platform. The robot has been developed with legacy, low-cost sensors, including an RPLiDAR C1 and a Kinect for Xbox 360 depth camera, chosen for their affordability and compatibility with the ROS ecosystem. It is also readily available in our laboratory. We detail the hardware configuration and the ROS 1-based software architecture that enable simultaneous localization, mapping, and autonomous navigation in both 2D and 3D environments. The performance of the proposed system is evaluated through simulation in the Gazebo environment and real-world experiments. Results demonstrate that the robot can operate effectively, generating accurate maps and following planned trajectories. In ten repeated real-world trials, the maximum deviation in the generated 2 D maps was measured at 1.06 % in length and 1.75 % in width. The proposed robot offers significant potential for educational and research applications in mobile robotics due to its affordability, flexibility, and reproducibility.

Document title: Novel Hybrid MICMAC-TOPSIS based Framework for Solar Photovoltaic Module Cleaning
Abstract: Solar PV systems need efficient panels and electricity production. In addition to overheating and shadowing, certain locations are prone to PV panel dust. To decrease dust and restore plant performance, certain cleaning processes are required. Maintaining photovoltaic system efficiency requires efficient solar panel cleaning. MIC-MAC and TOPSIS, multi-criteria decision-making methodologies, are used to assess and identify the best cleaning solutions in this research. MICMAC classifies solar panel cleaning factors such surface material, location, tilt, orientation, weather, cleaning frequency, agents, safety, accessibility, cost, efficiency, manufacturer recommendations, and professional services. MICMAC analyzes direct and indirect impacts and dependencies of driving and dependent power factors for solar panel cleaning. TOPSIS rates robot water-based, robot pressure-based, manual, and nano-coating solar panel cleaning techniques. Criteria weights depend on MICMAC relevance. The option matrix is normalized and weighted to produce separation measures from ideal and negative-ideal solutions. Closeness to the finest option sorts cleaning techniques. A full approach shows nano-coating solar panel cleaning is most successful, with a relative closeness of 0.787, followed by two robotic methods and manual cleaning. The MICMAC-TOPSIS system helps choose the optimal solar panel cleaning techniques for performance and sustainability. Research promotes coordinated decision-making for renewable energy technology maintenance optimization.

Document title: An Open-Source Multi-Robot Framework System for Collaborative Environments Based on ROS2
Abstract: Despite the rise of robotics and automation in industrial applications, the widespread adoption of collaborative robotics still needs to be improved due to the lack of interoperability between robots and the low adaptability of existing systems. Solving this problem would mean a significant advance in robotics and industrial automation. Under this context, an open-source MultiRobot Framework based on ROS2 was developed in the present research to effectively communicate and coordinate robotics agents and sensors in closed collaborative environments. A simulation-based control and software design was performed using the GAZEBO tool. A centralized architecture was obtained with an autonomous navigation module for the planning and robot routes monitoring, a computer vision module for the location and management of uncertainties, and a task controller module to assign mobilization mission objects. In conclusion, using ROS2 to communicate and coordinate various mechatronic systems effectively results in a robust, flexible, and scalable solution critical to industrial processes.

Document title: Int-Ball2: On-Orbit Demonstration of Autonomous Intravehicular Flight and Docking for Image Capturing and Recharging
Abstract: This article presents the system architecture and the orbital demonstration results of the Int-Ball2, a free-flying camera robot developed by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). The purpose of the Int-Ball2 project is to assist astronauts and reduce their workload in the International Space Station (ISS). This robot is an upgrade from the first Int-Ball, enhancing the propulsion subsystem for greater maneuverability and adding a new docking station (DS) for autonomous battery recharging. This study performed comprehensive ground tests for autonomous maneuvering and docking, employing a combination of a fully software-based simulator, a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulator, and a planar air-bearing facility. After a successful launch to the ISS, the Int-Ball2 demonstrated its ability to work in microgravity without relying on astronaut support. The results obtained from ground and orbital tests underscored the effectiveness of our system design and ground verification approach. Further, we present key technologies essential for the Int-Ball2’s successful implementation on board the ISS. We expect the insights from this project to be invaluable to future missions involving free-flying robots in microgravity.

Document title: Learning Goal-Directed Object Pushing in Cluttered Scenes With Location-Based Attention
Abstract: In complex scenarios where typical pick-and-place techniques are insufficient, often non-prehensile manipulation can ensure that a robot is able to fulfill its task. However, non-prehensile manipulation is challenging due to its underactuated nature with hybrid-dynamics, where a robot needs to reason about an object’s long-term behavior and contact-switching, while being robust to contact uncertainty. The presence of clutter in the workspace further complicates this task, introducing the need to include more advanced spatial analysis to avoid unwanted collisions. Building upon prior work on reinforcement learning with multimodal categorical exploration for planar pushing, we propose to incorporate location-based attention to enable robust manipulation in cluttered scenes. Unlike previous approaches addressing this obstacle avoiding pushing task, our framework requires no predefined global paths and considers the desired target orientation of the manipulated object. Experimental results in simulation as well as with a real KUKA iiwa robot arm demonstrate that our learned policy manipulates objects successfully while avoiding collisions through complex obstacle configurations, including dynamic obstacles, to reach the desired target pose.

Document title: Digital Twin-Enhanced Communication Architectures for Malaysia's Smart Manufacturing Sector
Abstract: The integration of digital twins into smart manufacturing has emerged as a transformative approach, revolutionizing the way factories operate, monitor, and optimize performance. In Malaysia's push toward Industry 4.0 and its upcoming transition to Industry 5.0, digital twinenhanced communication architectures play a critical role in ensuring real-time data synchronization, predictive analytics, and intelligent automation. This paper presents a comprehensive investigation into the design, implementation, and optimization of digital twin-augmented communication infrastructures tailored to Malaysia's smart manufacturing context. Leveraging edge computing, industrial IoT, 5G, and semantic interoperability standards, we propose a multilayered communication framework that addresses latency, data reliability, and system scalability challenges. Our research combines simulation modeling, industrial testbeds, and stakeholder interviews across key industrial corridors in Selangor and Penang. Findings indicate that digital twinenabled communication systems improve real-time process visibility by 58%, reduce downtime by 35%, and enhance predictive maintenance accuracy by 62% compared to conventional setups. Through architectural modeling, latency analysis, and digital twin synchronization protocols, the study demonstrates the viability of the proposed framework in small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs) and multinational manufacturing plants alike. The results underscore the necessity of standardized digital twin interfaces (e.g., OPC UA, MQTT, and ISO 23247), edge-driven latency mitigation strategies, and cloud-twin data fusion mechanisms to ensure full-loop control and scalability. This work contributes a technically validated, policy-aligned, and future-proof architecture that supports Malaysia's Smart Manufacturing Blueprint (2021-2030) and aligns with the MyDigital roadmap.

Document title: Dynamic Event-Triggered Optimal Control for Nonlinear Switched Systems by Using Adaptive Dynamic Programming
Abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) algorithm based on a dynamic event-triggered mechanism (ETM) for the optimal control problem of a class of continuous-time nonlinear switched systems. First, a performance index function that incorporates switching signals is introduced, followed by the derivation of a hybrid control strategy that includes both optimal control law and optimal switching law. To save computational resources, a dynamic ETM is introduced. Unlike time-triggered and static ETMs, dynamic event triggering provides more flexible triggering conditions. The single-layer critic neural network (NN) is constructed to solve the event-triggered HJB equation for the switched system. The weights of the critic NN are then trained using the gradient descent algorithm, and the stability of the closed-loop system is proven using the Lyapunov theorem. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified through a single-link robot arm plant.

Document title: ActiveGS: Active Scene Reconstruction Using Gaussian Splatting
Abstract: Robotics applications often rely on scene reconstructions to enable downstream tasks. In this work, we tackle the challenge of actively building an accurate map of an unknown scene using an RGB-D camera on a mobile platform. We propose a hybrid map representation that combines a Gaussian splatting map with a coarse voxel map, leveraging the strengths of both representations: the high-fidelity scene reconstruction capabilities of Gaussian splatting and the spatial modelling strengths of the voxel map. At the core of our framework is an effective confidence modelling technique for the Gaussian splatting map to identify under-reconstructed areas, while utilising spatial information from the voxel map to target unexplored areas and assist in collision-free path planning. By actively collecting scene information in under-reconstructed and unexplored areas for map updates, our approach achieves superior Gaussian splatting reconstruction results compared to state-of-the-art approaches. Additionally, we demonstrate the real-world applicability of our framework using an unmanned aerial vehicle.

Document title: Adaptive DQN: An Enhanced Approach for Robot Path Planning in Dynamic Environments
Abstract: Deep Q-Networks (DQN) have achieved remarkable success in solving complex control tasks but their performance is sensitive to the stability of the target network and learning efficiency. This paper proposes an enhanced algorithm that combines the Dueling DQN architecture with an adaptive target network update mechanism. The mechanism dynamically adjusts the update frequency of the target network based on the Bellman error and Q-value stability, thereby improving the stability and performance of the training process. Experimental results in the CartPole-v1 environment show that the Adaptive DQN outperforms both Fixed DQN and Dueling DQN in terms of average reward and stability. Specifically, the Adaptive DQN achieves average rewards that are 88.11% and 36.58% higher than Fixed DQN and Dueling DQN, respectively. Moreover, the average Bellman error of Adaptive DQN is reduced by 84.25% compared to Fixed DQN and by 82.91% compared to Dueling DQN. In path planning tasks within the FrozenLake-v1 environment, Adaptive DQN also demonstrates superior success rates and stability. It achieves a success rate of 0.015, which is significantly higher than the 0.008 for Fixed DQN and 0.008 for Dueling DQN. Additionally, the path length planned by Adaptive DQN is notably shorter at 25 steps, compared to 33 steps for Fixed DQN and 81 steps for Dueling DQN. In the continuous maze environment, Adaptive DQN effectively mitigates ineffective exploration behaviors in robotic path planning, enhancing the efficiency of reaching the target point. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the Adaptive DQN in enhancing the efficiency and stability of path planning.

Document title: A distributed energy generation scheduling algorithm based on reinforcement learning
Abstract: With the high proportion of distributed energy (DER) access, traditional centralized scheduling methods can not cope with the randomness and system complexity of renewable energy. In this paper, an optimization method for distributed energy generation scheduling based on reinforcement learning (RL) is proposed, which combines multi-agent near end strategy optimization (MAPPO) and flexible actor-critic (SAC) algorithm to achieve efficient and collaborative energy management. For centralized microgrid scenarios, SAC algorithm is used to optimize the combined output of photovoltaic, energy storage and traditional units, and its entropy maximization mechanism enhances exploration capabilities and effectively balances economic and environmental objectives. For distributed virtual power plants or multi-microgrid systems, MAPPO framework is used to realize cooperative scheduling among agents, and the contradiction between local observation and global optimization is solved through centralized training-distributed execution strategy. The simulation results show that the proposed method is significantly superior to the traditional optimization algorithm in reducing the operating cost, improving the consumption rate of renewable energy and ensuring the security of power grid. In addition, the convergence speed and strategy robustness of the algorithm are further improved by introducing preferential experience playback and hierarchical reinforcement learning. This study provides a scalable solution for intelligent scheduling of high-proportion renewable energy grids.

Document title: Multi-Finger Collaborative Grasping Control for Prosthetic Hands Using Proximity Sensors
Abstract: Traditional prosthetic hand grasping often relies on pre-programmed trajectories due to the lack of non-contact perception, leading to asynchronous finger contact, object displacement, and instability. To achieve synchronous multi-finger contact and adaptive pre-shaping, this paper presents a hierarchical control strategy driven by fingertip proximity sensing. We integrate miniature reflective light-intensity sensors on each fingertip for real-time distance measurement. The core innovations include: A master-slave phase compensation architecture featuring dynamic master finger election to coordinate finger movements towards an equidistant plane relative to the target object; Lyapunov stability-based anti-disturbance allocation to dynamically redistribute control effort among fingers when disturbances occur, maintaining grasp envelope stability. Implemented solely on an embedded microcontroller, the system requires no complex external computation or electromyographic signals. Experimental validation on a 5-DOF prosthetic hand demonstrates successful adaptive pre-shaping for various objects. Results show high positional accuracy, significantly improved grasp success rate, minimal multi-finger synchronization error, and robust disturbance rejection. This approach significantly enhances the continuity, stability, and environmental adaptability of prosthetic grasping in unstructured settings.

Document title: Trajectory Optimization via Virtual Motion Camouflage: A Dimensionality Reduction Method
Abstract: This paper presents a trajectory optimization framework based on virtual motion camouflage strategies to address trajectory planning challenges in complex environments for intelligent robotic systems. Inspired by predatory motion camouflage phenomena in nature, we innovatively construct geometric constraint relationships between virtual prey paths, dynamic camouflage lines, and parameterized control points. This approach transforms high-dimensional trajectory optimization problems into low-dimensional parameter optimization problems while naturally ensuring trajectory safety through the convex hull properties of Bézier curves. Through dynamic adjustment mechanisms in parameter space, the method flexibly adapts to environmental changes, significantly improving trajectory quality while maintaining computational efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to traditional Minimum Snap methods, our algorithm achieves significant improvements of 99.4%, 34.18%, and 66.7% in objective function cost, maximum curvature, and safety metrics, respectively. This provides a new technical solution for applications requiring stringent trajectory quality, such as industrial mobile robots and unmanned aerial vehicle inspection.

Document title: CBF-Based Constrained Optimization for Safe and Adaptive CPG Gait Planning in Rehabilitation Robots
Abstract: To address gait safety optimization in human-robot interaction during rehabilitation training, this paper proposes a safety-aware adaptive gait planning method integrating Control Barrier Function (CBF) and Central Pattern Generator (CPG) for synchronized motion between wearers and lower-limb exoskeletons. Initially, a CPG network generates biologically rhythmic trajectories with inter-joint coordination, while real-time adjustments of gait frequency and amplitude parameters are implemented based on the wearer's active torque. To mitigate safety risks induced by parameter adaptation, a hybrid constrained optimization framework is developed: By combining admittance modeling for human-robot dynamic characterization, a CBF-based safety constraint controller dynamically bounds CPG output parameters, guaranteeing biomechanically safe gait trajectories. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

Document title: Intelligent Shelf and AGV Collaborative Autonomous Delivery System for Scattered Metered Power Materials
Abstract: This paper establishes a collaborative autonomous outbound delivery model for smart shelves and automated guided vehicles (AGVs), aiming to improve the automation level and overall efficiency of the outbound delivery process. First, photoelectric sensors and high-precision intelligent weighing modules are integrated at the smart shelf level to enable real-time monitoring and data modeling of material location and inventory status. Second, material information is transmitted to the dispatching system via a data interface, providing the AGV with precise coordinates for picking up items. The AGV utilizes high-precision navigation technology that integrates lidar and vision, and is equipped with a gripping mechanism that combines adaptive gripping and vacuum suction to handle loose items of varying sizes and weights. A hybrid optimization strategy based on an improved A* algorithm and a dynamic window method is employed for path planning, dynamically adjusting driving paths in a multi-task environment to reduce idle travel and waiting time. In a simulation of 10,000 outbound delivery missions, the system achieved an average outbound delivery efficiency improvement of approximately 60.9%, with material positioning errors kept within ±3 mm and an average success rate of approximately 93%. Furthermore, under low-load conditions, the system feedback latency remains at 21.0 ms, meeting the real-time control requirements of power supply warehouses.

Document title: Neural-Network-Based Sliding Mode Trajectory Tracking Control of Tendon-Driven Space Flexible Manipulators*
Abstract: Tendon-driven space manipulators, characterized by their large span, long reach, and high torque, are ideal devices for future on-orbit construction tasks. However, due to the unique structural features of tendon-driven space manipulators, residual vibrations often occur at the end-effector during point-to-point motion, which severely degrades the positioning accuracy and dynamic performance of the manipulator during on-orbit operations. To address this issue, this paper proposes a control strategy that combines trajectory planning with active vibration control methods. Firstly, the dynamics model of the tendon-driven space flexible manipulator is established. Then, a hybrid particle swarm optimization algorithm is given to optimize the motion trajectory, aiming to reduce residual vibrations and obtain the desired trajectory for trajectory tracking. Furthermore, a neural network based sliding mode controller via fully actuated system approach is introduced to realize trajectory tracking control, with a detailed stability analysis presented. Finally, numerical simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Document title: COLLAGE: Collaborative Human-Agent Interaction Generation Using Hierarchical Latent Diffusion and Language Models
Abstract: We propose a novel framework COLLAGE for generating collaborative agent-object-agent interactions by leveraging large language models (LLMs) and hierarchical motion-specific vector-quantized variational autoencoders (VQ-VAEs). Our model addresses the lack of rich datasets in this domain by incorporating the knowledge and reasoning abilities of LLMs to guide a generative diffusion model. The hierarchical VQ-VAE architecture captures different motion-specific characteristics at multiple levels of abstraction, avoiding redundant concepts and enabling efficient multi-resolution representation. We introduce a diffusion model that operates in the latent space and incorporates LLM-generated motion planning cues to guide the denoising process, resulting in prompt-specific motion generation with greater control and diversity. Experimental results on the CORE-4D, and InterHuman datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in generating realistic and diverse collaborative human-object-human interactions, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Our work opens up new possibilities for modeling complex interactions in various domains, such as robotics, graphics and computer vision. Paper website: https://collagemotion.github.io/

Document title: Improving Traceability and Efficiency: Industry 4.0 and Blockchain’s Transformation of Production Processes
Abstract: The main goal of this article is to depict the automation and digitization of the real production process and to describe an entire system for achieving complete product traceability based on a decentralized knowledge graph, blockchain, and Industry 4.0 technologies. Presented sys-tem architecture provides the possibility of interoperability between existing enterprise re-source planning systems and blockchain. Different traceability levels were accomplished in practice by using and combining certain Industry 4.0 technologies which led to full final product verification. At the same time, stated research undoubtedly illustrates the actual shift from a traditional production process to a digital one, which is firmly established on new technologies and the OriginTrail blockchain.

Document title: Modeling and Task Planning of an Integrated UVMS Platform for Underwater Operation Disposal
Abstract: This paper develops an Underwater Vehicle-Manipulator System (UVMS) platform capable of executing underwater missions in order to enhance the operational accuracy of autonomous underwater vehicles. First of all, a task-oriented architecture is established through systematic hardware configuration and communication system design, accompanied by functional modularization and spatial layout optimization of the UVMS. Kinematic and dynamic models are derived based on the UVMS platform's unique mechanical configuration. Furthermore, the operational workflow is elaborated through practical case studies of underwater manipulation tasks, with particular emphasis on the end-effector's spline interpolation trajectory planning and tracking during mission execution. The experimental validation demonstrates the platform's effectiveness in achieving precise trajectory control for complex underwater operations.

Document title: An Intelligent Handling Robot System Based on a Master-Slave Architecture with Multimodal Fusion Control
Abstract: Autonomous Mobile Robots face significant challenges in intelligent logistics scenarios, including dynamic turntable picking, narrow passage navigation, and high-precision palletizing. Existing competition robot solutions often suffer from low dynamic visual recognition rates, insufficient omnidirectional positioning accuracy, and error accumulation between modules. To address these issues, this paper designs and implements an intelligent handling robot system based on a master-slave architecture utilizing a Mini Personal Computer as the upper computer and an STM32F103ZET6 microcontroller as the lower computer. A multimodal fusion control strategy is proposed where the upper computer is responsible for task parsing, visual recognition through Hue-Saturation-Value segmentation and Hough circle detection, and path planning. The lower computer handles real-time motion control integrated with a trapezoidal acceleration-deceleration algorithm, drives the execution mechanisms, and acquires Inertial Measurement Unit data. Simultaneously, motion errors are compensated through the fusion of visual and inertial measurement data. Experimental results demonstrate that the system achieves an average deviation of 4.2 millimeters over a 1000 millimeter straight-line movement, a dynamic turntable material recognition rate of 95 percent, and color ring placement accuracy within 3 millimeters. The system exhibited stable performance in simulated competition workflows and ultimately won the first prize in the 2025 Provincial Competition, providing a reliable technical solution for lightweight warehouse automation.

Document title: Communication for UAV Swarms: an Open-source, Low-cost Solution Based on ESP-NOW
Abstract: Multi-UAV systems typically require complex in-frastructure to deploy in real-world scenarios, limiting their accessibility and scalability. In addition, current research often relies on custom solutions or proprietary hardware to facilitate inter-UAV communication. In this paper, we propose an open-source, low-cost, plug-and-play solution to enable decentralized UAV-to-UAV communication over 2.4GHz Wi-Fi using a con-nectionless protocol. Our approach simplifies the deployment of decentralized systems by allowing UAVs to easily exchange any type of binary data, seamlessly interfacing with ROS2. The solution uses an ad-hoc style network that allows UAVs to join or leave dynamically without requiring centralized governance or a priori configuration. We describe the architecture of the system, assess the network performance in an outdoor environment using UAVs, and evaluate the system's ability to share information as a swarm through hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) and experiments using UAVs. Our results show that the proposed system facilitates connectivity and is able to transmit mission-critical data for real-world UAV operations. HITL experiments show that a decentralized planning algorithm running on three simulated UAVs can effectively reach consensus on decentralized task allocation. We have made the code public and thus provide a viable solution for researchers seeking to implement decentralized UAV swarms using cost-effective commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware and minimal infrastructure.

Document title: Design of Insert Assembly Workstation in Injection Mold and Visual Algorithm
Abstract: This paper focuses on the needs for precise positioning and efficient operation in the automated assembly process of inserts in injection molds, and conducts research on the design of workstation assembly based on machine vision algorithms. Firstly, in response to the process characteristics and technical requirements of insert assembly, the overall structural design and process planning of the workstation are completed. Through two chapters, the mechanical structure layout, transmission system selection, control system architecture and assembly operation process of the workstation are elaborated in detail, laying a hardware and process foundation for automated assembly.To achieve high-precision recognition and positioning of inserts, the KNN algorithm is introduced for improvement based on the traditional SURF algorithm. Feature points of inserts and assembly stations are extracted via the SURF algorithm, and the KNN algorithm is utilized to optimize the matching and classification of these feature points.
