This effectively enhances the accuracy and anti-interference capability of feature matching, addressing the issue that traditional algorithms tend to suffer from insufficient matching precision due to the influence of illumination and noise in complex industrial environments.Experimental results indicate that the improved SURF-KNN algorithm achieves higher matching accuracy than the traditional SURF algorithm in recognizing inserts in injection molds, which meets the precision requirements of automated assembly. The workstation based on this vision algorithm can stably perform the grabbing, positioning and assembly of inserts, significantly improving production efficiency and providing a feasible technical solution for the automated assembly of inserts in injection molds.

Document title: Direct Policy Transfer Method for Multi-UAV Autonomous Navigation in Unknown Environment
Abstract: Autonomous navigation for UAV swarms in unknown environments holds critical importance for applications ranging from disaster response to military reconnaissance, yet faces multifaceted challenges including dynamic obstacle avoidance, real-time computational constraints, and absence of environmental priors. Conventional path planning methods (e.g., artificial potential fields, APF) frequently succumb to local optima under global information scarcity, while deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approaches, despite their environmental adaptability, suffer from low sample efficiency and slow convergence. This study proposes a Direct Policy Transfer-enhanced Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization framework (DPT-MAPPO), merging APF spatial modeling efficiency with DRL adaptive optimization. Specially, the framework accelerates environment-task mapping during early training via APF-guided policy priors and resolves inherent local minima in conventional APF through DRL-driven stochastic exploration. Experimental validation across three representative unknown scenarios demonstrates that the proposed method attained 4-fold acceleration in convergence compared to MAPPO algorithms and 16% higher success rate compared to APF algorithms, confirming the framework’s dual advantages in safe navigation and computational efficiency for complex unknown environments.

Document title: Hierarchical Decentralized Stochastic Control for Cyber-Physical Systems
Abstract: This letter introduces a two-timescale hierarchical decentralized control architecture for Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS). The system consists of a global controller (GC), and N local controllers (LCs). The GC operates at a slower timescale, imposing budget constraints on the actions of LCs, which function at a faster timescale. Applications can be found in energy grid planning, wildfire management, and other decentralized resource allocation problems. We propose and analyze two optimization frameworks for this setting: COpt and FOpt. In COpt, both GC and LCs together optimize infinite-horizon discounted rewards, while in FOpt the LCs optimize finite-horizon episodic rewards, and the GC optimizes infinite-horizon rewards. Although both frameworks share identical reward functions, their differing horizons can lead to different optimal policies. In particular, FOpt grants greater autonomy to LCs by allowing their policies to be determined only by local objectives, unlike COpt. To our knowledge, these frameworks have not been studied in the literature. We establish the formulations, prove the existence of optimal policies, and prove the convergence of their value iteration algorithms. We further show that COpt always achieves a higher value function than FOpt and derive explicit bounds on their difference. Finally, we establish a set of sufficient structural conditions under which the two frameworks become equivalent.

Document title: Offshore Subsurface Infrastructure Imaging From AI Deep Learning-Based Three-Dimensional Acoustic and Magnetic Data Inversion
Abstract: Hurricane Ivan in 2004 was a catastrophic event that toppled an oil production platform in the Northern Gulf of Mexico, displacing it over 250 m from its original location. Oil well conductors attached to the platform and many other metallic structures were also displaced and scattered across the existing sea floor. In 2022, Couvillion engaged Kraken Robotics to deploy their proprietary imaging technology, Acoustic Coring (AC), to image these conductors, currently buried beneath a 30 to 45 m thick layer of delta-released sediments below the mudline. The three-dimensional imaging technology, developed by [1], was designed for the shallow sub-seabed to identify and characterize geohazards and stratigraphy. This technology requires specular and non-specular returns with spatial accuracies that exceed those of current conventional seismic surveys (i.e., towed streamer-based methods) [2]. This was achieved through sub-seabed interrogation using a stationary transmitter and receiver array, which holds a spatially centimetre-spaced network across a horizontal imaging dimension of 14 metres [1] [2]. A total of 63 AC scans, consisting of 21 rows along three scanning columns spanning a 205 m x 60 m survey area, were conducted to determine the extent, expanse, orientation, and characteristics of lost conductor pipes. Of significance were continuous linear conductors reposing onto a basement geology lying directly across from the containment dome towards the location of the original conductor bay, following the basement slope closely. The pipes' endings show an abrupt spread-out termination with an undulating humped, slightly down-looking character around survey Row 11. In the region around this termination, gas-laden soil inhibited the acoustic ability to get acoustic returns and collect further data. It was postulated that the conductors were severed at this location, no longer existed, or continued uninterrupted toward the original oil well location. To help clarify the possibilities, a high-resolution magnetometer survey comprised of four three-component flux gate magnetometers integrated into a Millenium Plus ROV was conducted. The aim was to survey a region defined as an area of 460m (1509ft) by 405m (1328ft) to determine whether magnetometer data collected beyond Row 11 and extending toward the conductor bay could indicate the presence of buried pipes. The high-quality magnetic data showed continuity and agreement with the pre-survey modelling results. The results concorded with the acoustic conductor features mapped initially, and the responding magnetic lobes were consistent with debris targets predicted by modelling. Out-of-plane influences, such as the rotated displaced oil rig platform and heavy accumulation of metal debris around the original well, complicated the signals. However, the recorded magnetic data by itself shows a termination of the high-intensity lobe 40 m NE of the known location of the well conductor bay. The nature and geometry of the conductor bundle, as it extended beyond the last imaged location in the AC and towards the well bay, was not easily deciphered by common human vision-driven interpretation of magnetic data. To obtain this information, extensive AI -based modelling was developed utilizing the precision and details of the Acoustic Corer data results to train the AI system on the magnetometer data [5]. The 3D Training Models were created using an 8 GPU computer cluster handling 110 Epochs (in computing, an epoch is a fixed date and time used as a reference from which a computer measures system time). High-performance cloud-based computation clusters from AWS were deployed to simulate forward models to generate input training data rapidly. 202,000 3D training models and their magnetic response at 2 m intervals (high resolution) were generated. A deep learning architecture was then deployed to learn how to predict the underlying 3D magnetic model from the simulated response. This was achieved on another cloud-based system hosted by Shadeform, utilizing a network of 8 GPU machines, each equipped with 80 GB RAM. In this paper, the AI imagery is presented. It shows that damage to the well site is evident, revealing debris around the original well and where the conductors appear after Row 11. The continuity trend of the conductor pipes exhibits variation in signal strength responses beyond Row 11, indicating that past Row 11 and nearing the location of the original well, the conductors have sustained damage and may contain separated and fragmented pipes. However, the AI enhancements delineate continuity, highlight the trajectory of the pipe infrastructure toward the well placement, and partially encircle it. Simultaneously, a secondary parallel conductor trajectory branches off and leads forty meters north of the original well. This secondary trajectory consists of fragmented conductors or pipe-related debris and terminates where the high survey-based magnetic main anomaly lobe also concludes. As will be shown in the paper, the resulting magnetometer imagery was influenced by a complicated geometry of scattered metallic debris. Aspects of the critical conductor system, as imaged in detail by the Acoustic Corer, correlated well. The conductor package continues beyond Row 11; the last imaged location of the conductors seen in the acoustic thins out in places but continues towards the original well bay, albeit 40 m to the northeast, as suggested by the high anomaly lobe in the magnetic data. However, the AI imaging brought out a hidden subtle secondary branch of the conductor package veering and connecting with the metallic debris near the well bay, establishing clear evidence of a potential flow path from the well bay back to the downed jacket and oil /gas collection dome. These results could be achieved only through the fusion of acoustic imaging, magnetic data, and the intensive AI Deep Learning analysis that could look deep into the magnetic responses to reveal the subtle, hidden, buried features at higher discriminating resolutions.

Document title: Intelligent Grasp Planning Using Open-Vocabulary Image Segmentation and Large Language Models
Abstract: Intelligent autonomous grasp planning is a key challenge in real-world deployment of robotic systems. Generating robust grasp require solving multiple challenges such perception, semantic segmentation, motion planning and grasp stability optimization. Over the years, many techniques have been proposed to solve one or more of the above challenges. Recent evolution of end-to-end learning for grasp planning has demonstrated the use of deep learning methods that map sensory data, such as images or point clouds, directly to grasp action. But these approaches require large datasets to train, and often struggle at sim-toreal transfer. Moreover the trained architecture is usually not interpretable and cannot guarantee safety or repeatability, which are important factors in real-world deployments. To address these limitations, we propose a novel grasp planning pipeline that can leverage the inference capability of Large Language Models, along with open vocabulary image segmentation. The depth image segmentation is further processed using classical algorithms that fit primitive shapes to the segmented point cloud data, resulting in stable grasp pose. The overall pipeline results in a repeatable and explainable pipeline for intelligent grasp generation, especially for everyday objects. The proposed pipeline was evaluated on two different scenes consisting everyday objects with varying clutter density. The pipeline was also compared with a data driven model on a set of standard shapes. Results indicate reliable grasp generation for everyday objects as well as comparable performance with the data driven approach on the standard set of objects.

Document title: Language-Guided Predictive Control: Synthesizing Semantic Safety Constraints for Adaptive Navigation
Abstract: To become effective collaborators, autonomous robots must bridge the semantic gap between a human’s qualitative instructions and the quantitative world of a motion controller, particularly for safety warnings like "avoid the spill" which traditional systems struggle to ground in physical reality. This paper introduces a hierarchical control architecture featuring a Large Language Model (LLM) based planner that autonomously synthesizes geometric safety constraints (exclusion zones) from abstract warnings and uses a "semantic centroid" method to translate nuanced motion modifiers into a continuous parameterization of a downstream Model Predictive Controller (MPC). The resulting plan guides a dynamic path planner that reconstructs its navigation graph on-demand to generate consistently safe trajectories for complex multi-robot tasks, including cooperative transport. We validated our framework in a high-fidelity simulator, demonstrating that the system successfully generates paths that maneuver around language-defined hazards, representing a significant step towards creating more intuitive, adaptable, and trustworthy robotic collaborators for human-centric environments.

Document title: Digital Twin-Driven Multi-Intelligent Body Simulation System for Building Emergency Evacuation
Abstract: Building emergency evacuations often suffer from inefficiencies due to static planning and delayed response to environmental changes. To address these limitations, a digital twin-driven multi-agent simulation model is developed to enhance real-time evacuation decision-making. The model integrates Building Information Modeling (BIM)-based 3D geometry with multi-source sensor data, enabling dynamic perception of building states. A method combining multi-agent behavioral models with hybrid $A^{*}$ path planning achieves synergistic optimization of congestion metrics and path length. Real-time feedback from digital twin technology ensures adaptive path adjustments during unexpected events. Analysis indicates that compared to the static $A^{*}$ framework, the dynamic $\mathbf{A}^{*}$ framework reduces evacuation time by 31.2 seconds and 14.4 seconds, respectively, while lowering congestion indices by 8.4 % and 4.5 %. Demonstrating strong adaptability in highdensity environments, this digital twin-based intelligent simulation technology holds significant promise for enhancing safety in complex buildings.

Document title: Context-Aware Artificial Intelligence Systems for Long-Horizon Decision Making
Abstract: Long-horizon decision making remains a fundamental challenge in artificial intelligence, particularly in complex, dynamic environments where agents must reason over extended temporal sequences while maintaining contextual awareness. This paper presents a novel Context-Aware Long-Horizon Decision Making (CA-LHDM) framework that integrates hierarchical reinforcement learning with transformer-based context encoding to enable effective planning and execution over extended time horizons. Our approach leverages attention mechanisms to capture temporal dependencies and contextual information across multiple abstraction levels, enabling agents to decompose complex tasks into manageable subgoals while maintaining global coherence. We introduce a hybrid architecture combining model-based planning with model-free learning, supported by an adaptive memory module that selectively retains relevant historical information. Experimental evaluation on benchmark tasks including MuJoCo continuous control and multi-agent coordination scenarios demonstrates that CA-LHDM achieves $\mathbf{4 7 {\%}}$ improvement in cumulative reward and $\mathbf{3 5 {\%}}$ reduction in planning time compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Our ablation studies reveal the critical role of context encoding in achieving superior performance, with the attention-based context module contributing 28% of the overall performance gain.

Document title: Prediction-Driven Motion Planning: Route Integration Strategies in Attention-Based Prediction Models
Abstract: Combining motion prediction and motion planning offers a promising framework for enhancing interactions between automated vehicles and other traffic participants. However, this introduces challenges in conditioning predictions on navigation goals and ensuring stable, kinematically feasible trajectories. Addressing the former challenge, this paper investigates the extension of attention-based motion prediction models with navigation information. By integrating the ego vehicle's intended route and goal pose into the model architecture, we bridge the gap between multi-agent motion prediction and goal-based motion planning. We propose and evaluate several architectural navigation integration strategies to our model on the nuPlan dataset. Our results demonstrate the potential of prediction-driven motion planning, highlighting how navigation information can enhance both prediction and planning tasks. Our implementation is at: https://github.com/KIT-MRT/future-motion.

Document title: Cooperative Multi-AUV System for Underwater Data Collection and Path Optimization
Abstract: The growing demands for marine resource exploitation and environmental monitoring have exposed critical challenges in Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (UWSNs), including imbalanced energy consumption, limited data timeliness, and insufficient adaptability to large-scale deployments. Existing AUV-assisted solutions remain constrained by periodic return requirements for storage offloading, failing to meet real-time demands, while conventional path-planning algorithms are prone to local optima. To address these issues, this paper proposes a multi-Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) cooperative data collection system specifically designed for the shoal-and-reef environment of the South China Sea. A hybrid hierarchical communication architecture integrating acoustic, optical fiber, and blue-green laser links is developed, enabling peripheral AUVs to collect sectorial data and relay it in real-time to a central AUV. This is complemented by a mobile AUV that facilitates near-realtime cross-medium transmission. Furthermore, to resolve the complexity of AUV path planning within this framework, we introduce an information entropy-enhanced Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm. This approach incorporates a dynamic parameter adaptation mechanism and multi-agent cooperative optimization strategy, significantly accelerating convergence speed and enhancing robustness. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing methods in path optimization, energy efficiency, and delay control, achieving an average path length reduction of $15.7 \%$ and reducing total node energy consumption by $42.3 \%$. These improvements effectively extend network lifetime and enhance resource utilization balance, validating the system’s efficacy for long-term, large-scale underwater data acquisition missions.

Document title: Development of a Wheeled Quadruped Robot for Rough Terrains
Abstract: This study presents the development of a wheeled quadruped bionic platform, building upon an existing opensource quadruped robotic system. The proposed robotic architecture integrates a variety of components, including controllers, cameras, sensors, and motors, into a unified bionic robot platform. This innovative wheeled quadruped design facilitates intelligent switching between legged and wheeled locomotion modes, thereby enhancing its adaptability and mobility across diverse terrain conditions. A depth camera is mounted at the front of the platform to capture terrain information ahead. The acquired depth images are initially transformed into pseudo-colored depth maps and subsequently processed using the EfficientNet-Lite convolutional neural network for real-time terrain classification. Simultaneously, edge detection is applied to the RGB captures from the camera to evaluate trajectory deviations during movement. In walking mode, inverse kinematics is employed to determine the positions of the leg end effectors and the corresponding joint angles, along with gait planning strategies. Data from an onboard inertial measurement unit is utilized to dynamically adjust leg height and pose in real-time, enabling self-balancing locomotion. In wheeled mode, a fuzzy control system manages body posture and wheel velocity differentials to correct any path deviations. The performance of our wheeled quadruped robot is validated through a series of terrain experiments, demonstrating the viability of its hybrid mobility modes and trajectory correction capabilities, while underscoring its potential for future development and application in complex environments.

Document title: Application and optimization of reinforcement learning algorithm for coal yard transportation scheduling
Abstract: Aiming at the transportation scheduling problem of coal yard, this paper proposes an optimization algorithm framework based on reinforcement learning (RL). Firstly, the coal yard transportation scheduling problem is modeled as markov decision processes (MDP), and a state space including dynamic environment and equipment state is designed, as well as an action space including vehicle path planning, equipment start-stop strategy and task priority adjustment. Furthermore, a multi-objective dynamic reward function is constructed, and an adaptive weight mechanism is introduced to balance short-term tasks and long-term equipment maintenance costs. To enhance algorithm performance, this paper adopts a hybrid framework that combines a rule engine with the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm to improve system robustness. Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) with the QMIX algorithm is utilized to achieve coordinated scheduling between vehicles and equipment, reducing path conflicts. Through simulation experiments and validation with real-world data, the results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms traditional methods in transportation costs, penalty costs, and maintenance costs. It significantly improves task completion rates, reduces the number of path conflicts, and optimizes equipment utilization. Sensitivity analysis of dynamic weights shows that the adaptive weight mechanism effectively responds to environmental changes, achieving more efficient, environmentally friendly, and safer operational management.

Document title: The Emergence of Deep Reinforcement Learning for Path Planning
Abstract: The increasing demand for autonomous systems in complex and dynamic environments has driven significant research into intelligent path planning methodologies. For decades, graph-based search algorithms, linear programming techniques, and evolutionary computation methods have served as foundational approaches in this domain. Recently, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has emerged as a powerful method for enabling autonomous agents to learn optimal navigation strategies through interaction with their environments. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of traditional approaches as well as the recent advancements in DRL applied to path planning tasks, focusing on autonomous vehicles, drones, and robotic platforms. Key algorithms across both conventional and learning-based paradigms are categorized, with their innovations and practical implementations highlighted. This is followed by a thorough discussion of their respective strengths and limitations in terms of computational efficiency, scalability, adaptability, and robustness. The survey concludes by identifying key open challenges and outlining promising avenues for future research. Special attention is given to hybrid approaches that integrate DRL with classical planning techniques to leverage the benefits of both learning-based adaptability and deterministic reliability, offering promising directions for robust and resilient autonomous navigation.

Document title: Building Robust GNSS–GIS Data Fusion Platforms for Autonomous Robots: Perspectives and Recommendations
Abstract: In this work, we provide a conceptual overview of the research pertaining Geographical Information Systems (GIS) and Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) integration in autonomous robotic platforms. Instead of presenting a full localization pipeline, our focus is on discussing which GIS-based tools and methods can most effectively complement GNSS in degraded environments and how this GIS-GNSS integration has been achieved so far. We further outline how GIS elements could be integrated into a new architecture. A front-end would provide real-time visualization of the robot state, mission planning interfaces, and terrain layers, while a back-end would support GNSS correction distribution, GIS dataset management, and semantic access to spatial information. Together, these elements define a roadmap for a future robust GNSS–GIS fusion platform.

Document title: Development and Implementation of an Intelligent Deep Learning-Based Brain Tumor Detection System Integrated with Raspberry Pi for Real-Time Diagnostic Applications in the Field of Biomedical Engineering
Abstract: In recent times, tumors—especially brain tumors-have emerged as one of the leading causes of serious health complications and are now the second most common cause of cancer-related deaths. The growing number of patients at risk has created an urgent need for faster, more accurate, and reliable methods of detection. Early and precise identification of a tumor plays a crucial role in timely treatment and improving patient outcomes. When tumors are detected properly and at the right time, doctors are in a better position to plan treatment and potentially save lives. In this context, advanced image processing techniques have become vital tools in the medical field. Traditionally, the detection and diagnosis of brain tumors rely heavily on manual examination of MRI scans by specialists, which can often be time-consuming and prone to human error. To address this, our work introduces an automated system that utilize DL—specifically CNN's (CNN)—with transfer learning techniques for detecting the availability of the tumors in the brain. The model analyzes input images and predicts whether a tumor is present or not. When a tumor is identified, K-means clustering is used to localize its position within the image. The system is also designed to integrate with embedded hardware platforms for practical deployment. Using a Raspberry Pi, the tumor's location is processed, and with the help of an Arduino controller, robotic wheels can be precisely directed to the tumor's location—offering a novel step toward automation in tumor detection and treatment support. This hybrid integration of deep learning, clustering algorithms, and robotic navigation demonstrates a promising leap forward in medical technology, aiming to reduce diagnostic delays and enhance accuracy in critical care scenarios.

Document title: Multi-UAV Path Planning in Complex 3D Terrain Using Genetic-Enhanced Nutcracker Optimization
Abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly deployed in complex missions such as reconnaissance, delivery, and search operations. Effective path planning is critical for enabling UAV autonomy, especially in multi-agent scenarios involving complex terrain and operational constraints. This paper addresses the problem of collaborative path planning for multiple UAVs operating in mountainous environments. The problem is formulated as a constrained multi-objective optimization model that simultaneously considers path length, constraint violations, and trajectory smoothness. To solve this, we propose the Genetic-Enhanced Nutcracker Optimization Algorithm (GNOA), a hybrid metaheuristic that integrates genetic algorithm operators into the Nutcracker Optimization Algorithm (NOA) to improve search diversity and convergence performance. GNOA introduces a crossover-enhanced foraging strategy, a mutation-driven cachesearch recovery mechanism, and adaptive boundary constraints to ensure feasibility. Experimental results demonstrate that GNOA achieves superior performance compared to existing algorithms in generating collision-free and energy-efficient trajectories in complex three-dimensional environments.

Document title: Industrial Predictive Maintenance for Sustainable Manufacturing
Abstract:
Summary

As industries have moved towards growth, the incorporation of advanced technologies is very crucial. One of the most important benefits of these technologies is the possibility of using them for scheduling, in particular, for the prediction of failures and the optimal planning of maintenance work. This chapter focuses on the impact of predictive maintenance in a variety of industries, and its value in reducing or avoiding costly breakdowns, increasing the profitability of the business, and increasing the overall performance indicator of industrial processes. Compared with traditional strategies, predictive maintenance is a completely different approach to perform maintenance.

Condition monitoring of equipment is done continuously to check on the equipment's state and if it is operating differently from the usual state, then it is time for equipment maintenance. After a particular equipment has been identified as likely to fail in the near future, it is possible to plan the maintenance at the best time that will not interrupt the production process while at the same time making the best use of the maintenance resources available.

A comparative analysis of different research works is also done to show the efficiency of predictive maintenance in various fields. Within manufacturing, one example showed a 30% improvement of the effective use of machines by applying IoT sensors and using machine learning models to anticipate the failure of key machines. The use of predictive maintenance has been implemented in the energy sector specifically in wind turbines, where it has cut the cost of maintenance by a quarter, besides increasing the lifespan of the turbines. Automotive manufacturing has also been positively impacted as predictive maintenance has helped in detecting possible failures in robotic arms and other components; this has realized a 20% improvement in the overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) and cost savings. However, as is often the case with new methodologies, the introduction of predictive maintenance is not without its challenges.

Some challenges include high initial costs associated with the installation of IoT devices and sensors, integration of the predictive maintenance systems and architectures with the current system architecture, and the need for skilled personnel to manage as well as to analyze data from the systems. The chapter also describes the application and examples of using the predictive maintenance in practice and other industries, showing that this approach can provide tangible benefits and bring considerable improvements in companies’ performance. The automotive industry has been able to use predictive maintenance in improving the operational efficiency of production lines and minimize equipment failure.

Document title: Dual-Bubble Coordinated Acoustic Micromanipulator for Multidirectional Object Rotation*
Abstract: Micromanipulation techniques struggle to achieve three-dimensional rotational control at the microscale without compromising biocompatibility or spatial flexibility. Conventional methods based on mechanical contact, optical forces, or confined microfluidics constrain dynamic reconfiguration and surgical accessibility. Here, we introduce a dual-bubble acoustic micromanipulator that enables multidirectional rotation through controlled hydrodynamic fields. By placing oscillating microbubbles at the tips of micropipettes, this system creates adjustable vortex patterns: a single microbubble generates toroidal flows for out-of-plane rotation, while two microbubbles produce shear forces for in-plane spinning. This approach uses simple mechanical adjustments to control rotational axes in open fluid environments, without needing frequency modulation or phase synchronization. Flow-field simulations and experiments with polystyrene microspheres confirm deterministic orientation control, and tests with shrimp embryos demonstrate rotation at clinically relevant speeds. The open architecture integrates seamlessly with standard microscopy and robotic injection systems, offering a non-contact, precise tool for applications such as polar body alignment, intracellular surgery, and 3-D imaging.

Document title: VGGT-Mapping: A Mapping System for Robot Navigation based on Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
Abstract: Long-term spatial memory is critical for autonomous robotic navigation. Explicit 3D point cloud maps, as a versatile spatial memory representation, are widely used for robot localization and path planning. However, traditional mapping methods rely on expensive depth cameras or LiDAR. To address this, we propose VGGT-Mapping, a system that constructs dense 3D point cloud maps using only a monocular camera. Our work extends the capabilities of the feed-forward reconstruction model, VGGT, overcoming its bottleneck in processing long sequences and significantly enhancing global map consistency. By fusing a sparse feature map with a dense point cloud map, we create a hybrid map representation. This representation overcomes the dilemma where traditional monocular Visual SLAM maps are too sparse for planning, while maps from pure feed-forward models are difficult to use for robust localization. Extensive experiments on both public datasets and our self-collected datasets demonstrate that our proposed system exhibits superior performance over state-of-the-art methods.

Document title: Integrative AI Practices Across Disciplines: Innovations in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, and Economics Education
Abstract: This full innovative practice paper describes an interdisciplinary approach leveraging generative AI tools to enhance teaching and learning across computer science, electrical engineering, and economics education. Driven by rapid AI technology development and recognizing that traditional lectures often fail to address individualized learning gaps, educators from these disciplines implemented innovative AI practices, utilizing key tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google NotebookLM. These approaches support technical, operational, and strategic learning objectives by tailoring experiences, designing dynamic in-class activities, preparing comprehensive quiz reviews, and generating realistic scenarios that bridge theories with practical applications. In Computer Architecture, for instance, instructors utilized the POSED framework (Plan, Outline, Sources, Evaluation, Draft) to efficiently create and refine teaching materials while rapidly incorporating student feedback. At the same time, Google NotebookLM offered personalized support through lecture summarization and quiz generation. Built on prior research in AI-based tutoring and constructivist pedagogies, this framework extends traditional applications by incorporating agentic AI and personalized learning pathways. To evaluate the effectiveness of the integrated AI technology, a survey-based study revealed those integrations increased student engagement and enhanced comprehension of complex topics. However, the evaluation also indicates varied acceptance levels, with concerns regarding the optimal pacing of AI integration, the necessity for robust ethical oversight, and the ongoing challenge of maintaining a balance between AI support and instructor-led guidance. The findings offer actionable strategies for educators to align AI functionalities with pedagogical goals, providing insights into scalable, interdisciplinary AI-enhanced teaching practices. Future work will examine long-term retention and refined assessment frameworks.

Document title: Developing AI Agents for Course Planning: A Fine-Tuned LLaMA-3 Framework with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
Abstract: Higher education institutions require course leaders to continuously develop and refine academic modules to align with evolving educational standards and university guidelines. This paper presents a domain-specific AI-powered assistant developed for Teesside University that leverages a fine-tuned LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct model integrated with Retrieval-Augmented Generation and an agentic decision-making layer. The system generates policy-compliant course content using Low-Rank Adaptation and 4-bit quantisation for efficient training on limited hardware. A hybrid retrieval system combining FAISS for dense semantic search and BM25 for lexical matching grounds responses in institutional documents. Evaluation demonstrates a perplexity of 7.38, Hits@3 of $\mathbf{1. 0 0}$, cosine similarity of $\mathbf{0. 7 5 6 5}$, and hallucination rate of 0.00. Human evaluators rated outputs with an average score of 8.25 out of 10 across relevance, fluency, completeness, and organisation metrics, confirming the system's practical utility in academic planning while ensuring alignment with educational policy.

Document title: Reinforcement Learning Control for Blind Walking of Quadruped Robot in Sand Terrain
Abstract: Quadruped robots exhibit significant potential in complex scenarios such as field exploration and disaster rescue due to their exceptional terrain adaptability. However, the dynamic mechanical properties of unstructured surfaces, such as soft sand, impose limitations on the stability of robotic locomotion. Traditional model predictive control methods often struggle to accommodate real-time variations in terrain characteristics. Although research indicates that elastic legs require lower torque and provide enhanced propulsion efficiency when navigating sandy terrain, existing control strategies still face challenges in optimizing performance. Recent advancements in deep reinforcement learning have shown promise in the control of quadruped robots; however, there remains a need for separate modeling of the unique dynamic characteristics associated with sandy environments. To address this, this study employs the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm based on an asymmetric actor-critic network architecture, dynamically adjusting ground parameters in a virtual environment to reflect sandy terrain characteristics and optimizing the reward function. This approach facilitates stable traversal of sandy surfaces, thereby validating the potential of reinforcement learning in blind navigation tasks on complex soft terrains and providing valuable technical support for applications such as planetary exploration and operations on sandy substrates.

Document title: Space-air-ground Integrated Networks With Task-driven Connected Intelligence
Abstract: Space-air-ground integrated network (SAGIN) aims to offer seamless data connectivity across various vertical layers, including satellites and aeri-ai/ground/marine vehicles/ships at different altitudes. In this article, we foresee that with the rapid advancement of platforms' capabilities in sensing, computing, communication, and intelligence, traditional communication nodes will evolve into intelligent agents to facilitate task-driven functional networking across different SAGIN segments. In particular, we propose a novel task-driven multi-agent intelligent networking (MAIN) architecture for connected intelligence in SAGIN. Specifically, the intelligent agents in MAIN enjoy a high level of semantic intelligence fueled by advanced large language models with rich common and domain knowledge, which enhance the sensing, decision-making, control, and communication functions to meet the requirements of various complicated tasks and improve task-accomplishment efficiency. Furthermore, a novel intent-driven cross-domain management and control mechanism is conceived for MAIN, wherein the physical entity, communication, and mission intent domains are all managed and controlled by an intent-driven plan to comprehensively orchestrate the cross-domain functions and resources within SAGIN for specific tasks. Finally, we identify the challenges in the technical transition toward task-driven connected intelligence with MAIN. This work sheds light on task-driven multi-functional MAIN within SAGIN, highlighting the significance of semantic intelligence in the designs of task-driven networks.

Document title: Engineering Imaging Systems Using AI for Advanced Biotechnological Visualization
Abstract: The use of robotics in the medical field has been growing. But these unmanned systems lack the intelligence layer for automated diagnostics and cure. Imaging is at the core of this problem. Modern medical imaging plays a central role in diagnostics, yet each modality carries unique strengths alongside unavoidable limitations. Drawing on insights from Stanford’s Mini-Fellowship in Molecular Imaging Techniques, this study introduces FusionScan, a novel framework that unites Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Computed Tomography (CT) with an AI-driven enhancement system. The goal is to evaluate whether this combination can achieve greater depth, resolution, and functional detail by harnessing the complementary advantages of both modalities, offering a more comprehensive solution for complex diagnostic needs. The approach involves merging MRI and CT data and applying AI algorithms to refine resolution and increase molecular specificity. Particular emphasis is placed on the challenge of multimodal alignment, with strategies proposed to ensure precise registration between imaging outputs. Publicly available medical imaging datasets will serve as the testing ground for assessing how AI improves reconstruction, resolution, and adaptive adjustment of imaging parameters. An integrated feedback mechanism is also planned, allowing the system to modify scanning parameters in real time based on preliminary AI assessments. This feature is designed to minimize radiation exposure, shorten scan durations, and concentrate detail on regions requiring closer examination. Ultimately, this study envisions an equitable, autonomous imaging ecosystem that combines AI, robotics, and multimodal data fusion to make advanced diagnostics more accessible across healthcare systems worldwide. The proposed architecture demonstrates how intelligent imaging and robotic coordination can extend highperformance diagnostics beyond traditional hospital settings, aligning with global goals of healthcare equity and sustainability.

Document title: Offline-Online Mixed Trajectory and Action Planning for Multi-UAV Collaborative Sensing Over Unpredictable Points of Interest
Abstract: The rapid advancement of mobile crowd sensing (MCS) has spurred increasing adoption of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms for efficient data collection, particularly in dynamic environments with unpredictable Points of Interest (PoIs). However, most existing studies assume static PoIs, neglecting the spatio-temporal uncertainties inherent in real-world scenarios. This paper investigates multi-UAV collaborative sensing in MCS with dynamically emerging PoIs, each characterized by uncertain types, time window, locations, and rewards. We formulate a joint trajectory-action planning problem aimed at maximizing cumulative reward under energy, initial-task, and obstacle-avoidance constraints, which is characterized by NP-hardness. To address this challenge, we propose a Multi-Agent Online-Offline Hybrid Optimization (MAO ${ }^{\mathbf{2}} \mathbf{H O}$) framework. In the offline stage, a breadth-first search (BFS)-based strategy precomputes energy-efficient, collision-free paths; while in the online stage, UAV actions are replanned in real time via a net-reward-driven task allocation mechanism. Experiments with up to 40 UAVs demonstrate that MAO ${ }^{2} \text{HO}$ consistently outperforms baseline methods in terms of total reward over the whole time horizon, first-timeslot task completion rate, and detour-reward ratio.

Document title: Counter UAV Swarms: Challenges, Considerations, and Future Directions in UAV Warfare
Abstract: Modern advances in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology have widened the scope of commercial and military applications. However, the increased dependency on wireless communications exposes UAVs to potential attacks and introduces new threats, especially from UAVs designed with the malicious intent of targeting vital infrastructures. Significant efforts have been made from researchers and other United States (U.S.) Department of Defense (DoD) agencies for developing countermeasures for detection, interception, or destruction of the malicious UAVs. One promising countermeasure is the use of a counter UAV (CUAV) swarm to detect, track, and neutralize the malicious UAV. This article aims to recognize the state-of-the-art swarm intelligence algorithms for achieving cooperative capture of a mobile target UAV. The major design and implementation challenges for swarm control, algorithm architecture, and safety protocols are considered. A prime challenge for UAV swarms is a robust communication infrastructure to enable accurate data transfer between UAVs for efficient path planning. A multi-agent deep reinforcement learning approach is applied to train a group of CUAVs to intercept a faster malicious UAV, while avoiding collisions among other CUAVs and non-cooperating obstacles (i.e., other aerial objects maneuvering in the area). The impact of the latency incurred through UAV-to-UAV communications is showcased and discussed with preliminary numerical results.

Document title: Socially-Aware Robot Navigation Enhanced by Bidirectional Natural Language Conversations Using Large Language Models
Abstract: Robotic navigation plays a pivotal role in a wide range of real-world applications. While traditional navigation systems focus on efficiency and obstacle avoidance, their inability to model complex human behaviors in shared spaces has underscored the growing need for socially aware navigation. In this work, we explore a novel paradigm of socially aware robot navigation empowered by large language models (LLMs), and propose HSAC-LLM, a hybrid framework that seamlessly integrates deep reinforcement learning with the reasoning and communication capabilities of LLMs. Unlike prior approaches that passively predict pedestrian trajectories or issue pre-scripted alerts, HSAC-LLM enables bidirectional natural language interaction, allowing robots to proactively engage in dialogue with pedestrians to resolve potential conflicts and negotiate path decisions. Extensive evaluations across 2D simulations, Gazebo environments, and real-world deployments demonstrate that HSAC-LLM consistently outperforms state-of-the-art DRL baselines under our proposed socially aware navigation metric, which covers safety, efficiency, and human comfort. By bridging linguistic reasoning and interactive motion planning, our results highlight the potential of LLM-augmented agents for robust, adaptive, and human-aligned navigation in real-world settings. Project page: https://hsacllm.github.io/.

Document title: Cooperative Beam Management for Neighboring LEO Satellites Without Ground Control
Abstract: Due to the uneven spatial distribution of ground communication demands and the multi-coverage characteristics of Low Earth Orbit satellites, efficient coordination of multiple satellite beams is essential to meet heterogeneous ground requirements. Traditional methods typically rely on centralized beam planning at ground control centers, which often leads to scheduling delays and increased communication overhead, thereby limiting system responsiveness and flexibility. This paper proposes a Neighboring Satellite Beam Cooperation algorithm based on Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (NSBC-MDRL), enabling autonomous inter-satellite coordination without Ground Control Center. We model the beam cooperation problem under a full-frequency reuse scenario, aiming to maximize system throughput. To improve scheduling timeliness and avoid additional communication overhead, NSBC-MDRL adopts an architecture that combines centralized offline training with distributed onboard inference. During the inference phase, each agent independently makes decisions based on local observations and inferred behaviors of other agents, enabling implicit coordination without inter-satellite communication. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed NSBC-MDRL algorithm consistently outperforms existing benchmark methods across all evaluated scenarios.

Document title: Neuro-Adaptive Direct Inverse-Model-Based Control for Uncertain Nonaffine in the Control Systems with Prescribed Performance
Abstract: In this work, a novel neural network-based inverse model controller is introduced for uncertain Single-Input Single-Output (SISO) nonaffine in the control systems. The proposed control scheme employs an invertible neural network architecture, namely the Unconstrained Monotonic Neural Networks (UMNNs), whose parameters are updated online through a gradient adaptive law to derive the inverse dynamic model of the plant. Furthermore, the Prescribed Performance Control (PPC) technique is implemented to ensure accurate tracking despite the lack of knowledge of the system nonlinearities. A stability analysis is provided to demonstrate that the aforementioned control policy ensures tracking with predefined transient and steady-state performance, as well as bounded closed-loop signals, regardless of the parameters of the adopted approximation structure. Finally, a real-world experiment on a 1-DOF robotic manipulator validates the effectiveness of the control strategy.

Document title: Large-Scale Path Optimization using Dual-Strategy Enhanced Ant Colony Optimization Algorithm
Abstract: To address the slow convergence and local optima inherent in traditional ant colony optimization (ACO) algorithms for large-scale path optimization, this paper proposes a dualstrategy enhanced ACO algorithm (DE-2opt-ACO) that integrates differential evolution (DE) and 2-opt local search. This approach leverages the DE algorithm's mutation/crossover operations to diversify the population, enhancing global exploration before pheromone updates. Furthermore, the 2-opt algorithm is introduced to exchange path nodes, improving local exploitation efficiency. Experimental validation is conducted using a traveling salesman problem benchmark (30-90 nodes) and real-world logistics data from 161 Cainiao stations in Hengyang, China. Results demonstrate that, compared to the classic ACO algorithm, DE-2opt-ACO reduces path length by 5.2 %, iterations by 32.7 %, and significantly improves stability (lower standard deviation). This hybrid strategy effectively balances global exploration and local exploitation, providing a highly efficient optimization solution for logistics distribution, robotic path planning, and other fields.

Document title: CommonOcean-Sim: A Traffic Simulation Environment for Unmanned Surface Vessels
Abstract: Autonomous vessels have the potential to enhance maritime safety and mitigate environmental, economic, and injury risks. However, research in this domain remains limited, partly due to a lack of benchmarks and open-source tools tailored to maritime applications. The CommonOcean platform addresses this gap by providing software and traffic scenarios for motion planning research on unmanned surface vessels. In this paper, we introduce a major extension: CommonOcean-Sim, a modular simulation environment for heterogeneous multi-agent maritime traffic. CommonOcean-Sim enables configurable simulation using real-world or handcrafted safety-critical maritime scenarios, and various vessel types. Users can select controllers that ensure reactive and traffic rule compliant navigation according to the Convention on the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGS). CommonOcean-Sim features a modular architecture that allows for seamless integration of custom control algorithms as well as extensive configurability and scalability to a multitude of traffic situations, including heterogeneous high-density traffic. We demonstrate these capabilities on a variety of traffic scenarios, highlighting the potential of CommonOcean-Sim to facilitate research on autonomous vessels. CommonOcean-Sim is available at commonocean.cps.cit.tum.de/commonocean-sim.

Document title: Agentic AI Framework for Autonomous and Self-Managing Cloud Services
Abstract: The growth in cloud-native applications has made their usage hard to plan and monitor. The rule-based Kubernete execution is more active and flexible than its peers, which in itself is a challenge when the cloud is evolving in obscure ways. This is the reason behind our framework which utilizes multiple agent deep learning for needs application orchestration. It is an orchestration framework that employs Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) to permit crafted agents to optimize the method and goals simultaneously and adapt to variable parameters. We explain the components of the structure and deep learning models that focus on decision making in the framework architecture. Using a cloud cluster in a simulation, we were able to show that our approach, unlike the other orchestration systems, did greatly better in relation to resource usage, service latency, and operational resilience. This is strong evidence for the intelligent, self-managing cloud architecture we propose.

Document title: Composable Trust in Agentic AI: Bridging Architectural Capability and System-Level Assurance
Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (Agentic AI) systems have undergone a significant evolution, progressing from static predictive models to autonomous entities capable of intricate reasoning, planning, and action over extended temporal horizons. While Agentic AI demonstrates considerable utility across diverse application domains, its deployment in critical infrastructure increasingly highlights fundamental challenges concerning its trustworthiness. Current agentic architectures primarily prioritize performance and flexibility, yet they frequently lack inherent compositional guarantees for critical attributes such as safety, robustness, and accountability. In this position paper, we contend that trust in agentic AI remains largely fragmented and is predominantly established through external mechanisms rather than being intrinsically integrated into system design. We present a perspective on composable trust that bridges the gap between advanced agentic capability and dependable deployment by conceptualizing trust as a compositional property spanning agent loops, interactions, and operational environments. We further outline a roadmap toward system-level assurance by identifying structural limitations in existing architectures and defining the prerequisites for enforceable trust.

Document title: Agentic Orchestration: Evolving Team Topologies and Resource Allocation in Human-AI Hybrid Team
Abstract: The emergence of “Agentic AI” autonomous systems is changing how we manage engineering teams, as they can now plan their own work, utilize tools, and solve complex problems independently. Old automation just followed a set list of steps, but this new AI works like a 'digital teammate' that can make its own decisions as it goes. This paper examines the transition from traditional engineering management to Agentic Orchestration, a novel leadership style where humans and autonomous AI agents collaborate as a unified team. We identify three main changes: first, managers must now count both people and AI “workers” as part of their team, giving them big goals rather than small tasks. Second, while AI handles mundane tasks, it requires humans to expend more effort in reviewing the AI's work. We offer a plan to balance this, so people do not get burned out. Finally, we show how these AI bots break down walls between different departments, allowing software to be built faster and more flexibly. Overall, we provide a guide for managers to lead this new mix of human and digital teammates effectively. The paper concludes with a simple, step-by-step guide, known as the Hybrid Maturity Model (HMM). This roadmap helps managers gradually integrate AI into their teams, starting with basic bots for small tasks and progressing toward intelligent AI that functions like a full teammate. By adopting this new approach to leadership, managers can enable their teams to work significantly faster. Most importantly, this plan ensures that human engineers still feel safe, happy, and able to grow in their careers, even as AI takes on more work.

Document title: Knowledge Graph-Grounded BDI Architecture for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Orchestration in Enterprise Workflow Automation
Abstract: Enterprise decision-making increasingly relies on multi-agent systems powered by large language models (LLMs), yet these systems lack structured reasoning for traceable, auditable decisions. Although many frameworks adopt Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) terminology, surveys reveal pervasive conceptual retrofitting where beliefs, desires, and intentions serve as rhetorical labels without formal implementation. This paper introduces KG-BDI, a hybrid framework grounding BDI cognition in an enterprise knowledge graph, unifying three paradigms: BDI for structured deliberation, LLMs for flexible plan generation, and a knowledge graph for a queryable, auditable belief foundation. Factual beliefs are typed graph triples with provenance, inferred beliefs emerge from LLM-guided traversals, and episodic beliefs reside as vector embeddings. Desires are prioritized goal nodes with dependency edges; intentions are LLM-generated plans verified via three-stage pre-commitment checks. A fivephase reasoning cycle governs agent behavior, and a shared knowledge graph layer enables multi-agent coordination. Ablation across 4,998 scenarios confirms each component addresses a distinct dimension: removing the knowledge graph causes the largest accuracy drop (-0.124) with hallucination rising to 37.3%, disabling the BDI cycle collapses explainability from 0.929 to 0.286, and substituting the LLM reduces accuracy by −0.094. Fully integrated, KG-BDI achieves 0.931 accuracy, 0.965 F1, 0.929 explainability, and 8.4% hallucination, outperforming all baselines.

Document title: Agentic AI Frameworks for Autonomous Multi Agent Reasoning and Enterprise Decision Intelligence
Abstract: The evolution of artificial intelligence has enabled autonomous AI agents to reason, plan and make decisions in complex and dynamic environments. AI that behaves human-like is not a single model or a rule-based system. It is a collection of agents that collaborate to find solutions to issues that a single AI model is unable to handle. This paper discusses the development of agentic AI frameworks, their implementation, and specific instances of its use for autonomous multi-agent reasoning, especially for business decision intelligence. We assess the degree to which LLM-powered agents can solve complex issues in a way that appears natural to humans by using tools, gathering knowledge, planning, and interacting with one other. The study also looks at the advantages of these frameworks for business decision-making, such as real-time data analysis, predictive insights, workflow automation, and creating strategies that adapt to changing conditions. The study also talks about how decision intelligence may be utilized in real life in several fields of business, like monitoring the supply chain, making financial predictions, managing customer relationships, and improving operations. Agent coordination, scalability, dependability, explainability, and ethical control are all thoroughly investigated and debated. Additionally, this study offers a conceptual framework that illustrates the interactions between the many components of a multi-agent system, including perception, thinking, planning, and action. The results suggest that AI frameworks that adopt an agentic approach can considerably increase the accuracy, efficiency, and adaptability of business decisions. They also show how important it is to have good governance structures to make sure that business autonomous decision-making is reliable and clear.

Document title: Secure Orchestration and Low-Latency of Agentic Digital Twins for Industrial Intelligent Reality
Abstract: Agentic digital twins (ADTs) enhance traditional digital twins with reasoning and execution capabilities, but scaled deployment remains constrained by two coupled requirements: service-level agreements (SLAs) for response time and secure delegation of action. This short paper proposes an architecture and evaluation framework for low-latency, secure orchestration of ADTs in industrial intelligent reality environments. The architecture combines a three-layer cyber-physical stack-physical sensing and actuation, synchronization and state management, and orchestration-with two cross-cutting planes for zero-trust governance and immersive operator oversight. Deterministic multi-agent system (MAS) controllers handle routine decision making, while a large language model (LLM) orchestrator is reserved for cross-domain exceptions that require broader contextual reasoning. To bound reasoning latency, the design maps Shift Parallelism for dynamic tensor-parallelism/sequenceparallelism (TP/SP) switching and Prefix-Aware Attention (PAT) for shared-prefix-aware decoding to the industrial orchestration path. For action execution, the framework separates reasoning authority from execution authority through approval-aware security policies and an explicit end-to-end latency budget. To address the absence of plant data, a fixed-seed synthetic disturbance trace is added as a simulation-based sanity check of the latency budget. The paper therefore contributes a defined architecture, equationbased latency model, simulated latency test, and benchmark protocol for policy-governed ADT orchestration without claiming plant-scale deployment validation.

Document title: Multi-Agent AI assisted Multimodal Content Synthesis: Knowledge Sharing across Barriers
Abstract: Enabling cross-pollination of ideas across geographies can unlock new possibilities among communities. While video based knowledge exchange has proven effective within local communities, its potential for global impact remains unrealized due to barriers in language, literacy levels, and the digital divide. This paper introduces a novel Multi-Agent AI solution designed to overcome these challenges. The solution employs a set of intelligent agents that autonomously create & execute dynamic plans to re-represent complex video content into highly accessible infographic & short-video in local languages. More importantly, the intelligent system optimizes the AI generated content for cognitive load to be accessible for many personas: young semi-literate to elderly illiterate. We designed, implemented, and deployed the solution for a live demo at https://sites.google.com/view/ai-multimodal-sharingagri. The research gap addressed is the Iterative Refinement Multi-Agent AI Orchestration Design Pattern for Multimodal Content Synthesis for intelligent refinement of AI generated content to optimize for the user’s cognitive load. To address the literacy gap, our agents synthesize content that is easy to understand for farmers with varying literacy levels. Thus, the solution enables scalable, cross-lingual transfer of best practices.

Document title: Agentic Test Automation Framework for Complex Software and Database Systems
Abstract: Many organizations today work with software systems that span multiple services, data stores, and constantly changing architectures. In these environments, traditional automation frameworks often fall behind. They rely heavily on manual test design, fixed scripts, and scattered validation steps, which can leave important gaps in coverage and slow down the discovery of defects. This paper introduces an agentic test automation framework designed to address these challenges by combining large language models (LLMs) with autonomous software agents. These agents collaborate to generate, run, and validate tests across complex software and database environments. The framework brings together code understanding, API reasoning, dataflow checks, and schema aware validation to produce test plans that adapt as the system evolves. We evaluated the approach on enterprise-scale applications and observed notable improvements in defect detection, coverage, and overall testing efficiency. The findings suggest that agentic automation can support reliable end to end testing across services, workflows, data pipelines, and database layers. As a result, it offers a promising direction for teams working to modernize their quality engineering practices in cloud native and data-intensive settings.

Document title: Mininet-AI: Emulating Network Agentic AI
Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the Mininet-AI, a novel network emulation framework designed to enable experimentation with Agentic AI in networking environments. The system integrates distributed intelligent agents capable of reasoning, planning, and executing network operations based on highlevel intents. By extending the well-established Mininet emulator and its abstractions with an agentic control layer, Mininet-AI enables autonomous decision-making, continuous adaptation, and closed-loop interaction through telemetry-driven feedback. The framework lowers the barrier to experimentation and provides a reproducible platform for studying and advancing distributed, agent-driven network systems. Our initial evaluation shows that Mininet-AI can emulate Agentic-AI-driven routing behavior, achieving improved performance relative to selected classical data center routing strategies.

Document title: Beyond Single-Framework Architectures: A Systematic Evaluation and Hybrid Design for Scalable Multi-Agent Coordination
Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent frameworks have emerged as powerful tools for complex coordination tasks, yet systematic comparisons across realistic, large-scale scenarios remain limited. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of three prominent frameworks, i.e., CrewAI, AutoGen, and LangChain, alongside a novel hybrid architecture that strategically combines their complementary strengths. Using CREW-WILDFIRE, a realistic wildfire response benchmark featuring heterogeneous agents and partial observability, we evaluated the framework’s performance across 17 task levels and 7 behavioral competencies. Our results reveal distinct architectural trade-offs: CrewAI achieves 34% higher task designation scores through hierarchical coordination but lacks adaptability; AutoGen demonstrates 28% superior plan adaptation via conversational feedback, yet incurs high token costs; LangChain offers maximum flexibility at the expense of a 42% increase in computational overhead. Based on these insights, we propose and validate a hybrid LangGraph-CrewAI architecture that achieves a 96.1% success rate while reducing token consumption by 76.2% and decision latency by  $14.5\times $  compared to pure CrewAI implementations. Our comprehensive validation across 51 episodes (17 scenarios  $\times 3$  seeds) demonstrates perfect scores in task designation and agent capitalization competencies, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. This work provides evidence-based guidance for framework selection, highlights fundamental scalability challenges in current systems, and demonstrates that intelligent hybrid designs can overcome individual framework limitations while maintaining cost-efficiency.

Document title: Integrating Agentic AI and IoT for Irrigation Optimization and Farm Automation
Abstract: New developments in smart agriculture use IoT (Internet of things) systems to monitor temperature, humidity, soil moisture, CO2 concentration and air quality at any given moment but the traditional dashboards are dormant and need to be interpreted manually. This paper introduces an IoT framework powered by an Agentic AI (Artificial Intelligence) to assist with perception, reasoning, and action planning to facilitate autonomous and context-sensitive decision making. The system includes ESP32 controller platform, sensors-actuator, MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry transport) protocol, demo. Thingsboard cloud services and agentic AI workflow with a locally hosted OLLAMA (Omni-Layer Learning Language Acquisition Model) to provide inference with minimum latency. Smart agents process sensor trends, identify stress, and produce the most efficient irrigation and alerting, which leads to water efficiency and crop stability and false alarms. Findings depict a higher level of responsiveness, minimized human intervention, and a scalable base of accurate and sustainable farm management.

Document title: A Semantic Agentic AI Architecture for Context-Aware ERP Systems in Electronics Manufacturing
Abstract: Enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems in electronics manufacturing incorporate artificial intelligence (AI) for automation and prediction, yet they largely lack contextual awareness and semantic reasoning. Unlike existing AI-ERP approaches that process data without shared semantic grounding, this paper proposes a Semantic Agentic AI Framework (SAAF) that integrates ontology-based semantic representation with agentic autonomy to support semantically grounded reasoning and autonomous inter-module coordination. Central to the framework is the Semantic-Agent Reasoning Loop (SARL), which formalizes a five-stage cognitive cycle of perception, semantic representation, reasoning, action, and learning, embedding semantic interpretation at each stage unlike traditional rule-based agent loops. Within SAAF, core ERP modules including procurement, inventory management, production planning, quality control, and finance operate as autonomous semantic agents coordinated through a shared enterprise ontology. The primary contribution is a unified architectural and cognitive reference framework (SAAF + SARL) that formalizes integration of semantic computing and agentic AI within ERP systems for electronics manufacturing. Following a design-science research methodology grounded in systematic literature synthesis, the framework establishes a structured foundation for future empirical validation through simulation and controlled pilot deployments in this domain.

Document title: A Cognitive Multi-Agent System for Formula 1 Sports Analytics
Abstract: Multi-agent systems built on large language models typically coordinate through hand-crafted rules: fixed confidence thresholds trigger delegation, static affinity matrices select partners, and post-hoc verifiers discard bad outputs without informing future generation. These design choices yield systems that execute collaboration but do not learn it, limiting adaptability and making evaluation shallow. We present AgentF1, a multi-agent architecture for multilingual Formula 1 question answering that addresses three open problems. (1) Collaboration as policy learning. We cast inter-agent delegation as a contextual bandit whose reward combines Critic verification confidence, response latency, and a hallucination indicator, allowing delegation behaviour to be optimized from interaction logs rather than hand-tuned. (2) Plan-level reasoning. A hierarchical planner generates directed acyclic task graphs with explicit evidence requirements per node; a structural completeness check rejects ill-formed plans before any agent executes. (3) Closed-loop verification. A Critic-as-Teacher module feeds its confidence score back as an epistemic loss term and a calibration signal, so agents that repeatedly produce unverifiable claims are systematically corrected rather than merely overridden. We further contribute the first Arabic motorsport sentiment corpus—500 samples across Gulf, Egyptian, and Modern Standard Arabic dialects (κ=0.74). Together, these contributions shift multi-agent sports analytics from static orchestration toward adaptive, self-improving coordination.

Document title: From Generative to Agentic: A Survey of Autonomous AI Systems and Their Evolving Capabilities
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has progressed from traditional rule-based systems that were generally not very intelligent to current advanced generative models and most recently to an even newer generation of AI called Agentic AI (or autonomous AI). Unlike traditional AI that uses pre-defined prompts to perform operations, agentic AI systems have the ability to sense their surroundings, think about their objectives, create multi-step plans and take action with very little help from people. The purpose of this paper is to provide an overview of Agentic AI; focusing on how it is structured and operates, including the types of core technologies (such as large language models (LLM), reasoning systems, memory systems, and technologies that allow agentic systems to use tools) that provide the foundation for agentic AI. In addition, important applications of agentic AI are reviewed, including, but not limited to, health care, software development, education, finance and gaming. Furthermore, the paper identifies current research issues concerning reliability, safety, governance, and ethical alignment for developing trustworthy autonomous AI systems. Finally, this paper discusses future avenues of research in developing trustworthy autonomous AI systems.

Document title: Agentic AI vs Non-Agentic AI: Motivation, Security Implications, and Research Foundations
Abstract: A significant change in the development and application of artificial intelligence (AI) systems is the transition from non-agentic to agentic AI. Non-agentic AI systems, such as prompt-based language models and classical machine learning models, operate reactively, producing outputs only in response to inputs. They lack long-term memory, long-term goals, or the capacity to act independently. Agentic AI systems, on the other hand, are made to act more autonomously through goalsetting, multi-step planning, tool use, memory storage, and action execution in physical or virtual environments. This paper aims to explain the emergence of agentic AI, distinguish it from non-agentic AI, and examine the new security and governance challenges arising from this novel mode of operation. The approach used in this paper includes research about intelligent agents, large language models (LLMs) based agents, AI security, and governance frameworks. The paper also highlights how autonomous behaviour increases AI attack surface, shifts security concerns, and focuses from isolated model errors to risks involving decision-making logic, persistent memory, delegated permissions, and long-running agent behaviour. Finally, the paper argues that although agentic AI may increase the threat surface, it can be deployed responsibly provided that appropriate systemlevel safeguards are in place. This highlights the need for new or extended security and authorisation frameworks focusing specifically on agentic AI.

Document title: Agentic AI Architecture for Autonomous Customer Experience Enhancement in Digital Banking
Abstract: The research is a proposal of an Agentic AI Architecture that will be used to improve autonomous customer experience in digital banking. The planned architecture uses a Hybrid Multi-Agent System (MAS) combined with a Reinforcement Learning (RL) in order to manage customer interactions, transactions and personalized suggestions autonomously. The system relies on the distributed decision-making concept based on special agents, where each agent is trained on real-time customer data and enhances as time progresses using the TensorFlow (TF) as the basic tool. The architecture will deal with the scalability, efficiency, and personalization issues in modern banking settings. The experimental outcomes prove the presence of significant improvements, such as an increase in customer satisfaction by one quarter, an improvement in the processing efficiency by a quarter, and a decrease in operational costs by a quarter as opposed to the traditional approaches. The efficient scaling and adaptability of the system to the dynamic customer demands is another factor that demonstrates how it can transform the digital banking services, providing a streamlined customer experience, which is AI-based and cost-effective in terms of performance.

Document title: COGNIA: A Cognitive Collaboration Framework for Adaptive Decision-Making in Autonomous Embodied Intelligence
Abstract: Autonomous embodied intelligence has emerged as a promising new paradigm to enable intelligent agents to perceive, reason, and interact with dynamic environments. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs), vision-language models, and multi-agent systems have greatly improved embodied decision-making. But many current approaches work by treating perception, reasoning, memory, and cooperation separately. As an effect, the model adaptation is relatively minimal and long term planning generally unwise. To meet these challenges, we propose COGNIA, a Cognitive Collaboration Framework for Adaptive Decision-Making in Autonomous Embodied Intelligence. Combining adaptive context representation, hierarchical cognitive memory, collaborative reasoning, decision optimization, explainable action planning, and self-reflection together, the proposed framework constitutes a powerful cognitive architecture. Additionally, a new Cognitive Collaboration Score (CCS) is proposed to assess candidate decisions jointly based on contextual relevance, memory consistency, reasoning confidence, and execution feasibility, allowing firm and contextually sensitive choice of actions. This framework was previously studied across several embodied AI benchmarks, as well as benchmarking against state-of-the-art solutions (ReAct, AutoGen, MetaGPT, RT-2, PaLM-E and Voyager). Experimental data show that COGNIA achieves a Task Success Rate of 97.48%, Planning Accuracy of 97.91%, Precision of 97.62%, Recall of 97.34%, F1-score of 97.48%, and Collaboration Efficiency of 96.84%, with an average planning time of 2.91 s. Ablation and scalability analysis additionally validate the use of the proposed cognitive modules and validate the robustness and scalability of the approach for solving difficult tasks in embodied intelligence.

Document title: Agentic AI for Personalized Physiotherapy: A Multi-Agent Framework for Generative Video Training and Real-Time Pose Correction
Abstract: At-home physiotherapy compliance remains critically low due to a lack of personalized supervision and dynamic feedback. Existing digital health solutions rely on static, prerecorded video libraries or generic 3D avatars that fail to account for a patient's specific injury limitations or home environment. In this paper, we propose a novel Multi-Agent System (MAS) architecture that leverages Generative AI and computer vision to close the tele-rehabilitation loop. Our framework consists of four specialized micro-agents: a Clinical Extraction Agent that parses unstructured medical notes into kinematic constraints; a Video Synthesis Agent that utilizes foundational video generation models to create personalized, patient-specific exercise videos; a Vision Processing Agent for real-time pose estimation; and a Diagnostic Feedback Agent that issues corrective instructions. We present the system architecture, detail the prototype pipeline using Large Language Models and MediaPipe, and outline our clinical evaluation plan. This work demonstrates the feasibility of combining generative media with agentic autonomous decisionmaking to scale personalized patient care safely and effectively.
