Document title: From Rule-Based to Goal-Oriented: A Systematic Review of Agentic AI in Education
Abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence in education is rapidly shifting from reactive language models to Agentic AI—autonomous, multi-agent ecosystems capable of sustained reasoning, dynamic tool use, and long-horizon goal planning. While these systems offer new opportunities for personalized tutoring and dynamic assessment, their unchecked deployment risks prioritizing computational efficiency over genuine cognitive development. This systematic review synthesizes 53 studies (2022–2026) following PRISMA guidelines to map the current landscape of agentic educational technologies. We analyze the literature across five core domains: specialized multi-agent architectures, pedagogical applications, dynamic knowledge tracking, theoretical alignment, and new evaluation methodologies. Specifically, we scrutinize the emerging theory of Agentivism and address the long-term risks of automated cognitive offloading. A critical evaluation of prominent multi-agent systems reveals significant methodological gaps in the current state of the art, notably a widespread over-reliance on small synthetic benchmarks, unfair baseline comparisons, and a severe lack of longitudinal testing in authentic classrooms. In addition, we examine emerging socio-technical vulnerabilities, such as epistemic lock-in and the need for human-in-the-loop oversight. To address these challenges, we propose a research roadmap emphasizing the rigorous empirical validation of cognitive impacts, the development of standardized educational benchmarks, and the implementation of neuro-symbolic governance to ensure system safety. Ultimately, this review establishes a guide for the responsible and pedagogically sound development of autonomous learning companions.

Document title: Agentic AI in Healthcare: Current Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions
Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI), comprising autonomous, goal-oriented systems capable of reasoning, planning, and coordinating multi-step clinical workflows under clinician oversight, is emerging as a transformative paradigm in modern healthcare. This study presents a systematic review of its conceptual foundations, architectures, applications, challenges, and future research directions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic review of agentic AI in healthcare conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, providing researchers, clinicians, and policymakers with a structured, reproducible evidence base for this rapidly evolving field. A systematic search of the Web of Science and Scopus databases (January 2020–December 2025) identified 3,467 records, which were narrowed through multi-stage screening to 70 eligible studies. Results show that agentic AI systems are typically operationalized through four core components, namely planning, action, reflection, and memory, and are most commonly instantiated as multi-agent or supervisor/hierarchical architectures applied across diagnosis, clinical decision support, treatment planning, drug discovery, personalized care, and patient monitoring. Application maturity is concentrated in diagnosis and monitoring, where proof-of-concept and retrospectively validated systems predominate, while robotics and system-level applications remain largely conceptual; notably, no included study reported prospective clinical trial evidence or regulatory-cleared deployment. The most persistent barrier across architectures is the lack of standardized, transparent engineering reporting, compounded by unresolved ethical and regulatory gaps, data privacy concerns, algorithmic bias, limited interpretability, hallucinated outputs, and multi-agent coordination complexity. Addressing these barriers through robust governance frameworks, bias mitigation strategies, explainable architectures, and standardized validation protocols represents the field’s most urgent research priority. Overall, agentic AI signals a shift toward adaptive, clinician-supervised, and collaborative healthcare systems capable of delivering more efficient, personalized, and resilient care, contingent on systematically resolving these technical, evidentiary, and governance challenges.

Document title: Toward Human-Centered Explanations for Agentic AI: Taxonomy, Mapping, and Evaluation
Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (Agentic AI) systems differ from conventional predictive models in three structural respects that directly affect how explanations must be designed: they produce extended decision trajectories rather than isolated outputs, they invoke external tools and update persistent memory across steps, and they interact with multiple stakeholders whose explanation needs evolve over time. Existing Explainable AI (XAI) frameworks, including feature-attribution methods such as Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) and counterfactual approaches, were developed under a single-input single-output assumption that does not hold in agentic settings. This paper develops a human-centered framework for explanation in agentic AI built on four contributions. First, we propose a four-dimensional taxonomy organized along explanation need, form, timing, and stakeholder, distinguishing explanations as interaction artifacts from explainability as a system property. Second, we introduce an Explanation-to-Agentic-Stage Mapping that aligns the four dimensions with six stages of the agentic lifecycle, namely goal formulation, planning, action execution, tool use, memory update, and reflection, and identifies which existing XAI methods remain applicable, which require adaptation, and which fail at each stage. Third, we identify humancentered design requirements, namely stakeholder adaptation, adaptive timing, cognitive load management, interactivity, and auditability, from the gap between agentic decision structure and current explanation practice. Fourth, we propose a multi-layer evaluation framework that complements faithfulness metrics with interaction outcomes, including trust calibration, mental model alignment, and longitudinal collaboration performance. Together, these contributions reframe explanation design for agentic AI from a model-centric transparency problem to an interaction design problem, and surface three open challenges, namely the fluency-faithfulness gap, longitudinal evaluation methodology, and the absence of agentic explanation benchmarks, as priorities for future research.

Document title: NeuraDesk: An Agentic AI Powered Personal Digitalworkspace
Abstract: People today manage their finances, health, nutrition, routines, and personal knowledge across many separate apps, leading to scattered decisions, repeated effort, and weak long-term planning. NeuraDesk solves this by offering a unified multi-agent AI system that analyzes a user's daily life, syncs context across domains, and takes proactive actions without manual input. Its intelligent agents-covering finance, nutrition, fitness, lifestyle, and notes-learn user patterns and adapt plans automatically. The system's uniqueness comes from true agentic automation, including auto-budgeting, portfolio rebalancing, meal plans from groceries, injury-safe workouts, personalized routines, automatic transaction categorization, and weekly AI life reviews powered by cross-agent reasoning. NeuraDesk acts as a personal life operating system that lowers cognitive load, strengthens decision-making, and builds a continuously evolving roadmap for healthier, more productive living. It demonstrates how coordinated autonomous agents can transform everyday life management into an intelligent, self-optimizing experience.

Document title: SOULSYNC: An AI-Driven Emotional and Cognitive Support System for Alzheimer's Care
Abstract: Alzheimer disease is a progressive disorder that affects memory, cognition, and emotional stability hence increasing care giver dependency and lowering the quality of life. The majority of available mobile health apps are based on the principle of reminders and schedule planning, without emotional and cognitive support. This paper suggests SOULSYNC, an AI-based mobile emotion assistant that would improve both cognitive and emotional health of patients with Alzheimer disease. The system operates offline-first architecture in which patient information such as reminders, mood data, memory content, and activity log are stored locally with the help of SQLite and updated with the cloud backend when the network connection is present. The analysis of emotion trends and routine patterns are applied to create individualized interventions including music therapy, cognitive games, and relaxing activities. A caregiver-related feature is a source of real-time notifications, emergency messages, and health-related information to maintain constant assistance. The flow application encompasses secure authentication, dashboardbased interaction, emotive tracking, cognitive interaction and intelligent feedback.

Document title: Adaptive Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Models for Financial Question Answering
Abstract: In the future, the introduction of agentic AI (which is an improved form of AI that can reason, plan, and make decisions that change based on what happens) will change how we do business in the financial markets. This report will put together recent progress in agentic AI into different groups. It will cover algorithmic and automated trading systems, as well as AI-generated responses. This report looks at and talks about some important agentic AI traits, such as the ability to set and achieve goals on its own, the ability to learn new things all the time, and the ability to coordinate interactions between different agentic AI systems. Furthermore, evidence indicates that agentic AI can markedly enhance the efficiency and liquidity of financial markets while concurrently improving the overarching management challenges encountered by financial institutions. To furnish the research community and practitioners with a thorough, meticulously researched, and structured methodology for the analysis of agentic AI and its ramifications on the financial markets, a systematic and extensive assessment of the pertinent existing literature, technical infrastructures, and financial market applications/governance frameworks has been conducted to elucidate the implications of agentic AI on the financial markets. This evaluation also points out and lists other research, investigation, and funding opportunities that will make financial markets run more smoothly and be more resilient thanks to the benefits of agentic AI.

Document title: Agentic AI in Wind Energy Systems: Multi-Agent Architectures for Optimization and Resilience
Abstract: The rapid rise of wind energy introduces persistent challenges related to variability, control, and operational reliability. While traditional machine learning supports forecasting and optimization, its scope is narrow and typically operator-dependent. We propose an agentic AI paradigm in which autonomous, goal-directed agents interact with turbines, the wind farm, and the grid to manage complexity in real time. A multi-agent architecture coordinates turbine-, farm-, and grid-level decisions to enhance efficiency and resilience. We present three concise case studies illustrating optimization at complementary scales: Case 1 (turbine-level) an AI agent adjusts upstream derating setpoints to mitigate wake effects and increase overall farm power production, at the cost of reduced power from the derated turbines; Case 2 (farm-level) a coordinating agent aligns multiple turbines to meet plant-wide energy and reliability objectives under operational and environmental constraints; Case 3 (grid-level) a system agent balances wind with other generators and consumer demand while honoring transmission limits and minimizing cost. Together, these cases show how local actions and global coordination increase energy yield, reduce structural loading, and improve reliability. Applications span adaptive forecasting, wake management, predictive maintenance, market participation, and cyber-physical security. We outline research needs in data quality, interoperability, safety, and regulation, and advocate hybrid designs that fuse reinforcement learning with digital twins to advance intelligent wind infrastructures.

Document title: Multi-Agent Architecture for Decision Support Systems in Agricultural Data Analysis
Abstract: Automated multi-step analysis over tabular crop-phase datasets demands systems that plan tasks, invoke tools, and reason adaptively—capabilities that static-workflow decision support systems cannot provide. This paper presents a multi-agent architecture for an AI-Powered Decision Support System (DSS) applied to paddy agricultural data analysis. The proposed system combines a web-based analytical dashboard with an orchestrator–router multi-agent architecture supporting structured task planning, dynamic tool invocation, and natural language interaction through five specialized sub-agents. A dual-layer Guardrails mechanism enforces input-stage prompt injection prevention and output-stage consistency. We evaluate the system using Task Completion Rate (TCR), Automation Rate (AR), Error Rate (ER), and System Usability Scale (SUS) across six functional modules comprising 65 TCR items, 30 AR items, and 30 ER items. The proposed system achieves TCR of 94.6%, AR of 86.7%, ER of 6.7%, and SUS of 88.9 (Excellent), showing higher performance than two directional baselines: a rule-based DSS (TCR: 62.0%, AR: 54.0%) and a tool-free LLM system (TCR: 74.0%, AR: 61.0%). These results confirm that orchestrated multi-agent specialization with integrated Guardrails improves both analytical task execution and automation coverage in agricultural decision support.

Document title: Demonstration of Centralized Multi-Agentic AI for Telecom Network Operation
Abstract: The evolution towards autonomous networking requires intent-based management. The application of agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) to network control and management facilitates such evolution as it enables to respond to user intents by breaking down complex tasks and taking independent actions using tools. In this demonstration, we showcase a centralized multi-agentic AI control plane for autonomous telecom network operation. The proposed architecture combines a Multi-Agent System (MAS) and an on-premises Large Language Model (LLM). Network tools and traditional control are integrated to ensure determinism and explainability to operational decision making. A workflow for packet connectivity provisioning is used to illustrate how natural-language operator intents are translated into network configuration actions.

Document title: A Dual-Roofline Runtime Model for Capacity Planning in Shared-Backend LLM Multi-Agent Social Simulation: A Case Study of AgentSociety
Abstract: LLM-based multi-agent social simulations are jointly shaped by message frequency, cognitive inference, and shared-backend queueing, yet still lack interpretable runtime models. Using AgentSociety’s fixed-step social simulation as a case study, we model the average step time of a complete run with a dual-Roofline formulation: the cognitive phase and the message phase are treated as two resource-bounded regions sharing one vLLM backend, and the saturation point of each phase is determined by the per-GPU token budget divided by the measured average prompt length. Call-level traces and source-code inspection show that the message-dispatch stage is not pure routing but includes message-triggered LLM decisions. Ray scheduling remains at only 1.8–2.4ms, whereas mean vLLM service time rises from 0.30s to 1.63s as the agent count grows from 5 to 500, confirming that shared inference throughput and cross-phase queueing are the dominant bottlenecks. We therefore decompose total step time into environment overhead, a cognitive Roofline, a message Roofline, and a cross-phase queueing term. Compared with a linear model, a single Roofline, and a dual Roofline without queueing, the full model reduces mean absolute error from 8.6%, 2.4%, and 1.2% to 0.7%. Across eight scale points spanning 4 to 500 agents, the model achieves R2 =0.9999 and reveals three regimes: compute-bound, message-saturated, and fully saturated with cross-phase queueing. It further yields two practical capacity-planning rules: at large scale, message frequency should be the first control lever; for the 500-agent setting, about 10 replicas remove superlinear growth and about 27 replicas recover an almost constant-step regime. These results show that analytic performance modeling can bridge the gap between large-scale LLM multi-agent simulation and practical infrastructure capacity planning, contributing to the systems foundation of intelligent social computing.

Document title: An Agentic Risk-Aware QA Framework for Smart Elderly Care
Abstract: Smart elderly care demands safe, personalized, and privacy-preserving decision support under dynamic health conditions. However, conventional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems remain similarity-driven and lack risk-aware reasoning and controllable action planning. We propose an agentic risk-aware Question Answering (QA) framework that integrates multi-modal data encoding, risk-aware context optimization, and agentic task planning into a closed-loop decision architecture. Multi-source elderly care data are aligned into a unified knowledge substrate, from which an optimized reasoning context is selected via relevance-risk balancing. An agentic policy then generates structured, priority-aware task plans that are executed through external tools, while long-term memory is continuously updated to enable adaptive behavior. The proposed framework enhances interpretability, safety, and personalization in elderly care scenarios, providing a structured and controllable alternative to purely generative RAG systems.

Document title: Position: Cross-Layer Co-Design Is Necessary to Safely Deploy Agentic AI in Real-Time Systems
Abstract: This position paper argues that recent advances in agentic AI, particularly Large Language Model (LLM) systems capable of planning and tool use, enable new forms of autonomy in real-time (RT) cyber-physical systems where high-level reasoning interacts with real-time decision-making. We observe that integrating such probabilistic AI workloads with deterministic RT execution introduces a fundamental temporal mismatch. We delineate two convergence modes: isolation of agentic workloads from RT tasks on shared platforms, and integration of agentic AI into time-sensitive decision loops. For each, we identify representative applications, outline challenges such as resource contention and temporal unpredictability, and survey emerging solutions. We conclude that safe deployment requires cross-layer co-design, including new timing models, time-aware agentic frameworks, and certification methodologies capable of reasoning about probabilistic execution behavior.

Document title: AgenticNav: A Hierarchical Multi-Agentic System for LLM-Driven Autonomous Problem-Solving in Robotics
Abstract: A primary challenge in autonomous robotics is bridging the semantic-execution gap in environments where pre-defined plans fail. This paper presents AgenticNav, a cognitive architecture that achieves autonomous problem-solving through a hierarchical Multi-Agentic System (MAS) orchestrated by a Large Language Model (LLM). Within this framework, specialized agents handle environmental perception and task execution, while a stateful agentic hierarchy facilitates failure detection and strategic recovery. When an environmental impasse is encountered, the hierarchical mechanism isolates high-level reasoning from low-level execution and escalates the execution failure to a strategic level where the LLM re-evaluates the environment’s topological structure to autonomously generate a viable alternative route. Validated in both a high-fidelity simulation and on a physical robot, the system demonstrates the ability to move beyond rigid instruction-following toward greater goal-oriented autonomy. Our results show evidence that the MAS framework effectively facilitates real-time, reason-based replanning, allowing robots to autonomously resolve complex execution failures in unpredictable real-world settings. The comprehensive evaluation data are available at https://github.com/AgenticNav/mas-llm-robotics-eval

Document title: Edgent: Towards an Agentic AI Framework for eBPF-Based Service Deployment and Orchestration at the Edge
Abstract: The evolution towards 6G edge-cloud ecosystems demands autonomous, intent-based network management to handle unprecedented infrastructure complexity. While Large Language Models offer promising capabilities for translating high-level user intents into network configurations, current monolithic approaches suffer from cognitive overload, hallucinations, and a profound inability to safely execute low-level data plane mutations. To bridge this gap, we introduce Edgent, a novel framework that integrates hierarchical Agentic AI with Extended Berkeley Packet Filter technologies via the Model Context Protocol. Edgent utilizes a state-driven Supervisor, enhanced by Retrieval-Augmented Generation, to decompose abstract human intents into deterministic execution graphs and dynamically delegate tasks to domain-specific worker agents. We empirically validate the framework by autonomously deploying a distributed, in-kernel DDoS mitigation pipeline across scaled containerized topologies containing up to 85 nodes. Extensive evaluations demonstrate high orchestration reliability; notably, even heavily quantized Small Language Models (e.g., 4B parameters) achieve near-perfect zero-shot execution and 100% overall task completion through autonomous error recovery. Finally, latency and resource profiling confirm that the multi-agent framework can be efficiently driven by fully localized models compatible with orchestration tasks directly within resource-constrained edge environments, therefore this work positions Edgent as a pragmatic step toward the realization of zero-touch nextgeneration networks.

Document title: Cognitive OS Agents: A Safe, Explainable, and Autonomous Architecture for Planning, Learning, and Acting at the Operating System Level
Abstract: Conventional operating systems operate as deterministic execution platforms and rely on explicit user commands, providing limited support for autonomous reasoning or adaptation. Although recent automation frameworks and virtual assistants improve usability, they remain reactive and fragile in dynamic task environments. This paper presents Cognitive OS Agents, a safety-aware and explainable architecture that embeds autonomous planning, learning, and reasoning directly into the operating system layer. The proposed system combines a cognitive core for figuring out goals, hybrid task planning that uses symbolic reasoning and big language models, episodic and semantic memory for long-term adaptation, and an explainability layer that makes decision traces that people can understand. A permission-based safety framework with sandboxed execution and rollback features makes sure that everything works as it is. Evaluation on standard OS automation benchmarks shows that the proposed agent improves task success rates by up to 14%, increases failure recovery by over 20%, and achieves higher user trust scores compared to existing OS-level agents, while maintaining acceptable execution latency.

Document title: Explainable Agentic AI: Concepts, Scope, and Research Questions
Abstract: The emergence of agentic artificial intelligence (agentic AI) which is capable of autonomous planning, reasoning, tool use, and adaptive decision-making has introduced new challenges for explainability beyond those addressed by traditional explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). Unlike conventional predictive models that focus on isolated input–output mappings, agentic AI operates through temporally extended decision trajectories involving goals, memory, external tools, and iterative reflection. This paper examines the conceptual foundations of explainable agentic AI and argues that existing XAI methods are insufficient for capturing the complexity of autonomous, process-oriented behavior. Through an exploratory literature review, we analyze how current approaches attempt to extend traditional XAI techniques to agentic systems and identify their methodological limitations. The paper structures the discussion around four core research questions: why agentic AI needs to be explainable, what should be explained, when explanations should be generated, and how explanations can be produced. Particular attention is given to the notion of faithfulness, namely whether explanations accurately reflect the underlying decision process rather than merely providing plausible post-hoc rationalizations. We argue that explainable agentic AI should be understood not as a simple extension of existing XAI paradigms, but as a distinct explanatory framework centered on process-level reasoning, causal correspondence, and trajectory-based accountability. Finally, we discuss open challenges including explanation evaluation, causal attribution across heterogeneous components, observer effects in self-explanatory systems, and compositional explanation pipelines. The paper concludes that explainability must become a foundational property of future agentic AI systems to ensure transparency, trustworthiness, safety, and effective human–AI collaboration.

Document title: Agentic RAG for Structure Aware Long Document Reasoning
Abstract: Graph-based and multimodal retrieval frameworks provide a strong foundation for long-document question answering, but single-pass retrieval can remain brittle when queries are ambiguous, multi-step, or misaligned with the indexed evidence. We present Agentic-RAG, a structure-aware retrieval-augmented generation framework that combines a MinerU-LightRAG-based document processing and graph retrieval pipeline with an LLM-based agentic query-control layer. The base pipeline supports structure-aware parsing and VLM-based captioning for textual, visual, and tabular evidence, while the agentic layer performs query planning, LLM-based evidence reranking, answer generation, groundedness checking, relevance checking, and query reformulation. The framework does not modify the underlying graph construction or indexing mechanism; instead, it improves retrieval control by guiding the base retriever toward evidence that better matches the user's information need. Experiments on HotpotQA and ASQA show that Agentic-RAG improves context precision on HotpotQA from 0.1682 to 0.2462 and substantially improves context precision and context recall on ASQA from 0.5045/0.2783 to 0.6522/0.4783. The results indicate that agentic query control is especially useful for ambiguity-heavy long-form reasoning, while sparse multi-hop evidence chaining remains a bottleneck for future work.

Document title: CyberJustice Tutor: An Agentic AI Framework for Cybersecurity Learning via Think–Plan–Act Reasoning and Pedagogical Scaffolding
Abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into cybersecurity education for criminal justice professionals is currently hindered by the "statelessness" of reactive chatbots and the risk of hallucinations in high-stakes legal contexts. To address these limitations, we propose the CyberJustice Tutor, an educational dialogue system powered by an Agentic AI framework. Unlike reactive chatbots, our system employs a "Think–Plan–Act" cognitive cycle, enabling autonomous goal decomposition, longitudinal planning, and dynamic context maintenance. We integrate a Pedagogical Scaffolding Layer grounded in Vygotsky’s Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD), which dynamically adapts instructional support based on the learner’s real-time progress. Furthermore, an Adaptive Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) core anchors the agent’s reasoning in verified curriculum materials to ensure legal and technical accuracy. A comprehensive user study with 123 participants, including students, educators, and active law enforcement officers, validated the system’s efficacy. Quantitative results demonstrate high user acceptance for Response Speed (4.7/5), Ease of Use (4.4/5), and Accuracy (4.3/5). Qualitative feedback indicates that the agentic architecture is perceived as highly effective in guiding learners through personalized paths, demonstrating the feasibility and usability of agentic AI for specialized professional education.

Document title: Human Society-Inspired Approaches to Agentic AI Security: The 4C Framework
Abstract: AI is moving from domain-specific autonomy in closed, predictable settings to large-language-model-driven agents that plan and act in open, cross-organizational environments. As a result, the cybersecurity risk landscape is changing in fundamental ways. Agentic AI systems can plan, act, collaborate, and persist over time. It is now functioning as participants in complex socio-technical ecosystems rather than as isolated software components. Although recent work has strengthened defenses against model and pipeline level vulnerabilities such as prompt injection, data poisoning, and tool misuse, these system-centric approaches may fail to capture risks that arise from autonomy, interaction, and emergent behavior. This article introduces the “4C Framework” for multi-agent AI security, inspired by societal governance. Our 4C Framework organizes agentic risks across four interdependent dimensions: Core (system, infrastructure, and environmental integrity), Connection (communication, coordination, and trust), Cognition (belief, goal, and reasoning integrity), and Compliance (ethical, legal, and institutional governance). Our 4C Framework shifts AI security from a narrow focus on system-centric protection to the broader preservation of behavioral integrity and intent. It complements existing AI security strategies and offers a principled foundation for building agentic AI systems that are trustworthy, governable, and aligned with human values.

Document title: Edge General Intelligence Through World Models, Large Language Models, and Agentic AI: Fundamentals, Solutions, and Challenges
Abstract: Edge General Intelligence (EGI) represents a transformative evolution of edge computing, where distributed agents possess the capability to perceive, reason, and act autonomously across diverse, dynamic environments. This vision is increasingly realized through agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems, which often leverage large language models (LLMs) for complex reasoning and planning. However, language-based reasoning alone struggles to capture high-dimensional physical dynamics. Central to overcoming this challenge are world models, which act as proactive internal simulators that not only predict but also actively imagine future trajectories, reason under uncertainty, and plan multi-step actions with foresight. This proactive nature allows agents to anticipate potential outcomes and optimize decisions ahead of real-world interactions. While prior works in robotics and gaming have showcased the potential of world models, their integration into the wireless edge for EGI remains underexplored. This survey bridges this gap by offering a comprehensive analysis of how world models can empower agentic systems at the edge, enhancing their foresight beyond the limits of LLM-based reasoning. We first examine the architectural foundations of world models, including latent representation learning, dynamics modeling, and imagination-based planning. Building on these core capabilities, we illustrate their proactive applications across EGI scenarios such as vehicular networks, uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) networks, the Internet of Things (IoT) systems, and network functions virtualization, thereby highlighting how they can enhance optimization under latency, energy, and privacy constraints. We then explore their synergy with foundation models and digital twins, positioning world models as the cognitive backbone of EGI. Finally, we highlight open challenges, such as safety guarantees, efficient training, and constrained deployment, and outline future research directions. This survey provides both a conceptual foundation and a practical roadmap for realizing the next generation of intelligent, autonomous edge systems.

Document title: Cognitive Enterprise Architecture: Extending the Business Motivation Model through Temporal Knowledge Graphs and Agentic AI for Dynamic Strategic Alignment
Abstract: In contemporary business environments, achieving sustainable organizational agility remains challenging due to a persistent gap between strategic intent and technical implementation. Traditional enterprise architecture frameworks, including the Business Motivation Model (BMM), provide standardized vocabularies for documenting strategic directions; however, they remain predominantly static and descriptive rather than operational. This research introduces the Cognitive BMM, an extension of the Object Management Group's Business Motivation Model that integrates temporal knowledge graphs and artificial intelligence to enable adaptive enterprise architecture capable of dynamic strategic alignment. The proposed framework extends the BMM with a temporal dimension that enables recording validity periods for objectives, capabilities, and IT resources, ensuring that decisions are predicated upon current business facts. Upon this temporal foundation, we superimpose agentic AI capabilities through a multi-layered architecture comprising: (i) a memory layer implemented as a temporal knowledge graph; (ii) a reasoning layer employing large language models; and (iii) a planning layer that decomposes strategic objectives into actionable tactics. To address limitations of standard RAG systems, we introduce corrective retrieval strategies that evaluate document relevance. Through responsibility-based alignment formalization and multi-agent systems representing organizational hierarchy, Cognitive BMM transforms business-IT alignment from a periodic planning exercise into a continuous, self-correcting system.

Document title: DUPLEX: Agentic Dual-System Planning via LLM-Driven Information Extraction
Abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) provide semantic flexibility for robotic task planning, their susceptibility to hallucination and logical inconsistency limits their reliability in long-horizon domains. To bridge the gap between unstructured environments and rigorous plan synthesis, we propose DUPLEX, an agentic dual-system neuro-symbolic architecture that strictly confines the LLM to schema-guided information extraction rather than end-to-end planning or code generation. In our framework, a feed-forward Fast System utilizes a lightweight LLM to extract entities, relations etc. from natural language, deterministically mapping them into a Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) problem file for a classical symbolic planner. To resolve complex or underspecified scenarios, a Slow System is activated exclusively upon planning failure, leveraging solver diagnostics to drive a high-capacity LLM in iterative reflection and repair. Extensive evaluations across 12 classical and household planning domains demonstrate that DUPLEX significantly outperforms existing end-to-end and hybrid LLM baselines in both success rate and reliability. These results confirm that The key is not to make the LLM plan better, but to restrict the LLM to the part it is good at—structured semantic grounding—and leave logical plan synthesis to a symbolic planner.

Document title: Harness Engineering for Multi-Agent Data Visualization with Small Language Models
Abstract: Turning a natural-language question into a correct, publication-ready data visualization usually takes several rounds of coding, inspection, and debugging. Large language models can draft plotting code, but a single-shot model call has no way to run the code, look at the resulting image, recover from execution errors, or decide whether the chart actually answers the user. We demonstrate a visualization harness: an engineered scaffold that wraps a team of seven specialized agents in a bounded Plan–Execute–Verify–Refine control loop. The harness, not any single model, supplies the capabilities that make the system reliable—a sandboxed execution environment with timeouts, vision-based verification of the rendered PNG, error-driven routing between re-planning, re-coding and debugging, per-agent model assignment, and persistent run state for resume and reproducibility. Because the harness owns reliability, the underlying models can be small: a hybrid configuration that runs four agents on local small language models (3–8B) and routes only the three failure-prone agents to inexpensive cloud models reaches a 100% verification pass rate across five heterogeneous datasets at roughly one-third the cost of an all-cloud baseline. The live demo, built on a lightweight FastAPI web UI, lets attendees upload a dataset, type a query, and watch agent steps and intermediate charts stream in real time over Server-Sent Events until a verified visualization appears.

Document title: AgriTwin: A Multi-Agent Digital Twin Framework with Deep Reinforcement Learning for Resource-Aware Precision Agriculture
Abstract: This study introduces AgriTwin, a resource-aware digital twin framework for precision agriculture that integrates a layered Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructure, a belief–desire–intention (BDI) multi-agent system, ensemble machine learning, and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for adaptive irrigation management. The architecture combines Edge, Fog, Cloud, and Mobile layers to enable real-time sensing, communication, and decision-making. A multi-agent system coordinates monitoring, prediction, and actuation tasks, whereas a physics-based digital twin model simulates soil–water–plant dynamics using a Hargreaves-based reference evapotranspiration estimate (a FAO-56–recommended method for conditions with limited weather-sensor data) and water balance equations. Crop health was estimated using an ensemble regression model combining Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, and LightGBM. Irrigation scheduling was optimized using a Deep Q-Network (DQN) policy trained using a digital twin simulation environment. Experimental evaluation using a public agricultural dataset and prototype deployment on 20 microgreen containers demonstrated promising monitoring accuracy and simulated water savings, highlighting the potential of AgriTwin as a proof-of-concept framework for autonomous, resource-aware precision agriculture. However, its small-scale validation necessitates broader field trials to confirm its real-world scalability and performance.

Document title: From Prompts to Pavement Through Time: Temporal Grounding in Agentic Scene-to-Plan Reasoning
Abstract: Recent attempts to support high-level scene interpretation and planning in Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) using ensembles of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) continue to treat time as a secondary property. This lack of temporal grounding leads to inconsistencies in reasoning about continuous actions, undermining both safety and interpretability. This work explores whether temporal conditioning within inter-agent communication can preserve or enhance coherence without introducing degradation in semantic or logical consistency. To investigate this, we introduce three planner architectures with progressively increasing temporal integration and evaluate them on curated subsets of the BDDX dataset using semantic, syntactic, and logical metrics. Results show that while temporal conditioning reshapes reasoning style, it yields no statistically significant improvements in standard NLP-based correctness metrics. However, qualitative analysis reveals predictive hazard reasoning, stable corrective behavior, and strategic divergence in the Sentinel. These findings clarify the limits of prompt-based temporal grounding and establish the first empirical benchmark for temporal scene-to-plan reasoning.

Document title: Distributed Agentic AI Framework for Autonomous Edge-Cloud Service Orchestration
Abstract: Orchestrating services across heterogeneous 6G edge-cloud infrastructures requires autonomous coordination systems managing distributed computational resources while satisfying Quality-of-Service (QoS) requirements. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) enable development of autonomous agents capable of complex reasoning and decision-making for such orchestration tasks. However, applying generic agentic AI frameworks from the machine learning literature to orchestration domains introduces reliability limitations, as trial-and-error decision patterns are unsuitable for environments where errors disrupt services. This work presents AgentEdge, a novel distributed intelligence framework that implements specialized autonomous agents in four orchestration roles: intent processing, infrastructure monitoring, strategic planning, and action execution. AgentEdge introduces the PARES (Perceive, Act, Reason, Evaluate, Sustain) framework establishing minimum capabilities required for autonomous agent qualification. Central to AgentEdge is the ActSimCrit (Action-Simulation-Critic) planning methodology, which validates orchestration plans through digital twin simulation before execution, eliminating direct infrastructure experimentation risks. Agents coordinate multi-step operations and adapt strategies based on constraint feedback. Structured outputs constrain agent decision spaces to feasible orchestration actions while preserving optimization flexibility. Experimental evaluation in six orchestration scenarios validates AgentEdge through comparison with baseline agentic frameworks and ablation studies. AgentEdge achieves  $2.76\times $  higher success rate compared to generic agentic frameworks (ReAct, LATS) and  $10\times $  reduction in API call variability. The core ActSimCrit digital twin component alone contributes  $1.47\times $  success improvement when compared to direct planning without simulation. AgentEdge achieves significant power savings across infrastructure scales from 8 to 35 nodes.

Document title: Integrating Predictive Sampling and Diffusion Policy for Adaptive Control in Simulated Robotic Arms
Abstract: This paper presents a hybrid control approach that combines Predictive Sampling and Diffusion Policy to achieve smooth and adaptive motion in robotic arms. Traditional control systems such as PID and Model Predictive Control provide stability but have limited adaptability under uncertain or changing conditions. In contrast, diffusion models can generate smooth control actions but do not ensure physical consistency. In the proposed method, Predictive Sampling is used to plan short term control actions based on the robot dynamics, while the Diffusion Policy refines these actions through a learning based denoising process. The system is implemented on a 2R robotic arm using the MuJoCo simulator with Python and PyTorch. Experimental results show that the hybrid controller produces smoother trajectories, reduces torque noise, and improves overall motion stability when compared to conventional control methods. The results demonstrate how combining model based and data driven techniques can enhance adaptive control in robotic systems.

Document title: Agentic Digital Twins for Urban Traffic Control: A Reasoning-Validation Framework for Autonomous Systems
Abstract: Urban Traffic Control (UTC) faces challenges with congestion and complex intersection coordination. Many existing Digital Twins act as passive Digital Shadows, mirroring data without autonomous intervention, which limits safety and explainability. This paper presents an Agentic Digital Twin framework that integrates AI agents with an Agentic Reasoning Layer (Perception, Planning, Memory, Tool Use) and a synchronized simulation environment, enabling strategies to be tested virtually before deployment. A key contribution is the Validation and Control Layer, which validates candidate strategies in Shadow Mode before deployment. A rule-based prototype was implemented in SUMO and demonstrated the framework outperforms a fixed-time baseline, achieving an 18.4% reduction in mean queue length and an 89.2% reduction in mean waiting time, while improving safety and reliability through validated, transparent decision-making in urban traffic management.

Document title: Developing Agentic AI Systems with Ethical Integrity and Reliable Deployment
Abstract: Agentic AI systems are autonomous, goal-directed artificial intelligence agents capable of reasoning, planning, and acting in dynamic environments. As these systems become increasingly integrated into critical domains such as healthcare, finance, governance, and industrial automation, ensuring ethical integrity and reliable deployment is paramount. This article provides a comprehensive review of agentic AI architectures, highlighting various models ranging from rule-based and multiagent systems to reinforcement learning and hybrid frameworks. Ethical considerations, including fairness, transparency, privacy, and value alignment, are analyzed in the context of real-world applications. Deployment strategies emphasizing robustness, scalability, security, and continuous monitoring are discussed to ensure that agentic AI systems operate safely and effectively in practical environments. The paper concludes with future research directions to advance the development of trustworthy and responsible agentic AI systems, bridging technical innovation with societal impact.

Document title: Engineering Guided Determinism in Neuro-Symbolic Agents: A Comparative Study of Orchestration Strategies for Supply Chain Replenishment
Abstract: Mission-critical enterprise domains demand AI systems that are not merely reactive interpreters of user prompts, but proactive agents capable of planning, constrained reasoning, and reliable execution. While large language models (LLMs) enable flexible natural language interaction, their stochastic behavior introduces unacceptable risk in high-stakes workflows such as supply chain replenishment. This paper presents an agentic neuro-symbolic architecture for engineering Guided Determinism, enabling the transition from reactive natural language interfaces to proactive agentic decision support systems. The proposed framework adopts a dual-layer Classifier-Planner design with an Intent-Aware Reasoning Scheduler, decoupling intent recognition, symbolic planning, and executable action through a governed semantic layer. Five agent orchestration strategies are systematically evaluated within this architecture, ranging from neural-only to tool-augmented agents with redundant symbolic enforcement. An empirical study over realistic replenishment queries quantifies the trade-off between execution accuracy, computational cost, and latency, revealing a clear Pareto frontier. Results demonstrate that fully autonomous agents require strict symbolic grounding to achieve 100% execution reliability, while tool-augmented agents offer a cost-efficient alternative, with a 90.2% reduction in token consumption, for human-in-the-loop analytics. The study further identifies an Evaluator Paradox, showing that recursive neural self-correction degrades reliability in structured decision tasks. These findings provide actionable engineering guidance for deploying reliable agentic AI in realworld enterprise systems.

Document title: Agentic AI for Autonomous Decision-Making in Large-Scale Distributed Systems: Patch Orchestration for Critical Infrastructure
Abstract: Maintaining software patches is essential for the security and reliability of modern distributed systems, especially in infrastructure environments that rely on geographically dispersed endpoints. Traditional patch management approaches use static rollout policies and reactive failure handling, which can increase operational risk at scale. This paper proposes a bounded agentic AI framework for autonomous patch orchestration in large-scale distributed systems. The framework combines patch impact analysis, environment-state assessment, digital-twin-based simulation, policy-constrained multi-objective risk scoring, phased deployment, and adaptive feedback. Candidate rollout strategies are evaluated before execution, and deployment decisions are refined using telemetry from prior rollout stages. A scenario-driven simulation over 1,000–5,000 endpoints compares the proposed framework with a rule-based static rollout baseline. Under representative simulation assumptions, the results indicate potential reductions of 81% in rollout planning time from 4.0 hours to 0.75 hours, 46% in critical patch MTTR from 26 hours to 14 hours, 43% in rollback rate from 6.8% to 3.9%, and 71% in network transfer from 14.4 TB to 4.2 TB per cycle. The main contribution is a decision-oriented architecture that integrates agentic planning, digital twin validation, and closed-loop adaptation for safer patch orchestration in critical distributed infrastructure.

Document title: AGRINERVE: React-Based Neural Multi-Agent Systems for Smart Vineyard Health
Abstract: Crop health observation has been revolutionized by the integration of artificial intelligence and precision agriculture, especially in vineyard cultivation, where disease identification is critical for maximizing grape production. AgriNerve, an intelligent multi-agent system for real-time vineyard health observation and grape leaf disease identification, is the central theme of this literature review. AgriNerve provides valuable services in overall disease identification and analysis by integrating computer vision, agent-based artificial intelligence, and environmental data analysis in a complementary fashion. Specifically, AgriNerve employs a Python Flask backend framework in combination with a React-based frontend interface to offer accurate leaf disease identification through the application of powerful, state-of-the-art architectures such as MobileNet and ResNet in transfer learning tasks. AgriNerve offers a new paradigm where multiple agents collaborate and employ autonomous communication to achieve specific tasks, such as the explanation of illnesses, weather relationships, and computer vision. The relevant details about computer vision in plant disease diagnosis, multi-agent system design, and neural networks for agricultural applications are briefly discussed in this review article. With the integration of visual diagnosis and weather information in real-time, the proposed system fills the significant gaps in the current vineyard monitoring systems and enables adaptive decision-making through continuous learning processes. By discussing the latest advances in deep learning-based plant pathology detection, agent-based AI systems, and precision agriculture, this paper establishes the theoretical basis for the design of AgriNerve. These technologies have the potential to improve agricultural efficiency by providing intelligent autonomous vineyard management. The technology will provide farmers with valuable information through an intuitive interface, which will enable them to make the most of their resources and take appropriate intervention measures in the viticulture industry.

Document title: Agentic Ai in Remote Sensing: Foundations, Taxonomy, and Emerging Systems
Abstract: The paradigm of Earth Observation analysis is shifting from static deep learning models to autonomous agentic AI. Although recent vision foundation models and multimodal large language models advance representation learning, they often lack the sequential planning and active tool orchestration required for complex geospatial workflows. This survey presents the first comprehensive review of agentic AI in remote sensing. We introduce a unified taxonomy distinguishing between single-agent copilots and multiagent systems while analyzing architectural foundations such as planning mechanisms, retrieval-augmented gener- ation, and memory structures. Furthermore, we review emerging benchmarks that move the evaluation from pixellevel accuracy to trajectory-aware reasoning correctness. By critically examining limitations in grounding, safety, and orchestration, this work outlines a strategic roadmap for the development of robust, autonomous geospatial intelligence.

Document title: Agentic AI Architectures for Autonomous Decision-Making in Dynamic Environments
Abstract: The increasing complexity of real-world systems has revealed the shortcomings of traditional artificial intelligence models that usually base on a set of rules or offline training. These strategies fail to work well in flexible settings where the conditions keep on changing and decisions are made on the fly. This article presents an agentic architecture of artificial intelligence that will facilitate autonomous adaptive, and goal-driven decision-making in these settings. The suggested architecture integrates the reasoning of large language models with the scalability of multiagent systems, the learning potential of reinforcement learning, and the reasoning potential of large language models. The system is designed around important functional models, such as environmental perceptions, contextual reasoning, policy learning, and coordinated action execution. The system learns via feedback by continually engaging with its environment and optimizing its decision strategies, and additionally keeps context aware via highlevel reasoning. The suggested model enables active behavior and long-term planning and autonomous cooperation between two or more intelligent agents in contrast to traditional AI systems. The research points towards the benefits of this combined method to enhance system responsiveness, adaptability, and uncertainty strength. The possible uses include autonomous transportation, intelligent manufacturing, healthcare decision support, and intelligent urban infrastructure. The findings indicate that agentic AIs can bridge the reactive automation to genuine autonomous intelligence.

Document title: A Hybrid Multi-Agent Architecture for Resilient Logistics Planning Under Demand and Supply Uncertainty
Abstract: Modern supply chains operate under volatile demand and frequent disruptions, demanding planning systems that are both locally adaptive and globally coordinated. Traditional multi-agent system (MAS) architectures for logistics struggle to balance this trade-off, creating a significant governance gap in autonomous decision-making. This paper proposes a novel hybrid MAS architecture formally grounded in the subsidiarity principle to address this gap. The architecture is structured around a three-level governance model (operation, tactical, strategic) with specialized agents, formalized interactions using Foundation for Intelligent Physical Agents (FIPA) protocols, and a shared Web Ontology Language (OWL) ontology for semantic interoperability. Its adaptive behaviour is realized through an integrated suite of risk-aware algorithms distributed across all levels, enabling balanced decisionmaking from real-time reaction to long-term strategic evolution. The paper further contributes a comprehensive experimental design for validation, defining canonical baseline models (centralized and decentralized) and key performance indicators (KPIs) for simulation-based comparison. Together, these components provide a coherent framework for resilient logistics planning. The work contributes both a principled blueprint for building intelligent supply chain systems and a rigorous methodology for their empirical evaluation.

Document title: Agentic AI for Embodied-Enhanced Beam Prediction in Low-Altitude Economy Networks
Abstract: Millimeter-wave or terahertz communications can meet demands of low-altitude economy networks for high-throughput sensing and real-time decision making. However, high-frequency characteristics of wireless channels result in severe propagation loss and strong beam directivity, which make beam prediction challenging in highly mobile uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAV) scenarios. In this paper, we employ agentic AI to enable the transformation of mmWave base stations toward embodied intelligence. We innovatively design a multi-agent collaborative reasoning architecture for UAV-to-ground mmWave communications and propose a hybrid beam prediction model system based on bimodal data. The multi-agent architecture is designed to overcome the limited context window and weak controllability of large language model (LLM)-based reasoning by decomposing beam prediction into task analysis, solution planning, and completeness assessment. To align with the agentic reasoning process, a hybrid beam prediction model system is developed to process multi-modal UAV data, including numeric mobility information and visual observations. The proposed hybrid model system integrates Mamba-based temporal modelling, convolutional visual encoding, and cross-attention-based multi-modal fusion, and dynamically switches data-flow strategies under multi-agent guidance. Extensive simulations on a real UAV mmWave communication dataset demonstrate that the proposed architecture and system achieve high prediction accuracy and robustness under diverse data conditions, with maximum top-1 accuracy reaching 96.57% under the original 64-beam codebook.

Document title: LOCARD: An Agentic Framework for Blockchain Forensics
Abstract: Blockchain forensics inherently involves dynamic and iterative investigations, while many existing approaches primarily model it through static inference pipelines. We propose a paradigm shift towards Agentic Blockchain Forensics (ABF), modeling forensic investigation as a sequential decisionmaking process. To instantiate this paradigm, we introduce LOCARD, the first agentic framework for blockchain forensics. LOCARD operationalizes this perspective through a TriCore Cognitive Architecture that decouples strategic planning, operational execution, and evaluative validation. Unlike generic LLM-based agents, it incorporates a Structured Belief State mechanism to enforce forensic rigor and guide exploration under explicit state constraints. To demonstrate the efficacy of the ABF paradigm, we apply LOCARD to the inherently complex domain of cross-chain transaction tracing. We introduce Thor25, a benchmark dataset comprising over 151 k real-world crosschain forensic records, and evaluate LOCARD on the GroupTransfer Tracing task for dismantling Sybil clusters. Validated against representative laundering sub-flows from the Bybit hack, LOCARD achieves high-fidelity tracing results, providing empirical evidence that modeling blockchain forensics as an autonomous agentic task is both viable and effective. These results establish a concrete foundation for future agentic approaches to large-scale blockchain forensic analysis. Code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/xhyumiracle/locard and https://github.com/xhyumiracle/thorchain-crosschain-data.

Document title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Protocol for Scalable Agentic AI Systems
Abstract: Agentic AI systems are rapidly emerging as a new paradigm - shifting away from static Large Language Models (LLMs) toward autonomous, goal-oriented entities capable of reasoning, planning, and collaboration. In the past, to integrate AI systems with external applications, developers had to implement unique, task-specific code for each interface. This approach led to limited scalability and imposed a significant burden on the development process. In this view, this paper presents a comprehensive review of two emerging open standards designed to address these limitations: the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol. MCP provides structured and standardized access to tools, data sources, and contextual memory, while A2A communication frameworks define standard mechanisms enabling agents to exchange information, coordinate tasks, deliberate on decisions, and establish collaborative or competitive relationships. This paper analyzes MCP and A2A in terms of their respective roles, architectural features, and their relevance to the development of robust agentic AI systems. We compare their functionalities, identify their complementary strengths, and discuss how each contributes to the broader goal of building scalable, decentralized, and reliable autonomous AI agent environments.

Document title: Neuro-Symbolic Agent Graphs (NSAG): A Verifiable Architecture for Safe and Sustainable Agentic AI
Abstract: Conventional agentic AI systems often lack formal safety guarantees, leading to violations of energy, privacy, and operational constraints that limit their applicability in regulated and sustainability-critical environments. We propose Neuro-Symbolic Agent Graphs (NSAG), a hybrid framework that integrates probabilistic neural planning with symbolic verification over structured execution graphs. The framework employs REINFORCE-based policy optimization with entropy regularization, while an SMT-based verifier using the Z3 solver enforces hard energy and privacy constraints prior to execution. The NSAG architecture additionally incorporates feature normalization, dynamic energy budget recalibration, and staged joint optimization to improve real-world robustness and training stability. Experimental evaluation on synthetic workloads and real-world UCI Building Energy and Appliances Energy datasets demonstrates strong convergence, symbolic safety enforcement, and cross-dataset generalization. Training rewards improved from −1.31 to 4.31 over 12 epochs, approval rates approached complete symbolic compliance on Building Energy workloads. NSAG consistently rejected unsafe schedules violating symbolic constraints, enabling reliable, sustainable, and constraint-aware agentic decision-making.

Document title: From Predictive Personalisation to Fiduciary Agency: A Human-Centric Agentic AI Framework for Industry 5.0 Banking
Abstract: The banking sector is currently navigating a “Generative Paradox,” where the adoption of Generative AI (GenAI) has solved content scalability but failed to deliver autonomous economic execution. This paper presents a transition from “Hyper-Personalisation” to “Micro-Economic Execution Agents,” defined using autonomous systems capable of reasoning, planning, and executing complex financial workflows. Building on an empirical Minimum Viable Product (MVP) study $(n=300)$ that demonstrated an 85.7% increase in session duration using GenAI personalisation, we contrast these engagement gains with the critical “execution gap” revealed by the FinGAIA benchmark, where state-of-the-art agents achieve only 48.9% accuracy compared to 84.7% for human experts. To bridge this gap, we propose the Human-Centric Agentic Banking Framework (HC-ABF). This architecture integrates a Hierarchical Supervisor multi-agent pattern with the AGENTSAFE governance protocol, utilizing Action Provenance Graphs (APG) to mathematically enforce fiduciary duties. Furthermore, we address the critical “evaluation gap” in autonomous finance by proposing a novel evaluation protocol utilizing Agent-as-a-Judge methodologies and the FinGAIA benchmark. We provide simulated results demonstrating a $4.17 x$ relative uplift in task execution accuracy. This work provides a blueprint for Industry 5.0 banking that elevates human decision-making through safe, verifiable autonomy which is human centric at its core.

Document title: A Survey on Autonomous Compliance Enforcement using Agentic AI
Abstract: Infrastructure compliance enforcement is increasingly considered for agentic AI systems that can plan, act and self-correct over many steps. A structured examination of the literature reveals several significant gaps. Multi-agent compliance pipelines have been architecturally proposed in several works but none report a functioning prototype with measurable compliance outcomes. Theoretical discussions extensively cover the safety hazards arising from the granting of autonomous control to an LLM agent over remediation of infrastructure. However, there are no documented real-world cases of an LLM agent outputting an operationally dangerous output in a compliance setting. The concept of utilising cross-run memory for compliance agents has been recognised but no lightweight implementation has yet been demonstrated to change the behaviour of agents. This paper surveys the field along seven dimensions: agentic architectures, compliance automation, LLM output safety, anomaly detection, multi-agent coordination, statefulness, and cloud-native deployment drawing on 46 representative works. Six specific gaps are identified through structured analysis. A hybrid architecture is then proposed that integrates the Isolation Forest anomaly detection with a four-agent LLM pipeline consisting of an Analyser that interprets system state and prior run history, a Planner that generates remediation strategies, a Verifier that applies LLM safety constraints, and an Explainer that produces human-readable audit reports. The architecture further incorporates deterministic value-level validation and persistent SQLite-based cross-run memory. In controlled experiments, the system improved compliance scores from 60% to 100%. Notably, a concrete instance of LLM overreach was observed during testing: the Planner agent generated a remediation plan that would have locked out SSH access by closing all network ports, a failure mode not previously reported in empirical literature. The paper concludes with a feature-by-feature comparison across twelve prominent works, a discussion of open challenges, and a proposed hybrid cloud extension.

Document title: A Review of Agentic AI for Autonomous Intrusion Detection and Response in IoT Networks
Abstract: This The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) environments has increased the scale, heterogeneity, and attack surface of cyber networks, making traditional static defense mechanisms less effective against evolving attacks. Recent research increasingly combines deep learning-based intrusion detection with intelligent response mechanisms to improve detection accuracy, adaptability, and automation in resource-constrained IoT settings. At the same time, nature-inspired optimization has gained attention for feature selection, hyperparameter tuning, and multi-objective balancing between security performance and computational efficiency. Emerging work on agentic AI further extends this direction by enabling systems to perceive, reason, plan, and act with greater autonomy in cybersecurity workflows. This review examines the intersection of agentic AI, hybrid deep learning, and nature-inspired optimization for autonomous intrusion detection and response in IoT cyber networks. It analyzes threat models, intrusion detection and response paradigms, representative datasets, evaluation metrics, and open research challenges, and it outlines future directions for trustworthy, adaptive, and deployable IoT cyber defense.

Document title: A Human-in-the-Loop LLM–Assisted Multi-Agent Framework for Distribution Grid Reliability Planning
Abstract: This paper presents a human-in-the-loop LLM–assisted multi-agent framework for distribution grid reliability planning. Traditional reliability planning relies on deterministic simulations and manual engineering workflows, which can be difficult to scale for large feeder portfolios and evolving grid conditions. The proposed framework integrates large language model (LLM) reasoning with deterministic reliability analysis and optimization tools within a coordinated multi-agent architecture. Specialized agents perform data ingestion, reliability evaluation, planning optimization, and compliance reporting, while numerical simulation tools validate candidate planning actions generated by the LLM. Case studies on 100 real-world utility feeders demonstrate that the framework reduces planning time and manual engineering effort while maintaining acceptable planning accuracy for large-scale screening and scenario analysis.

Document title: Agentic AI for Trip Planning Optimization Application
Abstract: Trip planning for intelligent vehicles increasingly requires selecting optimal routes rather than merely producing feasible itineraries, as interacting factors such as travel time, energy consumption, and traffic conditions directly affect plan quality. Yet existing systems are largely designed for feasibility-oriented planning, and current benchmarks provide only reference answers without ground truth, preventing objective evaluation of optimization performance. In our paper, we address these limitations with an agentic AI framework that enables dynamic refinement through an orchestration agent coordinating specialized agents for traffic, charging, and points of interest, and with the Trip-planning Optimization Problems Dataset, which supplies definitive optimal solutions and category-level task structure for fine-grained analysis. Experiments show that our system achieves 77.4% accuracy on the TOP Benchmark, significantly outperforming single-agent and workflow-based multi-agent baselines, demonstrating the importance of orchestrated agentic reasoning for robust trip planning optimization.

Document title: A Survey on Multi-Agent LLM Frameworks with Semantic Memory Integration and Dynamic DAG Orchestration
Abstract: The rapid advancement of large language models has created substantial transformations throughout the artificial intelligence domain. The system development process results in the development of collaborative multi-agent systems which implement agent pipelines. The system operates through distributed reasoning which combines task decomposition with autonomous functionality. System operations become possible through the implementation of modern frameworks which support role instantiation. The process needs agents who specialize in particular tasks which include planning and coding and verification and critical assessment. The system operates through orchestration layers which enable coordination between its components. The system needs to incorporate vector-based semantic memory to improve its ability to understand context. The systems show successful applications in their three main fields which include software engineering and scientific analysis and enterprise automation. The current systems operate with limited functionality because they run programs through predetermined execution processes and fail to scale properly at both system and network infrastructure levels. The review presents an extensive evaluation and critical analysis of current LLM-based multi agent systems which focus on architectural paradigms. The system operates through DAG orchestration and semantic memory integration and microservice-based deployment methods. The system encounters primary problems which stem from high coordination requirements, weak fault detection capabilities, and the absence of appropriate system design standards. The evaluation process needs standardized evaluation methods and objective assessment systems. The research examines vital elements which consist of memory architectures and system-level telemetry and their essential functions for system operation.

Document title: A Security-by-Design Framework for Bounded Agentic AI in ERP-Integrated Smart Semiconductor and Electronics Manufacturing
Abstract: Semiconductor and electronics manufacturers increasingly operate enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, manufacturing execution systems (MES), and Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) infrastructure. These platforms operate as cyber-physical systems rather than as standalone business tools. Their expanded connectivity and automated operations increase the attack surfaces. Simultaneously, conventional ERP automation remains largely rule-based and parameter-driven, providing auditability but limiting adaptability. Recent advances in multiagent systems and agentic AI suggest a shift toward ERP systems that act as autonomous decision layers across IoT-connected semiconductor fabs and electronics manufacturing lines. However, introducing such autonomy fundamentally alters the security and trust assumptions of existing ERP and MES architectures. This paper proposes a fivephase security-by-design methodology and a reference architecture for migrating from rulebased ERP automation to bounded agentic AI. The methodology specifically targets secure manufacturing and supply chain assurance by bounding agentic ERP authority over production planning, supplier selection, and yield-critical workflows in IIoT-connected semiconductor fabrication plants (fabs) and electronics manufacturing service (EMS) lines.

Document title: Leveraging Multi-Agent System (MAS) and Fine-Tuned Small Language Models (SLMs) for Automated Telecom Network Troubleshooting
Abstract: Telecom networks are rapidly increasing in scale and complexity, making management, operation, and optimization increasingly challenging. Although Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been applied to various telecom tasks, existing approaches are often limited in scope, require extensive labeled data, and struggle to generalize across heterogeneous deployments. Consequently, network troubleshooting still relies heavily on Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to manually correlate multiple data sources and determine root causes and corrective actions. In this paper, we propose a Multi-Agent System (MAS) that leverages an agentic workflow in which Large Language Models (LLMs) coordinate specialized tools to enable auto-mated network troubleshooting. Upon fault detection by AI/ML-based monitoring systems, the framework dynamically activates multiple agents—including an orchestrator, solution planner, executor, data retriever, and root-cause analyzer—to diagnose issues and recommend remediation strategies in near real time. A key component is the solution planner, which generates executable remediation plans grounded in internal operational documentation. To enable this capability, we fine-tune a Small Language Model (SLM) using proprietary troubleshooting documents to produce domain-specific solution plans. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves troubleshooting automation and efficiency across both Radio Access Network (RAN) and Core network domains.

Document title: Agentic AI in Healthcare and Medicine: A Seven-Dimensional Taxonomy for Empirical Evaluation of LLM-Based Agents
Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents that plan, use tools and act has begun to shape healthcare and medicine. Reported studies demonstrate competence on various tasks ranging from EHR analysis and differential diagnosis to treatment planning and research workflows. Yet the literature largely consists of overviews which are either broad surveys or narrow dives into a single capability (e.g., memory, planning, reasoning), leaving healthcare work without a common frame. We address this by reviewing 49 studies using a seven-dimensional taxonomy: Cognitive Capabilities, Knowledge Management, Interaction Patterns, Adaptation & Learning, Safety & Ethics, Framework Typology and Core Tasks & Subtasks with 29 operational sub-dimensions. Using explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria and a labeling rubric (Fully Implemented ✓, Partially Implemented  $\Delta $ , Not Implemented ✗), we map each study to the taxonomy and report quantitative summaries of capability prevalence and co-occurrence patterns. Our empirical analysis surfaces clear asymmetries. For instance, the External Knowledge Integration sub-dimension under Knowledge Management is commonly realized (~76% ✓) whereas Event-Triggered Activation sub-dimenison under Interaction Patterns is largely absent (~92% ✗) and Drift Detection & Mitigation sub-dimension under Adaptation & Learning is rare (~98% ✗). Architecturally, Multi-Agent Design sub-dimension under Framework Typology is the dominant pattern (~82% ✓) while orchestration layers remain mostly partial. Across Core Tasks & Subtasks, information centric capabilities lead e.g., Medical Question Answering & Decision Support and Benchmarking & Simulation, while action and discovery oriented areas such as Treatment Planning & Prescription still show substantial gaps (~59% ✗). Together, these findings provide an empirical baseline indicating that current agents excel at retrieval-grounded advising but require stronger adaptation and compliance platforms to move from early-stage systems to dependable systems.

Document title: A Survey of Agentic AI-Enhanced Multimodal Deep Learning Approaches for Early Detection and Progression Risk Prediction of Parkinson's Disease
Abstract: Parkinson's disease is the world's fastest-growing neurodegenerative disorder; clinical diagnosis is typically delayed by 2–6 years from symptom onset, by which time 50–70% of dopaminergic neurons have already been lost. Computational approaches based on clinical scores, speech recordings, or neuroimaging have individually shown promise, yet their isolated use limits diagnostic robustness and progression forecasting. Recent advances in multimodal deep learning enable joint reasoning over heterogeneous data sources, while the emerging paradigm of agentic artificial intelligence autonomous systems that plan, act, remember, and adapt with limited human supervision offers a path toward closed-loop clinical decision support that conventional rule-based systems cannot provide. This survey reviews the landscape of deep learning methods for PD across clinical, speech, and imaging modalities, taxonomizes multimodal fusion architectures, and analyses the role that agentic AI components planner, reasoning, and memory agents can play in early detection and longitudinal progression risk prediction. We compare 25+ representative methods, evaluate longitudinal assessment protocols using standard metrics (AUC, RMSE, C-index), summarize publicly available datasets including PPMI, PC-GITA, and UCI Parkinson's voice, and identify open research challenges encompassing missing-modality robustness, computational feasibility, explainability, federated deployment, and clinical safety. The survey concludes by motivating an Agentic AI-enhanced multimodal framework that integrates clinical, speech, and imaging data to support adaptive, patient-specific care planning.

Document title: Agentic Command Assistant: Integrating Visual Perception with Generative AI for Advanced Tactical Decision Support
Abstract: Modern tactical reconnaissance increasingly is predicated on UAVs and mobile sensor structures; However, their effectiveness is regularly restricted with the aid of occlusion, suboptimal approximations, and visually negative situations that reduce the reliability of deep getting to know-primarily based object detectors. Traditional fashions along with YOLO and DETR offer sturdy perceptual abilities, however act as passive, feed-forward systems that cannot actively remedy ambiguous identities, resulting in much less reliable intelligence and extended cognitive load for human operators. To overcome these limitations, this work proposes an Agentic Command Assistant, a singular closed-loop structure that integrates a hybrid visual notion engine with a generative AI-pushed cognition module for advanced tactical choice help.
