Despite recent progress in VLM-based agents for 3D editing, the fundamental trade-off between editing precision and agent responsiveness remains unresolved. To overcome these limitations, we present EZBlender, a Blender agent with a hybrid framework that combines planningbased task decomposition and reactive local autonomy for efficient human-AI collaboration and semantically faithful 3D editing. Specifically, this unexplored Plan-and-ReAct design not only preserves editing quality but also significantly reduces latency and computational cost. To further validate the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed edge-autonomy architecture, we construct a dedicated multi-tasking benchmark that has not been systematically investigated in prior research. In addition, we provide a comprehensive analysis of language model preference, system responsiveness, and economic efficiency. Our example dataset and code are available at: https://github.com/Aztech-Lab/EZ_Blender

Document title: An AI-Driven Multi-Objective Optimization Model for Sensor-Based LED Lighting and Urban Place-Making
Abstract: With the development of smart cities, urban public space lighting is evolving from a simple form of illumination to a medium that carries culture and emotions. However, the existing intelligent lighting systems overly focus on energy efficiency, while seriously neglecting “local creation” and “human emotional experience”. To address this, this study proposes and validates an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven multi-objective optimization model for LED lighting based on IoT multimodal sensors. The research draws theoretical inspiration from contemporary public art (such as the light and shadow installations by Tatsuo Miyajima and Toyomi Hoshina), extracting three core parameters: “individual heterogeneity rhythm”, “biological electric drive randomness”, and “memory narrative space anchor”. Based on this, this paper constructs a real-world experimental framework integrating passive infrared, environmental lightsensitive, and plant bioelectric potential sensors, and uses the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) as the core AI computational approach to collaboratively optimize three constraints: lighting energy consumption, visual/emotional comfort, and digital place creation index. The field deployment results indicate that this AI-driven dynamic lighting model significantly mitigates the “light island effect” of traditional sensor-based lighting, achieving a 42.5% system-level energy saving. At the same time, by introducing ecological micro-electropotential and personalized light and shadow interaction, the observed average stay time of pedestrians in the urban decline square is extended by nearly three times (from 3.5 to 12.4 minutes), significantly enhancing the regional social interaction density and public emotional satisfaction. This study provides a quantifiable AI-based guideline integrating technical and humanistic values for the design of empathetic infrastructure in future smart cities.

Document title: Voice or Text? A Qualitative Examination of Communication Modality in Conversational Agents
Abstract: Conversational agents (CAs) increasingly operate through text and voice modalities, yet limited qualitative research explains how users interpret these modalities in terms of authenticity, usability, motivation, and collaborative engagement. This study presents findings from a qualitative investigation comparing text-based and voice-based CAs across two applied scenarios: holiday planning and in-car navigation. Forty participants interacted with a single modality and responded to open-ended questions about authenticity, ease of use, motivation, social interaction, attitudes, and value co-creation. Thematic analysis reveals that authenticity is primarily constructed through perceived competence rather than emotional realism, usability is highly contextual, and utilitarian motivation dominates co-creation intentions across modalities. While voice-based systems are perceived as more natural in mobility contexts, efficiency and functional value remain central drivers of engagement. The findings provide theoretical and design implications for modality selection in conversational systems.

Document title: An Intelligent Inspection Robot System for Offshore Wind Power Platforms
Abstract: As offshore wind power advances to far-reaching sea areas, traditional manual operation and maintenance is plagued by harsh conditions, high risks, low efficiency and severe data isolation. Aiming at the technical bottlenecks of poor environmental adaptability, low autonomous inspection precision and inadequate remote operation capability of robots in the high-humidity, high-salt-spray and strong wind-wave marine environment, this paper studies the key technologies of an intelligent inspection and teleoperation maintenance robot system for offshore wind power platforms. We design a high-reliability system including three kinds of robots, with composite adaptive anti-disturbance components for specific inspection purposes. A multi-modal intelligent inspection system is constructed with spatiotemporal adaptive denoising perception, cross-modal transfer detection and cloud-edge collaborative deployment to improve defect identification performance. A cloud-edge-end integrated platform is built and verified in wind turbine nacelles and booster stations. Experimental results show the system meets key indicators: repeated positioning accuracy ≤±5mm, equipment state recognition accuracy ≥98%, master-slave attitude deviation ≤±1°, response delay ≤200ms, IP65 protection grade and manipulator end load ≥3kg. It can increase inspection frequency by over 5 times and cut labor costs by 60%~80%, significantly improving the intelligent operation and maintenance level of offshore wind power assets. This research fills the domestic technical gap in far-reaching offshore wind power intelligent inspection and maintenance robots, providing technical support for safe and efficient operation of offshore wind power platforms, with broad prospects in offshore oil and gas platforms and nuclear power plant auxiliary plants.

Document title: ChargeLink-X: AI-Orchestrated Bidirectional Conductive V2V Energy Exchange EV for Affordable and Clean Energy Applications
Abstract: The rising adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has escalated the pressure to have effective and smart energy management systems to overcome the range anxiety and lack of enough charging systems. The paper suggests ChargeLink-X, an AI mediated bi-directional conductive Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) bidirectional energy transaction model that is aimed at facilitating efficient, adaptive, and predictive energy exchange in EVs. The system proposed combines Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to predict the State of Charge (SOC) accurately in the future to make a proactive energy planning. The use of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) model is necessary to enable smart vehicles negotiating the energy so that the energy spread is optimal and equitable. Also, a hybrid Harris Hawk Optimization (HGO) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is employed to control adaptive converter, and a fuzzy logic-based controller is employed to have a safety and long life of the battery. A power routing system that is efficiency conscious also reduces the number of losses incurred in transfer. The results of the simulation illustrate that the given framework can contribute to SOC prediction with agreater accuracy, provide a higher level of energy transmission, minimize battery degradation, and provide system stability in comparison with the traditional methodology. The ChargeLink-X platform offers an open scalable and intelligent platform of EV energy ecosystems of the next generation.

Document title: Hierarchical Attention-based Temporal Financial Optimization Framework for Corporate Financial Management and Risk-aware Treasury Optimization
Abstract: In recent years, Corporate Financial Management (CFM) has become increasingly complex due to dynamic operational activities, market volatility and continuously changing economic conditions. Traditional CFM systems rely on static Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP)-based processing and rule-based decision making, which are insufficient for proactive financial decision-making and adaptive management of treasury functions. To address these limitations, Hierarchical Attention-based Temporal Financial Optimization (HATF-OTP) framework is proposed for managing an organization's finances and optimizing their treasury function. The digital twin financial architecture is designed for constructing synchronized virtual representation of company’s financial ecosystem through modeling of asset reserve liquidity, investment commitments, tax commitments and payment obligation. To capture nonlinear multi-scale temporal financial dependencies, Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT)-based forecasting module is employed for enable predictions future liquidity fluctuations, treasury instability, debt escalation and operational financial risks. Graph Attention Network (GAT)-based dependency learning mechanism is utilized to model hidden transactional relationships and financial interactions among enterprise entities. Finally, hierarchical explainable multi-agent Reinforcement Learning (RL) optimization framework integrated to generate adaptive and transparent enterprise financial policies. Experimental results demonstrates that the proposed HATF-OTP framework achieves forecasting accuracy of 0.90 and highest state-action value update score of 340.175 when compared to existing model.

Document title: A CNN-Based Smart Farming Robot for Plant Disease Detection and Crop Management
Abstract: Agribusiness, the backbone of many countries' economy, has many challenges posed by plant diseases that may compromise the yield and quality of the produce. The disease detection approaches that have been in use are time-consuming and inaccurate as they depend on human vision. The paper describes the design and implementation of an autonomous smart farming robot for the detection of chilli plant diseases. The proposed method uses a hybrid architecture for image classification with the inclusion of an InceptionResNetV2 model for the detection of diseases in chilli plants. The idea is to use pictures of leaves to figure out if a chilli plant has a disease. We are looking at five kinds of diseases in chilli plants: Healthy, Leaf Curl, Leaf Spot, Whitefly and Yellowish diseases. We are using a system that combines different ways of looking at pictures to see if a chilli plant is sick. This system uses something called an InceptionResNetV2 model to look at the leaves and find diseases in chilli plants. Using leaf image classification for chilli plants will really help us find out what is wrong, with the plant. This method will make it a lot easier to detect leaf diseases in chilli plants. Experimental results for 50 epochs indicate that the approach is highly precise and would be an optimal solution for the detection of leaf diseases in chilli plants.

Document title: SmartTrip: An AI-Powered Travel Planning Platform with Intelligent Agent Support, Voice and Multilingual Capabilities
Abstract: This paper presents Smart Trip, an AI-enhanced travel planning and booking platform designed to serve both travelers and travel agents through a unified interface. The system incorporates role-based logins, enabling travelers to search, plan, and manage trips while allowing agents to perform bookings and manage client interactions. Smart Trip features intelligent chatbots for both travelers and agents, supporting voice interaction and multilingual capabilities to ensure inclusive and accessible communication. It leverages invoice and expense scanning using OCR(Optical Character Recognition) and AI(Artificial Intelligence), enabling users to manage financial records seamlessly within chat interfaces. Embedded summarization tools provide real-time financial summaries for enhanced decision-making. The backend leverages Google Vertex AI with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and embeddings for contextual responses and personalization. The platform is designed with scalability in mind, and a React/Next.js frontend ensures a modern, userfriendly experience. This paper presents the system architecture, technology stack, testing results, and future directions for Smart Trip, highlighting its potential to revolutionize personalized travel management and agent workflows.

Document title: Design, Implementation, and User Evaluation of an Intelligent Travel Real-Time Itinerary Adjustment System Based on Generative Artificial Intelligence
Abstract: Traditional travel itinerary planning is timeconsuming and prone to disruptions from unexpected events like weather or closures, leading to traveler frustration. This paper proposes a smart itinerary planning system that combines multi-source data integration and generative AI to provide personalized pre-trip itineraries and real-time adjustments during travel. The system features a multi-layer architecture with a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mechanism for feasible itinerary generation and a rule-based engine for dynamic adaptation via a LINE messaging bot interface. A user study (n=20) evaluated planning efficiency, and usability. Results show the system significantly reduces planning time and cognitive effort, improves adaptability to sudden changes (e.g., bad weather or closures), and achieves high usability (most SUS scores > 80). This human-centered AI approach enhances traveler experience and supports more sustainable travel decisions by avoiding wasted trips to closed or congested venues.

Document title: Video-to-BT: Generating Reactive Behavior Trees from Human Demonstration Videos for Robotic Assembly
Abstract: Modern manufacturing demands robotic assembly systems with enhanced flexibility and reliability. However, traditional approaches often rely on programming tailored to each product by experts for fixed settings, which are inherently inflexible to product changes and lack the robustness to handle variations. As Behavior Trees (BTs) are increasingly used in robotics for their modularity and reactivity, we propose a novel hierarchical framework, Video-to-BT, that seamlessly integrates high-level cognitive planning with low-level reactive control, with BTs serving both as the structured output of planning and as the governing structure for execution. Our approach leverages a Vision Language Model (VLM) to decompose human demonstration videos into subtasks, from which BTs are generated. During the execution, the planned BTs combined with real-time scene interpretation enable the system to operate reactively in the dynamic environment, while VLM-driven replanning is triggered upon execution failure. This closed-loop architecture ensures stability and adaptivity. We validate our framework on real-world assembly tasks through a series of experiments, demonstrating high planning reliability, robust performance in long-horizon assembly tasks, and strong generalization across diverse and perturbed conditions. Project website: https://video2bt.github.io/video2bt_page/

Document title: A Hybrid Motion Planning Framework with Learned Reactive Action Model for Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance
Abstract: Real-time motion planning for robotic manipulators in dynamic environments is challenging due to the inherent conflict between long-horizon global optimality and the need for instantaneous collision reaction. Traditional sampling-based planners often suffer from significant reaction latency when facing sudden disturbances. This paper proposes a hybrid motion planning framework that augments an incremental sampling-based planner (RT-RRT*) with a learned reactive action model, enabling immediate responses to dynamic obstacles without extensive resampling. Besides, the framework utilizes a learned evaluator to monitor collision risks and triggers the reactive model to execute reflexive avoidance maneuvers. Once the threat is resolved, a tree realignment strategy ensures a smooth transition back to the global plan. Evaluated on a 6-DoF humanoid manipulator, the proposed method achieves a 91% success rate and reduces task completion time by 25% compared to the traditional sampling-based method. Our results demonstrate that the proposed architecture effectively bridges the gap between deliberative planning and reactive control, ensuring both safety and efficiency in complex dynamic workspaces.

Document title: An Experimental Study of Planar Homography Augmentation for Real-World Instance Segmentation
Abstract: Planar homography augmentation is widely used to increase viewpoint diversity in instance segmentation, under the implicit assumption that scene geometry is approximately planar. However, its behavior under realistic depth variation and extreme camera viewpoints remains poorly understood. This paper presents a controlled empirical study of planar homography augmentation for real-world instance segmentation. We compare homography-augmented and non-augmented models using standard metrics alongside geometry-conditioned, image-wise analysis. To isolate geometric effects, we incorporate training budget matching, a padding-only control, a depth-variance proxy for scene non-planarity, and cross-architecture evaluation using YOLOv8-Seg and Mask R-CNN. Our results show that while planar homography augmentation improves performance in near-planar and synthetic settings, it does not consistently improve and can degrade performance in realistic scenes with non-planar structure and severe foreshortening. Qualitative analysis reveals recurring geometric failure modes that are not captured by aggregate metrics, highlighting the need for geometry-aware evaluation when deploying synthetic viewpoint augmentation in robotic perception systems.

Document title: Analyzing the Influence of Reference Groups on Consumer Brand Connectivity Through Behavioral Modeling
Abstract: Brand connectivity, or the emotional connection that customers have with a brand, is more vital than ever for businesses to do well in today's increasingly competitive business world. Reference groups, which are groups of individuals who people look up to, like friends, family, and social media influencers, are one of the many things that determine how people act as consumers. These groups have a huge impact on how customers feel, what they believe, and what they buy. Reference groups are crucial, but the models we have today don't do a good job of measuring how they effect brand loyalty. This study suggests a hybrid behavioralmodeling method that combines Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) as a way to simulate how consumers interact with one other when there are different reference group influences. The first poll got data from five hundred people, who came from a wide range of backgrounds. We ran the simulations with NetLogo and did the statistical analysis with R. There were three kinds of agents that illustrated how the reference group worked: opinion leaders, followers, and people who didn't have an opinion. We looked at how well it functioned by comparing it to baseline models using decision trees, sentiment scoring, and linear regression. The TPB-ABM model that was suggested was 17% better at making predictions than the one that is currently doing the best. This is why it worked better than the normal ways. There was a statistically significant link between how connected a person felt to a brand and how much they enjoyed it, how socially acceptable they believed it was, and how much their friends liked it. The simulation results indicated that being part of a group was even more crucial when it came to adopting a brand. The results showed that groups who were highly close to each other agreed on brand choices more quickly.

Document title: When the Manual Lies: A Realistic Benchmark to Evaluate MCP Poisoning Attacks for LLM Agents
Abstract: The rise of tool-using Large Language Model (LLM) agents, standardized by protocols like the Model Context Protocol (MCP), has unlocked unprecedented autonomous execution capabilities for LLM Agents by integrating external open-domain knowledge and tools [1]. However, this interoperability introduces a covert attack surface targeting the agent’s cognitive planning layer. This paper systematically investigates Tool Description Poisoning (TDP), a novel semantic attack. In TDP, malicious instructions are not embedded in a tool’s executable code, but rather covertly injected into its descriptive metadata — the very "manual" an agent relies on for secure planning and decision-making. To rigorously and systematically evaluate this emerging threat, we introduce the MCP-TDP Security Benchmark. This high-fidelity sandbox environment comprises 32 realistic, real-world test cases spanning 6 distinct risk categories. Our evaluation of 8 mainstream LLMs reveals severe vulnerabilities, with leading models like GPT-4o exhibiting a nearly 100% Attack Success Rate (ASR) in six high-risk scenarios. Furthermore, our findings demonstrate that common prompt-guardrail defenses are largely ineffective and can, counterintuitively, even be counterproductive (a phenomenon which we term the "Firewall Fallacy"). Crucially, we also propose a defense mechanism: "Reactive Self-Correction," where an agent autonomously detects and reverts its own malicious actions post-execution. This work provides the first specialized security benchmark tailored for TDP, offering essential insights for securing the cognitive and planning layers of advanced agentic systems.

Document title: Intent-Driven and Constraint-Verified Service Composition via Evolving Verified Experience
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong potential for complex planning and tool-use tasks, yet reliable service coordination and cooperation across multiple services remains challenging. In real-world service coordination scenarios, the system must coordinate heterogeneous services, manage crossstep dependencies, and satisfy both explicit and implicit user constraints simultaneously. Existing multi-agent and direct generation approaches offer flexibility in decomposing such tasks, but they often struggle to guarantee executability and hard-constraint satisfaction. In contrast, formal verification methods provide stronger rigor, but typically solve each request from scratch, leading to limited adaptability and high computational cost. To address this gap, we propose an experience-driven framework for intent-driven and constraint-verified service composition, which combines the flexibility of LLM-based planning with the rigor of formal verification. It converts a natural-language request into structured bindings and a normalized workflow, reuses, adapts, or synthesizes sub-workflows based on verified past experience, and validates the resulting composition through execution and constraint checking. Successful solutions are then stored as verified experience for future requests. Experiments on the TravelPlanner benchmark show that the proposed framework achieves a 77.0% Final Pass Rate on the test set, outperforming strong direct LLM baselines and a verification-based neurosymbolic baseline. At the same time, it reduces token consumption by $\mathbf{6 5. 6 \%}$ and average runtime by $\mathbf{6 6. 1 \%}$, while improving operational stability. In addition, we find that an easy-to-hard evolution order yields the best performance, suggesting that curriculumstyle accumulation of verified experience is particularly beneficial for building reliable and reusable service compositions. These results indicate that evolving verified experience provides an effective foundation for scalable, reliable, and constraint-aware service coordination and cooperation.

Document title: Hierarchical Optimization Algorithm for Multi-Agent Coverage Path Planning Fusing Frequency Memory
Abstract: Multi-agent cooperative coverage path planning in large-scale complex scenarios is prone to falling into local optima. Existing optimization methods based on simulated annealing mostly focus on local search, lacking global guidance and historical information reuse, making it difficult to break through performance bottlenecks in overall system completion time, total task cost, and load balancing. To address this, a hierarchical optimization algorithm for multi-agent coverage path planning fusing frequency memory is proposed. A threelayer architecture of “initial solution generation → tabu search for global region optimization → simulated annealing for local path refinement” is constructed. By leveraging cross-stage frequency memory transfer and a soft-constraint weighting mechanism, synergistic optimization of region allocation and path planning is achieved. Experiments show that in large-scale scenarios containing multiple static obstacles, the proposed algorithm achieves a superior trade-off among task efficiency, multi-agent synergy, and cost compared to simulated annealing optimization methods, effectively mitigating the local optimum problem and breaking through relevant performance bottlenecks. Compared with the classical VOR (Voronoi) algorithm, the overall system completion time is reduced by 57.5%, and the load balancing rate is improved by 122.1%. Convergence analysis validates the convergence speed and solution stability of the proposed algorithm regarding the overall system completion time metric.

Document title: Low-Altitude UAV-Assisted Reliable Communication for Disaster Relief IoT Networks via Diffusion Model- Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: In disaster-stricken areas, maintaining reliable communication networks is essential for effective rescue operations. This paper proposes a novel approach to enhance the connectivity of rescue networks by integrating collaborative beamforming with low-altitude uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) trajectory planning. We model a scenario where Internet of Things (IoT) devices transmit collected environmental data to the rescue control center (RCC) through a ground-based virtual antenna array (GVAA), with UAVs serving as relays in this disaster-affected network. The primary objective is to minimize communication outages and reduce the energy consumption of both the UAVs and ground-based devices. Due to the dynamic movement of the RCC toward target areas, the system exhibits significant dynamism, requiring long-term optimization of UAV positions to maintain consistent connectivity. To address this, we propose a diffusion model-based proximal policy optimization (DMPPO) algorithm, which optimizes UAV trajectories and other system parameters to minimize communication outage rate while also reducing energy consumption. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DMPPO reduces the outage probability and energy consumption of UAVs and IoT devices by 88.71%, 3.02%, and 50.31%, respectively, compared to the suboptimal benchmark. This indicates that DMPPO is more suitable for the considered emergency scenarios. Furthermore, the DMPPO algorithm consistently outperforms benchmark methods across various challenging configurations, such as different UAV numbers and distances, demonstrating its scalability and robustness.

Document title: On the Generalization Gap in LLM Planning: Tests and Verifier-Reward RL
Abstract: Recent work shows that fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) can achieve high valid plan rates on PDDL planning tasks. However, it remains unclear whether this reflects transferable planning competence or domain-specific memorization. In this work, we fine-tune a 1.7B-parameter LLM on 40,000 domain–problem–plan tuples from 10 IPC 2023 domains, and evaluate both in-domain and cross-domain generalization. While the model reaches 82.9% valid plan rate in in-domain conditions, it achieves 0% on two unseen domains. To analyze this failure, we introduce three diagnostic interventions, namely (i) instance-wise symbol anonymization, (ii) compact plan serialization, and (iii) verifier-reward fine-tuning using the VAL validator as a success-focused reinforcement signal. Symbol anonymization and compact serialization cause significant performance drops despite preserving plan semantics, thus revealing strong sensitivity to surface representations. Verifier-reward fine-tuning reaches performance saturation in half the supervised training epochs, but does not improve cross-domain generalization. For the explored configurations, in-domain performance plateaus around 80%, while cross-domain performance collapses, suggesting that our fine-tuned model relies heavily on domain-specific patterns rather than transferable planning competence in this setting. Our results highlight a persistent generalization gap in LLM-based planning and provide diagnostic tools for studying its causes.

Document title: Go Gentle Into the Final Dance: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs in Telecom
Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have driven remarkable progress across diverse NLP benchmarks. However, the application of these models to sophisticated domains such as wireless communications raises new challenges. This paper addresses the evaluation gap for LLMs in telecommunications by introducing Last Dance of Telecommunications (LDOT) – a comprehensive benchmark suite for telecom-related tasks. LDOT encompasses a broad range of problem categories, including conceptual telecom questions, mathematical and logical reasoning problems, and complex network optimization scenarios, specifically designed to challenging LLMs’ high-level reasoning and domain-specific knowledge. Using LDOT, we rigorously assess state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs (both closed-source and open-source) on domain-specific tasks. Our results reveal that while general-purpose LLMs exhibit strong performance on basic telecom knowledge questions, they struggle with reasoning-intensive wireless problems. Notably, certain multi-step optimization and planning tasks in LDOT remain unsolved by even the best models, exposing performance gaps that are not apparent from existing saturated benchmarks. We provide a detailed failure analysis to pinpoint whether these limitations arise from insufficient telecom-specific knowledge or from inadequate reasoning capabilities. The LDOT dataset and our evaluation findings aim to facilitate the development of more robust domain-adapted LLMs for next-generation wireless communications.

Document title: LAVATour: A Career Digital Twin Platform for AI-Driven Trajectory Simulation and Consultation
Abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of the artificial intelligence (AI) era, traditional career planning tools—often based on static psychometric assessments like RIASEC or MBTI—fail to account for dynamic external variables such as algorithmic displacement and economic volatility. This paper introduces LAVATour, a web-based intelligent career navigation platform designed to operationalize the LAVA framework (Lifecycle, Algorithmic Displacement, Vocational Entropy, Active Inference). Unlike conventional tools that provide a single "snapshot" of career fit, LAVATour utilizes a React-based architecture and D3.js visualization libraries to render a dynamic, 100-year career trajectory. The system integrates a "Vocational Entropy" simulation engine that visualizes skill decay over time and an "Active Inference" module powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate personalized, entropy-reducing milestone recommendations. We describe the system architecture, the mathematical logic underlying the trajectory generation, and the prompt engineering strategies used for context-aware consultation. LAVATour represents a paradigm shift from static career matching to dynamic career digital twinning, providing students with a "flight simulator" to navigate the complexities of the future labor market.

Document title: Decoupling Geometric Planning and Execution in Scalable Multi-Agent Path Finding
Abstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) requires collision-free trajectories for multiple agents on a shared graph, often with the objective of minimizing the sum-of-costs (SOC). Many optimal and bounded-suboptimal solvers rely on time-expanded models and centralized conflict resolution, which limits scalability in large or dense instances. We propose a hybrid prioritized framework that separates geometric planning from execution-time conflict resolution. In the first stage, Geometric Conflict Preemption (GCP) plans agents sequentially with A* on the original graph while inflating costs for transitions entering vertices used by higher-priority paths, encouraging spatial detours without explicit time reasoning. In the second stage, a Decentralized Local Controller (DLC) executes the geometric paths using per-vertex FIFO authorization queues and inserts wait actions to avoid vertex and edge-swap conflicts. Experiments on standard benchmark maps with up to 1000 agents show that the method scales with an near-linear runtime trend and attains a 100% success rate on instances satisfying the geometric feasibility assumption. Page of the project: https://sites.google.com/unizar.es/multi-agent-path-finding/home

Document title: A Simulation-Based Design for a Warehouse 4.0 Packing Facility in Automotive Logistics
Abstract: Traditional warehouse design approaches are often inadequate for evaluating system performance prior to implementation, particularly when new packaging, handling, and storage processes are introduced. This study proposes a simulation-modelling framework for a Warehouse 4.0 packing facility that supports an automotive parts distribution centre. The research develops a hybrid simulation model that combines Discrete-Event Simulation (DES) to represent warehouse process flows with Agent-Based Modelling (ABM) to capture the behaviour and interactions of operational resources. The model is implemented in AnyLogic to simulate key warehouse activities, including receiving, storage, inspection, repacking, and dispatch. The simulation model enables ex-ante analysis of warehouse layout configuration, manpower allocation, material-handling strategies, and packing-station capacity under uncertain volume projections. Several experimental scenarios are conducted to evaluate throughput, resource utilisation, processing time, and bottleneck formation. The results demonstrate that the proposed model can identify effective design trade-offs among space, labour, and equipment while supporting future expansion planning and operational resilience. The proposed approach provides a practical decision-support tool for the design of smart packaging warehouses and contributes to the adoption of Warehouse 4.0 principles in service-parts logistics environments.

Document title: Research on automated review method for UHV project BIM models based on multi-agent collaboration
Abstract: Addressing the challenges in Building Information Modeling (BIM) model review for Ultra-High Voltage (UHV) engineering, such as complex standard systems, low efficiency of manual review, and poor consistency, this paper proposes an automated review method that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with multi-agent collaboration. The system employs a privately deployed DeepSeek model as its cognitive core and constructs a task execution architecture based on multi-agent collaboration. Utilizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technology, the system assists in converting unstructured regulatory texts into structured, executable review rules and achieves intelligent scheduling of specialized review tools through a function calling mechanism. Within the system, a master control agent is responsible for dynamically planning the overall review task flow, coordinating specialized agents for model parsing, property checking, spatial analysis, etc., forming a complete "Understanding-Planning-Execution-Feedback" review closed loop. Experimental results from a new 750kV substation project show that compared to traditional manual methods, the system improves review efficiency by over 90%, achieves a review coverage rate of over 96%, and significantly enhances review quality and automation levels.

Document title: ReMALIS: Inference-Guided Intention Propagation for Multiagent Stochastic Task Coordination With Large Language Models in Complex Networks Domains
Abstract: Effective collaboration in multiagent systems requires communicating goals and intentions between agents. Current agent frameworks often suffer from dependencies on single-agent execution and lack robust inter-module communication, frequently leading to suboptimal multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) policies and inadequate task coordination. To address these challenges, we present a framework for training large language models (LLMs) as collaborative agents to enable coordinated behaviors in cooperative MARL. Each agent maintains a private intention consisting of its current goal and associated sub-tasks. Agents broadcast their intentions periodically, allowing other agents to infer coordination tasks. A propagation network transforms broadcast intentions into teammate-specific communication messages, sharing relevant goals with designated teammates. The architecture of our framework is structured into planning, grounding, and execution modules. During execution, multiple agents interact in a downstream environment and communicate intentions to enable coordinated behaviors. The grounding module dynamically adapts comprehension strategies based on emerging coordination patterns, while feedback from execution agents influences the planning module, enabling the dynamic re-planning of sub-tasks. Results in collaborative environment simulation demonstrate intention propagation reduces miscoordination errors by aligning sub-task dependencies between agents. Agents learn when to communicate intentions and which teammates require task details, resulting in emergent coordinated behaviors. This demonstrates the efficacy of intention sharing for cooperative multiagent RL based on LLMs.

Document title: A Hybrid Centralized and Decentralized Framework for Traffic Management in Advanced Air Mobility
Abstract: The dynamic and safe routing of aircraft within Unmanned Aircraft Systems Traffic Management (UTM) is a key issue for the development of Advanced Air Mobility (AAM). The future framework of AAM will involve many autonomous vehicles occupying the same airspace with differing levels of priority, requiring scalable, efficient, and safe solutions. Machine Learning (ML) is a key candidate for this area, specifically through the usage of Reinforcement Learning (RL) for dynamically routing aircraft and resolving potential spatial and temporal conflicts that occur. However, to incorporate a system utilizing ML into the safety-critical environment of AAM, rigorous guarantees of safety are necessary to maintain the operational safety of the National Airspace System. Therefore, formal methods must be explored to build a safety harness around the RL model. This theoretical paper provides a survey of current solutions in the areas of RL for UTM, Safe RL, and Safe RL for UTM. After establishing the current state of the art and providing necessary background information, a Hybrid Centralized and Decentralized (HC/Dc) framework is proposed integrating formal methods into Deep RL to dynamically and safely route AAM traffic. The scope of this work focuses on concept development for a dynamic and safe Air Traffic Management framework for AAM. The centralized component handles pre-tactical flight planning, whereas the decentralized component performs tactical low-level conflict resolution. Both components integrate RL and formal methods to ensure efficiency and safety. In the future, the proposed framework will be validated through a series of simulation experiments on a proof-of-concept prototype.

Document title: Federated Multi-Agent Mapping for Planetary Exploration
Abstract: Multi-agent robotic exploration stands to play an important role in space exploration as the next generation of robotic systems ventures to far-flung environments. A key challenge in this new paradigm will be to effectively share and utilize the vast amount of data generated onboard while operating in bandwidth-constrained regimes typical of space missions. Federated learning (FL) is a promising tool for bridging this gap. Drawing inspiration from the upcoming CADRE Lunar rover mission, we propose a federated multi-agent mapping approach that jointly trains a global map model across agents without transmitting raw data. Our method leverages implicit neural mapping to generate parsimonious, adaptable representations, reducing data transmission by up to 93.8% compared to raw maps. Furthermore, we enhance this approach with meta-initialization on Earth-based traversability datasets to significantly accelerate map convergence—reducing iterations required to reach target performance by 80% compared to random initialization. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach on Martian terrains and glacier datasets, achieving downstream path planning F1 scores as high as 0.95 while outperforming on map reconstruction losses.

Document title: Development of a Miniaturized 6-DoF Surgical Instrument with a 4-mm Elbow and 3-mm Wrist for Transoral Robotic Surgery
Abstract: Current platforms for Transoral Robotic Surgery (TORS) are suboptimal for confined oropharyngeal workspaces, particularly in pediatric applications. To address this, we present the design and characterization of a novel cable-driven robotic instrument providing 6 degrees-of-freedom (DoF)—shaft roll, elbow pitch/yaw, wrist pitch/yaw, and grip—for dexterous manipulation. The system integrates a miniaturized 4-mm proximal elbow with a previously developed 3-mm distal wrist. This architecture is enabled by a novel "sandwich" link architecture that facilitates high-density cable routing through the joint’s center plane, providing a compact, rigid alternative to traditional pin-jointed designs. Experimental validation identified significant kinematic coupling between in-plane joint pairs. An empirical real-time compensation strategy reduced this coupling rate by 82.9% for pitch and 80.8% for yaw. Workspace analysis confirmed the proximal elbow enables high distal dexterity at regions critical for complex surgical tasks. Integration with a Franka Research 3 manipulator enabled fully coordinated macro-micro teleoperation, providing a pilot demonstration for TORS workflows. This represents the first demonstration of a 4-mm elbow-3mm wrist mechanism for TORS, providing the hardware foundation necessary for future evaluation of dexterity-intensive tasks, including suturing and dissection.

Document title: Securing Customer Data and Tool-Using AI Agents in Retail Banking
Abstract: Banks have moved fast on agentic AI. Customer-support copiotos now read account histories, dispute managers call refund tools, and KYC assistants pull documents from third parties. The control assumptions that worked for chatbots do not apply to these systems, because the agent now exercises authority on the customer's behalf. We surveyed published prompt-injection benchmarks, OAuth gaps relevan to agent plaforms, and the regulatory expectations that examiners are starting to articulate. Three findings stand out. First, indirect prompt injection through retrieved documents remains the dominant attack path, and defenses based on input filtering miss roughly four in ten attempts in published evaluations. Second, current OAuth scopes are too coarse to express the bounded delegation an agent needs, which forces builders to grant broader privilege than the task requires. Third, the regulatory map (GLBA Safeguards Rule, PCI DSS 4.0, GDPR, DORA, NIST AI RMF, SR 11-7) has gaps for ephemeral, agent-issued actions. We propose a five-plane reference architecture with a three-dentity authorization model based on RFC 9396 Rich Authorization Requests, and we illustrate the trade-offs through scenario analysis on an account-services workload. The architecture is intentionally conservative, and we name the operational costs in Section VIII.

Document title: Feasibility Study of Programming Compliant Bimanual Tasks with Reasoning LLMs
Abstract: Programming bimanual robot manipulation in contact-aware environments is a complex process, requiring the simultaneous tuning of trajectories, coordination strategies, and impedance parameters. This feasibility study investigates the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) with reasoning capabilities to automate this workflow, moving beyond high-level planning to direct low-level controller parameterization. This approach is validated on two setups: Softbank's Pepper robot (hardware) and a dual-arm Franka FR3 system (simulation). It is demonstrated that reasoning models can generate a unified control policy, encompassing Cartesian trajectories, impedance gains, and coupling stiffness, from natural language instructions. This work provides a framework for reasoning-based code generation in compliant manipulation, feasibility results on physical hardware, and the first implementation of such compliant tasks on the Pepper robot.

Document title: AI-Driven Optimisation of Electric Vehicle Battery Systems: A Comprehensive Review
Abstract: The high rate of EVs adoption requires effective, precise and deployable battery management systems to optimize safety, life, and costs. This manuscript serves as a synthesis of the literature and addressed the topic of AI-assisted optimisation of Lithium-ion batteries. It includes research on state-of-health and state-of-charge estimation, and the forecasting of the remaining useful life, degradation modelling, thermal management, and smart charging plan. Various modern methodologies reviewed in this works are sequence models, such as LSTM, GRU, and 1D CNN networks, transformer and attention-based systems, hybrid physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and Neural Ordinary Differentiations (ODEs), ensemble training, and Bayesian uncertainty estimation approaches, and reinforcement-learning controllers to charging and V2G systems. In this compilation of modern literature, it is tried to emphasize the necessity of exceptionally well-defined experimental protocols, as well as the single systematic prioritization of standardized metrics and thus acceleration of the incorporation of well-founded and generalizable artificial intelligence paradigms into commercial electric-vehicle battery systems. The review is presented into major methodological groups, and in conclusion their relative performance is compared.

Document title: Design and Analysis of a Novel High-Extension Modular Manipulator for Dexterous and Confined-Space Operations
Abstract: Conventional rigid-link manipulators are ineffective in cluttered and confined environments, such as in-home assistive care or industrial maintenance, which require high dexterity and adaptability. Hyper-redundant manipulators (HRMs) offer a solution, but many existing modular designs lack full 3D maneuverability, particularly yaw rotation, and are limited by low extension ratios. This paper presents the design, kinematic analysis, and experimental validation of a novel high-extension modular HRM architecture. The manipulator is constructed as a serial chain comprising two novel types of parallel-link modules: a Bending-Extension (BE) module and a Bending-Extension-Rotation (BER) module. The integration of the BER module provides crucial yaw rotation at the module level, enabling full 3D motion and overcoming the planar limitations of similar designs. The 14 degrees of freedom proof-of-concept prototype achieves a high stretch ratio of 197.6% (extending from 581 mm to 1148 mm) while maintaining a hollow-core structure. We present the kinematic analysis of the individual modules and the complete manipulator, including analytical workspace evaluation. A prototype is fabricated, and its control system, based on resolved-rate control using the pseudo-inverse Jacobian. Finally, we demonstrate the manipulator’s practical viability by successfully performing a complex, confined-space assistive task: the raising and lowering of trousers on a mannequin.

Document title: GPU Accelerated Architecture for Robotic Coverage Planning With Dual Viewpoint Visualization
Abstract: Conventionally, the path planning for robotic inspection/survey of 3D structures has been performed offline (especially in the offshore marine industry applications). Operators (usually ROV or drone pilots) receive waypoints around a 3D mesh model of the structure, with no means to observe or adjust the resulting surface coverage interactively before the operation. The discrepancies in the estimated planned coverage and actual coverage have been costing significant time, money and resources to the industry stakeholders. In this paper, we present a GPU accelerated interactive planning system, using which the operator can select waypoints around the structure and adjust camera orientation while visually observing the coverage feedback updates every frame in real time. This enables the planners to plan waypoints yielding better coverage around geometrically complex structures and mitigate unforeseen gaps in coverage in real time. We propose a central architectural contribution of a decoupled dual camera rendering pipeline. The system consists of two camera views, where one camera evaluates per-triangle mesh visibility from the planned waypoint, while a second, independently controlled camera displays the resulting coverage coloring from the operator's freely chosen orbit viewpoint. Further, we propose an integrated coverage state machine that tracks coverage in three tiers namely, instantaneous, per-face cumulative, and global persistent coverage, enabling progressive “paint on” visualization as the operator steps through the planned path. The design thinking principles are integrated in the system workflow that enables auto or manual waypoint generation, face by face planning, per waypoint gimbal adjustment, hybrid planning and selective replanning without loss of previously finalized coverage. Visibility is evaluated by a CUDA kernel that tests each triangle against the rasterized depth buffer in a single parallel pass, achieving $36 \times$ to $48 \times$ speedup over single threaded CPU evaluation. Experiments on six real structural meshes demonstrate that the complete coverage evaluation pipeline executes in $\mathbf{1. 1} \boldsymbol{-} \mathbf{4. 7 ~ m s}$ per frame on a commodity desktop GPU, well within interactive rates. In a proof of concept study with one operator, interactive visual feedback enabled up to 71 % more coverage than blind automated planning with an identical waypoint budget.

Document title: ALIoTh: Orchestrating Multi-Agent LLMs for Autonomous IoT Penetration Testing
Abstract: Penetration testing in Internet of Things (IoT) environments, especially those composed of various different devices, e.g., smart plugs, smart cameras, and smart doors, presents great challenges across the phases of information gathering, attack surface enumeration, privilege escalation, and lateral movement. This paper introduces ALIoTh, a multi-agent, workflow-driven penetration testing framework that integrates Large Language Models agents within a Self-Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Self-RAG) architecture to autonomously identify and exploit vulnerabilities in IoT and Industrial-IoT (IIoT) environments. By leveraging state-of-the-art language models and orchestrating specialized agents via the LangGraph framework, ALIoTh dynamically plans and executes a full-spectrum offensive pipeline. This includes network, devices, and service enumeration, vulnerability assessment, payload generation, reverse shell deployment, and privilege escalation on each device. The Self-RAG mechanism equips expert agents with contextual access to IoT security knowledge, e.g., related documentation, tool manuals, and known attack techniques, enhancing their reasoning capabilities in scenarios involving multiple device exploitation and group policy manipulation.

Document title: A Logic-Assisted Hybrid-Mode Ising Machine Based on a 3D Topology for 3D Path Planning
Abstract: Path planning is a fundamental task in robotics, autonomous systems, and spatial optimization, in which real-time and energy-efficient computations are crucial. Conventional digital architectures exhibit limited parallelism when exploring large search spaces, leading to challenges in power efficiency, latency, and scalability. The Ising model offers a promising hardware framework for addressing such problems through energy-minimization dynamics. The spins that represent obstacles and paths in an Ising model update simultaneously, providing substantial acceleration in large-scale pathfinding. However, existing implementations are constrained by inefficient problem mapping and are typically limited to two-dimensional (2D) scenarios. To address these challenges, this work presents a CMOS Ising machine with a three-dimensional (3D) lattice topology for efficient 3D path planning, achieving a 91.3% reduction in transistor count compared with prior work. CMOS simulations verify that the proposed system correctly solves a 16 × 16 × 16 maze within 45 iterations, consuming 8.625 μW per spin and occupying 496.31 μm2 per spin.

Document title: Weighted Multiobjective Metaheuristic Optimization of PID-SMC for a 2-DOF Manipulator Under Torque Disturbances: MGO vs AHA
Abstract: This paper investigates metaheuristic tuning of a PID-Sliding Mode Control (PID-SMC) structure for stepresponse of a 2-DOF planar robotic manipulator under additive torque disturbances. The controller parameter vector is optimized using two recent optimizers, the Mountain Gazelle Optimizer (MGO) and the Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm (AHA), and is benchmarked against Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Ant Colony Optimization for Continuous Domains (ACOR). Optimization minimizes a scalar cost obtained by weighted-sum scalarization of multiple terms. All tuned controllers achieve stable step regulation for both joints; however, notable tradeoffs arise in overshoot and control activity. In the nominal case, MGO attains the best overall objective $(J(\theta)=120.071643)$ and achieves the lowest Joint 2 overshoot (20.32 %) compared with PSO $(42.90 \%)$, AHA $(40.08 \%)$, and ACOR $(28.75 \%)$. Under disturbance, tracking remains bounded for all methods, but the classical 2% settling-time metric becomes less informative due to the persistent excitation. The torque-norm plots reveal pronounced high-frequency switching (”chattering”), which is expected in discontinuous SMC implementations and is amplified by disturbance/noise. Overall, the comparative results support MGO as competitive tools for tuning PID-SMC controllers, while also highlighting the need for explicit chattering-mitigation mechanisms when implementing SMC in noisy/disturbed settings.

Document title: Visual-Language Foundation Models and Artificial Intelligence Agents in Healthcare: Bridging from Technological Innovation to Clinical Impact
Abstract: Recent advances in foundation models (FMs) have enabled artificial intelligence systems to acquire generalizable capabilities, with language and visual models demonstrating adaptability across diverse healthcare applications and multimodal vision-language FMs (VLFMs) supporting complex tasks such as report generation and question answering. Building on these developments, autonomous agents, particularly vision-language agents (VLAs), represent the next frontier, extending AI from perception and recognition to cognition, decision-making, and action. By integrating multimodal understanding with planning, interaction, and tool use, VLAs introduce autonomous intelligence capable of managing multi-step clinical workflows, adapting over time, and collaborating with clinicians. This survey provides a comprehensive perspective on VLAs in healthcare. We examine their current progress, analyze the major challenges hindering their integration, and highlight promising directions for future development. Unlike prior surveys that primarily focus on diverse FMs, our work prioritizes emerging VLFMs and incorporates agentic concepts, emphasizing their transformative potential beyond narrow research prototypes. Specifically, we (i) evaluate VLAs in terms of VLFM architectures and adaptation strategies and agentic design, (ii) assess their potential impact across diverse clinical workflows, and (iii) discuss pathways towards next-generation clinical decision support, considering technical and clinical challenges.

Document title: Research on Autonomous Inspection System for Warehouse Robots Based on Ros
Abstract: To address the requirements of safeguarding warehouse inventory, cutting down enterprise operational expenditures, and elevating both production efficiency and product quality, this paper presents a ROS-based warehouse patrol robot system and conducts systematic experimental validation on the developed platform. Firstly, the robot is capable of constructing a 2D SLAM map utilizing LiDAR sensors, thereby enabling autonomous patrolling throughout the warehouse environment. Secondly, the robot is integrated with a real-time alarm module and an autonomous positioning subsystem, which empowers it to detect anomalous events in the warehouse and transmit alarm information promptly. Finally, by integrating the $\mathbf{A}^{*}$ algorithm for global path planning with the Dynamic Window Approach (DWA) for local path planning, the robot achieves high-precision autonomous navigation and accurate positioning in complex warehouse scenarios.

Document title: Hybrid PID-Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Mars Quadrotor Attitude Control
Abstract: Mars aerial exploration is a core direction of deep space exploration, and the attitude control of quadrotor aircraft is the key technology to ensure its flight stability. However, the Martian environment with thin atmospheric density and frequent dust storms poses extremely high requirements for the stability and adaptive anti-disturbance capability of the control method for rotor robots. Traditional control methods such as Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) and Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) rely on accurate dynamic models and have poor adaptive capacity to unknown disturbances; pure Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) methods represented by Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) suffer from weak training efficiency and unstable random exploration in the early stage. For the trajectory tracking control method of underactuated quadrotor UAV, the coordinated position attitude coupling compensation is mainly studied. It improves the tracking accuracy under nominal conditions, but heavily depends on accurate dynamic modeling and assuming bounded interference. A fast nonsingular terminal sliding mode combined with angular velocity planning(FNTSM-AVP) is used for the full attitude control of quadrotor. It has finite time convergence and strong interference suppression ability in the earth environment. However, its performance depends on accurate parameter tuning and system dynamics knowledge. In contrast, PG-DDPG optimizes its control strategy online through reinforcement learning, thus maintaining stable control performance even when the model is imprecise. PG-DDPG can also gradually adapt to unknown disturbances through empirical learning and strategy optimization. Existing hybrid control methods combining PID and DRL mostly adopt fixed weight fusion and lack a smooth control authority transfer mechanism, which cannot well adapt to the harsh Martian flight environment. To address these problems, this study proposes a PID-Guided Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (PG-DDPG) hybrid control framework for Mars quadrotor attitude control. Inspired by the natural teaching behavior of gradual guidance reduction, a dynamic exponential decay weighting mechanism is designed to integrate the stable feedback of PID with the adaptive intelligence of DDPG, realizing a smooth transition of control authority from PID-dominated to DRL-dominated during training. First, a six-degree-of-freedom nonlinear dynamic model of Mars quadrotor is established with consideration of Martian gravity and motor dynamic response, and then the state-action space and a multi-component composite reward function are designed for the attitude control task. Finally, the framework is validated through both extensive simulation experiments and hardware implementation on a real quadrotor platform under simulated Martian disturbance conditions. Extensive simulation experiments and physical platform validation show that the rise time of PG-DDPG is 79% faster than PID, 37.5% faster than ADRC, and 21% faster than standard DDPG. The settling time of PG-DDPG is 46.8% less than PID, 35.9% less than ADRC, and 16.7% less than standard DDPG. For continuous disturbances, maximum attitude deviation was reduced by 82.4% compared to PID, 49.5% compared to ADRC, and 14.9% compared to standard DDPG, while recovery times improved by 95.8%, 75.7%, and 33.3% respectively. For transient impact disturbances, despite slightly higher peak overshoot, PG-DDPG achieved significantly faster recovery times (82.5% faster than PID, 34.3% faster than ADRC, and 12% faster than DDPG). The PG-DDPG approach demonstrated approximately 30% greater training efficiency compared to standard DDPG. The proposed framework provides a robust solution for Mars quadrotor attitude control and also offers a new idea for the fusion of classical control and deep reinforcement learning in complex aerospace control scenarios.

Document title: An LLM-Based Multi-Agent Architecture for Schema-Aware Data Mining in Intelligent Information Systems
Abstract: Heterogeneous operational data ecosystems often contain multiple event sources, registry tables, implicit join paths, and domain specific field semantics, making natural language analytical access difficult for non technical stakeholders. This paper presents an LLM-based multi-agent architecture for schema-aware data mining in intelligent information systems. The proposed framework transforms natural language analytical requests into grounded and executable computations through semantic intent classification, adaptive orchestration, registry driven dataset routing, schema-constrained join derivation, retrieval supported schema grounding, and controlled Python code execution. Unlike direct question-answering or text-only retrieval approaches, the system explicitly separates query interpretation, source selection, schema grounding, executable computation, and stakeholder facing reporting. The workflow is implemented as a stateful multi-agent architecture in which each execution step produces inspectable intermediate artifacts, including selected data sources, candidate joins, grounding context, generated analytical plans, executed code, structured outputs, and final responses. This design supports inspectable data mining operations over heterogeneous structured sources and helps reduce structurally inconsistent analyses caused by invalid source selection, missing bridge tables, or incorrect aggregation levels. The framework is evaluated on a proprietary urban parking analytics case study involving heterogeneous operational sources, including payment transactions, control events, enforcement records, spatial registries, and IoT derived occupancy signals. A 45 query benchmark is used to assess functional robustness, structured analytical correctness against gold artifacts, and answer level decision support quality. Results show zero crash cases, 40 execution successful runs, an artifact level gold-success rate of 71%, an answer relevance of 0.780, and strong clarity in LLM-as-a-judge evaluation (4.62/5). These findings suggest that schemaaware orchestration can support bounded operational analytics in the considered urban parking case study, while also showing that compositional queries involving time series, grouped ratios, and matrix-style outputs require stronger validation mechanisms.

Document title: SUBTA: A Framework for Supported User-Guided Bimanual Teleoperation in Structured Assembly
Abstract: In human-robot collaboration, shared autonomy enhances human performance through precise, intuitive support. Effective robotic assistance requires accurately inferring human intentions and understanding task structures to determine optimal support timing and methods. In this paper, we present SUBTA, a supported teleoperation system for bimanual assembly that couples learned intention estimation, scene-graph task planning, and context-dependent motion assists. We validate our approach through a user study (N=12) comparing standard teleoperation, motion-support only, and SUBTA. Linear mixed-effects analysis revealed that SUBTA significantly outperformed standard teleoperation in position accuracy (p < 0.001, d = 1.18) and orientation accuracy (p < 0.001, d = 1.75), while reducing mental demand (p = 0.002, d = 1.34). Post-experiment ratings indicate clearer, more trustworthy visual feedback and predictable interventions in SUBTA. The results demonstrate that SUBTA greatly improves both effectiveness and user experience in teleoperation.

Document title: Lite-Tracker: A Lightweight Tracking Flight Planner Considering Environmental Topology
Abstract: This article presents Lite-Tracker, a lightweight planning method that considers environmental topology on point cloud map tracking, minimizing memory and computational costs while ensuring tracking stability. Unlike existing methods, the proposed approach introduces a dual-layer environmental architecture that handles tracking at the topological level and obstacle avoidance at the point cloud level, effectively reducing computational time and memory consumption. Specifically, it constructs an incremental k-d tree (ikd-tree) directly on the point cloud map for tracking planning, significantly reducing memory requirements. In addition, extracting geometric structures from environment enables rapid generation of efficient tracking paths and enhances path stability through topological checks. Furthermore, global forward sampling is designed to rapidly generate spherical flight corridors. Additionally, a multiconstrained spatio-temporal optimizer produces trajectories efficiently with minimal cost. Benchmark comparisons and real-world experiments demonstrate that Lite-Tracker achieves the superior performance in terms of tracking stability, computational efficiency, and memory usage in complex scenarios.

Document title: LLM-Guided Task- and Affordance-Level Exploration in Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a promising approach for robotic manipulation, but it can suffer from low sample efficiency and requires extensive exploration of large state-action spaces. Recent methods leverage the commonsense knowledge and reasoning abilities of large language models (LLMs) to guide exploration toward more meaningful states. However, LLMs can produce plans that are semantically plausible yet physically infeasible, yielding unreliable behavior. We introduce LLM-TALE, a framework that uses LLMs’ planning to directly steer RL exploration. LLM-TALE integrates planning at both the task level and the affordance level, improving learning efficiency by directing agents toward semantically meaningful actions. Unlike prior approaches that assume optimal LLM-generated plans or rewards, LLM-TALE corrects suboptimality online and explores multimodal affordance-level plans without human supervision. We evaluate LLM-TALE on pick-and-place tasks in standard RL benchmarks, observing improvements in both sample efficiency and success rates over strong baselines. Real-robot experiments indicate promising zero-shot sim-to-real transfer. Code and supplementary material are available at https://llm-tale.github.io.

Document title: A Parallel Decoupling Self-Planning Search-Attack Algorithm for Multi-UAV With Reward Estimation
Abstract: This paper proposes a novel algorithm for multiple uncrewed aerial vehicles (multi-UAV) cooperative search-attack missions operated in uncertain environments. A parallel decoupling self-planning search-attack algorithm (PDSPSA) is designed to solve the uncertainty of the mission environment and the coupling of the search-attack. To this end, the proposed algorithm can be divided into four modules: a Beta distribution-based probability map module to obtain more information in uncertain environments, a distributed ant colony optimization algorithm (ACO)-based cooperative search module, a Dubins curve-based waypoints online optimization module, and a reward estimation-based parallel decoupling module. Therefore, the threat avoidance algorithm in the online optimization module is designed for possible threat areas and information exchange to update the feasible trajectory, and the parallel decoupling module based on reward estimation is composed of a short-term reward and expected future reward with a heuristic basis. Finally, the stability and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm are evaluated through both simulations and physical experiments. Its performance is further confirmed by comparison with alternative algorithms commonly employed in the multi-UAV cooperative search-attack coupling problem.

Document title: Mask-Scheduled Hybrid Locomotion of Wheeled-Legged Humanoids in Unified Whole-Body Control Framework
Abstract: While combining wheels and legs enhances robotic versatility, it introduces significant control complexity when relying on traditional explicit finite state machines (FSMs). To address this, this paper presents a multi-level mask scheduling strategy based on independent contact and rolling masks. By leveraging sequential mask scheduling, the proposed strategy generates decoupled planning references for continuous rolling and discrete stepping. These references are subsequently executed within a unified whole-body controller (WBC) formulated through Quadratic Programming (QP). Rather than relying on rigid constraints, our WBC actively resolves the dynamic coupling inherent in over-constrained hybrid maneuvers by reformulating contact constraints into soft tracking objectives. Extensive simulations and physical hardware experiments confirm that the proposed framework ensures robust stability and control continuity, maintaining reliable force distributions even during continuous contact point translations.

Document title: Hierarchical Zero-Shot Robotic Manipulation Framework in Unstructured Environments Via Semantic-Geometric Alignment
Abstract: Robotic manipulation in unstructured real-world environments remains a formidable challenge, primarily due to the inherent ambiguity of semantic instructions in human-robot interaction and the long-tail distribution of object categories. While existing end-to-end paradigms often suffer from limited generalization in unseen scenarios, conventional modular approaches struggle to effectively bridge the schism between high-level linguistic intent and low-level geometric execution. To surmount these obstacles, this paper presents Hierarchical Semantic-Geometric Planning (HSGP), a framework predicated on semantic-geometric alignment. Leveraging GPT-4o as the cognitive core, HSGP synergizes Grounding DINO and the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for open-vocabulary localization, while integrating GraspNet to establish a taskagnostic perception-action pipeline linking natural language instructions to physical execution. To mitigate semantic dissipation during instruction mapping, we introduce a ContextAffordance Reasoning mechanism. This empowers the cognitive core to explicitly extract fine-grained affordance prompts and enforce safety constraints derived from ambiguous directives. Furthermore, to reconcile the misalignment between geometric graspability and task semantics, we design a SemanticGeometric Alignment Scorer. This module formulates a joint optimization objective that synthesizes geometric stability with semantic fidelity, adaptively filtering for grasp poses that are physically robust and semantically consistent. Extensive experiments conducted in real-world tabletop organization scenarios demonstrate that our method exhibits superior robustness in handling unseen objects and complex instructions.

Document title: An ASCF Path Planning Method for a Hybrid Robot in Coating Inspection Scenarios
Abstract: To address heavy obstacles in narrow constrained spaces during coating inspection, this paper proposes an integrated path planning algorithm (ASCF), which fuses the Improved Artificial Potential Field (IAPF), Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), and Control Barrier Functions (CBF) for hybrid robots to perform obstacle avoidance and grasping. In the training phase, the joint potential keypoint-based improved APF serves as expert guidance to accelerate SAC's smooth convergence, and a staged mechanism develops a coarse collision-avoidance grasping model. In deployment, the model is integrated with a multi-point-constrained CBF-QP safety filter for emergency obstacle avoidance of the manipulator's scritical control points. Experiment 2 in two real-world scenarios show that ASCF outperforms APF+SAC, PPO, and TD3 in obstacle avoidance and task completion rates, guarantees safety constraints on multiple control points, and exhibits superior convergence and environmental adaptability. Its obstacle avoidance rate reaches 97.30 % in scenario 1 and 92.39 % in scenario 2, superior to the other three algorithms $\mathbf{ (9 0. 0 0 \% / 8 5. 9 3 \%, 9 5. 3 0 \% / 6 7. 6 8 \%, } \mathbf{8 9. 7 0 \% / 8 7. 8 8 \%}$ respectively).

Document title: Calibrated-Trust Orchestration: A Meta-Layer Framework for Coordinating Task-Level AI Agents Across the DevSecOps Continuum
Abstract: Generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) tools are being adopted throughout the DevSecOps continuum, yet current deployments remain fragmented: each tool operates on an isolated task, exposes its own ad-hoc confidence signal, and is trusted - or distrusted - by developers on the basis of anecdote rather than measurement. Recent industry synthesis has identified this fragmentation, together with the absence of a mechanism for recalibrating human trust in AI outputs over time, as a primary barrier to safe adoption of AI-assisted software engineering. This paper proposes Calibrated-Trust Orchestration (CTO), a meta-layer framework that sits above individual tasklevel AI tools and agents and governs the autonomy each is granted using a continuously updated, task-conditioned trust score. The score combines historical acceptance rate, humanoverride frequency, and a hallucination-risk proxy specific to each pipeline stage (plan, code, build, test, release, deploy, operate, monitor). Rather than treating every AI suggestion identically, CTO assigns each agent to one of three autonomy tiers - autonomous, suggest-with-rationale, or human-gated-and migrates agents between tiers as evidence accumulates. We present the formal trust-score model, the tier-assignment algorithm, an architecture for embedding CTO into an existing CI/CD toolchain, and a worked illustrative scenario showing how the framework would behave across a release cycle. The proposal directly targets two gaps identified in prior work: the lack of cross-tool coordination and the absence of a structured human/machine recalibration loop. We close with a discussion of validation requirements and threats to the approach.

Document title: Hybrid Membrane–Solenoid Valves for High-Flow, Precisely Controlled Soft Robotic Actuation
Abstract: Fluid-driven soft robots promise high-dimensional motion and cost-effective scalability, but their performance is constrained by the limited flow capacity of compact solenoid valves and the integration challenges of large membrane valves. This paper introduces a modular hybrid valve architecture that couples a high-flow membrane valve with an integrated miniature solenoid pilot. The resulting composite element achieves both high mass flow rates and precise electronic control while maintaining a compact, lightweight, and fabrication-friendly design. We present the design, modeling, and control strategies for these valves, and evaluate their performance through three experiments: tank pressure regulation, actuation of a weight-curling robot, and integration into a planar two-stage tossing robot. Across all cases, the hybrid membrane valves significantly outperformed solenoid valves, exhibiting faster pressurization and venting, higher bandwidth, and over a five-fold increase in mechanical power output. These results demonstrate that membrane–solenoid hybrid valves provide a scalable and integrable solution for overcoming the "piping problem," enabling hyper-actuated soft robotic systems.

Document title: Architecture of digital twin management and control system for production workshops driven by multi-agent collaboration
Abstract: Digital twin technology offers the feasibility of real-time control of production processes, significantly improving equipment health management, production process optimization, and resource scheduling efficiency. However, current production control still relies on manual experience-based decision-making, which is limited by response lag, strong subjectivity, and poor adaptability, making it difficult to cope with the multi-objective conflicts and dynamic disturbances in complex manufacturing environments. This research aims to overcome the bottlenecks of traditional experience-based control by constructing a digital twin control architecture driven by multi-agent collaboration, thereby upgrading the control mode from passive loss prevention to proactive intervention. This architecture comprises a physical perception layer, a digital twin interaction layer, and a multi-agent collaborative decision-making layer. The method agent is responsible for real-time response to disturbance events such as equipment failures and emergency orders, generating prioritized control plans based on case-based reasoning. The mechanism agent optimizes the system's anti-interference rules through deep reinforcement learning, enhancing system resilience. The resource agent strategically restructures production factors, forming a three-level adaptive closed loop consisting of instantaneous disturbance event response, short-term anti-interference rule iteration, and long-term resource reorganization. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed architecture is demonstrated by a case study of a conveyor jam.

Document title: A Hybrid Soft Asynchronous Actor–Critic Framework for UAV-Assisted IoV Task Offloading With Vehicle Trajectory Prediction
Abstract: With the rapid increase in computing demand for the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), the limited on-board computing resources have gradually become a bottleneck restricting the efficient processing of tasks. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), with their high mobility and flexible deployment capabilities, have become an ideal platform for assisting IoV task offloading. However, the dynamic environment and the mobility of vehicles pose significant challenges for task offloading and resource allocation in UAV-assisted IoV networks. This article proposes a soft asynchronous actor–critic (SAAC) framework with vehicle trajectory prediction based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for UAV-assisted IoV task offloading.
