Meanwhile, in order to solve RRT slow local update problem of exceeding dimensional scope and dynamic environment, designed a multi-level path planning architecture that combines the two of the global sampling and local replanning, and introduced the environment-aware pruning algorithm to effectively eliminate the redundant path redundancy caused by the obstacle change. The experimental results show that the proposed method improves the path success rate of RRT and its variants in dynamic obstacle interference.

Document title: LLM-Enabled Low-Altitude UAV Natural Language Navigation via Signal Temporal Logic Specification Translation and Repair
Abstract: Natural language (NL) navigation for low-altitude uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) provides an intuitive interface for non-expert operators and supports more accessible aerial services. However, deploying this capability in urban environments requires grounding often underspecified instructions into safety-critical and dynamically feasible motion plans under spatiotemporal constraints. To address this challenge, we propose a unified framework that translates NL instructions into Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifications and subsequently synthesizes trajectories via mixed-integer convex programming (MICP). Specifically, to generate executable STL formulas from free-form NL, we develop a reasoning-enhanced large language model (LLM) trained with chain-of-thought (CoT) supervision and group-relative policy optimization (GRPO), which improves syntactic validity and semantic consistency. Furthermore, to resolve infeasibilities induced by overly restrictive logical, spatial, or temporal requirements, we introduce a specification repair mechanism. This module combines MICP-based diagnosis with LLM-guided semantic reasoning to select predicate and temporal repair modes, while constraints assigned the no-relaxation mode remain hard in the subsequent optimization. Experiments on NL-to-STL translation, simulation studies, and real-world flight tests show that the proposed framework improves executable specification generation, restores feasibility through semantic repair, and supports safe, interpretable UAV navigation in complex scenarios.

Document title: An Edge-Enabled Intelligent Real-Time Feedback Control System for Industrial Robotic Arms
Abstract: Edge computing is changing the way industrial robots respond to their environments, making their movements faster and more accurate. An architecture that moves timecritical control tasks from the cloud to local servers so that managers no longer worry about signal delays or weak networks. By placing sensors, processors, and actuators in the same industrial cell, our framework delivers sub-millisecond actuation, greater fault tolerance, and steady performance whether payloads change suddenly or network traffic spikes. Motion plans are continuously refined through a closed loop that collects raw sensory data, analyses it on a lightweight edge node, and feeds adjustments back to the arm within the same computational cycle. A compact machine-learning engine running at the edge also flags anomalies and predicts upcoming disturbances, freeing operators to focus on strategic tasks. Tests on a six-degree-of-freedom industrial arm, controlled in a realistic production setting, show that feedback delay shrinks by up to 40 % and recovery from sensor faults takes almost half the time needed with standard Programmable Logic Controller. The solution upgrade brings the autonomy, speed, and safety needed by modern welding, assembly, and material-handling applications while meeting the strict timing deadlines set by safety standards. The proposed edge-enabled control system demonstrates significant quantitative gains over traditional architectures. It achieves a 40.7 % reduction in average latency $\mathbf{(} \mathbf{3. 2 ~ m s}$ vs. $\mathbf{5. 4 ~ m s}$ PLC), improves fault detection accuracy to 97.4 %, reduces recovery time by 49 %, and maintains low trajectory RMSE $(0.28-0.41 ~\text{mm})$ under varying load conditions.

Document title: Evaluating the Reliability of Self-Learning AI Architectures Through Multi-Domain Empirical Experiments
Abstract: Hospitals, banks and industrial plants are now using artificial intelligence systems where errors can cause major damages. Due to this fact, it is necessary to not only test the accuracy of these systems, but also the stability of such systems under the varying conditions. This paper reviews the reliability of self-supervised learning (SSL) models in three fields, namely, healthcare, finance, and industry, in a systematic SMART reliability framework. The technique integrates the analysis of structure of the system, the adversarial testing, the causal modeling, and the repetition of the experiments with varying random seeds to guarantee consistency in the results. Experiments with the ADNI, scSSL-Bench, and CableInspect-AD datasets indicate that the trained SSL models have a balanced accuracy of 93.0% and an AUC of 0.96 with domain shift and are also robust to adversarial noise. Nevertheless, the performance is reduced with low-data environments and when the domain changes are extreme. A hybrid cause-SSL model is more stable than the supervised models. The research presents a good reliability testing procedure and helps deploying the SSL systems with stronger safety in the real world.

Document title: Hybrid Contact Dynamics and Residual-RL Framework for Multi-Point Object Pushing
Abstract: Robotic contact manipulation involves applying controlled forces at contact points to guide an object along a desired trajectory while respecting the underlying physical interactions. This letter presents a novel framework that integrates dynamic modeling and Reinforcement Learning (RL) to achieve robust object pushing with a redundant robotic arm. First, a comprehensive dynamic contact model is formulated, incorporating unilateral constraints and a box friction model to capture the nonlinearities present in real-world contact dynamics. Second, the model is extended to handle multiple simultaneous point contacts, enabling effective trajectory planning and tracking for a redundant robotic arm in multi-contact pushing tasks. Third, an RL strategy is introduced as a residual module that augments a model-based controller to improve pushing performance. Simulation and real-world experiments with a Kinova Gen2 arm demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accurate trajectory following and stable contact interactions, significantly outperforming traditional PD control strategies in dynamic pushing scenarios.

Document title: Learning-Based Lane Selection and Driving Orders for Connected Automated Vehicles at Multi-Lane Freeway Merging Sections
Abstract: Cooperative control of connected automated vehicles (CAVs) offers a promising solution for reducing traffic congestion and accidents. However, existing optimization-based and search-based methods for trajectory planning and vehicle scheduling struggle with real-time multi-vehicle control. This paper introduces a hybrid bi-level approach that nests optimization modelling within deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to jointly optimize vehicle sequences, lane selections, and trajectories, providing a rapid, safe, and high-quality solution to enhance traffic performance at multi-lane freeway merging sections. Specifically, we approach the problem of lane selection and vehicle sequencing for multiple vehicles as a multi-step decision-making process. At the upper level, we design a DRL agent with an attention-based encoder-decoder structure that auto-regressively constructs driving sequences and lane choices. It generates a probability matrix to select the next passing vehicle and target lane based on prior decisions at each step. The attention mechanism enables the centralized upper level to adapt to scenarios with varying vehicle counts without the need to retrain. At the lower level, we formulate a model predictive control (MPC) planner to generate safe trajectories. The resulting travel delay guides the upper-level DRL agent learning to maximize overall traffic efficiency. Moreover, we introduce a leader-and-lane-specific credit assignment mechanism that leverages domain knowledge to link each action with associated travel delays. This mechanism enables the agent to accurately recognize the impact of decisions on total delay, enhancing learning performance. Simulation results suggest that the proposed approach’s superior real-time performance and scalability from several to over a dozen vehicles, making it well-suited for practical automated merging tasks.

Document title: AI-Powered Personalized Medication Recommender by Using RAG
Abstract: I believe that modern healthcare cannot afford to adhere to generalized recommendations since this usually results in ineffective treatment solutions and dangerous responses to medication- primarily due to the lack of consideration of the specific features of every patient. We are intending on the implementation of an AI-based Personalized Medication Recommender System, which will dynamically prescribe an optimised dosage and therapy plan using a state-of-the-art generative model known as RAG, to each individual. The fundamental approach will extract real-world and large-scale clinical data using MIMICIII and MIMIC-IV databases, authenticate the pharmacological knowledge using DrugBank, and conform to the international health standards using the WHO API. The difference here is the RAG architecture, which integrates the retrieval of factual information, such as with the use of such techniques as the vector based embeddings, and highly aggressive reasoning provided by finetuned large language model. This evidence-based framework will ensure the safety, evidence-based, and highly individualized nature of the recommendations provided by clinicians, and will offer a clear rationale behind each suggestion; hence, developing a strong foundation to a scalable and ethical clinical decision support framework.

Document title: Mechanistic Biocomputing From Canopy to Clinic, Plant Centered Review
Abstract: Computational biology blends mechanistic models with data-driven AI. In this survey, we focus on plant systems, with occasional pointers to human biology that were useful. We review four advances, organ-level growth models that allocate resources among leaves, stems, and fruit (e.g., GreenLab), whole-tree models linking physiology and form (e.g., L-PEACH), plant microbe models for nitrogen fixation (e.g., AMIGO), and AI workflows from high-throughput phenotyping to protein-structure prediction (e.g., AlphaFold). For each topic, we outline the core equations in plain terms, state key assumptions and identifiability limits, and give practical validation steps using open datasets, standard metrics, and simple ablations. We also clearly separate the survey from a forward-looking idea mimicking plant metabolism, which we present as future work, not a finished result. We end with concrete next steps: calibrating across scales, quantifying uncertainty, testing models across species and sites, and sharing reproducible pipelines that connect simulations with AI. Our aim is a tighter, clearer guide for both method builders and applied researchers. To bridge plant science and computer science, we suggest modeling plant metabolism mathematically. Such models mirror biochemical pathways, deepen biological insight, and open new avenues for algorithm design in computational biology. We argue that the convergence of computational biology and AI will advance plant science and, more broadly, benefit medicine, ecology, and environmental science. This paper summarizes the current state of the field and outlines a practical path for future work.

Document title: Multi-Robot Collaborative Interactive Obstacle Avoidance via Spatial-Cooperative Graph Neural Networks and Model Predictive Control
Abstract: Multi-robot interactive navigation in highly constrained and unstructured environments faces the dual challenges of high-dimensional computation and physical safety. To address the lack of strict safety guarantees in pure learning methods and the curse of dimensionality in centralized planning, this paper proposes a novel Imitation Learning-guided Hierarchical Interactive Navigation framework that decouples macroscopic scheduling from microscopic execution. The architecture consists of three layers: the top layer generates safe macroscopic preview trajectories via a cascaded planner; the mid-layer utilizes a Spatial-Cooperative Graph Neural Network (GNN), pre-trained offline via Expert Imitation Learning, as a distributed inference engine to output yield offsets and resolve spatial deadlocks; the bottom layer employs an optimization-based MPC controller to track the GNN-modulated reference while reducing constraint violations and improving local execution safety. Experiments in Habitat-Sim show that the proposed framework achieves an 80.0% task success rate and reduces the deadlock rate to 13.0% over 100 randomized constrained-navigation episodes, while still exhibiting a 7.0% collision rate in highly constrained cases.

Document title: Look Before You Reason: Hierarchical Verification and Self-Reflective Recovery for Remote Sensing Agents
Abstract: Tool-augmented multimodal agents are emerging as a practical interface for remote sensing (RS) analysis, where answering a query typically involves localization, counting, segmentation, unit conversion, and multistep reasoning over a tool chain. Current RS agents remain unreliable because planners ignore RS priors such as scene-object compatibility and ground sampling distance (GSD), intermediate tool outputs are consumed without validation, and no principled mechanism exists for repairing a failed step. We propose SR2A, an RS agent with three matched components. RS-aware planning injects geospatial priors. Hierarchical verification checks every tool output at pixel (PX), region (RG), perception-verification (PV), and global (GL) semantic levels. Two-tier recovery repairs failed steps through a deterministic rule patch, escalating to a model-driven correction only for residual semantic or stability errors. On the ThinkGeo benchmark, SR2A improves end-to-end (E2E) answer accuracy by 1.9 points and step success by 8.0 points over the ReAct-style agent under the same tools and controller while recovering 68.9% of initially failed steps.

Document title: From Automated to Autonomous: Hierarchical Agent-Native Network Architecture (HANA)
Abstract: Realizing Level 4/5 Autonomous Networks (AN) demands a shift from static automation to agent-native intelligence. Current operations, reliant on rigid scripts, lack the cognitive agency to handle off-nominal conditions. To address this, this letter proposes a hierarchical multi-agent reference architecture enabling high-level autonomy. The framework features a Dual-Driven Orchestrator that coordinates specialized Executive Agents, supported by a shared Public Memory for unified domain knowledge. A key innovation is the integration of agent self-awareness, which empowers the system to harmonize deliberative strategic governance with reflexive fault recovery. We instantiate and validate this architecture within a 5G Core environment. Case studies demonstrate that the system sustains critical throughput under congestion and reduces Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) by 86%, confirming its efficacy in unifying strategic planning with operational resilience.

Document title: Distributed Secondary Control for Voltage Regulation in Microgrids Using an Event-Triggered Communication Mechanism
Abstract: The emerging adoption of distributed generation in DC microgrids requires more complex secondary control schemes that can guarantee voltage regulation, power sharing, and less communication overheads. This paper introduces a dynamically controlled secondary control architecture of the coordinated voltage regulation of a number of distributed generators (DGs) under different conditions of power demand. In contrast to traditional time-based strategies, the given approach will only update the control actions if the predetermined triggering conditions have been broken, which will considerably decrease the amount of unneeded communication and control updates. The performance of the scheme is measured in two working conditions, which are constant power demand and load step changes. The outcome of the simulation shows that there is smooth convergence in consensus, stable voltage condition and sound transient operation in all DG units. Further, the initiation of activity is limited to short bursts, which proves the effectiveness of event-driven mechanism in reducing communication load but maintaining the stability and flexibility of the system. These findings confirm the suggested plan to be a credible and scalable solution of intelligent microgrid management of energy.

Document title: ReaAct: Bridging Robotic Reasoning and Action Generation Toward Real-World Spatial Generalization
Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a central paradigm for multi-modal robot learning, yet most frameworks rely on end-to-end mappings from visual observations to actions, limiting generalization even when adapted from pre-trained VLMs with strong multimodal understanding capabilities. To better leverage existing robot data for robust generalization and novel behaviors, we propose ReaAct, a unified VLA framework that integrates a multi-stage Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning mechanism, enabling a structured process from visual perception through language reasoning to action generation. The reasoning process is decomposed into semantic understanding, coarse trajectory planning, spatial affordance prediction, and fine-grained waypoint estimation, bridging abstract cognition with executable actions. To enhance spatial reasoning, which is critical for real-world deployment, we develop an automated Opeline that generates large-scale structured annotations and in-domain VQA pairs from robot demonstrations, reducing domain gaps and enabling spatial generalization without additional data. Experiments on the Astribot S1 humanoid robot show that ReaAct substantially improves spatial reasoning, transfers reasoning to action generation, and achieves robust real-world manipulation performance.

Document title: Activity-Based Costing Framework for Total Cost of Ownership Analysis of LLM Services
Abstract: The proliferation of Large Language Models (LLMs) requires robust financial planning, yet traditional software cost models cannot capture the unique economics of generative AI. This paper presents a formal Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) framework grounded in Activity-Based Costing (ABC). We deliver a dual-layered accounting architecture: a mathematically tractable, provably convex engine for technical infrastructure costs, alongside a comprehensive, modular taxonomy blueprint for human operational, governance, and organizational cost pools. The framework systematically incorporates LLM-specific cost drivers, including token consumption, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) operations, and agentic inference steps. To demonstrate practical applicability, the framework is subjected to a multi-faceted empirical validation programme: the technical infrastructure submodel is validated on a 12-month production RAG chatbot deployment, yielding a predictive formula that links high-level business metrics directly to infrastructure expenses with sub-5% forecasting error, and is further exercised on a second institutional deployment through a synthetically augmented dataset of 95,150 user sessions. Complementary cross-case scenario simulations—spanning regulated, high-scale API, and autonomous agentic regimes—together with hybrid local–cloud serving and retrieval-versus-fine-tuning comparisons, illustrate the framework’s structural generalizability across distinct governance, throughput, and multi-step execution regimes. By integrating time-varying vendor prices, stochastic uncertainty, and hybrid deployment extensions, this work provides a rigorous, transparent decision-support tool for the strategic financial management of LLM-based services.

Document title: Controlling Large Language Model-Based Agents for Large-Scale Decision-Making: An Actor-Critic Approach
Abstract: The recent breakthroughs in Large Language Models (LLMs) have given rise to innovative methodologies for addressing complex tasks. In particular, the incremental refinement of their common-sense reasoning and in-context learning capabilities has culminated in their seamless integration into the planning and decision-making architectures of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS), thereby yielding more general and effective solutions. However, as the number of agents increases, the issues of hallucination in LLMs and coordination in MAS have become increasingly prominent. Additionally, the efficient utilization of tokens emerges as a critical consideration when employing LLMs to facilitate the interactions among a substantial number of agents. In this paper, we develop a modular framework called LLaMAC to mitigate these challenges. LLaMAC implements a value distribution encoding similar to that found in the human brain, utilizing internal and external feedback mechanisms to facilitate collaboration and iterative reasoning among its modules. Through evaluations involving system resource allocation and robot grid transportation, we demonstrate the considerable advantages afforded by our proposed approach.

Document title: Safe and Energy-Efficient Trajectory Planning for Heterogeneous Multi-UAV Enabled Mobile Edge Computing
Abstract: Mobile edge computing (MEC) has recently gained significant attention as a promising solution for processing delay-sensitive and resource-intensive computational jobs. Existing system schedulers in MEC networks typically assume homogeneous service providers, uniformly distributed user equipment (UE), and identical service requirements, making them unsuitable for practical MEC scenarios where jobs are randomly generated with varying service and completion time requirements. Thus, in this work, we jointly optimize job scheduling and resource allocation in a heterogeneous multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) enabled MEC network, considering practical factors such as diverse service requirements of jobs, unknown distribution of UEs, and spatial-temporal job arrivals. We aim to reduce the overall job miss rate and the average energy consumption of both UAVs and UEs by jointly planning safe UAV trajectories and onboard resource allocation. To learn uncertain and dynamic UE-side states (e.g., job arrivals and mobility patterns) and ensure the UAV’s safety during the flight, we propose a multi-agent safe reinforcement learning algorithm that combines a Shared Soft Actor-Critic architecture for extracting features of heterogeneous UAVs and a two-agent Markov Game of Intervention mechanism for collision avoidance, named SSAC-MGI. In particular, SSAC-MGI further incorporates a fine-grained resource allocation scheme to improve onboard resource utilization and reduce job miss rate. Extensive real trace-driven simulations based on Alibaba cluster data validate the effectiveness and superiority of SSAC-MGI, compared with several state-of-the-art algorithms.

Document title: AI-Driven Therapeutic Robot Incorporating Amber-Based Contact Interfaces for Personalized Health Intervention
Abstract: The use of artificial intelligence in therapeutic robotics has created new opportunities in the provision of personalized health interventions. In this paper, the author proposes an AI-powered therapeutic robot which uses Deep QNetworks (DQN), a method of reinforcement learning (RL), to optimize patient-centered therapy dynamically by using amberbased contact interfaces. DQN framework allows the robot to continually learn best intervention plans by monitoring the responses of the patient in real time and modifying interventions like the level, length, and nature of the therapy according to the patient. Surface contact made of amber is bio-interactive and increases the sense of touch, facilitating natural interaction between humans and robots, which is essential to promote patient comfort, trust, and compliance. A cognitive model is also used to determine the behavior of the patient and this can be used to advise the DQN agent to take actions that will deliver maximum therapeutic benefits to the patient during the session. Both simulated experimental and real-world assessments indicate that the proposed system can be much more effective in-patient engagement, intervention accuracy, and the effectiveness of the therapeutic process in general than the nonadaptive robotic system used orally.

Document title: Quality Weighted Multipoint Depth Buffer Visibility and Coverage Planning for Robotic 3D Structural Inspection
Abstract: Robotic inspection of structures requires complete visual coverage of the target surface. This is critical, especially for 3D reconstruction applications. Most existing offline coverage path planners treat geometric visibility as a sufficient proxy for inspection data quality. Typical coverage path planners for robotic structural inspection evaluate visibility of a mesh element as a binary predicate (either seen or not). But geometric visibility does not automatically guarantee good data quality. This paper demonstrates that binary coverage systematically overestimates inspection quality. We identified following three sources of overestimation. Grazing incidence angles that reduce effective pixel density, large mesh triangles on flat surfaces that exceed a single camera footprint, and the absence of any mechanism to verify planned coverage against actual reconstruction data. To address these issues, we propose a quality weighted coverage metric based on the angle of incidence between the camera viewing direction and the surface normal of the mesh triangle. The metric is computed along with a multipoint depth buffer visibility test in a single GPU accelerated pass. This provides real time coverage feedback as operators create inspection waypoints. A verification architecture using registered dense point clouds detects coverage gaps and model to reality discrepancies during execution. Experiments were done on five different structural meshes (150 K to 6.2 M triangles) to measure the gap between binary and quality weighted coverage. It was found that binary assessment overestimates actual viewing quality by 2.7 to 7.5% (5.5% average) across meshes of varying size and complexity.

Document title: A Structured Method to Assess for AI Agent Compatibility
Abstract: With agentic AI systems, as AI agents that can plan, decide, and act on their own, become more practical, businesses are investigating how they can revolutionize enterprise processes. However, not every issue calls for the intricacy and independence of AI agents. Many would benefit more from straightforward AI models or conventional rule-based automations. In this paper, we present a comprehensive methodology for evaluating business scenarios to determine if they align with agentic traits. With agentic traits as its foundation, the proposed method provides a scoring mechanism, an agentic system architecture, and structured user prompt generation to collect context. This approach enables decision-makers to distinguish between scenarios that are better suited to conventional AI methods and those that are more suitable for agentic autonomy. To help well-informed decisionmaking, this effort also integrates responsible AI techniques, including PII redaction, transparent scoring, and explanations for every process step.

Document title: LLM-PD: A Large Language Model-Driven Policy Distillation-Based Method for Multi-UAV Path Planning
Abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has accelerated the adoption of multi-uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) systems in applications, such as urban inspection and emergency response. However, the effective path planning in dynamic environments remains challenging due to slow convergence, weak coordination, trajectory oscillation, and limited generalization. To address these issues, this article proposes a large language model-driven policy distillation (LLM-PD)-based method for multi-UAV path planning. By integrating LLM-based semantic reasoning with multiagent reinforcement learning (MARL), LLM-PD introduces a three-stage training paradigm—policy distillation, imitation pretraining, and reinforcement-based self-optimization—to enhance the policy quality and generalization. The problem is formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP). A teacher model combining a dynamic graph attention network (GAT) and a large language model (LLM) is designed, where the GAT constructs a dynamic heterogeneous topology of UAVs, obstacles, and targets, while the LLM performs semantic reasoning to generate coordinated expert strategies. A joint action evaluation mechanism further builds a high-value expert knowledge base. The student model adopts a hybrid imitation–reinforcement framework. Imitation learning (IL) first clones expert behaviors from the knowledge base to accelerate policy acquisition, after which a centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE)-based PPO stage refines the policy using interaction data, improving adaptability to wind disturbances and dynamic obstacles. This unified framework enables an effective transition from expert-guided learning to autonomous optimization. Simulation results show that LLM-PD substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in path efficiency, convergence speed, cooperative stability, and generalization. Ablation studies further confirm the complementary benefits of LLM reasoning, GAT structural perception, and the imitation–reinforcement integration mechanism.

Document title: CoCoPlan: Adaptive Coordination and Communication for Multi-Robot Systems in Dynamic and Unknown Environments
Abstract: Multi-robot systems can greatly enhance efficiency through coordination and collaboration, yet in practice, full-time communication is rarely available and interactions are constrained to close-range exchanges. Existing methods either maintain all-time connectivity, rely on fixed schedules, or adopt pairwise protocols, but none adapt effectively to dynamic spatio-temporal task distributions under limited communication, resulting in suboptimal coordination. To address this gap, we propose CoCoPlan, a unified framework that co-optimizes collaborative task planning and team-wise intermittent communication. Our approach integrates a branch-and-bound architecture that jointly encodes task assignments and communication events, an adaptive objective function that balances task efficiency against communication latency, and a communication event optimization module that strategically determines when, where and how the global connectivity should be re-established. Extensive experiments demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods by achieving a 22.4% higher task completion rate, reducing communication overhead by 58.6%, and improving the scalability by supporting up to 100 robots in dynamic environments. Hardware experiments include the complex 2D office environment and large-scale 3D disaster-response scenario.

Document title: VLION: Vision-Language Guided Interactive Object Navigation with Mobile Manipulation
Abstract: Object navigation for mobile robots typically assumes that targets are visible and paths are unobstructed. However, real-world scenarios often involve occluded targets like objects hidden behind doors or inside containers. Such scenarios require interactive navigation and manipulation by mobile manipulators. To address this challenge, we propose VLION, a vision-language model-guided framework for interactive object navigation (ION) that enables robots to locate and access such targets efficiently. VLION constructs a probabilistic occupancy map and dynamically identifies frontiers for efficient exploration. It leverages vision-language models (VLMs) to perform joint semantic reasoning at both the scene and object levels, generating Scene-Target and Object-Target Value Maps from egocentric observations. These maps are adaptively fused based on spatial entropy to guide target selection and dynamically balance navigation and manipulation priorities for multi-step decision-making. A hybrid A* planner ensures safe and feasible navigation, while star-convex manipulation regions enable interaction with objects. Extensive experiments in iGibson simulations and real-world environments demonstrate the effectiveness of VLION in zero-shot transfer and on-board deployment, advancing the state of the art in ION.

Document title: mCoT-VLA: Towards Robust Vision-Language-Action Models via Multimodal Chain-of-Thought
Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic intelligence by leveraging large-scale vision-language pretraining and diverse robot demonstrations to map perception to control across tasks. However, existing VLAs are predominantly end-to-end pattern learners that lack explicit reasoning and hierarchical planning, limiting their generalization to complex, long-horizon tasks. To address this limitation, we introduce mCoT-VLA, a VLA framework augmented with multimodal Chain-of-Thought (mCoT) reasoning. Specifically, the model autoregressively predicts intermediate subgoals in two complementary forms—visual subgoal images that depict the desired future state and textual descriptions that specify objects, relations, and intents—and subsequently generates action sequences conditioned on these subgoals. A hybrid attention mechanism is employed, where causal attention ensures autoregressive consistency in subgoal generation, full attention enables parallel decoding of action blocks, and a cross-modal alignment loss enforces semantic consistency between modalities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that mCoT-VLA achieves state-of-the-art performance, underscoring the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Document title: A multi-axis simultaneous motion controller design for a 6-axis articulated manipulator
Abstract: This study introduces a high-performance motion controller specifically engineered for multi-axis articulated manipulators. By harnessing the heterogeneous computing synergy between a System-on-Chip (SoC) and an FPGA, we realized a synchronous 6-axis motion control framework. This architecture employs the SoC as a specialized kinematic engine, delegating the execution of transcendental forward and inverse equations to the processing system. Simultaneously, the FPGA acts as a deterministic accelerator, facilitating concurrent closed-loop regulation of position and velocity for the entire multi-axis array. This distributed control strategy effectively decouples real-time kinematic computations from the PC-based host, which is then redirected to focus on high-level spatial trajectory planning. These planned trajectories are subsequently discretized by the SoC and streamed to the FPGA for synchronized execution, ensuring the end-effector meets rigorous precision standards.

Document title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Control of a Quadruple Tank Plant Under Partial Observability
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for controlling nonlinear and highly coupled dynamical systems, particularly in scenarios where accurate models are difficult to obtain. This paper investigates architectural strategies for deploying deep reinforcement learning controllers in strongly coupled Systems of Systems under partial observability, using the Quadruple Tank Plant (QTP) as a benchmark case study. A centralized Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient controller is first trained with full state information and evaluated in simulation and on a real laboratory-scale QTP. The control problem is then decomposed into decentralized agents with limited local observations, which independently generate control proposals. To coordinate these decentralized decisions, a supervisory reinforcement learning agent is introduced, learning to fuse and minimally correct the agents’ proposals based on partial system measurements. The proposed hierarchical architecture enables effective control even in scenarios where subsystem objectives are locally feasible but globally conflicting. Experimental results in simulation and on real hardware demonstrate that the decentralized–supervised architecture can achieve comparable or improved aggregate tracking performance relative to a centralized policy, while preserving decentralized proposal generation and enabling execution-time supervisory coordination under partial observability. The results also show stable sim-to-real behavior in the presence of sensor noise, actuator delays, and modeling inaccuracies.

Document title: Real-Time UAV Path and Role-Coordinated Planning Method for Emergency Communications via Hierarchical Optimal Control
Abstract: Cooperative path planning for UAVs using hierarchical optimal control is a critical technology for urban emergency communication networks. Existing methods typically decouple trajectory optimization from communication scheduling, which inherently leads to suboptimal performance. Attempting to solve the problem monolithically creates a large-scale Mixed-Integer Non-Linear Program that is computationally intractable for real-time deployment. Compounding this, current models often overlook the need for dynamic UAV role-switching, limiting the system’s functional flexibility and operational adaptability. We propose a hierarchical control framework that decomposes the problem into a dual-layer model predictive control architecture. Specifically, we linearize the original problem within a receding horizon control loop for long-term task and trajectory planning in the strategic layer. Guided by this, the lower trajectory layer employs non-linear model predictive control, solved via sequential convex programming, to generate real-time trajectories and perform adaptive role switching. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces mission makespan by 8.6% and increases the total data collected by 2.4%, validating its efficiency and robustness.

Document title: Design and Implementation of an IoT-Enabled Solar-Powered Pole Bot for Integrated Agricultural Monitoring
Abstract: Modern precision agriculture needs organized monitoring of soil conditions, crop health, and environmental elements so that choices may be made quickly and based on data. Several IoT-based agricultural platforms have shown that they can do things like measure soil moisture or recognize diseases in images, but most of them are still confined to single tasks and don't have multimodal analysis or the ability to move about the field on their own. This paper proposed a solar-powered Autonomous Pole Bot with distributed IoT vision nodes for smart agriculture monitoring and prediction to get around this problem. The system uses a multilayer IoT architecture that includes measuring pH and moisture, sensing macro- and micro-nutrients, detecting plant diseases using hyperspectral imaging, analyzing soil texture with near-infrared light, and monitoring the environment in real time. Adaptive multimodal fusion for crop recommendation and quantitative fertilizer prediction uses edge-level preprocessing and cloud-based machine learning. A solar management system that is aware of energy use may keep working for a long time in distant farming areas. Testing in real-world situations shows that the system can reliably classify diseases, forecast crop compatibility, estimate fertilizer needs, and use energy more efficiently. The suggested framework provides a scalable and self-sufficient IoT-based solution for precision agricultural applications of the future generation.

Document title: Hallucination-Aware Hierarchical LLM for Autonomous UAV Mobility Control: A Safe Reinforcement Learning Approach
Abstract: This paper proposes SafeGPT, a hierarchical framework that integrates generative pretrained transformer (GPT)-based large language models (LLM) with safe reinforcement learning (safe-RL). SafeGPT addresses the large-scale random multi-point tour problem (RMPT) for multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The target platforms are large electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) class rotary-wing UAVs. Such platforms suit wide-area logistics and infrastructure inspection rather than small drones. The hierarchical architecture enables scalable UAV coordination by centralizing strategic planning and distributing local route computation, mitigating the complexity issues of conventional methods. To mitigate LLM hallucination risks, i.e., the generation of plausible routes that violate physical constraints, a safe-RL method is implemented as a constrained Markov decision process (MDP) with Lagrangian actor-critic optimization, which promotes constraints on energy consumption, communication efficiency, and duplicate visits. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate SafeGPT’s performance advantages in battery efficiency, communication reliability, and travel distance across problem scales from 500 to 2000 waypoints. Even in demanding scenarios, constraint violation rates remain below specified thresholds. These results establish SafeGPT as an effective solution for large-scale UAV route planning, respecting operational constraints without compromising efficiency.

Document title: Research on Multi-Goal Path Planning Method Based on Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: To address the long-horizon sequential decisionmaking problem in multi-target robotic manipulator path planning, this paper proposes a hierarchical reinforcement learning architecture based on the Semi-Markov Decision Process. Through the decoupled design of a high-level meta-controller and a low-level execution module, the architecture introduces a vision-prior-based topological state space dimensionality reduction mechanism that compresses 3D spatial interference relationships into a discrete topological interference matrix, effectively overcoming the state explosion and sparse reward bottlenecks faced by traditional flat reinforcement learning. The low-level module reuses pre-trained residual reinforcement learning skills from single-target scenarios and achieves robust continuous control through information isolation and local subgoal guidance. Experimental results on a robotic simulation platform show that the proposed architecture achieves a relatively high episode completion rate for multi-target pick-and-place tasks, reduces the average total path length, and improves action smoothness, demonstrating the superiority of the hierarchical design in longhorizon complex manipulation tasks.

Document title: A Comprehensive Survey and Systematic Real-World Evaluation of Embodied Vision-and-Language Navigation
Abstract: Navigation is a fundamental capability of autonomous systems, yet most existing approaches rely on highly structured models and strong prior assumptions, limiting their robustness in open and uncertain real-world environments. Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) offers a promising direction by enabling robots to integrate natural language understanding with visual perception in a data-driven manner. Although VLN has attracted increasing research attention, systematic methodological taxonomy and real-world validation remain limited. This survey presents a comprehensive review of VLN research. Specifically, state-of-the-art methods are organized along two orthogonal dimensions: action paradigms, including hierarchical and monolithic frameworks, and model paradigms, including discriminative and generative approaches. A critical analysis of their respective strengths and limitations is provided. Additionally, we conduct a systematic real-world evaluation of representative VLN system configurations on a physical robotic platform. Experiments across ten diverse real-world scenes show a substantial performance gap between simulation and real-world deployment under the tested configurations: a representative monolithic RGB-only method achieves 61% success in simulation but drops to 22% in real-world deployment, while a hierarchical framework achieves a higher real-world success rate of 51%, suggesting stronger robustness in our evaluation setting. Finally, we highlight key challenges in perception, decision-making, and control that must be addressed in future research. Note to Practitioners—For practitioners building mobile robots that navigate using natural language commands, this survey provides practical guidance on selecting, designing, and deploying VLN systems. Our empirical evaluations in real-world environments indicate that architectural choices have a substantial impact on both navigation performance and operational safety. At present, hierarchical navigation systems that combine panoramic visual perception with explicit 3D sensing and decompose navigation into high-level planning and low-level control achieve more reliable task success and lower collision frequencies. At the same time, several practical limitations remain. Current VLN systems often struggle to determine when to stop based on the semantic intent of an instruction rather than simple distance-based heuristics. They also show limited robustness when faced with ambiguous or underspecified instructions that commonly arise in complex human-robot interactions. Continued advances in intent understanding, safety-aware reasoning, and real-world learning are expected to gradually enable more flexible and robust deployment in less structured settings.

Document title: Knowledge Guided Neural Network Task Planning for Generalization to Unseen Robotic Environments
Abstract: This paper proposes the use of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network architecture for High-level task action and location planning in robotic manipulation and navigation environments. We evaluated flat feedforward networks, Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for predicting both actions and target locations and compared their performance to symbolic planners based on the Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL). Experimental results demonstrate that LSTMs achieved a 95% success rate in manipulation tasks, significantly outperforming GRUs $(76 \%)$, and demonstrated strong generalization with $91\%$ accuracy in unseen environments. Furthermore, LSTMs reduced planning latency by approximately $3.5 \times(0.031 \mathrm{s}$ vs 0.109 s) compared to the PDDL baseline, validating its suitability for real-time robotic operation.

Document title: Natural-Language-Driven Mobile Manipulation for Autonomous Pick-and-Place Tasks
Abstract: This paper presents a unified control architecture for a mobile manipulator capable of performing automated pick-and-place operations in both industrial and domestic environments through natural language commands. The proposed system integrates SLAM-based navigation, deep-learning-driven object detection, RGBD grasp planning, and a deterministic language interpretation module within a cohesive ROS-based framework. The robotic platform includes a Robotnik Kairos+ mobile base equipped with a Universal Robots UR10e manipulator and an Intel RealSense D435i RGBD camera mounted on the end-effector. The perception pipeline leverages RGBD sensing by fine-tuning a YOLO11 object detector and combining it with a depth-based 6-DoF grasp generation approach using FGC-GraspNet. Experimental evaluation conducted in two realistic scenarios representing industrial and domestic-like conditions achieved an end-to-end task success rate of 73%. The results confirm the feasibility and robustness of voice-guided mobile manipulation in real-world environments.

Document title: Decentralized Hierarchical 3D UAV Swarm Coordination Using Hierarchical MARL and Graph Neural Networks
Abstract: The rapid deployment of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle swarms exposes critical vulnerabilities in centralized control architectures, including single points of failure and poor scalability. This paper proposes a decentralized hierarchical three-dimensional swarm framework integrating Hierarchical Multiagent Reinforcement Learning with Graph Neural Networks. The architecture decouples operations into three layers: strategic mission planning, cluster control for decentralized coordination, and tactical real-time navigation. Evaluated in PyBullet simulation across swarms of ten to one hundred agents, the framework achieves more than ninety percent mission completion with minimal collisions under stochastic disturbances. Empirical results demonstrate that Graph Neural Network-integrated coordination yields twenty-five times more efficient spatial awareness compared to non-graph baselines, while maintaining fault-tolerant task reassignment latency less than two seconds. Communication overhead scales sub-linearly, validating the suitability of the architecture for large-scale, resilient aerial deployments.

Document title: Convex-Guided Elastic Dynamical Systems: A Unified Framework for Stable and Collision-Free Motion Generation
Abstract: In cluttered and dynamic environments, robotic manipulators must generate collision-free motions that are both safe and efficient. Existing dynamical-system (DS) modulation methods offer strong reactivity but are prone to local minima near nonconvex obstacles, whereas convex-set approaches construct collision-free corridors that provide global guidance. However, these approaches often fail to preserve the structure of demonstrated trajectories or to generalize across tasks. This work introduces a convex-guided elastic DS framework for robotic manipulator motion generation that integrates global guidance with local reactivity. In the planning stage, demonstration trajectories defined at the end-effector level in SE(3) are elastically edited under convex-set constraints to generalize to new goals and task constraints. In the execution stage, a convex-guided modulation combines state-dependent modulation with corridor-direction guidance, enabling reliable convergence under dynamic disturbances while preventing convergence to local minima. The resulting end-effector velocity commands are tracked by an impedance controller for execution on multi-DoF robot arms. Simulations and real-robot experiments demonstrate safe and efficient performance in cluttered interactive environments.

Document title: An Application of a Universal Adaptive Learning System (UALS) to Adult Reading Comprehension Strategy Instruction
Abstract: This work-in-progress presents (Universal Adaptive Learning System) UALS, an LLM-powered multi-agent system designed to support the authoring and refinement of adult reading-comprehension lessons. Through an instructor-centered, human-in-the-loop workflow, UALS assists educators in generating adult-relevant texts, comprehension questions, dialogue-based instructional lesson scripts aligned with selected reading comprehension pedagogical strategies. The current prototype supports lesson authoring, module assignment, lesson simulation and analytics, and instructional adjustment. Ongoing development focuses on improving curriculum alignment, educator control, and the pedagogical quality of AI-generated materials. Planned cognitive labs, retrospective interviews, and expert reviews with adult literacy educators will examine the system’s usability, feasibility, and instructional value. This work aims to establish a scalable foundation for educator-guided, AI-assisted adult literacy instruction.

Document title: Design of a Target Localization and Manipulator Motion Planning System Based on YOLOv8 Binocular Stereo Vision and ROS 2-MoveIt 2
Abstract: In this paper, a hybrid real-world simulation motion planning system based on YOLOv8 and binocular vision is proposed. The system uses the YOLOv8 detection algorithm to identify objects and combines it with a binocular camera to obtain the three-dimensional coordinates of the target. The inverse kinematics of the manipulator is solved through TF pose transformation and ROS2-MoveIt2, and the joint angles of the manipulator are obtained. The experimental results show that the system can stably realize the complete closed-loop process from visual perception to simulation execution, providing a low-cost and reproducible technical route for the development, debugging, and method verification of the grasping system under the condition of lacking a real manipulator.

Document title: ANSI/RIA R15.08-1/2 and ANSI/A3 R15.08-2 Compliant Safety-Oriented Software Components for Industrial Mobile Robots
Abstract: Recent advancements in industrial robotics have led to the introduction of updated safety standards, including ANSI/RIA R15.08-1/2 and ANSI/A3 R15.08-2, which establish guidelines for Industrial Mobile Robots (IMRs). However, many aspects of these standards have not yet been explored in the context of IMR safety component development. This paper presents the design and integration of safety-oriented software components that align with these standards, with the goal of enhancing safety and efficiency of IMRs in intralogistics environments. We propose a multi-layer motion planning architecture, a planning and control framework for the manipulator, and a whole-body impedance controller that treats the IMR as a unified system. Additionally, we integrate components for robot intent communication, human perception, and human-robot spatial interaction to improve safety and user experience. Validation experiments in industrial settings demonstrate the effectiveness of the developed components in ensuring safe and adaptive IMR operation in shared and collaborative human-robot workspaces. The video demo can be seen at https://youtu.be/Zmt_1h1CSlE.

Document title: Trajectory Planning of a Mobile Robot Swarm Under Communication Interruptions: A Hybrid NLMPC and Time-Scale Theory Approach
Abstract: The increasing use of autonomous mobile robots in domains such as logistics, agriculture, and disaster management increasingly relies on cooperating robot swarms. However, most coordination approaches assume reliable and continuous communication between agents. In practice, communication channels are subject to interruptions, packet losses, and delays, which can significantly degrade performance and mission safety. This paper presents a hybrid approach combining ROS 2, Gazebo Classic, MATLAB/Simulink, and time-scale theory for trajectory planning and tracking of a differential robot swarm under random communication interruptions. The control strategy is based on a leader-follower architecture coupled with Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NLMPC) for the leader, while the followers maintain predefined positional offsets. Communication interruptions are modeled as discrete jumps within the timescale framework, allowing a unified treatment of continuous robot dynamics and discrete information exchanges. Simulation results show that the swarm successfully tracks the reference trajectory and maintains formation despite interruptions of varying duration and frequency, demonstrating the robustness of the proposed approach.

Document title: Optimizing Governance Sequence for Post-Disaster Recovery: A Multi-Scenario Genetic Algorithm Approach
Abstract: Organizations experience substantial delays in their governance processes because they need to arrange intricate decision sequences, multiple organizational levels, and secure executive authorization, especially during post-disaster recovery operations. The research creates a multi-scenario optimization system that combines agent-based modeling (ABM) with genetic algorithms (GA) to find optimal governance action sequences based on different institutional frameworks. Researchers use simulation outcomes and LTRG study data to establish three governance systems. These systems include a centralized model and two hybrid models that blend community leadership with resilience approaches. The research uses disaster governance literature and LTRG case data to establish empirical parameters that define agent conduct, system costs, and interagency relationship dynamics. The GA uses random sampling and self-adjusting search methods to maximize four critical performance metrics, which include recovery duration, administrative expenses, volunteer resource management, and regulatory adherence. Decentralized governance speeds recovery but generates non-compliance; hybrid models offer a balance of speed, cost, and regulatory strength. The research shows that adaptive governance sequencing methods combined with computational optimization help organizations create stronger institutions and develop better recovery plans.

Document title: Al-Based Simulated Auto-Trading Bot for Stock and Cryptocurrency Markets using Technical Indicators
Abstract: This paper proposes a new hybrid algorithmic trading The trading framework using Kaufman’s Adaptive Moving Average (KAMA) with FinBERT, a financial sentiment provided. model, and issue high-confidence buy/sell signals across equity and cryptocurrency markets. Unlike conventional strategies that static Simple Moving Average (SMA) crossovers, the pro- adjusts the sensitivity of its trend detection dynamically due to market efficiency, whereas a sentiment-gating mechanism removes signals that are technically correct but contextually unfavorable. We perform extensive backtesting on hourly price of Apple Inc. (AAPL) data and Bitcoin/USD (BTC/USDT) daily over a 12-month period using python libraries: yfinance and ccxt. It reached an ROI of $22.7 \%$ and max drawdown of $13.4 \%$, both being better than the SMA-based baselines for both assets classes. The architecture is fully modular, written in Python on Google Colab, and is planned to be used with broker APIs and deep sequence models in the future. The results offer a cross-asset and replicable validation of the effectiveness of adaptive multimodal trading strategies for academic research communities and practical applications in markets.

Document title: IAOM: An Intention-Aware Optimization Model With GNN-Based Policy Learning for Dynamic Multi-Robot Cooperative Task Allocation
Abstract: This paper studies dynamic multi-robot cooperative task allocation in multi-stage scout-rescue missions with unknown and evolving task demands. We propose IAOM, an Intention-Aware Optimization Model that encodes each robotś decision state–target task, role, and planner-derived ETA–as an intention vector and organizes robots and tasks into an execution-aware intention graph capturing residual demand and active commitments. A GAT-PPO policy is learned on this graph and coupled to a hybrid A* based motion layer, so that allocation, coalition formation, and congestion handling are optimized within a single framework. We evaluate IAOM on grid based urban rescue benchmarks with multiple map sizes and resource density regimes against optimization-, heuristic-, and learning-based baselines. Under abundant and normal resources, IAOM consistently reduces mission makespan and average completion time relative to the best baseline, achieving up to about 20% shorter makespan and about 50% lower completion time with comparable load balance. Under tight resources where robots barely meet total demand, gains are smaller and all methods are largely bounded by resource scarcity, but IAOM remains competitive. This paper was recommended for publication by Editor M. Ani Hsieh upon evaluation of the Associate Editor and Reviewers’ comments.

Document title: A Hybrid FL-MARL Framework for Optimal Trajectory Control and Resource Allocation in Integrated Terrestrial and Non-Terrestrial Networks
Abstract: In disaster-affected regions, damage to the ground communication infrastructure affects essential and critical services. In such scenarios, Integrated Terrestrial and Non-terrestrial Networks (ITNTNs), as envisioned by 6G technology, have the potential to ensure ubiquitous and resilient connectivity. A hierarchical ITNTN architecture, comprising High-Altitude Platforms (HAPs) and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), can support emergency communication and computational services. However, due to limited resources and constrained coverage, UAVs, along with HAPs, need to collaborate on dynamic trajectory planning and resource allocation to IoT nodes. Existing works in this area consider static conditions, limiting their applicability for real-time use cases. In this paper, we present an integrated HAP- and multi-UAV-enabled IoT network designed to maximize communication coverage and minimize latency and energy consumption for dynamic scenarios. We formulate a joint optimization problem for UAV trajectory and resource allocation, addressed by a two-stage learning approach – leveraging Density Peaks Clustering (DPC) to dynamically cluster IoT devices under different UAVs, and subsequently, a Federated Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (FL-MAPPO) algorithm to continuously optimize UAV trajectories and resource allocation. Simulation results demonstrate that FL-MAPPO with DPC outperforms the benchmark schemes, achieving a significant reduction in both latency and energy consumption of 13.32% and 15.95%, respectively, making it suitable for dynamic and real-time environments.

Document title: Edge–IoT Fabric for Zero-Downtime Predictive Fault Analytics in Sustainable and Resilient Manufacturing Systems
Abstract: The modern manufacturing facilities require continuity of equipment functioning to ensure the sustainability, productivity, and operational reliability. Traditional cloud-based analytics also bring about latency, bandwidth consumption, and slow fault mitigation making them inapplicable to real-time industrial monitoring. The given paper suggests an Edge-IoT Fabric of Zero-Downtime Predictive Fault Analytics, a combination of multi-sensor IoT industrial nodes and an edge-intelligent processing layer to provide early detection of anomalies and autonomous correction of faults. An edge-deployed hybrid lightweight learning model is a combination of Temporal Convolutional Networks and an Edge- Optimized Gradient Boosting classifier, which is used to assist the low-latency inference. The realistic assessments with 420 streams of industrial sensors show that it can predict faults with 97.6 correct rates, reduce planned stoppage by 82 percent, and save 28 percent of energy, as opposed to cloud-only baselines. The system has a high scaling rate, low communication rate, and strong prediction ability, which is appropriate in the next generation manufacturing that is sustainable and resilient.

Document title: Balancing Realism and Efficiency: A Comparative Review of Evacuation Models
Abstract: Recurring stampedes and crowd crushes around the world demonstrate the lack of predictive evacuation tools that can model human response under stressful situations. The review aims at the trade-off of behavioural realism and computational efficiency of microscopic evacuation models that bring together the advances of ABM, SFM, and CA with the hybrid and AI-based models. Although the Agent-Based models replicate the real behaviour of individuals, scalability is constrained due to computational limitations. In this summary, the developments between these paradigms are synthesized to provide an overview of the strengths and weaknesses to state an effective way forward. Significant areas of research are identified including the accurate calibration or modeling of models using real data, behaviour modeling, and multi-hazard modeling, particularly in high-density populations. The study suggests that, hybrid CA-ABM structures possess a good trade off, and a future research agenda to computational efficient, validated, and behaviourally rich models to realistic public safety planning.

Document title: A multimodal fusion-enhanced visual perception system for robotic tobacco leaf harvesting
Abstract: In response to the high-precision and high-robustness requirements of visual perception systems for tobacco leaf-picking robots in complex farmland environments, this paper proposes an enhanced visual perception system based on RGB-D multi-modal fusion. The core of the system includes a tobacco plant segmentation model based on an asymmetric dual-branch architecture, as well as two picking point localization methods based on traditional image processing and deep learning keypoint detection, respectively. The segmentation model effectively integrates the texture and color information from RGB images with the spatial structure information from depth maps through a local attention-guided feature selection module and a cross-modal global feature interaction module. The localization methods combine geometric constraints with end-to-end learning to achieve precise three-dimensional coordinate and pose estimation of picking points. Experiments on a self-constructed RGB-D dataset from real tobacco fields demonstrate that the proposed segmentation model achieves competitive performance while maintaining high inference speed, significantly outperforming traditional methods. This system provides a reliable technical solution for precise operations of agricultural harvesting robots in unstructured environments.

Document title: A Review of Active Collaborative Perception and Planning for Heterogeneous UAV-UGV Systems
Abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) offer complementary capabilities—wide-area aerial surveillance versus high-payload ground operation— making their coordination a compelling paradigm for complex real-world missions. Yet deploying such heterogeneous systems remains challenging owing to significant perceptual viewpoint discrepancies, tightly coupled decision-making, and constrained communication and computation budgets. Existing surveys address perception, planning, or control in isolation, leaving a critical gap in the systematic analysis of the full perception–planning– decision–control chain. This paper presents a structured review of UAV-UGV collaborative systems, covering cooperative architecture design, multi-source sensor fusion, active perception strategies, multi-agent planning and decision-making, and motion control. We further analyze key deployment bottlenecks under dynamic real-world conditions and discuss how large language models (LLMs) and embodied intelligence are poised to reshape the architectural paradigm of future air-ground systems.

Document title: XYZ robotic positioning of 3D microcomponents at the tip of an AFM cantilever
Abstract: This article deals with the realization of 3D and precise positioning tasks of components at the micrometric scale using robots. This scale is characterized by the predominance of surface forces that are difficult to predict, inducing huge challenges to accurately position two components. In this article, a hybrid vision-force robotic strategy is studied combining a planar positioning by vision associated with visual features and an out-of-plane positioning exploiting the real time measurement of these forces with an Atomic Force Microscope (AFM). This approach aims at achieving precise positioning in 3D and in a generic way because it can apply to a wide variety of components and tasks as long as one of the components can be mounted on an AFM cantilever. The experimental validation is carried out in a case study consisting of positioning nanophotonic components of a few tens of micrometers in typical dimensions. The results show that the proposed robotic strategy is repeatable and, to our knowledge, achieves a positioning precision of 23 nm along Z for the first time. This work opens unique and key perspectives in terms of material hybridization and component configurations such as possible out-of-plane positioning.

Document title: The Road Ahead: A Comprehensive Review of Recent Advances in Traffic Sign and Lane Line Recognition for Autonomous Systems
Abstract: The perception systems for Traffic Sign Recognition (TSR) and Lane Line Recognition (LLR) are foundational pillars for the safe and effective operation of Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) and fully autonomous vehicles. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of the latest academic research in these domains, strictly focusing on literature published from October 2024 to the present. The analysis reveals several key trends shaping the field. In TSR, architectural evolution is characterized by the refinement of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), the specialization of light-weight YOLO-based models for real-time embedded applications, and the emergence of hybrid CNN-Transformer architectures. Concurrently, a significant research thrust is dedicated to enhancing robustness against environmental adversities and a growing spectrum of sophisticated, physically plausible adversarial attacks. In LLR, the paradigm is rapidly shifting from 2D image-plane detection to full 3D spatial localization and topology reasoning, driven by Transformer-based models that excel at capturing global context and long-range dependencies. Cross-cutting themes common to both domains include a relentless drive for computational efficiency, a data-centric approach marked by the creation of new, challenging benchmarks for adverse conditions and 3D perception, and the nascent but transformative integration of multi-task learning and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to build systems capable of holistic scene reasoning. Despite significant progress, several key challenges persist in the field of domain generalization, particularly in handling long-tail corner cases and developing safety-aware evaluation metrics. Future research is expected to focus on self-supervised learning, stronger integration between perception and control systems, and the advancement of trustworthy AI through improved explainability and robust-ness. These efforts will lay the groundwork for the next generation of intelligent vehicle systems.

Document title: RO: Reliable Orchestration of LLM Programs via Deterministic-Generative Separation
Abstract: Failure analyses of multi-agent LLM systems show that the dominant failure mode is orchestration, not reasoning: across seven frameworks and 1,600+ execution traces, plan abandonment, state corruption, and tool-management errors dominate. We trace this to two coupled choices in current stacks: (i) the LLM is asked to perform deterministic bookkeeping (loops, state, control flow) and non-deterministic reasoning at the same time, and (ii) no program exists before execution-the LLM emits the next step turn by turn, so non-determinism leaks into control, not just data. We present RO (Reliable Orchestration), a storedprogram runtime for LLM workflows. A typed program $P$ exists before execution and is built from three node families: control & state, deterministic goal nodes (sandboxed code or MCP tools, auto-fulfilled by the runtime), and generative goal nodes (LLM oracle, bounded by an instruct-validate-repair (IVR) pattern with schema gating). The central invariant is precise: orchestration correctness is independent of LLM behavior. We show that the diagnostic controller for ITBench [1]-originally a 12,518-line Rust implementation-can be expressed as a 444-line RO program (a $28 \times$ reduction), inheriting its prior $7 \times$ Majority@k F1 gain over ReAct [2] while achieving $2-3 \times$ wallclock speedup from automatic concurrency.

Document title: Adaptive Task Allocation for in Forest Firefighting: A PPO-Based Hyper-Heuristic Approach
Abstract: To address the limitations of existing task allocation methods in balancing dynamic fire evolution with multi-type resource constraints, this paper proposes a two-layer prediction-correction collaborative task allocation framework. First, an initial plan is generated based on a fire-spread prediction model. A rolling-horizon strategy combined with real-time observations is used to trigger dynamic replanning. Second, to overcome the optimization difficulties in high-dimensional, time-varying search spaces, a hyper-heuristic algorithm based on proximal policy optimization is introduced. With this bi-level architecture, the high-level policy adaptively selects low-level rules and initialization methods according to the fire state, while the low-level layer integrates various dynamic multi-objective strategies to produce concrete allocations. The system computes deviations between predicted and observed states to activate closed-loop corrections, enabling a smooth transition from open-loop prediction to closed-loop control. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively coordinates heterogeneous agents for fire detection and suppression, improving swarm energy efficiency, response speed, and overall firefighting performance.

Document title: FA-MADT: Enhancing Offline Multiagent Reinforcement Learning With Factorized Attention and Decision Transformers
Abstract: Multiagent reinforcement learning (MARL) is a challenging issue in respect of scalability, coordination, and stability, particularly in the offline setting where exploration is restricted. Decision transformers (DTs) are an emerging technology in offline reinforcement learning (RL) for single agents by transforming RL into a sequence modeling problem, but their use in multiagent environments is not fully explored. In this work, we introduce factorized attention for multiagent decision transformers (FA-MADTs), new architecture that enhances coordination and sample efficiency, with design considerations aimed at improving scalability. FA-MADT uses factorized attention (FA) to model interagent dependencies and thus avoids the quadratic complexity of standard self-attention while preserving relevant coordination information. With the integration of return-to-go (RTG) conditioning, FA-MADT is capable of making trajectory-based decisions and thus performs well in long-term planning without the need for online exploration. Furthermore, behavior cloning (BC) regularization improves policy learning by preventing out-of-distribution (OOD) actions and enhancing the generality of the policy over different offline datasets. We evaluate FA-MADT on three benchmark suites—multiagent MuJoCo, the StarCraft Multiagent Challenge (SMAC), and multiagent traffic signal control—demonstrating consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines including MADT, TransMix, CQL-MA, and OMIGA. Our method improves coordination efficiency by up to 15%, reduces OOD action rates by 20%, and lowers memory usage by 12%. FA-MADT also reduces attention complexity from $\mathcal{O}(N^{2})$ to $\mathcal{O}(N\cdot d\cdot k)$ with $k\ll N$, supporting scalable policy learning. Additionally, BC regularization improves OOD action selection accuracy by up to 9.4% on the most challenging SMAC scenarios, contributing to more stable offline policy optimization. These results highlight FA-MADT as a promising step toward scalable and generalizable offline multiagent decision-making, with future work needed to validate its robustness in real-world systems involving noisy sensors and physical dynamics.

Document title: Energy-Efficient Data Offloading for Ultra-Dense Heterogeneous Vehicular Networks: A Multi-Population Mean-Field Reinforcement Learning Approach
Abstract: For ultra-dense vehicular networks, dynamic resource optimization among a large number of heterogeneous agents is rather challenging. This paper proposes a learning-based resource allocation scheme in a vehicle-assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) network, where the uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) and uncrewed ground vehicles (UGVs) are equipped with the MEC servers to provide the computational offloading services to the ground users with time-varying computing demands. Each self-interested vehicle jointly optimizes its trajectory planning and data offloading policies to maximize the expectation of its locally cumulative energy efficiency under the collision and energy constraints. We model the non-cooperative interactions among the massive co-channel vehicles as a multi-population mean-field game (MPMFG), where each vehicle constructs two types of mean-field terms to model the UAVs’ and UGVs’ population distributions, respectively. We propose a multi-population mean-field parameterized deep Q network (MPMF-PDQN) algorithm to solve the equilibrium among the vehicular servers in a discrete-continuous hybrid action space. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly enhances the average energy efficiency of the vehicles compared with the baseline algorithms.

Document title: Multi-USV Path Planning Algorithm Based on Distributional Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: To address the challenges of environmental perception uncertainty, stochastic flow field interference, and multi-agent coordination deadlocks in path planning for multiple Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) under complex and dynamic sea conditions, this paper proposes a collaborative path planning algorithm based on an improved Implicit Quantile Network (IQN). A dual-stream multi-head attention network is constructed, and a model incorporating a dueling architecture is designed. Furthermore, a velocity-aware adaptive Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) strategy is introduced, alongside a semi-cooperative game model based on a hybrid reward mechanism. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm exhibits superior adaptability and effectively resolves multi-ship path deadlock issues, thereby validating its efficacy.

Document title: RACER: Real-Time Adaptive Congestion-Aware Emergency Routing in Urban Vehicular Networks
Abstract: The smooth and efficient movement of emergency vehicles in congested areas has always been a problem in intelligent transportation systems (ITS). The conventional approach to routing, typically through static shortest path calculations, often fails to respond to dynamically changing traffic conditions, leading to avoidable delays in critical situations. In this article, we propose a new approach to routing, termed RACER (Real-time Adaptive Congestion-aware Emergency Routing), which dynamically responds to changing traffic conditions without requiring additional traffic-signal-control infrastructure, relying instead on congestion information obtained through standard vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) telemetry such as roadside units or cellular reporting, which we model in SUMO via its Traffic Control Interface (TraCI). This is implemented through a combination of a proactive multi-edge look-ahead approach, a congestion-aware cost function, and a controlled approach to rerouting, ensuring stability during navigation. The proposed approach is evaluated using the SUMO microscopic traffic simulator on two large-scale real urban road networks (Bhubaneswar and Visakhapatnam), across five source and destination pairs, three congestion levels (light, moderate, severe), and 20 random seeds, for a total of 1,200 controlled runs. Because emergency-vehicle travel times are heavily right-skewed, we report the median as the primary metric alongside the mean. RACER attains the lowest median travel time across all routes and congestion levels, improving on the strongest baseline in every route, and its median travel time remains essentially flat as congestion increases (372/395/385 s for light/moderate/severe), in contrast to static Dijkstra, which degrades sharply (993/1993/3321 s).
