Paired statistical testing confirms the improvements over all baselines are significant ( $p\lt 10^{-29}$ ), and measured wall-clock runtime confirms the method operates in real time. We further make explicit the vehicle-to-infrastructure communication architecture on which the method operates, and show that its bounded, cooldown-gated rerouting keeps the control-plane signaling overhead low (on average fewer than three route updates per trip), making congestion-aware routing feasible over capacity-limited vehicular networks. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of incorporating congestion awareness into routing decisions, leading to faster and more reliable emergency response in such congested areas.

Document title: Design of Smart Solar Panel Cleaning Robot
Abstract: The growth of photovoltaic (PV) panels becomes highly impaired by the presence of dust, dirt, and bird droppings on the panel surface and the solar energy has become one of the most significant renewable energy sources to power generation sustainably. Conventional methods of cleaning are either manual or labor intensive and ineffective in large-scale installations of solar. This paper proposes the design and construction of an autonomous solar panel cleaning robot combined with internet of things (IoT) that is an intelligent robot. The planned system is a dual-controller design with an ESP32-microcontroller that takes care of the robotic movement control and an ESP32-CAM-module that handles the real-time monitoring and captures images that show dust in the environment. The robot serves on the automatic, manual and intelligent cleaning mode so that it can maintain properness. The experimental assessment of this system proves that it is effective to eliminate surface contaminants, enhance the efficiency of solar panels, and ease the workload on the maintenance of photovoltaic systems, which is a scaling and cost-efficient solution to the task of maintaining photovoltaic systems.

Document title: EduQ (Educational Quadruped): Facilitating the Understanding of Theoretical Concepts through Hands-On Practice
Abstract: This work presents EduQ, an open-source quadruped robot designed as an accessible educational platform intended to support the reinforcement of fundamental concepts in mechatronics, robotics, and control engineering. The robot combines a lightweight 3D-printed structure, low-cost servomotors, and a Raspberry Pi–based control architecture with ROS 2 to enable real-time locomotion, inverse kinematics, and gait generation. EduQ supports multiple operating modes, including balancing, crawl, and trot, facilitated by analytical inverse kinematics and a PID-assisted stabilization system. A complete simulation environment was developed in Isaac Sim to allow students to test algorithms and validate motion before deploying them on the physical robot. An initial deployment of the platform, including assembly and operation by students with no prior robotics experience, demonstrates the feasibility of the proposed educational framework, while a formal quantitative evaluation of learning outcomes is planned as future work. The platform is complemented by comprehensive documentation, source code, CAD models, and user manuals to promote replicability in academic environments. Results from prototype evaluation confirm that EduQ is easy to manufacture, assemble, and program, making it a suitable tool for bridging theoretical coursework with hands-on learning. Its design and pedagogical orientation align with the objectives of Sustainable Development Goals 4 and 9 by promoting inclusive, high-quality education and fostering technological innovation.

Document title: Layered Safety: Enhancing Autonomous Collision Avoidance via Multistage CBF Safety Filters
Abstract: This paper presents a general end-to-end framework for constructing robust and reliable layered safety filters that can be leveraged to perform dynamic collision avoidance over a broad range of applications using only local perception data. Given a robot-centric point cloud, we begin by constructing an occupancy map which is used to synthesize a Poisson safety function (PSF). The resultant PSF is employed as a control barrier function (CBF) within two distinct safety filtering stages. In the first stage, we propose a predictive safety filter to compute optimal safe trajectories based on nominal potentially-unsafe commands. The resultant short-term plans are constrained to satisfy the CBF condition along a finite prediction horizon. In the second stage, instantaneous velocity commands are further refined by a real-time CBF-based safety filter and tracked by the full-order low-level robot controller. Assuming accurate tracking of velocity commands, we obtain formal guarantees of safety for the full-order system. We validate the optimality and robustness of our multistage architecture, in comparison to traditional single-stage safety filters, via a detailed Pareto analysis. We further demonstrate the effectiveness and generality of our collision avoidance methodology on multiple legged robot platforms across a variety of real-world dynamic scenarios.

Document title: Feasibility Study on Automating Composite Manufacturing Processes Using a Mobile Manipulator
Abstract: Manual composite layup processes are labor intensive and highly dependent on operator skill, often resulting in inconsistent quality. Although high-precision systems such as Automated Fiber Placement (AFP) exist, their use is frequently limited by high cost, fixed gantry architectures, and restricted steering capability on complex geometries. This paper presents a mobile dual-arm robotic system for semi-automated composite layup using prepreg strips. The proposed system is mobile and can reposition itself to access large or highly curved molds without dedicated infrastructure. The platform integrates structured-light 3D vision for pose estimation of deformable prepreg strips and mold surfaces, dual-arm manipulation for material handling, and hybrid force/motion control for compliant compression along non-planar geometries. The mobile base autonomously repositions around the mold to extend the effective layup workspace beyond the reach of a fixed-base manipulator. Experiments on a multi-angled mold show that the system maintains a nearly constant contact force and achieves stable layup quality across inclined surfaces of the mold. These results indicate that a mobile dual-arm manipulator can provide a cost-effective and adaptable alternative to traditional fixed-base layup solutions for composite manufacturing in flexible or variable production environments.

Document title: Constrained Behavior Tree Generation for Safe LLM-Driven Robot Navigation
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide a promising interface for mapping natural-language user instructions to robot actions, but unconstrained generation can produce invalid plans and unsafe behaviors when deployed on physical platforms. In this work, we present a three-level, defense-in-depth architecture that uses constrained behavior trees (BTs) as an intermediate, verifiable control mechanism for LLM-driven robot control. At the high-level layer, an LLM produces a task-level BT candidate in a restricted JSON format, limited to an allowed set of node types, actions, and parameter ranges. The candidate is then statically validated using human-defined rules, including schema checks and semantic safety constraints. Invalid candidates are rejected and re-generated up to a retry limit. At the mid-level layer, a BT interpreter executes the validated tree reactively using symbolic world-state updates and outputs motion primitives. A runtime safety monitor detects hazards such as obstacle proximity and execution stalls, overriding the command stream to trigger STOP or a safe fallback behavior. At the low-level layer, the system maps sensor data from the robot's perception into symbolic state features and converts motion commands from the upper layer into actuator control signals. Experiments in small-scale navigation scenarios demonstrate reliable task execution while enforcing user-specified safety constraints through validation and runtime monitoring.

Document title: Emulating Human-Like Cognition for Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Exploration in Unknown Hazardous Environments
Abstract: Autonomous exploration in hazardous and partially unknown environments presents critical challenges for multi-robot systems, including limited communication, environmental uncertainty, and the need for both fast reactive responses and long-term strategic planning. Inspired by the dual-system theory of human cognition, we propose a heterogeneous hierarchical multi-robot exploration framework that integrates a fast reactive system (expendable robots) with a slow deliberative system (local pivotal robot and a global brain robot). The global brain robot performs global reasoning, frontier detection, and optimal goal assignment, while local pivotal robots mediate task allocation and local coordination, and expendable robots execute real-time navigation and sensing. The system incorporates self-organizing communication and adaptive role reassignment, enabling resilience under partial network failures and dynamic hazards. Extensive simulations in structured and randomly generated environments demonstrate that our framework outperforms traditional centralized approaches in task success, coverage, and exploration efficiency, validating the effectiveness of combining cognitive-inspired hierarchy with self-organization for autonomous multi-robot exploration. Real-world experiments demonstrate our practical effectiveness and applicability.

Document title: A Policy-Aware Edge LLM-RAG Framework for Internet of Battlefield Things Mission Orchestration
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising interface for intent-driven control of autonomous cyber-physical systems, but their direct use in mission-critical Internet of Battlefield Things (IoBT) environments raises significant safety, reliability, and policy-compliance concerns. This paper presents a Policy-Aware Large Language Model Retrieval-Augmented Generation (referred as PA-LLM-RAG), an edge-deployed LLM orchestration framework for IoBT mission control that integrates retrieval-augmented reasoning and independent command verification. The proposed PA-LLM-RAG framework combines a lightweight retrieval module that grounds decisions in operational policies and telemetry with a locally hosted LLM for mission planning and a secondary JudgeLLM for validating user generated commands prior to execution.To evaluate PA-LLM-RAG, we implement a simulated IoBT environment using RoboDK and assess four open-source LLMs across controlled mission scenarios of increasing complexity, including baseline operations, threat detection, coverage recovery, multi- event coordination, and policy-violation requests. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework effectively detects policy-violating commands while maintaining low-latency response suitable for edge deployment. Gemma-2B achieving the highest overall reliability with 4.17 sec latency and 100% success rate. The findings highlight a clear tradeoff between reasoning capacity and responsiveness across models and show that combining deterministic safeguards with JudgeLLM verification significantly improves reliability in LLM-driven IoBT orchestration.

Document title: Learning Goodness Fields for Collision-Aware Robot Motion Planning
Abstract: Modeling collision structure in configuration space is essential for efficient manipulator planning, where sharp free–obstacle boundaries and narrow passages make geometric queries a major computational cost. This paper presents a unified comparison of three surrogate-modeling approaches for continuous goodness fields: Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) smoothing, Gaussian Process (GP) regression, and Radial Basis Function (RBF) interpolation. Using identical sampling budgets in a cluttered 2-DOF environment, we evaluate surrogate fidelity, boundary accuracy, sample efficiency, and downstream performance in A*, PRM*, RRT*, and Informed RRT*. GP surrogates achieve the highest F1, IoU, and lowest RMSE scores, providing sharply resolved boundaries and enabling consistently high planning success rates. RBF surrogates track GP performance but exhibit reduced confidence in free space, while FFT-based fields blur discontinuities and degrade planner reliability. We additionally study several goodness-guided refinement strategies and find that, in low-dimensional spaces with well-distributed initial samples, refinement yields negligible benefit compared to the choice of surrogate model. Overall, the results show that regression-based surrogates provide the fidelity required for robust surrogate-guided planning and motivate extensions to higher-dimensional manipulators and scalable hybrid models.

Document title: Switchable Neural Teleoperation
Abstract: Collecting demonstrations through human teleoperation is an effective approach for learning complex manipulation skills. However, challenges such as morphology gaps, control latency, and limited feedback make high-quality data collection costly and inefficient. In this paper, we introduce Neural Teleoperation, a shared-autonomy system that integrates human guidance with a robust grasping policy using a learning-based policy switcher. This hybrid framework allows users to focus on high-level planning while delegating fine-grained control to an autonomous policy when needed. Our system supports both immersive VR devices and lightweight 6-DoF controllers, making dexterous hand teleoperation more accessible. Real-world experiments across six manipulation tasks show that Neural Teleop increases success rates and reduces demonstration collection time compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

Document title: Gradient-Guided Prediction of High Manipulability Configurations for Potential Field Surface-Following Path Planning
Abstract: This paper proposes a computationally efficient motion-planning method that predicts locally high-manipulability configurations using manipulability-gradient information. The manipulability index is essential for maintaining stability and flexibility in constrained tasks, yet conventional optimization and sampling-based methods require iterative computation or large configuration-space exploration, making them unsuitable for realtime applications and tasks involving heavy data processing, such as point clouds. The proposed approach estimates locally optimal manipulability configurations by evaluating first and second order variations of the gradient, enabling prediction with only a few gradient computations. These predicted configurations are integrated into a potential field framework to generate motion that enhances manipulability while satisfying surface-following constraints. The method is validated through a surface-following experiment using a point cloud with a 7-DOF manipulator. Results demonstrate that the proposed technique achieves real-time performance within a 100 Hz control cycle and maintains stable contact forces, effectively balancing manipulability improvement and robust surface following.

Document title: Decision Accountability in LLM-Driven UAVs: A Privacy-Preserving Forensic Logging Framework
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being integrated into unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems to support mission planning, policy interpretation, safety assessment, and cyber–physical decision making. However, decisions generated by LLM-guided UAVs are often ephemeral, while conventional UAV logs mainly preserve telemetry, sensor measurements, control traces, and command records. These artifacts do not ordinarily preserve a structured and verifiable record linking a discrete decision to its retained context, selected action, temporal position, and integrity evidence. This limits accountability, forensic traceability, and regulatory auditability in privacy-sensitive operational environments. This paper proposes a privacy-preserving forensic logging framework for LLM-driven UAV decision systems. The framework introduces a compact DecisionRecord abstraction that captures decision semantics, temporal ordering, and integrity metadata in a model-interface-agnostic form. It also defines a constrained DecisionRecord′ representation under the P2 profile, excluding raw prompts, unrestricted reasoning, telemetry streams, precise locations, and complete candidate-choice lists while retaining selected evidence for post-incident investigation. Privacy preservation is operationalized as bounded data minimization rather than anonymization, PII detection, formal privacy protection, or resistance to inferential disclosure. Evidentiary integrity is protected using deterministic canonical serialization, SHA-256 hash chaining, and trusted checkpoint comparison. Evaluation using 200 deterministically sampled UAVBench instances produced  $0/800$  whole-field verbatim retention for the evaluated omitted source fields,  $1{,}400/1{,}400$  predefined evidence-group availability, and a 49.224% reduction in average canonical payload size relative to the canonically serialized source MCQs. Local verification detected all  $20/20$  independently executed record modifications and all  $5/5$  interior deletions. All five coherently recomputed suffixes passed local verification but were detected through mismatch with an independently retained trusted terminal checkpoint. Across 30 workstation executions, mean end-to-end record-construction latency was 0.563214 ms per record, and the complete 200-record chain occupied 220.795 KiB. The results establish benchmark-grounded feasibility for compact, data-minimized, and tamper-evident preservation of discrete LLM-guided UAV decision events. They do not establish decision accuracy, authenticated model identity, recovery of hidden reasoning, complete mission reconstruction, or onboard UAV performance.

Document title: A Dash of Pepper, A Dose of Care: A Context-Aware, Emotionally Adaptive, Intelligent Social Robot for Long-Term Medication Adherence
Abstract: Socially assistive robots are increasingly used in older adult care to address staff shortages and growing demand, providing cognitive, emotional, and practical support. However, prior approaches struggle to sustain long-term engagement and lack theory-based Behaviour Change Techniques (BCTs). This paper proposes a GPT-4o-powered system for personalized, context-aware, and factual medication support that integrates habit-based BCTs to promote long-term, autonomous adherence. The system integrates GPT-4o with a medical prompting framework, long-term memory via LangGraph, a tablet interface, and CNN-LSTM emotion recognition. Using context-dependent repetition theory, YOLOv5 object detection anchors reminders to daily routines such as meals and tooth brushing. Action planning and self-monitoring BCTs encourage reflection, while a decision-making engine reduces reminders as adherence improves. Evaluation of the system showed sub-2 second response times, routine detection within 20 seconds using object cues, recognition of six facial expressions, and medication dialogue that was factually consistent with information from MedlinePlus. By combining behavioural science with usercentred, emotionally adaptive interactions, this system has the potential to address key limitations in the field, laying the foundation for scalable socially assistive robots that promote long-term well-being in aging populations.

Document title: A CAD- and Chain-of-Thought-Based Robot-Teaching Dataset for Structured Manufacturing Task Representation and Verification
Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based robot planning is a promising direction for manufacturing automation, but the available learning resources are still dominated by visual observations, natural-language annotations, or action trajectories. These modalities do not by themselves provide an explicit, machine-readable account of manufacturing-equipment geometry, kinematic relationships, process constraints, and the rationale connecting a task state to a selected high-level action. This paper presents a CAD- and Chain-of-Thought (CoT)-based robot-teaching dataset for structured manufacturing task representation and verification. A reproducible semi-automated pipeline converts STEP models into STL and Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) representations, associates them with robot-state time series, and organizes the task rationale into four stages: Perception, Reasoning, Decision, and Execution. In this dataset, the Execution stage is a high-level action specification with expected preconditions and postconditions; it is not a joint trajectory, controller command, or direct robot-policy output. The dataset contains 120 CAD-based environment models, 360 robot-state sequences, and 480 instruction–answer samples, with a 25%/75% real/virtual composition. Four public 7B–8B-parameter LLMs are fine-tuned under identical quantized low-rank adaptation settings. Evaluation is limited to two representation-level tasks: URDF spatial question answering and CoT task-procedure consistency verification. In the full-data setting, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct obtains 99.71% URDF spatial-QA accuracy and 99.84% CoT-verification accuracy (1236/1238 decisions; precision, recall, and F1-score = 0.9985). These item-level scores quantify structured understanding and consistency verification and must not be interpreted as robot task-success rates. Component ablations show gains of 66.71 percentage points for URDF spatial QA and 53.94 percentage points for CoT consistency verification. The results support the dataset as a structured resource for explainable, traceable, and independently verifiable manufacturing-task representations, while end-to-end trajectory generation and physical task-success validation remain future work. The dataset is publicly available on AI Hub at https://aihub.or.kr/aihubdata/data/view.do?dataSetSn=71937

Document title: Design and Application of an Automatic Generation System for Primary Network Loss Reports
Abstract: This paper introduces a system that uses Robotic Process Automation (RPA) programs to automatically generate and verify primary network loss reports for provincial power grid dispatching, along with the design ideas, system architecture, and application effects of the relevant RPA programs. RPA tools are used to write scripts that automatically capture and format data from the electric energy acquisition system, and obtain supplementary data through automatic We-chat conversations with power plant data managers. The formatted collected data is used to instantiate a copy of the primary network loss report template to realize the automatic generation of the initial report draft. The node and branch balance rates are used to automatically identify missing data in the initial draft, and the data obtained via We-chat is used to supplement the missing data in the initial draft, thereby achieving the automatic generation and verification of the primary network loss report.

Document title: Comparative Hybrid Inverse Dynamics Identification Evaluation with Trajectory-based Evaluation of Jerk, Energy, and Time Completion
Abstract: This paper introduces the Inverse Dynamic Identification Model (IDIM) pipeline, a novel framework for predicting robotic joint torques. Our investigation focuses on the critical roles of signal conditioning and identification model selection, demonstrated using the publicly available UR3 dataset. We thoroughly explored the influence of three distinct acceleration estimation methods and various pre-processing strategies. The IDIM pipeline integrates ordinary least squares (OLS) with several machine learning regressors, including neural networks (NN), support vector regressors (SVR), gradient boost regressors (GBR), and Gaussian process regressors (GPR). Among all configurations, the OLS + Neural Network (OLS + NN) model achieved superior performance in the test data, obtaining a R2 score of 0.939, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.311, and a mean squared error (MSE) of 0.267. Based on these accurate torque estimations, we simulate and analyze the impact of varying joint speed settings on trajectory-level performance. Our evaluation considered total energy consumption, maximum joint jerk, and execution time in different speed scenarios, revealing inherent trade-offs in pre-planned robot operations. For example, increasing the joint speed from 10% to 90% of the maximum executed time reduces by more than 80%. However, this came at the cost of a ten-fold increase in energy consumption and a significant increase in jerk, potentially compromising motion quality. In particular, a mid-range speed setting (50%) demonstrated a favorable balance between efficiency and smoothness. This comprehensive investigation underscores the importance of integrating dynamic modeling with trajectory analysis to develop energy-aware and performance-conscious robot control strategies.

Document title: A Hybrid Path Planning Method for Mobile Robots Based on Adaptive Artificial Potential Field and Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: Path planning for mobile robots in complex environments remains challenging: classical artificial potential field (APF) methods suffer from local minima and oscillatory trajectories, while deep reinforcement learning (DRL) suffers from sparse rewards and inefficient exploration. Existing APF-DRL hybrid methods treat APF gain coefficients as fixed hyperparameters, which cannot adapt to varying local conditions. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a Critic-driven adaptive potential field parameter generation mechanism, in which a shared-backbone network with three output heads—Actor, Critic, and APF Parameter—dynamically generates the attractive and repulsive gains conditioned on the current state, establishing a bidirectional closed-loop between the potential field and the learning agent. Experiments on 50 randomized maps show that the proposed method achieves a 100% success rate and a smoothness index less than half that of the improved APF baseline, demonstrating superior reliability and trajectory quality.

Document title: Autonomous Sailboat Navigation: A Local Grid-Based Approach
Abstract: This paper proposes a hierarchical software architecture designed for the autonomous navigation of sailboats, specifically addressing the complex aerodynamic and hydrodynamic constraints inherent in wind-driven vessels. The framework employs a dual-layer mapping strategy: a persistent global occupancy grid derived from static nautical data is integrated with a dynamic local occupancy grid that uses Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) sensors to detect landmasses and maritime obstacles in real time. Navigation is driven by the Artificial Potential Field (APF) algorithm, significantly augmented with wind-aware obstacle avoidance logic. This reactive approach is benchmarked against A-star search (A*) and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) to evaluate path efficiency and computational overhead. To facilitate the transition from simulation to real-world deployment, the system features a robust validation pipeline and real-time visualization. This is achieved by broadcasting waypoints to OpenCPN via National Marine Electronics Association (NMEA) protocols and exporting mission data through GPX files for longitudinal research. By comparing local path-planning performance, this study identifies optimal algorithmic configurations for driving a sailboat, providing a scalable, deployment-ready solution for complex maritime environments.

Document title: Design of Robust 3D Vision Perception and Safe Interaction System for Collaborative Human-Robot Robots
Abstract: Current collaborative human-robot robots face the dual challenges of insufficient visual perception robustness and difficulty in ensuring dynamic interaction safety in complex unstructured environments. This paper designs a collaborative robot system integrating robust 3D vision perception and safe interaction decision-making. A tightly coupled perception-decision-control architecture is constructed: at the perception layer, a point cloud network integrating local feature aggregation and temporal GRU is proposed, outputting a 6D pose estimate with uncertainty metric; at the decision layer, a dynamic artificial potential field integrating probabilistic collision assessment is designed and embedded as a dynamic constraint into the model predictive control framework to achieve safe and smooth motion planning. Experiments show that the system achieves an average recognition accuracy of 94.8% in dynamic grasping and assembly tasks, maintaining $81.7 \% \text{mAP}$ even with 40 % point cloud occlusion; the success rate of interaction tasks reaches 95 %, and under sudden interference, it achieves an average response time of 85 ms and an average stopping distance of 52 mm, verifying the reliability and safety of the system in complex scenarios.

Document title: SA-DEM: Dexterous Extrinsic Robotic Manipulation of Non-Graspable Objects via Stiffness-Aware Dual-Stage Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: We propose a novel framework, SA-DEM, for extrinsic non-grasping manipulation of ungraspable objects in robotics. This approach is grounded in dual-stage reinforcement learning and decouples the overall task into two sequential phases: interactive mode decision-making and manipulation action planning. Notably, this framework innovatively incorporates the stiffness information of manipulated objects into the decision-making process, enabling the robot to autonomously perceive, decide, and plan manipulation strategies for objects with diverse physical attributes. The first phase of SA-DEM involves a high-level agent responsible for planning the grasping pose of objects and their interaction locations with the environment, based on the initial state of the objects, observations from environmental point clouds, stiffness representations, and prior knowledge of grasping regions. The second phase is executed by a low-level agent, which focuses on planning specific manipulation actions such as poking and flipping. These actions are derived from autonomous exploration during the training process, negating the need for manual customization. Both agents employ a hybrid discrete-continuous action space along with time-abstracted and spatially grounded representations centered around the point cloud, culminating in a unified actor-critic reinforcement learning framework. Note to Practitioners—By utilizing external resources like environmental contact and dynamic interaction, common low degree-of-freedom (DoF) parallel jaw grippers can achieve dexterity beyond their design capabilities. Existing research on extrinsic dexterous manipulation is often limited by constrained environments, manually designed meta-parameters, and specific interaction types, frequently overlooking the influence of object stiffness. This oversight results in methods designed for rigid objects facing challenges when manipulating soft ones. Our proposed reinforcement learning-based SA-DEM framework aims to address these challenges. Simulations and real-world experiments validate SA-DEM’s effectiveness in zero-shot transfer and generalization. This method enables non-grasping manipulation of objects with varying geometries, masses, and stiffnesses, relying solely on the planar and vertical supports provided by the environment. SA-DEM shows great promise for intelligent object manipulation solutions in applications involving low-DoF grippers, such as industrial automation, warehousing, logistics, and service robotics.

Document title: A Musculoskeletal-Inspired Virtual Shoulder Robot Model Based on a Parallel Mechanism Architecture
Abstract: Human shoulder complex facilitates a high degree of motion due to the interaction of many anatomical joints coordinating with each other; thus, it makes it to be one of the most biomechanically complicated parts of the human body. The design and analysis of shoulder rehabilitation robots require accurate modeling of this complexity; unfortunately, most of the current musculoskeletal models are either simplistic or analytically intractable and they do not apply to the development of robotic systems. In this paper, a Virtual 6 -4 Parallel Biomechanical Shoulder Robot Model (VBSRM), which is utilized as an anatomically based simulation of the human shoulder complex, is presented. The presented model has the parallel mechanism architecture, according to which the scapula is represented as a moving platform joined to the thorax with the help of six limbs, namely, fixed, passive and actively actuated constraints. The VBSRM is formulated in a kinematical way with the derivation of inverse kinematics and Jacobian relationship to describe the system motion. The model space that is feasible is then examined where the anatomical and actuator constraints are taken into consideration and motion is analyzed with reference to humeral abduction in scapular plane as an example of task. Those findings show that the proposed VBSRM can be used to achieve physiologically relevant shoulder motions characterized by smooth actuator profiles, which prove to be one of the reasons why the model is suitable to be used as a virtual biomechanical model of the shoulder and hence the design of a rehabilitation robot. The given structure is the basis of the future combination with physical shoulder rehabilitation robots.

Document title: Agent-Based Model for Auxin-Driven Development of Parallel Leaf Venation Pattern
Abstract: Addressing the projected global food security crisis driven by continuous Asian population growth necessitates improving crop photosynthetic efficiency, a goal tied to increasing vein density, a trait characteristic of highly efficient C4 plants and hypothesized to be an early step in photosynthetic evolution, with the process itself being strongly linked to the phytohormone Auxin (IAA). This study presents a multi-scale approach using an agentbased (intra- and inter-cell) model to demonstrate how parameter changes influence vein formation in an auxin-dependent system of parallel venation development. The hybrid agent-based model dynamically simulates cell differentiation: at the intercellular level, cells act as agents, and the auxin transport mechanism switches from up-the-gradient to with-the-flux when the cellular grid is saturated; at the intracellular level, auxin and transporter particles are treated as agents. A developed simulation interface allows for extensive parameter space exploration. Furthermore, BehaviorSearch integrated in NetLogo was used to optimize the model's fitness (mean final auxin level) by employing Genetic Algorithm and Simulated Annealing searches to replicate known biological phenotypes and validate emergent properties.

Document title: Demo: DetNet Packet Replication and Elimination for Resilience in 6G
Abstract: © 2026 IFIPThis demonstration showcases how integrating the IETF Deterministic Networking (DetNet) Packet Replication, Elimination, and Ordering Functions (PREOF) into the 6G architecture improves resilience and latency in an industrial scenario. Our setup connects two synchronized robotic arms via two disjoint and heterogeneous 6G networks, one employing a hardware-based and the other a software-based User Plane Function (UPF). Packets are replicated across both paths and eliminated upon reception, ensuring robust communication even in the presence of link or component failures. Additionally, latency is minimized as the receiver forwards the first arriving packet.

Document title: From Synchronized Testbed to MaskForceNet: End-to-End Force Estimation for Neurovascular Guidewires
Abstract: In robot-assisted neurovascular interventions, providing haptic feedback is crucial for preventing vessel perforation but remains challenging due to the physical constraints of integrating sensors into micro-guidewires. While vision-based force estimation offers a promising sensor-less alternative, existing studies predominantly target cardiac ablation catheters, overlooking the micro-force regime and complex deformations inherent to fragile neurovascular tools. To address this gap, we present an end-to-end framework for estimating 3-axis contact forces using catheter deformation. We developed a custom robotic testbed capable of acquiring synchronized multimodal data, pairing bi-plane video with high-precision ground-truth force measurements using a 0.035-inch guidewire. Leveraging this dataset, we propose MaskForceNet, a lightweight multi-modal architecture that fuses Siamese visual features from guidewire-centric segmentation masks with robot kinematic priors. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed segmentation-based approach significantly outperforms raw image inputs in terms of robustness against environmental noise, as confirmed by Grad-CAM analysis. The model achieved a high coefficient of determination for insertion forces, establishing a solid foundation for realizing real-time, sensor-less haptic feedback in telesurgery.

Document title: Balanced Collaborative Exploration via Distributed Topological Graph Voronoi Partition
Abstract: This work addresses the collaborative multi-robot autonomous online exploration problem, particularly focusing on distributed exploration planning for dynamically balanced exploration area partition and task allocation among a team of mobile robots operating in obstacle-dense non-convex environments. We present a novel topological graph structure that simultaneously characterizes both spatial connectivity and global exploration completeness of the environment. The topological graph is updated incrementally to utilize known spatial information for updating reachable spaces, while exploration targets are planned in a receding horizon fashion under global coverage guidance. A distributed weighted topological graph Voronoi algorithm is introduced implementing balanced graph space partitions of the fused topological graphs. Theoretical guarantees are provided for distributed consensus convergence and equitable graph space partitions with constant bounds. A local planner optimizes the visitation sequence of exploration targets within the balanced partitioned graph space to minimize travel distance, while generating safe, smooth, and dynamically feasible motion trajectories. Comprehensive benchmarking against state-of-the-art methods demonstrates significant improvements in exploration efficiency, completeness, and workload balance across the robot team. Note to Practitioners—This paper is motivated by the problem of collaboratively explore complex, obstacle-dense environments, such as disaster sites, warehouses, or large-scale industrial facilities. In practice, existing multi-robot exploration methods often lead to inefficiencies, redundant coverage, or an imbalance exploration load among robots. Our core innovation is a practical distributed planning framework that ensures robots dynamically balance the exploration load while efficiently covering the entire area. A novel hybrid topological graph efficiently constructs the relationship between reachable spaces and unknown exploration targets. A distributed weighted graph Voronoi partition algorithm guarantees the balancing exploration loads between robots in real-time. A local motion planner that provides safe and smooth trajectories. The performance and robustness of the proposed algorithm across different environments and parameters have been validated in multiple simulation and real-world scenarios.

Document title: Collaborative Robots in CNC Machining Cells: A Review
Abstract: Cobot-CNC cells are increasingly used for loading/unloading machines, probing and inspection, finishing and robotic machining. Their industrial deployment remains complex due to robot compliance, payload variability, calibration drift, process stability and safety constraints, which jointly affect perception, planning and control. This review organizes the literature according to a task-oriented structure covering interaction control, modeling and compensation, digital twins and virtual commissioning, monitoring, and artificial intelligence. The quantitative results are summarized and a comparative analysis of the methods with respect to reported performance and limits is provided in order to highlight the technical trade-offs, without claiming a unified frame of reference.

Document title: Distributed Task Allocation and Collaborative Obstacle Avoidance in Multi-AGV Systems
Abstract: This paper addresses real-time task allocation and path conflict resolution for heterogeneous agents in large-scale automated guided vehicle (AGV) systems within smart manufacturing. To overcome limitations of existing methods in dynamic and high-density environments, we propose a distributed market-based task allocation algorithm integrated with a cooperative multi-AGV obstacle avoidance strategy to ensure coordinated motion planning. A dynamic task buffer pool suppress system oscillations caused by frequent task arrivals. In addition, an incremental path caching mechanism is developed to reduce redundant computations during the 2-opt optimization process. The proposed Two-level priority mechanism effectively resolves multi-AGV collaborative obstacle avoidance and path conflict issues. Compared with existing approaches, the proposed method maintains robust conflict resolution among multiple AGVs while reducing task replanning frequency and computational cost. A standardized task allocation comparison framework is constructed to evaluate system performance under varying task scales. Simulation results based on real manufacturing layouts validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed hybrid algorithm. The results provide practical guidance for efficient task scheduling and collaborative obstacle avoidance in industrial AGV systems.

Document title: Standardization of a Multi-Species Plant Image Dataset for Improved Deep Learning based Classification
Abstract: Robotic weed identification and categorization have received immense attention in recent years because of their promising role in improving the efficiency and sustainability of advanced agriculture. However, deep learning models have proven their outstanding performance in classifying plant species in a complicated and varying setting. In this paper, a normalized and reliable image dataset with $\text{5, 5 3 9}$ RGB images of 12 different plant species is presented with an objective to improve the credibility and generality of deep learning models in classifying plant species. In this work, a normalized image dataset is comprehensively considered to remove varying effects during image acquisition. The performance of a normalized image dataset is tested using a pre-defined ResNet18 model and an advanced EfficientNet-B3 model presented in this manuscript. To assess the performance of both models, metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score have been calculated. Based on experimental analysis, EfficientNet-B3 performed better than a pre-defined model with an accuracy of 97.48 %, along with enhanced performance in terms of precision, recall, and F1-score, which confirms its superiority in terms of feature extraction and identification capabilities. The results highlight that standardization of dataset combined with an effective deep learning architecture substantially improves the performance in plant species classification. This work introduces a reliable benchmark dataset and an effective modeling approach for future research in robotic weed management, plant phenotyping, disease detection, and precision agriculture.

Document title: Research on Optimization of Emergency Building Evacuation and Cleaning in Multiple Scenarios
Abstract: This paper presents a multi-agent optimization framework for path planning and task allocation, defined in this study as the clearance, inspection, and operational processing of rooms or functional zones after occupants have been evacuated. with the objective of minimizing total mission completion time under priority and safety-critical constraints. The framework supports task allocation in structured indoor environments, The study quantifies four key factors affecting task execution, namely spatial complexity, room attributes, environmental risk, and agent resources, and converts them into computable parameters through quantitative modeling. The core methodology is a graph-theoretic optimization model for a baseline scenario. It represents the building layout as a weighted graph, where nodes denote rooms, corridors, and exits, and edge weights encode traversal and processing costs. By combining Dijkstra’s algorithm with the Hungarian algorithm, the proposed method achieves a minimum completion time of 6.57 min and an execution efficiency of 91.37%. The two algorithms also exhibit ideal load balancing, thereby validating the effectiveness of the divide-and-conquer strategy. To evaluate scalability and adaptability, the framework was further tested in six representative scenarios. Agent-scaling experiments revealed a diminishing-return trend. Specifically, increasing the number of agents from three to four reduced the completion time by 23.8% (from 17.20 to 13.10 min), while increasing from four to five yielded a further 16.0% reduction (to 11.00 min). Based on these observations, a scale-aware allocation guideline was derived for different environment sizes. The resulting hybrid framework balances solution optimality and computational efficiency by employing the Hungarian algorithm in small-scale scenarios and a Greedy algorithm in large-scale scenarios.

Document title: Do What You Say: Steering Vision-Language-Action Models via Runtime Reasoning-Action Alignment Verification
Abstract: Reasoning Vision Language Action (VLA) models improve robotic instruction-following by generating step-by-step textual plans before low-level actions, an approach inspired by Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning in language models. Yet even with a correct textual plan, the generated actions can still miss the intended outcomes in the plan, especially in out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios. We formalize this phenomenon as a lack of embodied CoT faithfulness, and introduce a training-free, runtime policy steering method for reasoning-action alignment. Given a reasoning VLA’s intermediate textual plan, our framework samples multiple candidate action sequences from the same model, predicts their outcomes via simulation, and uses a pre-trained Vision-Language Model (VLM) to select the sequence whose outcome best aligns with the VLA’s own textual plan. Only executing action sequences that align with the textual reasoning turns our base VLA’s natural action diversity from a source of error into a strength, boosting robustness to semantic and visual OOD perturbations and enabling novel behavior composition without costly re-training. We also contribute a reasoning-annotated extension of LIBERO-100, environment variations tailored for OOD evaluation, and demonstrate up to 15% performance gain over prior work on behavior composition tasks. The overall framework scales with compute (347ms at K = 10 samples) and data diversity. Project Website at: https://yilin-wu98.github.io/steering-reasoning-vla/

Document title: A Modular Underwater Robot Self-Reconfiguration Planning Method Based on Graph Isomorphism
Abstract: This article focuses on the problem of configuration generation in underwater modular robot systems. In this problem, a set of modules with different initial configurations need to self-reconstruct to form a specific target configuration in order to achieve the corresponding task objectives. This paper proposes a hybrid task allocation algorithm that combines graph isomorphism and game theory to address the problems of connection breakage and reconnection loss during self-reconstruction, as well as the challenges of center of gravity change and power source misalignment caused by topological structure changes. This algorithm approximates the search of isomorphic subgraphs to reduce the time and energy required for configuration generation, while maintaining the original topological connections of the robot as much as possible. On this basis, distributed motion planning is performed on the decomposed submodules, and their final allocation positions are determined while considering interference constraints between modules. The simulation experiment demonstrated the complete allocation process, and the results verified the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Document title: A Compliant Force Control Strategy for On-Orbit Assembly: Design, Implementation, and Reinforcement Learning-Based Optimization
Abstract: On-orbit assembly of large-scale space structures is critical for future space missions, yet it poses significant challenges for robotic systems. A fundamental difficulty in tasks like docking, which are highly contact-rich, lies in achieving both high precision and compliant force control to prevent damage. This trade-off between accuracy and safety is difficult to resolve using conventional methods. Furthermore, the development of advanced solutions is constrained by the scarcity of high-fidelity ground testbeds capable of emulating the complex contact dynamics of walking and docking. To address these issues, this letter presents a comprehensive system-level solution. First, a novel seven-degree-of-freedom walking and assembly integrated robotic platform, along with a high-load-bearing docking interface, is developed to facilitate practical verification. Second, based on this platform, a novel hybrid compliant control framework is proposed, which integrates a low-level impedance controller with a high-level Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (MBRL) planner. Unlike passive compliance schemes, the MBRL agent leverages a learned dynamics model to predict interaction forces and proactively generate corrective force trajectory commands. This hierarchical architecture allows the system to accommodate geometric uncertainties and maintain continuous contact without triggering excessive force spikes. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Compared to traditional impedance control, the hybrid control strategy significantly reduces contact forces during docking while achieving a final high assembly accuracy. This work demonstrates a viable system-level solution, from hardware design to intelligent control, for advancing robotic on-orbit assembly.

Document title: Sensor-Based Robot Path Planning Using Simulation and Vision Feedback for Industrial Surface Processing
Abstract: Industrial robots performing surface processing tasks like painting and polishing require complete and efficient path coverage plan. These paths must accommodate variations in workpiece geometry and obstacle placement. Traditional per-programmed trajectories lack flexibility when the environment fluctuates leading to the integration of sensor feedback while planning paths. This paper presents a hybrid approach that combines simulation-based path planning analysis with experimental vision-based trajectory generation. Grid-based coverage path planning strategies like left-to-right and zig-zag methods are used in the simulation phase. These strategies are quantitatively evaluated in ABB RobotStudio using the virtual line sensors to emulate obstacle detection and performance is assessed by varying robot speeds, obstacle spacing and density, and motion continuity constraints. In the experimental phase, vision-driven pipeline is developed using a Universal Robots UR10e collaborative robot equipped with a SICK Ranger vision sensor. Canny edge detection and contour extraction are applied to two-dimensional workpiece images to generate boundary-based trajectories which are communicated to robot for execution. The study provides quantitative insight into execution time trade-offs between traversal strategies in simulation, including a previously unreported non-monotic relationship between motion continuity zone size and strategy performace gap, and experimentally validates feasibility of sensor-guided trajectory generation on real robotic hardware. The work espablishes a validated baseline pipeline for 2D vision-guided path generation and proposes a concrete roadmap towards 3D-aware adaptive coverage for non-planar industrial workpieces.

Document title: AGRIROBO: An AI and IoT-Enabled Robotic Framework for Smart and Sustainable Farming
Abstract: Crop productivity is often affected by plant diseases, particularly when symptoms are not identified at an early stage and pesticides are applied inefficiently. These factors can result in significant yield loss and increased agricultural costs. To address this issue, this paper proposes AgriRobo, a locally deployed autonomous robotic system that utilizes edge-AI techniques for real-time crop disease detection and precision spraying. The system integrates a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Pi Camera for capturing leaf images, while a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) developed using Python and TensorFlow/Keras performs disease classification. To maintain efficient processing without relying on internet connectivity, model inference is executed on a local personal computer. Robot movement is controlled using an ESP32 microcontroller interfaced with an L298 motor driver, enabling systematic navigation through crop rows. When a diseased plant is detected, a relay-controlled water pump connected to the Raspberry Pi automatically activates to spray treatment only on the affected area. Experimental evaluation shows that the trained CNN model demonstrating reliable detection performance. By integrating computer vision, embedded control, and robotic automation within a fully local architecture, the proposed system reduces manual monitoring effort, minimizes excessive chemical usage, and enables lowlatency operation.

Document title: Design, Optimization, and Experimental Validation of a 3-DOF Parallel Robotic Ankle Based on a 2SPU-1RU Architecture
Abstract: This paper presents the design, implementation, and experimental validation of a 3-degree-of-freedom (3-DOF) parallel robotic ankle based on a 2SPU-1RU (two Spherical-Prismatic-Universal kinematic chains and one Revolute-Universal kinematic chain) architecture for transtibial prosthesis applications. The proposed design aims to replicate the complex kinematics of the human ankle across the sagittal, frontal, and transverse planes, addressing the limitations of conventional prosthetic ankles, which typically offer reduced mobility. The system was developed in accordance with ISO 10328:2016 load requirements (P4 level) and incorporates a parallel mechanism that enhances structural rigidity. A comprehensive methodology, including CAD modeling, kinematic simulation, finite element analysis (FEA), and electronic system integration, was implemented. Structural analysis results showed a maximum Von Mises stress of 193.2 MPa and a safety factor of 2.17, ensuring operation within elastic limits. The prototype, fabricated using 3D printing (PLA), integrates linear actuators, a servomotor, and a sensing system with closed-loop PID control. Experimental validation under noload conditions demonstrated that the system achieved clinically relevant ranges of motion, including 41.0° of plantarflexion, 16.5° of dorsiflexion, 26.1° of inversion, and 12.4° of eversion. The maximum angular deviation with respect to target values was 3.5°, confirming high kinematic fidelity. These results show the feasibility of the 2SPU-1RU configuration as a compact, efficient solution for advanced ankle prostheses, with potential for future integration into functional assistive devices.

Document title: Robotic Full-Coverage Path Planning and Local Path Tracking Control for Cleaning in Complex Environments
Abstract: To address the issues of fragmented paths, frequent turning, and missed coverage caused by conservative obstacle avoidance in complete-coverage path planning (CCPP) for cleaning robots in complex environments with static obstacles, this paper proposes a collaborative navigation framework that integrates global coverage planning and local tracking control into a unified architecture. At the global planning level, mechanisms including region decomposition and merging, optimal coverage direction selection and maintenance, an obstacle-crossing strategy, and an improved dead-zone escape mechanism are introduced based on the Bio-inspired Neural Network (BINN) to enhance coverage quality. Specifically, the region decomposition and merging, combined with the optimal direction selection mechanism, ensure regular coverage along the optimal direction within each sub-region. Furthermore, by relying on the local layer’s autonomous obstacle avoidance capability, the obstacle-crossing strategy intentionally ignores minor obstacles to prevent interference with neural activity caused by avoidance maneuvers, thereby avoiding subsequent tortuous paths and frequent turns, which further enhances overall operational efficiency. At the local planning level, a dual-layer controller architecture is developed. A local path controller fusing Model Predictive Control (MPC) and the Dynamic Window Approach (DWA) achieves high-precision path tracking and collision detection. When a collision risk is detected, a local path replanner re-optimizes the global path segments to enable minimal-amplitude, edge-following obstacle avoidance and rapid return to the global path, thereby preventing under-coverage and redundant coverage caused by excessive detouring. Simulation and real-world experiments conducted in a courtyard environment demonstrate that the redundant coverage rate in global planning is reduced to 7.01%, outperforming traditional methods in total path length and accumulated turning angles. For local planning, the Integral of Absolute Error (IAE) is 18.3296, which is 26.12% and 27.15% lower than those of the Timed Elastic Band (TEB) and DWA algorithms, respectively, while achieving a coverage rate of 91.16%. Furthermore, the overall discrepancy between real-world and simulation results is within 6%, validating the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method for practical cleaning tasks.

Document title: A Comparative RAG Agent vs. Base LLM for Community-Based Tourism Recommendations: A Pre-Deployment Validation Study
Abstract: Standard recommendation systems, which rely on static databases and historical user patterns, are fundamentally ill-suited for the dynamic and informal nature of Community-Based Tourism (CBT). In these environments, “items” such as local vendor schedules and seasonal activities are highly volatile and often undocumented, causing generic Large Language Models (LLMs) to frequently “hallucinate” or fabricate services that do not exist. This study presents a novel Tourism-Specific Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) Agent designed to bridge this gap. Unlike traditional recommenders that optimize for engagement, researchers' architecture optimizes for factual trustworthiness, integrating an agentic planner that autonomously retrieves real-time community data before generating advice. Researchers validated this approach through a comparative benchmark against a standard LLM baseline using 50 simulated traveler personas. The results quantify the critical risk of generic models: while the Base LLM achieved a dangerous Faithfulness score of only 0.25 (frequently inventing venues), researchers' RAG Agent achieved 0.56 Faithfulness and 0.60 Relevancy, with a complete elimination of unsafe recommendations. This work demonstrates that reliable tourism recommendation requires a specialized architecture capable of verifying ephemeral local knowledge, distinguishing it from general-purpose generative AI.

Document title: Autonomous Propellant-Constrained Multi-Target Space Debris Removal Planning via Action-Masked Deep Reinforcement Learning and RAG Operational Advisory
Abstract: The rapid accumulation of orbital debris threatens space sustainability. This paper presents a proof-of-concept hybrid planning framework that integrates action-masked Proximal Policy Optimization (MaskablePPO) with a BM25based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) compliance advisor for multi-target Active Debris Removal sequencing. Evaluated inside an intermediate-fidelity 3D Keplerian surrogate, the trained policy does not surpass deterministic greedy baselines in absolute target clearance (2.22 vs. 3.15 targets) but achieves sub-millisecond median decision latency $(930.1 \mu \mathrm{s})$, establishing a latency-optimality trade-off relevant to realtime operator consoles. The RAG layer retrieves international mitigation standards with Precision@3 of 83.3%. All results are conditioned on the surrogate simulator; high-fidelity propagator validation is identified as essential future work.

Document title: A Brief History of Application of Artificial Intelligence to Power Systems
Abstract: This paper tries to summarize the attempts to apply artificial intelligence (AI) to power systems, particularly power system planning and operations which require significant computer analysis. Although the term AI was coined earlier, this paper considers the beginning to be in the 1980s when the first expert systems were applied to power engineering. Of course, many of the analytical techniques applied can be traced to earlier statistical analysis and pattern recognition. The concept of expert systems was very much in line with the concept of AI. The various methods for applying AI to power systems are traced here. The historical journey in this paper closes with the great explosion of AI applications in the last decade when almost all power system analysis is trying to utilize AI techniques to help the transformation of the power system into a more efficient and carbon-free system. This proliferation of research in the application of AI is covered in the other papers in this series.

Document title: Adaptive Ant Colony Optimization With Dynamic Information Entropy for Multi-Robot Path Planning in Dynamic Environments
Abstract: Traditional Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algori thms often suffer from slow convergence, local optima trapping, a nd poor adaptability in dynamic multi-robot path planning scena rios. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Dynamic Infor mation Entropy Ant Colony Optimization (DIEACO) algorithm, which integrates three core improvements: (1) an adaptive phero mone evaporation strategy based on population diversity; (2) a dy namic heuristic function that fuses obstacle density and path smo othness; (3) an information entropy-based termination criterion $\mathbf{t}$ o reduce redundant iterations. Experiments are conducted in $\mathbf{5 0} \boldsymbol{\times} \mathbf{5 0}$ grid environments with static/dynamic obstacles, comparing D IEACO with standard ACO and hybrid ACO-artificial potential f ield (APF) methods. Results show that DIEACO reduces average path length by 4.81 %, shortens convergence time by 56 %, and im proves collision avoidance success rate to 98 % in multi-robot syst ems. This work provides a robust path planning solution for dyna mic intelligent systems such as warehouse robots and search-andrescue drones.

Document title: Enhancing Security Performance in Large-Scale UAVs System Based on Mean Field Game Theory
Abstract: The growing use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in wireless communication networks has increased the potential of eavesdropping, especially in the large-scale networks, which are the most vulnerable to this threat. This paper provides a solution, which uses mean field game (MFG) to improve the security and performance of large-scale communication networks of UAVs. The joint optimization of the UAV swarm in flight energy consumption, swarm congestion, obstacle avoidance risks, Quality of Service (QoS) constraint, and anti-eavesdropping requirement is modeled as a coupled system of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) and Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov (FPK) equations. A G-proximal Primal-Dual Hybrid Gradient (PDHG) algorithm is embraced to resolve this complicated system effectively. As shown in numerical simulations, the offered approach can make UAVs autonomously plan secure flight routes and dynamically change transmit power to avoid obstacles and guarantee the proper and safe communication with ground stations in a timely manner. Findings confirm the convergence and success of MFG-based model with probabilistic constrained conditions.

Document title: Research on Simulated Annealing Algorithm-Assisted Obstacle Avoidance Strategy and Platformization of Manipulator
Abstract: In response to the problems of traditional robotic arm obstacle avoidance algorithms being prone to falling into local optima, insufficient multimodal perception collaboration, and poor platform adaptation, this paper conducts research on simulated annealing algorithm assisted robotic arm obstacle avoidance strategies and platformization. Firstly, construct an obstacle avoidance algorithm that integrates improved artificial potential field method and simulated annealing: design joint space and Cartesian space dual potential fields to optimize path guidance, introduce Cauchy distribution perturbation and fast cooling strategy to improve simulated annealing, and solve the weak global optimization ability of traditional algorithms; Simultaneously combining fifth degree polynomial interpolation to achieve trajectory smoothing and ensure the smoothness of the robotic arm's motion. Secondly, a visual tactile multimodal perception module is built to enhance the robustness of obstacle environment perception through the coordination of highprecision visual positioning and tactile occlusion blind correction. Finally, a three-level platform architecture of “hardware software application” is constructed, relying on standardized interfaces and parameter databases to achieve rapid adaptation of multiple models of robotic arms. The experimental results show that the proposed strategy achieves obstacle avoidance success rates of 98.3%, 96.7%, and 93.3% in static, dynamic, and narrow channel scenarios, respectively. The planning time is shortened by more than 34% compared to traditional solutions, and the platform replacement of the robotic arm configuration time is controlled within 10 minutes, which can meet the efficient and reliable obstacle avoidance requirements of robotic arms in industrial scenarios.

Document title: Causality-Aware Scheduling and Mobility Control in Multi-UAV Cooperative MEC via Graph-Enhanced Dual-Timescale Learning
Abstract: Multi-uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) cooperative mobile edge computing (MEC) systems present significant challenges owing to task causal dependencies, dynamic channel variations, and multi-dimensional resource coupling. In this study, a multi-UAV cooperative MEC system with task causality constraints and time-varying wireless channels is considered, and the joint optimization of task offloading, task migration, dynamic UAV clustering, and continuous UAV trajectory planning is investigated. The objective is to minimize the long-term weighted sum of system latency and energy consumption while ensuring task queue stability. Lyapunov optimization is first introduced to transform the formulated stochastic mixed-integer problem into a deterministic per-slot optimization. Afterward, a dual-timescale graph-enhanced multi-agent proximal policy optimization (DT-HGMAPPO) framework is proposed to coordinate long-timescale UAV clustering and trajectory planning with short-timescale task offloading and migration. Specifically, this framework decouples the problem by utilizing dual-layer weighted hypergraph matching (DL-WHM) for joint clustering and association, a dynamic priority scoring (DPS) mechanism for intra-cluster load balancing, and a graph-enhanced MAPPO algorithm for trajectory optimization. Simulation results reveal that the proposed DT-HGMAPPO algorithm outperforms conventional multi-agent deep reinforcement learning baselines in terms of both convergence speed and policy stability. It achieves a final reward that is at least 18.0% greater than that of other multi-agent algorithms. Moreover, the proposed framework reduces total system cost by 33.3% compared with MASAC and 18.9% compared with MATD3, thereby achieving a superior delay-energy trade-off while ensuring queue stability.

Document title: Determining The Condition of City Green Spaces from Photographs
Abstract: Rapid urbanization and climate change threaten the health of urban green spaces, making timely detection of tree and shrub defects essential for public safety and environmental sustainability. Traditional manual inspections are labor-intensive and subjective, while existing mobile applications (such as PlantNet or iNaturalist) are limited to species identification and fail to diagnose trunk or crown defects in complex urban environments. This paper introduces GreenScan, a novel hybrid deep-learning system that simultaneously performs object detection, species classification, and defect diagnosis from ordinary photographs. Combining YOLOv8 for real-time localization and defect identification with EfficientNet-B3 for high-precision classification, the method overcomes urban challenges including object overlaps, variable lighting, and cluttered backgrounds. Trained on a custom dataset of over 10,000 annotated images (15 tree species, 14 shrub species, 10 defect classes), GreenScan achieves mAP@0.50 of 81.99 % for defects and Top-2 Accuracy exceeding 95 % for species. Implemented as a Flask web interface and Telegram bot with processing time under 2 seconds on GPU, the system enables automated, scalable monitoring, directly supporting UN Sustainable Development Goals 11 and 15 and outperforming baselines by 8–12 %.

Document title: Development of a Vision-Based Navigation System for Rendezvous and for Metrological Purposes
Abstract: The AltiCube+ mission involves the on-orbit assembly of multiple CubeSats to build two radar interferometers. To accomplish this, vision-based relative navigation is required both for target localization during rendezvous and for post-docking relative displacement estimation of structural deformation. This paper presents the design, simulation, and experimental validation of a compact monocular vision-based system capable of fulfilling both functions using a single camera architecture. The proposed system consists of a camera mounted on the chaser spacecraft and an active LED fiducial marker configuration on the target spacecraft. A non-planar marker geometry combined with colour-based segmentation enables robust detection over distances ranging from 10 m to close contact. Sub-pixel marker localization is performed using weighted centroiding and Gaussian fitting, followed by pose estimation through an Efficient Perspective-n-Point (EPnP) algorithm with iterative refinement. The results show that the proposed architecture can support both rendezvous localization and micrometre-scale structural deformation monitoring, providing a compact sensing solution for CubeSat assembly missions.

Document title: Machiavellian Robots and Their Theory of Mind
Abstract: The objective of this work is to develop and evaluate computational cognitive models of Theory of Mind (ToM) and Machiavellian behavior embedded in a humanoid robot. Machiavellianism, together with psychopathy and narcissism, is part of the Dark Triad (DT), three constructs that correspond to socially aversive yet not necessarily pathological personalities. The motivations of the present work are both theoretical and application-oriented. In the long term, we aim to: (i) Provide researchers with new insights into the Machiavellian as well as other DT constructs through simulated and robotic setups; (ii) Provide a tool to train psychologists to deal with social and antisocial behavior in a controlled setup; (iii) Help people become aware of the behavioral mechanisms that they may expect from people with DT traits in social and affective relationships; (iv) Assist robotic engineers in developing better robots by identifying behaviors that should be avoided. To this end, we explored a computational model of ToM in the popular Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL), and defined a domain with the necessary elements to induce Machiavellian behavior during planning and execution. Subsequently, we implemented our computational model in a software architecture controlling the behavior of a humanoid robot and recorded videos of the robot interacting with two actors. Finally, we conducted experiments with 300 participants divided into 6 conditions to verify whether the implemented framework is versatile enough to generate behaviors that participants would rate as either more Machiavellian or less Machiavellian based on their observations of the recorded videos.

Document title: A Dual-Robot Collaborative System Based on Visual Positioning for EOL Disassembly
Abstract: End-of-life (EOL) product disassembly is critical for industrial recycling and green manufacturing. However, manual dismantling is inefficient and high-risk, single-robot systems lack flexibility, and conventional HRC systems have task interruptions and weak dynamic planning, failing to meet SMEs’ low-cost and high-adaptability needs. To address this, a vision-guided dual-robot collaborative system based on Raspberry Pi master-slave architecture is proposed: visual positioning is achieved via OpenCV+YOLO (calculating L/S/V parameters for precise targeting); collaboration relies on dual Mycobot280PI arms (magnetic suction + gripper modules) with path planning by a “spatial hierarchy-connection strength-task unlocking” model, plus real-time communication (Socket) and motion control (pymycobot). Three-tier verification shows: Blender simulation reproduced workflows without conflicts; physical experiments (20 repetitions) achieved 100 % success in stable adsorption and precise clamping; MATLAB validated the algorithm' s dynamic adaptation. The low-cost, reusable system resolves traditional flaws, lowers SME thresholds, and lays a foundation for multi-product/multi-robot expansion, with future optimizations including voice control and deep learning-enhanced positioning.

Document title: An Improved Ant Colony Algorithm for Unmanned Collaborative Operations on Water Surfaces and Mult i-agent Task Allocation
Abstract: To address the issues of low path planning efficiency, uneven task allocation among multiple agents, and insufficient obstacle avoidance capabilities in complex environments during collaborative surface operations of heterogeneous unmanned systems, this paper proposes a collaborative operation architecture and optimization algorithm for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unmanned surface vessels (USVs) based on a partitioning strategy. First, a partitioned collaborative operation model is constructed, decoupling the global system optimization problem into two sub-problems: coverage path planning and multi-platform task allocation. Second, an improved ant colony algorithm is proposed to optimize target point traversal and dynamic obstacle avoidance path planning for USVs. A greedy algorithm is combined to achieve wide-area coverage path optimization for UAVs, and a particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to achieve balanced task allocation among multiple USVs. Results show that the proposed improved algorithm reduces the path length by 7.54% compared to the traditional greedy algorithm, improves the efficiency of UAV-USV collaborative operations by 80% compared to the traditional single-platform mode, and achieves a surface target detection accuracy exceeding 90%, validating the effectiveness of the proposed system and algorithm.

Document title: Agent Voyager: An Intelligent Travel Architect using AI Agents
Abstract: Modern destination planning is often seen to be overwhelming based on the overload of information, fragmented services, and language barrier that essentially hinder the ability of travellers to come up with an action plan in the form of a oneto-one, systematic planned travel. As a solution to these obstacles, the current project proposes a new application, Agent Voyager, a smart and multi-lingual travel advisor that is based on an advanced AI-based multi-agent framework. To provide a simplified experience of the entire travel-planning process, Agent Voyager tries to avoid the human touch in all that it does, including finding out the destination and recommending activities to do, as well as building an adaptive day-by-day itinerary based on personal preferences. Its architecture uses a team of dedicated agents, each endowed with specific tasks such as natural language understanding, new travel information reception, user preference modelling, integration of meteorological variables, among other distinct tasks so that Agent Voyager is capable of understanding the subtextual, multiphasic queries presented by its user and is able to generate scientifically optimized, contextually aware itineraries. The main element will be the Orchestration Agent, as it would coordinate the heterogeneous agents via the implementation of Large Language Models (LLMs), thus, guaranteeing smooth teamwork and informed decision-making across the platform. Together, Agent Voyager aims to provide a convenient and interactive travel-planning experience, resembling the effectiveness of a one-on-one travel-planner, consequent to the ability of their users to save time, and attain an enhanced degree of satisfaction with their forthcoming journey.

Document title: An Autonomous Agent for Closed-Loop Flight Procedure Execution and Verification in the X-Plane Simulator
Abstract: Scripted execution of flight crew procedures in the X-Plane simulator fails in a non-obvious way: realistic third-party aircraft add-ons monitor key state variables at roughly 20 Hz and reset external writes that disagree with their internal state machines, so a script that only writes target values never moves the ENGINE START switch. This paper describes an autonomous agent that executes structured procedure steps in X-Plane and verifying each step using state read-back instead of fixed timing. Write actions are dispatched through three channels, namely physical state variables, animation variables and add-on commands, in a staged order: physical and animation writes go first, and the command channel is invoked only when read-back shows the write was reset. Each step carries an entry assertion, an exit assertion and a time bound; verdicts use a verification delay, a stability window for lever-type controls, and latched trend assertions for rising indications. On 29 steps covering preflight preparation from a cold and dark state and the start of both engines of a mainstream aircraft, the No. 2 engine start chain passed 11 of 11 runs with a mean chain time of 79.16 s and a standard deviation of 0.36 s; an in-process Lua backend and an external Python backend returned identical verdicts on every step; an ablation that wrote physical variables only failed all 10 runs at the first step. Closed-loop execution also exposed two executor defects that no inspection of the generated scripts could reveal.

Document title: Trust-Aware Orchestration Architecture for LLM-Assisted Workflows in Multi-Tenant Enterprise Systems
